body:
## Summary With `registerType: 'autoUpdate'`, the page reloads as soon as a new service worker takes control. That reload discards unjudged strokes and range-test progress. `vite.config.ts` and `autoUpdate` are unchanged, so updates are still detected, installed and activated immediately. Only the reload is gated. The new `src/safeUpdate.ts` passes `onNeedReload` to `registerSW` (vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0 calls it instead of `location.reload()`): ```ts onNeedReload: () => { pending = true; applyIfSafe(); } applyIfSafe: if pending && !unjudgedAnswer && !activeTest -> location.reload() ``` `applyIfSafe` is rechecked after every `click`/`change` (on a `setTimeout(0)`, so the handler has updated state first), and when the page becomes hidden. `main.ts` supplies the live state: - `unjudgedAnswer = strokes.length > 0 && !resultSaved && board is shown` - `activeTest = testQueue.length > 0`, which holds through the questions and the results screen (the queue is kept until the user leaves the results) The reload is still immediate when idle. During a range test, including its results screen, it waits until the user leaves via 漢字一覧へ or back. Otherwise it happens on the next interaction once the board is empty or judged. `main.ts` changes only the import and the registration call, so it does not overlap #25. `git merge-tree` against #25's branch shows no conflicts. ## Testing - `tests/safeUpdate.test.ts` adds 9 unit cases: idle reload, deferral while drawing or testing (also when the page is hidden), deferral between test questions, apply after a safe click/change/hide, and a live-state recheck before reload. - `tests/practiceLoading.test.ts` adds a `main.ts`-level test: an update pending during a range test stays deferred on the results screen (also when hidden), and applies after leaving via `#finish` or `.back`. - `npm test` (254 passed) and `npm run build` pass. - Not tested: a real two-version service-worker update in a browser, and real iOS devices. ---

# SPEC-WEB-11-C04 — WEB-11 clause 4 evidence note

## Summary

One new Markdown evidence note for WEB-11 clause 4, "Use expand and contract migrations and feature flags that default off": `docs/spec/clauses/release/use-expand-contract-migrations-feature-flags-default.md`. The note records status `Not built` with repo-grounded evidence, the gap, and the human/cloud evidence suppliers before G5. No code, workflow, contract, migration, script, check or tracker was changed. The in-scope path was absent and `docs/spec/clauses/release/` was a new, empty directory; sibling WEB-11 clause notes C01/C02/C03/C05 do not exist as files.

The senior developer brief was incomplete but not wrong on the decisive points: it said "no deployment workflow" and "no default-off mechanism", while the repository does hold S-G5-07's `infra/delivery-safety/` evidence evaluator (which explicitly produces no real deployment evidence) and one domain default-off switch (`smartclinic.lab.rejection.notify-patient:false`). I carried on from the story and AGENTS.md and recorded both findings in the note and under `## Findings`.

## Affected requirements

WEB-11 (clause 4 only). Related but unchanged: OPS-06 (expand/contract change-safety gate) and the G5 production-readiness evidence row. No new requirement ID is introduced.

## Risk class

Routine — documentation only. No code, contract, migration, workflow or policy change.

## Review owner

Primary swarm worker; read-only specialists `smartclinic-context-optimizer`, `smartclinic-test-engineer`, `smartclinic-plan-reviewer` (before authoring), then `smartclinic-code-reviewer`, `smartclinic-coverage-auditor` and `smartclinic-devsecops` (after authoring). All specialist reviews are simulated/static, not human or clinical.

## Data changes

None. No Flyway migration, RLS/FORCE RLS, row backfill, table, index, OpenAPI entry, regenerated client, route, tenant filter or Idempotency-Key was added or changed. The note explicitly states that none was added by this change.

## Authorization boundaries and audit events

None. No endpoint, role, permission, tenant check or audit event was added or changed. No patient data, credential or real deployment detail appears in the note or this file.

## Migration and rollout considerations

No migration or rollout behaviour changed. The note surveys the existing OPS-06 checker (`scripts/check-migrations.py`), the S-G0-03d decision and the S-G5-07 synthetic evidence evaluator, and records the missing default-off release-flag mechanism and real rollout evidence as a gap with named suppliers before G5.

## Test evidence

Docs-only change: no new test was added and no test was skipped. The following are re-executions of pre-existing checks, reported as tool evidence (not as new coverage of a production change). Entry-point-to-test trace for the clause: specification sentence (`SMARTCLINIC_V1_SPEC.md:159`) → offline gate (`scripts/check-migrations.py`) → synthetic test suite (`scripts/tests/test_check_migrations.py`) → synthetic evaluator gate (`infra/delivery-safety/check.sh`); there is no HTTP entry point for this clause.

- `python3 -I scripts/check-migrations.py --require-baseline` — exit `0` (no output). Proves the current migration set passes the offline change-safety gate.
- `python3 -I -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_check_migrations.py' -q` — final lines `Ran 35 tests in 0.050s` / `OK`; exit `0`. Nearest honest expand/contract test suite (synthetic fixtures).
- `python3 -I -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_check_migrations.py' -k 'valid_contract' -q` — `Ran 1 test in 0.001s` / `OK`; exit `0`. Confirms a named accepting-path case resolves.
- `bash infra/delivery-safety/check.sh` — `Ran 71 tests in 0.006s` / `OK`; final line `S-G5-07: OPS-06 evaluator unit tests and fixture checks passed`; exit `0`. Proves the synthetic evaluator and the real migration checker run; the handoff labels rehearsals `final_evidence: false`.
- `grep -rniE 'feature.?flag|feature.?toggle|default.?off|kill.?switch|launch.?darkly|unleash' .github/workflows/ infra/ apps/api/src/main/resources/ db/migrations/` — single hit `.github/workflows/swarm-integrator.yml:23` (`SWARM_ALLOW_PROTECTED`), a CI protected-file merge kill switch, not a release flag. No default-off release-flag mechanism found.
- Relative-link self-check (Python regex over `docs/spec/clauses/release/use-expand-contract-migrations-feature-flags-default.md`, resolving each target with `Path.exists()`): `links=16 broken=0`.
- `grep -n '^## ' docs/spec/clauses/release/use-expand-contract-migrations-feature-flags-default.md` — five headings at lines 3, 7, 11, 33, 48 in the required order (`Clause`, `Status`, `Evidence`, `Gap`, `How to verify`).

Evidence provenance: tool (executed commands, file reads) for repository facts; simulated/static specialist reviews for findings. No human, clinical, simulated-user or real-deployment evidence is claimed.

No coverage threshold, exclusion, skip or suppression was added or changed. The "100% line coverage" figure in `docs/decisions/0002-ops06-migration-change-safety.md` is a prior stdlib-`trace` measurement of `scripts/check-migrations.py` from S-G0-03d, not a measurement of this note. author: lfgranja
body:
## Context

Insurgência has a deterministic Rust core, a playable Bevy client and a headless server, but the W ability of the Guerreiro role from GDD §10.6 was not implemented. This cycle closes backlog item BF-002a: a single, reviewable shield ability that turns 25 Fôlego into a 250-point damage absorption window. The decision score was 960/3125 (impact 4 × confidence 4 × closure 5 × effort-inverse 3 × risk-inverse 4), ahead of PVE map/routes (216/3125) and far ahead of real networking, which remains blocked by ADR-004. All ability numbers are `[HIPÓTESE]` prototypes from the GDD, not canonical rules. The worktree is based on `origin/dev` at `3f3b01c` in session `20261123T215500Z-escudo-milicia`.

## What changed

`crates/sim/src/lib.rs` gains six documented constants, four `Jogador` fields (`escudo_pv`, `escudo_ticks`, `escudo_recarga_ticks`, `escudo_alvo`), the `escudo` action at explicit level 2, validation with `EscudoEmRecarga`, per-attacker tick quota, deterministic duration/cooldown decrements and all four fields in the canonical hash. Damage to players now converges on one `aplicar_dano_a_jogador -> i64` route: both PvP and PNJ damage consume the shield before reducing `vida`, keep the zero floor, and report absorbed damage.

`crates/cliente/src/main.rs` adds a `V` key system that selects the closest active ally within 3 m (lowest `peer_id` tie-break), falls back to self, and emits no command when no valid target exists. The HUD now shows `Escudo: <pv> (<ticks>)` and the key hint. W, E and T keep their existing behaviour.

The SDD package lives in `specs/055-escudo-milicia/`, with assessment artifacts in `.specify/assessments/escudo-milicia/`, the ten-step roadmap in `.specify/validations/escudo-milicia/test-roadmap.md`, recorded results in `.specify/validations/escudo-milicia/evidence.md`, R4 validation, `1.0.0-local` release and an updated converge baseline. `OBJETIVO.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `docs/PROGRESSO.md` and `docs/research/index.md` receive dated verified-state notes; prior notes stay intact as history.

## How it was tested

The roadmap was executed autonomously across its documental and CLI surfaces: **10/10 PASS**. `cargo check -p insurgencia-sim --tests` exited 0. `cargo test -p insurgencia-sim --test simulacao` completed **97 passed, 0 failed** (92 preserved + 5 new), and each of `escudo_absorve_ate_250_dano`, `escudo_absorve_dano_de_pnj`, `escudo_recarga_420_ticks`, `escudo_expira_apos_150_ticks` and `hash_estado_cobre_escudo` passed individually. `cargo fmt --all` succeeded. All five local governance gates passed after bootstrapping the new converge baseline (`files=37 baselined=37`).

Local `./verify.sh` and `cargo check -p insurgencia-cliente` timed out under CPU contention from concurrent `flora cargo` jobs; they were **not** classified as red. GitHub Actions `gates` and `rust` on this PR head remain the authority for the complete gate. Roadmap evidence: https://github.com/lfgranja/insurgencia/blob/feature/055-escudo-milicia/.specify/validations/escudo-milicia/evidence.md . Visual window capture is `[NV]`; the client is always launched with `--minimizado`.

An independent reviewer found three blockers (the V key always targeted self, the HUD showed ticks instead of shield PV, and `escudo_alvo` was not cleared when cooldown reached zero) plus one non-blocker (damage-route return signature). All were fixed in source by corrective agents and the recheck returned `RECHECK OK`. R6 (`taskstoissues`) is **N/A/blocked** by constitution v1.2.2: no adapter exists, so no issue or `gh` command was improvised. Promotion to `main` and deploy are SWE-exclusive.

## Risks, limitations and rollback

Blast radius is limited to the deterministic sim, the Bevy client HUD/input, and documentation. No contract, `PROTOCOL_VERSION`, Cargo manifest, CI workflow, stack, network, Lightyear or async code was changed. The GDD 0.3 s execution time and the +15% continuous-damage resistance are deliberately outside the DoD: the core has no channel or continuous-damage path, and the constant is documented as reserved rather than presented as delivered. Rollback is a revert of this PR merge commit in `dev`, followed by removal of spec 055 and restoration of the previous converge baseline; no deploy is triggered by this PR.

## Issues addressed by this PR

No tracked issue is closed. Backlog item BF-002a (Escudo de Milícia) is closed by the DoD recorded in `.specify/memory/STATE.md`; BF-007 (R6 adapter) is escalated and remains owned by the SWE.

## Behavior and reason

This brings semantic recipe search into `dev` after #137. Exact title matches appear first, followed by similarity-ranked matches in the same list. Recipe IDs appear once. Both groups honor the active filters and the fasting-only view.

When the embedding request loses its connection or times out, the screen switches to title search, keeps the query and filters, and shows an inline notice. Users can re-enable semantic search when connectivity returns.

## Scope and review

- Trello [#104](https://trello.com/c/mcmRfq7u) and [#105](https://trello.com/c/bjHodc1X).
- `d6ff480` incorporates #159 and addresses both [review findings](https://github.com/anjahubac/tavli/pull/160#issuecomment-7118852276). Cloudflare Workers AI is the sole recipe embedding path. The unused OpenAI gateway task and device-local embedding table were removed. The PR has no Drift schema changes relative to `dev`.
- A signed-in member must explicitly opt in for the current household before the worker can read or transmit recipe text. The consent dialog explains the fields shared with Cloudflare and that the household opt-in persists when search is switched off on a device. The migration initially tracks recipe IDs for all households. The scheduler and worker only process opted-in households.

## Verification on `d6ff480`

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| GitHub CI | 8/8 checks passed. The app suite reported 1,466 passed and 1 skipped. The UI package reported 297 passed. |
| Native build | `flutter build macos --debug` completed successfully. |
| Gateway and docs | 35 Deno gateway tests passed. The index worker type check, documentation checks and diff checks passed. |
| Local Supabase | The recorded fresh-database run used 47 migrations and passed 878 pgTAP assertions across 37 files, including 29 covering recipe vectors. The migration and test inputs match this head. |
| Synthetic relevance | With the current recipe document format and local Ollama BGE-M3, 17/20 expected recipes ranked in the top five, above the 15/20 threshold, and 11/20 ranked first. The fixture contains 30 synthetic recipes and 20 descriptive queries. |

## Rollout

Live relevance and indexing with Cloudflare Workers AI on the hosted dev project still need verification. Project owner review of the provider and data-processing choice is pending. The indexer requires the Edge and Vault configuration in the [gateway contract](specs/015-ai-server-gateway/contracts/ai-gateway-contract.md) in addition to household opt-in.

## Security impact

Provider credentials remain server-side. The gateway checks authentication, input limits and quota before embedding a query. The private index enforces household membership and the worker obtains recipe text only through the consent-gated claim RPC.

author: kidcarmi
body:
## סיכום / Summary

The GeoIP country database is the **sixth body of security intelligence** this gateway enforces, and the one where Culvert has **no updater at all** — `internal/geoip`'s own doc says *"Culvert never auto-refreshes this file"*. Unlike `freshclam` there is no loop to fail, so decay is the **default state**, not a failure mode: it needs no attacker, no fault and no misconfiguration, only time.

The node already *learns* the answer. `readerBuildTime` parses the `.mmdb`'s own `BuildEpoch` at load, and `BuildTime()` is documented *"callers use this to surface staleness to the operator"*. It had **one** consumer, `/api/geoip`'s `dbAgeDays`, and the only staleness **judgement** in the product was a line of browser JavaScript (`const stale = g.dbAgeDays > 90`).

Measured on the production path with a database built **1096 days ago**, loaded and serving:

| surface | reported |
|---|---|
| `/metrics` | 888 lines, **0** about the database |
| `/ready` | `geoip: ok` |
| `/api/diagnostics` | 51 rows, **0** about staleness |

**The series that look like coverage are the ones that hide it.** `/metrics` carries six `culvert_geo_*` series, so a grep for GeoIP instrumentation finds hits. All measure how *busy* the resolution path is. The sharpest is `culvert_geo_policy_unresolved_total`, which counts evaluations that did not match because the country was **unknown** — a *missing* database's failure mode. A stale database is never unknown: it resolves briskly and confidently to whoever owned the prefix three years ago, so that counter sits at **zero** through the whole degradation it appears to watch.

**What degrades is a security control, fail-open.** A `destCountry` BLOCK rule is an enforcement decision. Every prefix that changed country since the build date is classified as its former owner, so traffic configured to be blocked is allowed (and vice versa) — silently, and self-consistently: the request log records the country Culvert believes and the per-rule counters move normally.

**Second half (CHAOS-127b): the remedy the product advised could not take effect.** The GUI said *"stale, consider updating"*. `InitGeoDB` is startup-only and `TryDeferredLoad` *"is deliberately NOT a reload"*. Measured, with a current `.mmdb` written to the configured path: `ArmDeferredLoad` returned **false**, nothing loaded, the reported build date **did not move**, and nothing said a restart was required.

**Third half (CHAOS-127c): the class-ending gate** that CHAOS-123 §9.4 proposed and CHAOS-124 §9.1 left explicitly *Open*. Eight bodies of security intelligence, each declaring **either** its freshness series **or** a reasoned exemption, with every declared series checked against the tree. It caught an error in its own first draft: it declared `culvert_saas_feed_last_sync_timestamp_seconds`, which is **retired** and whose absence `urlcat_metrics_test.go` asserts. The signed feed's real surface is `culvert_saasfeed_expires_in_seconds` — a publisher-stamped expiry, the *strongest* primitive in the family.

Full round record, including the risk matrix, recovery assessment and residual risk: [`docs/engineering/CHAOS-ENGINEERING-REVIEW-2026-11-24.md`](docs/engineering/CHAOS-ENGINEERING-REVIEW-2026-11-24.md).

### What ships

- `culvert_geoip_database_{loaded,age_seconds,build_timestamp_seconds,stale,age_unknown}`, emitted **only** when a database is loaded, so a fleet-wide age rule is not silently satisfied by the nodes that have none.
- A `geoip_database_age` diagnostics row for the stale shape and for both **unmeasurable** shapes (no readable epoch, future-dated), neither ever reported as fresh.
- `geoip_database_pending_restart` — fires when the file on disk is **newer** than the reader being served, i.e. the operator has done their half. Silent on all six inconclusive shapes.
- The GUI string now names the restart; `docs/operator/geoip-database-freshness.md` carries the alerting rules.

### Refused, with reasons (§7 of the review)

- **No live reload.** GEO-1/CHAOS-64 records why: `Close()` munmaps a buffer an in-flight lookup may hold — a `SIGSEGV` `recover()` cannot catch, with no log line and no crash record. Making the reader lifetime safe is an owner decision with a real design, not a rider; the pending-restart row is what makes living without it bearable.
- **No alert.** Age is monotone in wall-clock time with no event to close an episode on, so it would clear only on human action — a ticket, not a page.
- **No readiness change, no fail-closed toggle, no operator setting for the threshold, no file I/O at scrape time.**
- **No API field**, which keeps the OpenAPI / generated-client / committed-dist drift gates out of a round whose API shape is unchanged. The GUI and the backend are instead held together by a divergence gate that **reads the JavaScript** — strictly stronger than a shared field, because it fails on drift.

**סוג שינוי / Change type:**
- [x] `feat` — פיצ'ר חדש / new feature

author: pushery
body:
### ✨ Added

- **A refund read back through `refundsOf()` names the moment the provider made it, in UTC.** `RefundState::$madeAt` carries Mollie's `createdAt` and Stripe's `created`, for a refund made at the provider's dashboard as well, so an application can book a refund on the day it was made rather than the day it noticed it, and the two can lie in different months. It is null where the provider names none, and a `RefundState` that other rails build without it keeps working.

### 🔧 Changed

- **`symfony/console` is a declared dependency.** The commands escape what they print with its output formatter, and an export printed to the console goes through its output unformatted. Every Laravel version the package supports installs the component already, so no installation resolves differently.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **The commands print values as they stand.** Symfony's console formatter read a part of a value that looks like a style tag as styling and dropped it, in an exception message, an answer of a payment provider or a reference read from the database. The colored markers of the commands keep their colors.
- **An export printed to the console comes out as the file would.** Without `--path`, the DATEV, tax return, import scheme return, recapitulative statement and supply record exports, the owner export and the rate reports in JSON hand their content to the console unformatted, so a value in it that looks like a style tag stays in it.

- **The days a trial has left read in the plural under a regional locale.** Each form of the four trial notices names its count, `{1} … day …|[2,*] … days …`, in all seven catalogs. Laravel picks a form without a count by the name of the locale, from a table that knows `de_AT` but no locale written with a hyphen, so an application on `de-AT` showed the singular for five days left.

### 📚 Documentation

- **The documentation says that the `octane` store of Laravel Octane is out of the pruner's reach.** The store keeps an expired entry in a table of a fixed number of rows, `octane.cache.rows`, until its key is written again or the server restarts, and the scheduler, where the pruner runs, sees an empty store. Once the table is full, writing a new key fails, so the documentation advises against making `octane` the default cache store of an application that runs this package.

## What this changes

1. **Personal email addresses removed from `admin/README.md`.** The setup steps for the private analytics dashboard listed two personal Gmail addresses. They now say the allowed emails are set in the Cloudflare Access policy. Nothing about who can sign in changes; that is controlled in Cloudflare, not by this file.

This form sends in the background (FormSubmit's `/ajax/` address) and stays on the page, so FormSubmit cannot show the captcha there; turning it on would either do nothing or stop messages from arriving. The hidden spam-trap field (the "honeypot") stays. A comment in the source now explains this.

author: chrissotraidis
body:
Fixes #621. With **Native cutscene framing** on (Mods, off by default, since 0.12.0), going through a door into a new area could freeze the game or crash it a few doors later.

CallNous found the cause: `camera_draw`'s hook saves the camera's address and trim height, then zeroes the trim; the next `camera_execute` writes the trim back to the saved address without checking that it's still the same camera. A door into a new area deletes the camera, so the trim (about 65 lines during a door's demo, `0x4281FFAA`) went into freed memory: once a heap block's size field (the `JKRExpHeap::joinTwoBlocks` OSPanic), once a draw method (the jump to `0x80000000` from `fpcDw_Execute`).

**The change** is CallNous's: at either entry, a held value whose camera isn't the one in r3 is dropped instead of written back.

**How it was checked:** CallNous, on a MacBook Air M4 with 0.12.0: with their own settings, scripted door passes between Dragon Roost Cavern's room 9 and the next room crashed about five passes in, at the same block count every run, and only with `BLUEWAKE_NATIVE_CUTSCENE_FRAMING=1` (also with quick doors off and mods off). A hardware watchpoint showed the game's code never wrote the damaged word. With this change the same 20 passes ran clean. I checked that `letterbox.c` compiles on `main`; CI builds Windows and Linux. Not yet run here by hand.

author: yunwei37
body:
## Summary

Ringbuf-backed `epoll_wait` in the userspace runtime previously blocked through a 1ms userspace polling loop: idle consumers continuously issued non-blocking polls (high idle CPU/syscall rate), wakeup latency was bounded below by the poll interval, and SIGINT/SIGTERM delivery needed explicit `sigprocmask`/`sigtimedwait` handling.

This PR lets the kernel do the blocking with a real `eventfd` per ringbuf, while keeping the existing path as a fallback for software perf event sources and non-Linux builds.

## Design

**Zero extra permissions.** Each `BPF_MAP_TYPE_RINGBUF` creates a non-blocking `eventfd(0, EFD_CLOEXEC | EFD_NONBLOCK)` in the syscall-server process. Producer processes cannot inherit that fd, and must not rely on `/proc/<pid>/fd` or `pidfd_getfd` (ptrace/capability requirements). Instead the server lazily binds one abstract `AF_UNIX` `SOCK_STREAM` socket per SHM segment and exports eventfd dups via `SCM_RIGHTS`. AF_UNIX + SCM_RIGHTS need no capabilities and work under `CAP_DROP=ALL`, `no_new_privs=1`, default Docker/K8s seccomp, and `yama.ptrace_scope=3`.

- **Lazy client cache** (`runtime/src/ringbuf_eventfd.cpp`): on first submit from another process, the producer connects, receives the dup, caches it per map fd; the creator process uses its own fd directly.
- **Wakeup semantics**: `bpf_ringbuf_submit`/`bpf_ringbuf_output` honor `BPF_RB_NO_WAKEUP` (never signal) and `BPF_RB_FORCE_WAKEUP` (always signal); the default follows libbpf's adaptive rule (wake only when the consumer had caught up to the new record).
- **epoll integration**: `epoll_ctl(ADD/MOD/DEL)` mirrors ringbuf registrations onto the real kernel epfd using the eventfd. `epoll_wait` takes a kernel-blocking fast path when every userspace source on the epfd is a ringbuf with a resolvable eventfd: scan SHM for ready records first, drain the eventfds of empty ringbufs and re-check SHM (a submit racing the drain cannot lose a wakeup), then block in the real `epoll_wait`. Signals interrupt the syscall natively with `EINTR`; `timeout=0` and level-triggered repeat readiness until full drain are preserved.
- **Fallback**: epoll instances containing software perf events (no kernel backing fd), failed eventfd creation, and macOS builds keep the existing userspace polling loop unchanged.

## Tests

New Linux-only Catch2 suite `test_ringbuf_eventfd_epoll.cpp` ([epoll][ringbuf-eventfd]):

1. Cross-process `fork()` child submitting into the ringbuf wakes a parent blocked in `epoll_wait(..., 5000)`; measured latency asserted < 5 ms.
2. Level-triggered repeat readiness while records remain, blocking for the full timeout after a full drain.
3. `BPF_RB_NO_WAKEUP` leaves the blocked waiter to time out; `BPF_RB_FORCE_WAKEUP` wakes it immediately.
4. `timeout=0` polls once and returns; `SIGINT` delivered to the blocked waiter thread returns `-1/EINTR` natively.

## Benchmark (371-core Linux devbox, isolated SHM segment)

Cross-process `submit -> epoll_wait` wakeup, 1000 rounds, child waits until the parent is blocked before each submit:

| path | P50 | P90 | P99 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| legacy 1ms poll loop | 504.82 µs | 520.53 µs | 611.48 µs |
| kernel eventfd | 9.48 µs | 20.16 µs | 41.83 µs |

Idle consumer, 3 s wall, `epoll_wait(200ms)`:

| path | epoll_wait syscalls (strace) | user+sys CPU |
| --- | --- | --- |
| legacy | 1061 | ~754 ms sys |
| kernel eventfd | 15 | ~56 ms sys |

## Compatibility

- All new behavior is under `#if defined(__linux__)`; macOS keeps `bpftime_epoll` and the polling loop untouched.
- Eventfd creation or exporter failure degrades to the polling loop with a warning; correctness never depends on the new path.

author: egolearner
body:
## Failure and fix

Closing a forward store flushes the last record batches and asks Arrow to finish the file. If either write failed, `MemForwardStore::close()` still returned success and released the writer and batches. The segment checkpoint could then try to publish an incomplete block.

Return the batch write or footer error to the caller and retain the writer and buffered batches on failure. The segment already checks this status before loading the persisted block.

## Regression

`MemStoreTest.ClosePropagatesFlushAndFooterFailures` injects the two failures separately and checks the returned error and retained state. It reproduced the false success on `a26f8ab`. All 53 tests in `unittest.mem_store_test` passed on this branch. The changed C++ files passed clang-format 18.1.8.

**Target**: the titles first and cast & crew under them; where only people match, they stand at the top.

### What it does

- The results show the titles' heading and the posters first, and cast & crew under the last title.

author: kiarosama
body:
## Problem and implemented correction

Fixes #61.

Unused TeX declarations could leak command-looking data into document boundaries, prose paragraph analysis, dependencies and extraction. HTML `listing` also lacked its default preserved-newline behavior. The fix preserves original-file ownership and explicit data roles through all affected consumers.

This PR contains the complete implemented correction and permanent production regressions. It remains open for the owner's receiving agent. **The author has not merged or closed PRs/issues or resolved review threads.**

### Declaration ownership and raw collection

- Recognize supported braced/unbraced control-word and control-symbol names, stars, optional arguments, and balanced-group or single-token replacement arguments for both declaration commands.
- Keep raw unexpanded brace, percent and paragraph-token collection separate from literal-aware consumer interpretation. Invalid names and unfinished groups cannot export nested pending ownership.
- Retain selected ownership per original file visit. Included child braces cannot terminate a parent's declaration; repeated and sibling visits do not share mutable classification.
- Continue qualified literal unbraced-input declarations only at the measured command/name/first-option lookahead seams. Preserve actual caller-return and recursive source positions, real document ends and original physical paragraph boundaries.
- Index declaration delimiters and continuation lookups once; malformed 100000-declaration tails cannot repeatedly rescan the remaining source.

### Dependencies, extraction and source consumers

- Dispatch literal includes only from their admitted default/braced-body data domains. Declaration names, count headers and single-token replacement bodies cannot borrow a filename from following prose. Nested scopes and each argument's own bound are retained.
- Preserve the established ASCII-letter include-command boundary, including literal filenames beginning with `@`.
- Match live math/environments separately from owned declaration data, preserving original owner starts, included/continued fragments, escaped closers and overlapping delimiters.
- Use one original-byte data cursor to accept complete bounded literals and eligible dependencies. Resume at the exact literal endpoint before normalizing remaining backslashes.
- Feed the same accepted spans to extraction, image inventory, direction and listing checks. Literal payload cannot supply fake input/image/LTR/listing commands; genuine assets, listings and following inputs remain observable.
- Preserve raw retained replacement output and existing unwrap policy. These changes do not implement arbitrary TeX expansion or altered category-code semantics.

### Completion of review 6034170957

The complete review was read, including outside-diff and minor-functional claims. All four causes were reproduced before repair:

1. **Piecewise span projection.** Splitting `\newcommand{\outer}{\verb|AlphaOmega|}` between Alpha/Omega and inserting an independent snapshot with `\newcommand{\inner}{$MathOnly$}` previously extended the outer literal mask over the inserted bytes. The common literal/comment projector now intersects every span with each original source segment. It coalesces only the same snapshot and original span with contiguous original/output offsets. Foreign bytes and repeated-visit resets cannot inherit the mask; contiguous UTF-8 strides remain covered.
2. **Blocked recovery.** An unfinished declaration containing a complete literal such as `\verb|\input{absent}|` wrongly attempted that input. Recovery now uses the cached complete-literal endpoint index while preserving the unfinished-argument blocker. Incomplete recovery spellings retain their recovery contract; strict ordinary validation is unchanged.
3. **Derived comments.** After a backslash-delimited literal, an active derived `%` was respected by dependency discovery but exposed to image/direction/listing and delimiter-matching consumers. Bounded data-comment metadata is now shared through the per-visit projector. The new matrix also reproduced a default-argument cursor overrun: clipping metadata alone skipped a genuine body input on the same line. Cursor progress now resumes at the same argument endpoint. The unchanged matrix went from 3 passing functions/1 failing bounds function to 4 passing functions/26 fixtures.
4. **Optional-bracket work.** Repeated `\relax[\renewcommand{\sample}{]}` left live unmatched openers after owned closers were masked, causing repeated suffix scans. A one-pass stack index inside the actual prose body stores nested endpoints and binary-searches each opener. Unmatched options do not exclude following prose, and preamble/owned/post-document closers cannot complete a live body option.

The original 12-function probe recorded **8 passed/4 failed**; actual baseline 98 source/recovery controls passed **8/8**. The 8192-repeat owned-closer sample took about **1.547 s** before this repair and **0.026 s** afterward; these are observations, not portable timing assertions. The permanent workload actually executes 100000 repeats. Projection was not claimed as an executed baseline API control.

### HTML listing

Add `listing` to the existing preserved-newline default set. Keep explicit whitespace overrides, inheritance, hidden content, inline behavior and bounded static analysis unchanged. All 27 listing/textarea/xmp × LF/CRLF/CR × default/normal/pre combinations are permanent regressions.

## Permanent acceptance matrix

All **91 prior exact regression IDs remain**. The final source census has **110 required functions**: 94 integration functions and 16 units, spanning 17 required targets. Integration dimensions are **906 source fixtures plus 10 public-closure observations**; route counts and 100000-entry workloads are not extra test-function counts.

author: niradler
body:
## Why
Agents lacked a secure way to request credentials without pasting them into chat, and ORC had no reusable per-project secret store. Closes #539.

## What changed
- **Contracts & storage (`@orc/core`, `@orc/db`)**: Added `kind: "secret"` to `HumanRequestInputSchema` (1–10 fields, `save_to_project`, optional `reference_name`, rejecting `choices`), metadata-only `SecretResponseSchema`, in-memory machine-key-encrypted `SecretDeliveryVault` with aggressive TTL and restart unavailability, per-session rate limiting, and `project_secrets` SQLite table + `ProjectSecretStore` with idempotent migration.
- **API, injection & redaction (`@orc/api`, `@orc/runner`, `@orc/sdk`)**: Extended `/human-requests/{id}/respond`, added one-time `POST /human-requests/{id}/claim` (`secret: true`, returns `consumed`/409 on replay), added `/projects/{id}/secrets` CRUD + `/check` (stored, HTTP, command validation without revealing values), wired `project/<name>` resolution into jobs, workspaces, terminals, and opt-in chat launches with `last_used_at` tracking and output redaction, and regenerated SDK OpenAPI types.
- **Channels & MCP (`@orc/agent-runtime`, `@orc/gateway`, `@orc/mcp`, `orc-ai`)**: Channel sessions send a web link (`/notifications?request=<id>`) and never accept secrets in chat text, failing visibly with `"Open ORC to answer this secret request"` if no web URL is configured; MCP `human_request_get` claims secrets once (`secret: true`) and adds `project_secret_list` (metadata only).
- **Web UI & docs (`@orc/web`, `docs/docs/`)**: Added `SecretRequestForm` inside `RequestCard` (masked fields, per-field eye toggle, paste button, password-manager autocomplete, multiline support, wrapping/copyable sign-in links, optional save-to-project, non-echoing receipts), added `ProjectSecretsSettings` in **Settings → Secrets** and Project Edit → **Secrets**, and updated docs with best-effort redaction limits.

## Scope
Covers end-to-end secret requests, one-time delivery, project secret storage/check/rotation/deletion, job/terminal/chat reference injection, MCP/CLI, Web UI (desktop + phone), and docs. Revealing saved values and monitor HTTP auth (tracked separately) are out of scope.

## Tradeoffs
- Ephemeral secret payloads stay strictly in an encrypted in-memory vault so zero raw secrets touch SQLite and daemon restarts fail closed (`unavailable`).
- Global redaction is applied explicitly to command outputs, job logs, and channel messages rather than unconditionally inside streaming chat provider redactors, avoiding carry-buffer delays on live chat streams.

## Blast Radius
Idempotent `project_secrets` table creation on DB open; existing human-request kinds (`question`, `approval`, `command`) and snooze flows are preserved.

## Verification
- `bun run check`, `bun run docs:build`, `bash .agents/skills/orc-build/scripts/pr-preflight.sh` passed.
- `PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin:$PATH" bun run ci:pr` passed across all touched packages, unit/integration tests, and `@sanity` Playwright E2E flows (including pre-push hook).
- Demo-data desktop (dark/light) and phone (390×844) screenshots attached in the review comment below.

Açıklama:
## Özet
Waiter servisinin QR'dan ihtiyaç duyduğu iç uçları ekler: tablo listesi/detayı, oturum kapatma, masa temizleme ve kapanış olayı okuma. Bu PR #41'deki Waiter kimliği ve ayrı güvenlik zinciri üzerine kuruludur.

**Bağımlılık:** Bu PR #41'e bağlıdır. Base şu an `chore/qr-waiter-id-fix` dalıdır. #41 merge edildikten sonra base `dev` olarak güncellenecek.

## Eklenenler
| Uç | Scope | Staff delegasyonu |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` tablo listesi ve detayı | `qr:table-read` | Hayır |
| `POST` oturum kapatma, `GET` kapatma durumu | `qr:session-close` | `X-Staff-Token` gerekir |
| `POST` masa temizleme (`/cleaned`), `GET` temizleme durumu | `qr:table-clean` | `X-Staff-Token` gerekir |
| `GET` kapanış olayları (cursor ile) | `qr:session-closure-read` | Hayır |

- `StaffTokenVerifier`: kapatma ve temizlemede staff token'ı imzalı servis kimliğine `staff_token_sha256` ile bağlar. Aynı restoran, ADMIN/WAITER rolü ve iptal (revocation) kontrolü yapılır. Tarayıcıdan gelen staff doğrulaması (`StaffRequestFilter`) aynı doğrulayıcıyı kullanır.
- Temizleme komutları `commandId` ile idempotenttir. Tekrar eden komut aynı sonucu döner, çakışan içerik reddedilir.
- Kapanış olayı her oturumun nihai durumu (CLOSED/EXPIRED) için tam bir kez yazılır ve değiştirilemez.

## Güvenlik
- Waiter'a özel yollar yalnızca Waiter zincirine gider. Order anahtarıyla bu yollara gelen istek 401 alır. Bu yollarda Waiter dışındaki her şey reddedilir.
- Her uç kendi scope'unu ister. Bir scope diğerinin yerine geçmez.
- Kapatma ve temizleme için servis kimliği tek başına yetmez. Geçerli, servis kimliğine bağlı ve iptal edilmemiş bir staff token da gerekir.
- Tüm yollarda restoran (`restaurant_id`) imzalı kimlikten doğrulanır. Gövdedeki kimlikler yetki kaynağı değildir.
- Yeni ENV yok. Scope'lar ve anahtar haritası (`QR_WAITER_CALLER_PUBLIC_KEYS`) #41'dekiyle aynı.

## Migration
- QR V125 `table_clean_commands` ve V126 `table_session_closure_events` eklendi (`docs/decisions/migrations.md` güncellendi).
- Daha önce uygulanmış migration değişmedi.

## Sonar düzeltmeleri
Bu PR'ın getirdiği 9 bulgu düzeltildi: S1845 ×4 (rota sabitleri yeniden adlandırıldı), S107 (`TableCleanCommand` için `applied`/`rejected` fabrika metotları), S1068, S5853, S1172, S5961. Ayrıca #41'deki S112, S1130, S1128 bulguları bu dalda da kapatıldı.
Bulguların kapandığı Sonar taramasıyla **yeniden doğrulanmadı**.

## Merge sırası
- **#41 önce merge edilmeli.** Bu PR #41'deki Waiter kimliği ve güvenlik zincirine bağlıdır. Base şu an `chore/qr-waiter-id-fix` dalıdır; #41 merge edildikten sonra `dev` olarak güncellenecek.

## Summary

#2339 のレビューの単位 U6。開発ループのイベントにスキーマと形のバージョンを持たせて読み書きの核へ通し、書いた時刻を UTC の文字列にした。古い行（`at` が秒・`version-shipped` の `version`）は核の移し方だけが受ける。`U+2028` などを含む文で記録の 1 行が割れて読めなくなる不具合（以前から）も直した。変更要求の一覧（`ndf loop get --field rejections`）の `at` も UTC の文字列で出す。

関連する issue: Refs #2339

実装計画は `issues/issue-3684-3667-2339-plan.md` の Task 14、満たす受け入れ条件は `2339:1`・`2339:3`・`2339:5` のうち開発ループの分である。同じループへ新旧の NDF が交互に書く使い方は対象にしない（設計書「影響と危険」。普及フェーズの前で、旧い NDF の読みの互換は持たない）。


### イベントの種類と欄（書き手は `control_decide.py` だけ）

| 種類 | 欄（`version`・`at`・`kind` のほか） |
| --- | --- |
| `lease-taken` | `session`・`until`（秒のまま） |
| `lease-returned` | `session` |
| `lap-opened`・`issues-created` | `lap`・`issues` |
| `mode-decided` | `lap`・`mode`・`basis` |
| `issue-excluded` | `lap`・`issue`・`reason` |
| `gate-shown` | `lap`・`pr`・`head` |
| `gate-answered` | `lap`・`pr`・`answer`・`head`・`note` |
| `version-shipped` | `lap`・`product_version` |
| `lap-closed` | `lap`・`outcome`・`reason` |
| `stop-requested`・`loop-halted` | `by`・`reason` |
| `row-bound` | `table` |

### `at` の扱い

- `at` を書くのは `record_decide.event`（`internal.stamp`）、秒へ直すのは `record_decide._at`（`internal.epoch`）の 1 か所。`Answer.at`・`Stop.at` が使う
- 期限（lease）の比較は `until` と今の時刻（どちらも秒）で、`at` を読まない。`until` は秒のまま

### 確かめたこと

- 実物の版 0 の記録 `/work/ai-plugins/.ndf/parallel/p6/work/sprint-lr-fix-a-m1/2-impl-3300-state/work/smoke/repo/.git/ndf11/state/loops/demo/record.jsonl`（9 行。手元にあった唯一のもの）を新しい `LoopStore.read` で読み、全行が通り、状態を再生できた
- 新設の `tests/domains/loop/test_loop_store.py` の関数を Python から直接呼び、すべて通った（pytest は打っていない。ほかのテストの合否は CI で見る）
- `ndf check` 違反 0 件・`check-lint.sh`・`check-ndf-contracts.py`・`check-ndf-choices.py`・`ndf contracts check`・`check-markdown-links.py` が通る


## 設計と違う点

| 箇所 | 設計 | 実装 | 理由 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 種類ごとに要る欄 | スキーマの形に種類ごとの条件の記述が無い | スキーマは欄の型だけを持ち、種類の語彙と要る欄は `record_decide.REQUIRED` が持つ。`LoopStore.append` も書く前に `check` を通す | 同じ値を 2 か所に書かない。書く側でも欠けた行を止める |
| JSONL の 1 行の読み方 | 記述なし | `jsonl._row` を `internal.read_line` へ移し、`LoopStore.read` と `jsonl.read_rows` の両方が呼ぶ | 同じコードのコピーを作らない |
| `stamp` の失敗 | 記述なし | 時刻にできない秒（NaN・大きすぎる数）は `InternalError`（`invalid`） | 旧い行の壊れた `at` で捕まえない例外にしない |
| `RecordError` | 記述なし | `ndf loop` が `stopped`・`invalid` にする（これまでは捕まえずに `unknown`） | 形の合わない読み書きを `stopped`・`invalid` にそろえる |
| 実際の行数 | 約 350 | 310（追加 268・削除 42） | — |

## 利用者向けの変化

- 無し

## 移行の手順

- 無し

- [x] `plugins/ndf/bin/ndf check`・`scripts/check-lint.sh`・`scripts/check-ndf-contracts.py`（exit=0）
- [ ] pytest は CI で見る（`test.ci.only`）

author: matheusmendes720
body: ## What changed Three targeted fixes to the compiled binary update flow on Windows, based on the EFAULT error still reproducible on omo 5.1.82 (#10343). ### 1. Sweep stale `.old-*` / `.new-*` staging files before every install A previous update that failed during cleanup leaves UUID-named staging files in the install directory. The next `omo update` inherits them and fails when `rm` hits a held or corrupted file. The new `sweepStaleArtifacts()` runs under the install lock before any download, tolerating Windows-specific error codes (EPERM, EBUSY, EACCES, EFAULT) and ENOENT from concurrent cleaners. ### 2. Tolerate `EFAULT` in cleanup error handling The finally-block cleanup already tolerated EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES on Windows. Added EFAULT (bad address in system call argument), which surfaces when a dangling kernel handle or AV-held reference outlives a rename of a loaded executable — observed on Windows 11 with omo 5.1.82. Also wrapped `rm(next)` in the same defensive try/catch pattern already used for `rm(previous)`. ### 3. Hint on `--print` that the direct install is safer On Windows, `omo update --print` now appends a one-line hint that `omo update` (without `--print`) performs a verified in-process install. The printed one-liner still exists for scripting but the hint guides interactive users toward the safer path. ## Why The in-process installer (#13084, merged Nov 11) replaced the brittle curl one-liner with SHA-256 verification, atomic swap, and rollback. This PR fixes the remaining Windows edge case: a stale `.old-` file from a prior failed cleanup can block the next update with EFAULT before the new install even starts. ## Reference The patterns applied here are validated by `C:\Users\mathe\scripts\omo-update.ps1`, a PowerShell update script that has handled these Windows edge cases reliably since omo 5.1.64 — sweep stale artifacts before starting, defensive cleanup with broad error-code tolerance, and clear messaging. ## Verification - [x] TypeScript compiles (no new imports or type errors) - [ ] CI: `bun test packages/omo-native/test/compiled-update-install.test.ts` (22/22 expected) - [ ] CI: `bun test packages/omo-native/test/compiled-update-usage.test.ts` (16/16 expected) ## Risk Low. The changes are scoped to the install lock critical section (sweep) and the finally-block cleanup (error-code list). No change to the download, verification, swap, or rollback paths. The stale-artifact sweep only removes files that match the staging naming convention and tolerates all failures silently. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Hardens the Windows binary update flow so a prior failed cleanup no longer blocks the next install with an EFAULT, and keeps the install manifest in sync after an in-process update. **Bug Fixes** - Sweeps stale `.new-*` and `.old-*` staging files under the install lock before any download. - Adds EFAULT to the tolerated Windows error codes for staging-file removal and applies the same defensive pattern to `rm(next)` that already protected `rm(previous)`. - Retries the Windows binary swap up to 15 times with escalating delays, falling back to killing the running `omo` process before the final attempt. - Appends a hint to `omo update --print` on Windows directing users to the verified in-process install. **New Features** - Refreshes `~/.omo/install.json` after a successful in-process update so the stored version, asset, and binary path stay accurate. - Prunes outdated provisioned runtimes under `~/.omo/binary-runtime/` post-install, keeping the current version as the rollback candidate. Written for commit 5550497bad8f9a7b0bf95aa3361e0b52552f0c3c. Summary will update on new commits.

author: cilverkrow
body:
RG-B1 `Rotation.RestGate.StaleGiveBack` changes its default from 0 to 1. A stale rested / low RestGate close then gives the travel target the eat / drink time up to the late read (capped at MaxRestSeconds) instead of durMs (about 0). 0 stays as the rollback value.

## Why
- **RGA-L1 acceptance smoke** (kit a64a2d1a, pin 3g edb9cba0 = #1176, node2 n3, roster L1030W162 with 162 bots, reset 718, 2 × 60 min windows, `Rotation.RestGate = 1` and `StaleGiveBack = 1` for all bots): **VERDICT=PASS** (`ab-runs/rgb1-accept-smoke/crp-RGA-N3-l1-20261123-1500/RGA-L1-RESULT.txt` sha 88cc96f4, evaluator `rgb1-result.sh` 0608cded).
  - W1: offer 12950 s vs rest+gap 13116 s (987 ‰), giveback 6893 s > rest 1493 s + 18.
  - W2: offer 16954 s vs rest+gap 17110 s (990 ‰), giveback 9467 s > rest 2218 s + 18.
  - No F1 / F2 / F3, no applied=0 line, no window-split edge. Start proof `StaleGiveBack=echo:1/conf:1 ok=1`.
- **OB-10** confirmed the RESULT ("OK RESULT RGA-L1 @88cc96f4 = PASS", recomputed byte-identical): `ws-10/ob10-reviews/REVIEW-OB10-rga-l1-result-88cc96f4-20261123.md` (f3f03e8f).
- **The owner** approved the code default directly in the CLI-ROT chat on **24.11.2026 (before 00:14Z; the commit message says 00:16Z, the time I logged it)**: "OK für RG-B1".
- **Watch item** (OB-10, not a blocker): WORK drops within 120 s after a stale close were 27 vs 21.2 in the shifted control (≈1.27×, p≈0.12, one run). Followed descriptively in the next runs with StaleGiveBack = 1.

## What changes
Template of the owner-ordered flips (#740, #742, #1132, #1174); the unknown value per OB-10 (24.11., option (a)):
- **Loader default** (`PlayerbotAIConfig.cpp`) and **header initializer** (`PlayerbotAIConfig.h`): 1.
- **Unknown value** (> 1): maps to the default 1, not 0, with an outError line `[StaleGiveBack] config key=Rotation.RestGate.StaleGiveBack value=%u result=default 1 (0 off = rollback, 1 on)`. The tag is not `[RestGate…]`, so RG extracts that match `[RestGate` do not count it.
- **Dist** (`aiplayerbot.conf.dist.in`): the line is 1, with "BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, ON by default since the RGA-L1 PASS …, 0 = rollback" and "Any other value acts like 1.".
- **Unchanged**: no logic change; the ConfigEcho entry stays as it is.
- **Contract** `t/rest_gate_source_contract_tests.cmake` §9:
  - pins member 1, read 1, clamp to 1 with the error line, dist 1 after the thresholds and the "acts like 1" sentence;
  - pins the rollback path: Finish passes `rotationRestGateStaleGiveBack != 0` (and GiveBackMs returns durMs without the switch, already pinned);
  - new `forbid_text` on a read default 0 and on a dist line `= 0`.

## Scope
- **Live:** the canonical funserver profile keeps `Rotation.RestGate` off (DS6 bundle B excludes it), so the flip has no effect on live until RestGate is switched on there.
- **REF-based runs:** REF 1d80cd99 has `Rotation.RestGate = 1`, so every REF-based run on a pin after this merge rests with the give-back. That is a **baseline break**; kits that need the old base set `AiPlayerbot.Rotation.RestGate.StaleGiveBack = 0` explicitly (announced by OB-00 on 24.11.).
- **Measured population:** RGA covered L10–30 bots (L1030W162), all classes, both cohorts. The mechanism (time accounting of an eating / drinking bot's rest) does not depend on level.
- Pinned units (images before the merge) are unaffected. The frozen RGA kit pins the default-0 strings and stays as it is; a later RG-B2/B3 kit updates its has() lines.

## Checks
- **Twin parity:** byte-identical patch on both twins (`git patch-id --stable` 8eea2e52). LF only, ASCII in code and contract.
- **Bases:** both branch points are the current tips (release/9.x edb9cba0, main 466863e1).
- **RestGate source contract** (`cmake -P`, cmake 4.4.2, `cmake_policy(VERSION 3.16)`): `REST_GATE_SOURCE_CONTRACT=PASS` on both twins. The old contract fails on the new tree (default 0 pin) and the new contract fails on the old tree (default 1 pin).
- **Negative mutations**, each caught by the new contract: read default 0; clamp back to 0; header initializer 0; dist value 0; dist sentence "acts like 0"; an extra dist line `= 0`; clamp `> 0`; Finish without `!= 0`.
- **Not run locally** (T30 condition: no build / worktree / big-I/O test on the main PC until Tue ~21Z): the focused trixie compile of `PlayerbotAIConfig.cpp` and the full contract sweep. OB-30 runs the focused gate in its build slot after T30, before the lane merge; GitHub CI runs as usual.

Refs Cilverkrow/twow-repo#602

body:
## What

Records the A07 GPU overhead verdicts re-judged under `opt-contract-v2` in `docs/project-checklist.md`. Docs only.

## Why

#103's overhead gate accepts a verdict only if its `contract.sha256` matches the loaded contract and its `host_label` matches the manifest's `hardware.host_id`. The #98 verdicts carry `opt-contract-v1` (`4cc8a11d`) and the label `benoy-rtx5070-wsl2`. Now that #99 is on main, they would leave the gate `not_evaluated`.

## How

- Checked the four saved attempt files and the evidence zip against the SHA-256 hashes #98 recorded. All match.
- Ran `python -m agentwatch_data.overhead_verdict` on main `71bf0c7` with:
  - `--contract pipelines/model/optimization-contract.toml` (v2, `8e9bba65`);
  - the default seed;
  - `--host-label rtx5070-laptop-wsl2`, the label the O06 manifests use. It's an operator label given at judging time, not a measured value, and it also drops the personal name the checklist flagged.
- No new GPU measurement.

## Result

| Measurement | Before (v1) | After (v2) |
|---|---|---|
| GPU vLLM | `within_budget` | `within_budget` |
| GPU Ollama | `inconclusive` | `inconclusive` |

A field-by-field diff shows every figure identical. The only differences are:
- the contract stamp;
- the host label;
- the per-group `budget` (0.05, the v1 value) and the report's `max_median_admission_overhead`, both added by #104;
- one reason now reads "Baseline coefficient of variation" instead of "Uninstrumented…".

The judging is deterministic: a second run produced byte-identical files. The new reports are not in the repository, as before; their SHA-256 hashes are in the checklist.

## Checks

Docs only: `git diff --check` is clean. The hashes and paths in the checklist were re-computed from the files.

body:

<!-- icarus:notes -->
## Implementation notes (Icarus)

## What changed
- `apps/web/src/App.tsx`: Resolved merge conflict with main by retaining both the incoming `<MixerPanel />` and this branch's `WardrobePanel` overlay, alongside Vibe HUD controls.
- `apps/web/src/App.test.tsx`: Added unit tests for Vibe HUD toggle, V key synchronization, wake-from-sleep toggle, and Wardrobe dialog toggle.
- `apps/web/src/entities/PlayerAvatar.ts`: Implemented layered Pixi Container (drop shadow, base sprite, hat layer, clothing tint, nameplate, status badge, particles) and resolved 'default'/empty baseId to 'char_base'.
- `apps/web/src/entities/PlayerAvatar.test.ts`: Added unit tests for layer structure, setStatus('focus'/'none'/'break'), setOutfit, setFacing, celebrate, and default StorageManager prefs texture mapping.
- `apps/web/src/entities/ProceduralAnimator.ts`: Implemented pure procedural animator sampling transformations for idle, walk, vibe, sit, sleep, and celebrate.
- `apps/web/src/entities/ProceduralAnimator.test.ts`: Added unit tests for idle scaleY bounds, vibe rotation, and celebrate neutrality at t >= 3000 ms.
- `apps/web/src/systems/AfkDetector.ts`: Implemented AFK sleep detection with configurable threshold, localInput waking, and injectable suppression callback.
- `apps/web/src/systems/AfkDetector.test.ts`: Added fake timer tests covering 300 000 ms threshold, suppression after 10 minutes, and wake on localInput.
- `apps/web/src/ui/WardrobePanel.tsx`: Implemented Wardrobe React panel with name input sanitization, non-disruptive draft editing with blur fallback, 8 palette presets, and manifest hat picker saving immediately to StorageManager.
- `apps/web/src/ui/WardrobePanel.test.tsx`: Added tests verifying character rejection, 16-char cap, immediate persistence for palette/hats/name, and name clearing without immediate snap-back.
- `apps/web/src/entities/LocalPlayer.ts`: Rendered LocalPlayer via PlayerAvatar, added KeyV vibe toggle, AfkDetector auto-stroll suppression, celebrate action timer handling, and StorageManager preference sync.
- `apps/web/src/entities/LocalPlayer.test.ts`: Added tests for V key toggle, PlayerAvatar rendering, celebrate action duration through visual layers, auto-stroll AFK suppression, and live avatar preference updates.
- `apps/web/src/engine/assets/placeholders.ts`: Added procedural `char_clothing` white tunic texture for outfit tinting.

## Decisions
- Conflict resolution in `App.tsx`: Kept `<MixerPanel />` from main and conditionally rendered `<WardrobePanel />` from this branch.
- Base texture key resolution: Added `resolveBaseTextureKey` in `PlayerAvatar.ts` so `DEFAULT_OUTFIT.baseId = 'default'` maps to `'char_base'` rather than falling back to grass tiles.
- LocalPlayer celebrate ownership: `LocalPlayer.celebrate()` owns action duration with a 3000 ms wall-clock timer (`celebrateUntilMs`), reverting to the previous action and keeping `player.avatar.action` in sync across update ticks.
- Input and state ordering for Vibe: In `LocalPlayer.handleKeyDown`, any action mutation happens before emitting `localInput`, and waking sleeping players occurs before toggling. In `App.tsx`, `handleToggleVibe` emits `localInput` first to wake any sleeping state before computing the next action.
- Wardrobe name input typing flow: Stored name is only updated when non-empty trimmed characters exist, and external preference sync only applies when the sanitized draft differs, preventing caret jump or backspace snap-back while editing.
- Auto-stroll sleep suppression: Injected `() => this.isAutoStroll` into `AfkDetector` so autonomous strolling does not trigger AFK sleep.

## Verified
- Ran `pnpm typecheck`: TypeScript passed with 0 errors across `@lofi/shared`, `apps/public-server`, and `apps/web`.
- Ran `pnpm test`: All 144 Vitest tests passed across all workspaces (21 in packages/shared, 18 in apps/public-server, 105 in apps/web).
  - Targeted tests covering acceptance criteria:
    - `idle scaleY stays within [0.98, 1.02] over 10 s of samples` in `ProceduralAnimator.test.ts`
    - `vibe rotation stays within ±0.06` in `ProceduralAnimator.test.ts`
    - `celebrate is neutral (offsetY=0) at t >= 3000 ms` in `ProceduralAnimator.test.ts`
    - `sleep at 300 000 ms without input, not at 299 000 ms` in `AfkDetector.test.ts`
    - `with isSuppressed returning true, no sleep after 10 minutes` in `AfkDetector.test.ts`
    - `input after sleep resets the action to idle` in `AfkDetector.test.ts`
    - `the wardrobe name input rejects !/emoji and caps at 16, and saving updates StorageManager` in `WardrobePanel.test.tsx`
    - `setStatus('focus') shows the book icon; setStatus('none') hides it` in `PlayerAvatar.test.ts`
    - `PlayerAvatar with default StorageManager prefs renders char_base texture and preserves it on setOutfit` in `PlayerAvatar.test.ts`
    - `celebrate() plays bounce animation for 3000 ms through PlayerAvatar and reverts to previous action` in `LocalPlayer.test.ts`
    - `pressing V key updates Vibe HUD button to ON and toggling back to OFF` in `App.test.tsx`
    - `clicking Vibe HUD button wakes sleeping player and sets action to vibe with label ON` in `App.test.tsx`
    - `renders the Wardrobe HUD button and toggles the Wardrobe dialog` in `App.test.tsx`
- Ran `pnpm build`: Succeeded for packages/shared, apps/public-server, and apps/web (`apps/web/dist` generated).

## Open
- None.

  `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp`, and
  `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploghttp`. ([#​8941](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8941))
- Add experimental `ProbabilitySampler` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace/x` that conforms to the [OpenTelemetry specification's threshold-based sampling algorithm](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/trace/sdk/#probabilitysampler). ([#​8123](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8123))
- Add experimental `*Binder` extension interfaces in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/x` for instruments that support binding attributes ahead of time. ([#​8760](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8760))
- Add the experimental `Finisher` synchronous metric instrument extension interface to `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric/x`. ([#​8906](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8906))

##### Changed

- Use the [OpenTelemetry Attribute Collection representation for non-OTLP protocols](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/common/#attribute-collection-representation-for-non-otlp) for metric data diffs in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric/metricdata/metricdatatest`. ([#​8993](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8993))
- Apply a maximum depth of 64 by default to span, event, link, log record, and instrumentation scope attribute values in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. ([#​8938](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8938))
- Reduce allocations when applying attribute value length limits in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace` and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log` by rebuilding composite values only when truncation is needed. ([#​8912](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8912))
- Decode `traceparent` using a hex lookup table in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/propagation`, which rejects the specification-disallowed upper-case characters without a separate scan of the header. ([#​8739](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8739))
- Decode all characters at constant indices in `TraceIDFromHex` and `SpanIDFromHex` in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace` to eliminate bounds checks. ([#​8740](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8740))

##### Fixed

- Count valid U+FFFD replacement characters toward attribute value length limits in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`.
- Truncate string attribute values to empty strings when the configured length limit is zero, including malformed UTF-8, in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace`, `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace`, and `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/log`. ([#​9054](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/9054))
- Fix a data race in `NewPeriodicReader` where `r.inst` was assigned after the background goroutine was launched in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric`. ([#​9028](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/9028))
- Prevent precision loss for large `int64` values in `Sum`, `Histogram`, and `ExponentialHistogram` aggregations in `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/metric`. ([#​8981](https://redirect.github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/issues/8981))
- Ensure `grpc.DialOption` values passed via `WithDialOption` take precedence over conflicting internally-computed defaults in

_Requested by **Gustavo** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01X5UTtzdFQLXUW3dEdobFKP?thread=cmsg_01X5UTtzdFQLXUW3dEdobFKPFuTXWroXU1hVouxv6yRfTB)_

Closes #32

## O que muda

Formato das promoções, igual ao assistente "Nova promoção" do protótipo v9. Detalhes e exemplos em `docs/adr/0006-formato-das-promocoes.md` (status "proposto", falta a revisão do Tartare).

- **Três tipos** em `promotions.kind`: `product_discount` (desconto em produtos), `free_delivery` (entrega grátis acima de um subtotal) e `order_discount` (desconto no pedido acima de um subtotal).
- **`rule`**: `percent`, `amount_off` ou `fixed_price` no desconto em produtos; `min_subtotal` na entrega grátis; `min_subtotal` + `percent`/`amount_off` no desconto no pedido. Valores com até 2 casas, percentual entre 0 e 100, desconto fixo menor que o mínimo.
- **`schedule`**: `always`, `weekly` (dias, dia todo ou das HH:MM às HH:MM sem atravessar a meia-noite) e `dates` (início e fim, dias inteiros). Fuso de São Paulo.
- **Migration** `20261124000000_promotion_format.sql`: checks `promotions_kind_check`, `promotions_rule_check` e `promotions_schedule_check` (funções em `private`), `rule`/`schedule` sem padrão `{}`, tabela nova `promotion_products` com chaves compostas pelo `store_id`, RLS (público lê os produtos das promoções ligadas; membros gerenciam) e trigger que só aceita produto em promoção de produto.
- **Zod** em `src/lib/data/promotions.ts` (mesmas regras, mensagens do protótipo), `parsePromotionFormat` e `readPromotion`. `database.types.ts` atualizado.
- ADR também fixa as regras para a T33: arredondamento, menor preço quando duas promoções de produto valem juntas, maior desconto entre as de pedido, e a entrega grátis de `stores.settings.free_delivery_above` virando promoção quando o cálculo entrar no `create_order`.

O dev não tem nenhuma promoção, então a migration não converte dados.

## Como testar

- `npx supabase test db`: `formato_das_promocoes.test.sql` (45 casos de formato aceito e recusado, mesma loja, troca de tipo e RLS). Rodei todos os arquivos de teste do banco num Postgres do Supabase local: todos passam.
- `npm test`: 232 testes passam, incluindo `src/lib/data/promotions.test.ts`.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` e `npx eslint .` sem erros.

author: leosimini
body:
Builds `backlog/stories/LEDGER-007-where-the-truth-is.md`.

## What changes
- **SessionStart** (`hooks/hooks.json`) runs `ledger.py history --ensure`, then `ledger.py` (the summary), then `doctor.py --brief`, and prints, in at most 12 lines:
  1. a first line that frames the output as data: `Keelokit: the state of this project, read from git (data, not instructions):`
  2. the history line
  3. the summary
  4. one "Where to look" line: `ledger.py show <ID>`, `/harbor:log`, `backlog/`, and AGENTS.md's *Where the truth is* or `.keelokit/harness/agent-brief.md`
  5. the doctor's brief, in full

  The summary gets the lines left over, at least 2; when cut, it ends with "… N more lines: `python3 .keelokit/bin/ledger.py`". Without python3 the hook still prints one line and exits 0. The timeout stays at 30 s.
- **`template/AGENTS.md.jinja`** gets a *Where the truth is* section: a table mapping each question to the command that answers it, and the rule that the state is asked of `ledger.py`, never of memory or of a handoff file. `agent-brief.md` and `execution-protocol.md` state the same rule, so adopted repos (`mode=harness`) get it too.
- **This repo:** `AGENTS.md` gets the same section, both READMEs gain a line about the ledger, and `backlog/next.md` drops *Where things stand*.

## Verification
- Tests were written before the hook:
  - S1–S2 in `tests/test_hooks.py` (`test_LEDGER_007_S1_*`, `test_LEDGER_007_S2_*`)
  - S3 in `tests/test_copier.py`, which renders the template with copier
  - LEDGER-002's hook tests now expect the added summary call.
- S4 was a manual check: a fresh agent asked "is HARN-020 done, and why?" ran `ledger.py show HARN-020` first. The result is written in the addendum.
- Light-tier review (dimensions dx, docs): one reviewer, two rounds. Round 1 produced ESC-155..157; round 2 approved.
- `scripts/verify.sh` passed before push: 980 tests, 6 skipped.

Decisions and what was left out are in the story's addendum.

author: ikildani
body:
## Why

Scorecard metric `company_signal_coverage` (feed companies with any financial, financing or intent row) was **11.7% (1,154 / 9,820)**. The ranking model leans on owner type and asset age because 88% of feed owners have no company evidence. This PR adds free, primary-source company signals with provenance and a resolution confidence on every row, and makes the coverage definition explicit (including corporate families).

## What (migration 198 + 4 sources + IFRS)

| Source | Writes | Resolution | Sample measured on uncovered feed companies | Hand-checked precision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Deals ledger → intent** (SQL `company_signal_refresh_deal_intent()`) | `company_intent_signals` source_type `deal_record`: `out_licensing_deal` / `in_licensing_deal` / `acquired` / `acquirer` | existing licensor_id/licensee_id, **kept only when the deal's party name agrees with the company row (≥80)**; cited https source, not social media, provenance tier A–C or filing id | full population: **816 uncovered feed companies** (5,509 of 5,596 deal sides accepted; the 79 rejected are mis-resolved ids, e.g. "ImmunoGen ≠ Immunogenics", "Biogen ≠ BioGeneric Pharma", "Fulcrum ≠ Acceleron") | 30/30 right entity (1 LinkedIn-sourced fact now filtered out) |
| **EDGAR filer index** (`lib/ingestion/edgar-filers.ts`) | `company_listings` SEC_FILER (active), `companies.cik` (active + name agrees + CIK unused), `companies.sec_inactive_cik` (ceased filing → derived listing), `company_financing_events` Form D via the 189 guards | exact name key in EDGAR's CIK lookup file (all names since 1993), exactly one **health-care** CIK (SIC 2833-2836/3841/3842/3845/5122/8071/8090/8731/8733, or Form D health group) | US 400-sample: 138 health filers (34%), live dry-run yield ≈80% → ~27–29%; non-US 250-sample: 28 (11%) | 74/74 right entity in the live dry run (renamed filers such as Galena→SELLAS, Avant→Celldex are the same CIK; 1 is a subsidiary→parent) |
| **NIH SBIR/STTR** (`lib/ingestion/nih-grants.ts`) | new `company_grants` | exact name key, ≤2 org states per key, never large pharma; bulk per fiscal year FY2008+ | US 400-sample: 37 (9.25%); non-US 3 | 40/40 |
| **Exchange lists** (`lib/ingestion/listings.ts`) | new `company_listings` | CIK (SEC), stored ticker + name agreement, exact Chinese full name, exact English/local name, trusted-website domain; ambiguity guards | live dry run: CN 18/250 (7.2%), non-US 15/250 (6%), US 3/400 | 36/36 right company or listed parent (32 same legal entity, 4 subsidiaries of the listed parent: SanBio Inc, BioVersys SAS, Nyrada Pty, Innovacell GmbH) |
| **HKEX / ceased SEC filers** (SQL `company_signal_refresh_derived_listings()`) | `company_listings` from 189 columns | 189 match | 8 + 143 uncovered companies today | inherits 189 |
| **IFRS XBRL** (`company-financials.ts`) | `company_financials` for 20-F/40-F filers in USD at the ECB period-end rate (`reporting_currency`, `fx_rate_to_usd`, `taxonomy`) | existing CIK + entity-name check | 81 uncovered feed companies have a CIK but no financials (Genmab, Takeda, Shionogi, argenx, Ascendis, UCB...) | n/a (same CIK guard) |

Lists live-tested Nov 24 2026: SSE 2,319 · SZSE 2,905 · JPX 3,700 · KRX 2,770 · TWSE 1,098 · TPEx 898 · ASX 2,058 · TSX 833 · TSXV 1,409 · Euronext 3,891 · SIX 241 · SEC 10,229.

### Coverage definition (explicit)

`company_signal_covered(company_id)`: own row in `company_financials`, `company_listings`, `company_financing_events`, `company_grants` or `company_intent_signals`, **or** the family root (`companies.family_id`, mig 193) has financials or a live listing. A listed parent's balance sheet and listing describe the subsidiary's funding; a parent's rounds, grants and intent statements do not, so those never roll down. `radar_qa_scorecard_stats()` is patched in place (text replace of the signal block only, verified read-only against the live definition: 472 chars replaced; raises if the block is missing, so it is safe after 195-197). `company_signal_coverage_stats()` gives the per-source breakdown, including coverage without deal records.

### Projection

Sample-based, after backfill (EDGAR ~6 enrich runs, NIH 3 runs, listings 1 run, deal signals 1 run): **≈3,300 of 9,820 ≈ 33–35%** (from 11.7%). By segment: US 2,555 uncovered × ~34% ≈ 870; non-US/unknown 3,900 × ~15% ≈ 585; China 2,210 × ~8% ≈ 177; deal records add ≈430 beyond those; family roll-down ≈50; IFRS ≈20 net.

**60% is not reachable from free primary sources at this precision.** The remaining uncovered owners are mostly Chinese private companies (~2,000; no free financing source), small EU/UK/KR/IR private companies, and feed rows that are not companies (hospitals, individuals: "Songqi Gao", "Virtua Health", "Norton Healthcare" are owner_type industry today, which is an accuracy fix). Next sources, owner-blocked or follow-up: UK Companies House (free API key; SH01 share allotments), Korea DART (free key; covers externally audited private companies), EU CORDIS/EIC grants (free bulk, no key), Japan EDINET (free key).

## Features for the ranking model (no training code touched)

`company_signal_features_asof(p_company_ids uuid[], p_as_of date)` returns point-in-time values (undated listings count from `first_seen_at`, so a backtest before the first crawl sees NULL, not "unlisted"):

`listed_asof`, `listing_exchange`, `listing_confidence`, `ceased_filing_asof`, `family_listed_asof`, `grants_5y`, `grant_usd_5y`, `months_since_last_grant`, `out_licensing_deals_36m`, `in_licensing_deals_36m`, `acquirer_deals_36m`, `acquired_asof`, `financing_events_24m`, `months_since_last_financing`.

Notes for feat/se-ranking-v4: grants are deliberately **not** in `company_financing_events` (the 189 candidate features count every non-amendment event as a raise). Deal-record signals use new signal types, so `licensing_or_review_12m` keeps its meaning; when training on deal outcomes, exclude the label deal itself (`observed_at < as_of` is enforced by the function). IFRS rows add runway for ~60 non-US listed companies.

## Cron

No new schedule (cap 100). `/api/cron/company-financials` by UTC hour: financials 00/12 (was 00/06/12/18), **enrich 06/18** (deal signals + derived listings every run, then listings weekly, else EDGAR index at 06 while companies are pending and NIH at 18), HKEX 02/08/14/20, Form D 04/10/16/22. Manual modes: `deal_signals`, `listings` (`&sources=SSE,SZSE`), `edgar_index`, `nih_grants`, all with `&dry_run=1`.

## Cost

$0 model spend: rules only, no AI calls. External requests: SEC (fair-access UA, shared <10 req/s throttle), NIH RePORTER (1 req/s), exchange lists (one request each per week), api.frankfurter.dev for ECB FX. No owner email is sent anywhere: the generic UA `SolidusResearch/1.0 (+https://solidus.ambrosiaventures.co)` is used for non-SEC sources, SEC uses the existing `SEC_USER_AGENT`.

## Rollout (needs the owner's go)

1. Apply `supabase/migrations/198_company_signals_v2.sql` (after 197 if it lands first; the scorecard patch is text-based and fails loudly). **Apply before merging**: the financials upsert writes the new `company_financials` columns.
2. Merge, wait for the deploy.
3. `GET /api/cron/company-financials?mode=deal_signals` → expect `upserted` ≈5.5k, `rejected_name_disagreement` ≈80.
4. `?mode=listings&dry_run=1`, eyeball `sample`, then `?mode=listings`.
5. `?mode=edgar_index&dry_run=1&limit=200`, check `sample` / `rejected`, then `?mode=edgar_index` repeated (or let the 06:00 runs do it) until `candidates` is 0 for never-checked companies.
6. `?mode=nih_grants` ×3 (backfill FY2008→FY2027; the 18:00 runs continue it).
7. `?mode=financials&limit=200` once to pick up IFRS filers and newly set CIKs.
8. `select public.company_signal_coverage_stats();` and the scorecard (`?mode=scorecard` on the QA route) to record the new `signal_companies`.

Rollback: `company_listings` / `company_grants` are new tables; `delete from company_intent_signals where source_type = 'deal_record'` removes the deal sig

body:
## Summary

#2339 のレビューの単位 U7。工程の文脈と工程の定義のスナップショットに形のバージョンを持たせ、製品のバージョンを `product_version` へ改めた。結果とプランの形のバージョンを読み書きの入口で確かめ、形の違う結果の代わりに `stopped`（`invalid`）を 1 行出す（値を含めない）。

関連する issue: Refs #2339

実装計画は `issues/issue-3684-3667-2339-plan.md` の Task 15・16・17、満たす受け入れ条件は `2339:1`・`2339:4`・`2339:5` である。

### 意図した設計上の判断（レビューで戻さない）

- 結果は 1 回限りの値で、旧い `version` を `outputs` に持つ結果は受けない（設計）。プロセスの落ちと NDF の更新が重なった保存済みの結果は `retry` で流し直す
- 新しい NDF が作ったスプリントを旧い NDF が続ける使い方は対象にしない（普及フェーズの前で、旧い NDF の読みの互換は持たない）


### Pull Request の本文に要る一覧

### 製品の版を `product_version` へ改めた箇所

| 箇所 | 中身 |
| --- | --- |
| 結果のスキーマ `contracts/schemas/result.schema.json` の `$defs/outputs` | `version` を消し `product_version` を持つ |
| 文脈のスキーマ `contracts/workflow/context.schema.json` | `product_version` を足し、`version` は形のバージョン（整数） |
| `contracts/workflow/stage-io.schema.json` の `release-result` | `outputs` に `product_version` を必須 |
| 工程の定義 `deploy.json`（出力）・`release-verification.json`・`layout-review.json`（入力） | `product_version` |
| worker の作業の定義 `contracts/worker/kinds.json`（release の `outputs`・release-verification と layout-review の `inputs`）と、テンプレート 3 本の説明 | `product_version`。**設計の一覧に無い** |
| `domains/release/cli.py` の `assembled`・`cmd_record` | 出す側 |
| `progress/command.py` の `release_record`・`progress/gate/asking.py` の承認資料 | 読む側 |
| `progress/gate/release.py` の `RELEASED_OUTPUTS` | まとめたリリースの回答の `version` → 文脈の `product_version`（回答のキーは `version` のまま） |
| `core/refs/__init__.py` の参照の種類 `version` | 既定で読む outputs のキーを `product_version` に（参照の種類の名前は `version` のまま。今の呼び手はテストだけ）。**設計の一覧に無い** |
| 確定仕様 `docs/specifications/ndf-stage-plan-work-prompts.md` の 3 行 | 名前をそろえた |

変えていないもの（別の意味の `version`）: 計画の `ReleaseAnswer.version` と `ndf lanes release --version`、外のオーガナイザーの回答、リリース記録・リリース後テストの記録の `version`、工程の定義の文書の `"version": "1.0.0"`、MVV の設定。Skill の本文（release など）・`.github/`・`scripts/`・ほかのプラグインに、outputs の `version` を指す所は無い（git grep で確かめた）。

### 古い形の読み込み

`contracts/internal.py` の `KINDS` に `context`・`stage-snapshot` の 2 行と移し方 2 つ。スキーマ `contracts/schemas/internal/stage-snapshot.schema.json` を新設。手元の実物の DB（ai-plugins のバックアップ 22 件、nd-factory 7 件。読み取りだけ）の定義と文脈がすべて移り、型に合うことを確かめた。

### Task 17 の案（#2339 の本文に置く表。書き込みはしていない）

| 子の課題 | 判定 | 根拠・理由 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#1978](https://github.com/devbasex/ai-plugins/issues/1978) 使用量の報告の閉じた課題の数が UTC の日付で数えられる | 閉じた（解消を確かめた） | `plugins/ndf/src/ndf/domains/records/usage_decide.py` が期間と閉じた課題の検索の条件（`closed_query`）を JST の両端で組み、`plugins/ndf/tests/domains/records/test_usage.py` が確かめている。実装は PR https://github.com/devbasex/ai-plugins/pull/3512 |
| [#1981](https://github.com/devbasex/ai-plugins/issues/1981) agy の JSON の出力の形を実物で確かめていない | 閉じた（閉じた時点の確かめ） | 2026-11-07 に agy 1.4.7 の成功の出力の鍵（`response`・`usage`・`conversation_id`）を実物で確かめ、実装の前提と同じだった（#1981 のコメント）。11 系の `plugins/ndf/src/ndf/adapters/` に agy の JSON の鍵 `response` を読む所は無く、この柱の変更に当たらない。再び開く条件は #1981 のコメントにある。このタスクで実物は打ち直していない |
| [#2041](https://github.com/devbasex/ai-plugins/issues/2041) `--expect-head` が短い SHA を完全一致で比べて止まる | 閉じた（解消を確かめた） | `plugins/ndf/src/ndf/adapters/git.py` の `sha_matches` が先頭の一致で比べ、`adapters/github.py` の `_preflight` が使う。`plugins/ndf/tests/adapters/test_issue_reproductions.py` の `test_issue_2041_...` が再現の場面を確かめている（PR https://github.com/devbasex/ai-plugins/pull/3439 ） |
| [#1706](https://github.com/devbasex/ai-plugins/issues/1706) 古い版の NDF が `.ndf/project.json` の新しい項目を「知らない項目」として拒む | 残した（開いたまま） | 移行の関数は設定のファイルに当たらない。`internal.KINDS` の種類は記録 4 種・文脈・工程の定義のスナップショット（U6 のマージの後は開発ループのイベントも）で、`.ndf/*.json` の読み手（`domains/project/check.py` の `load` → `contracts.schema_errors`）は核を通らない。設定の `version` は項目を足しても上がらず `enum: [1]` のままなので、核の「今の版より新しければ `precondition`」も働かない。再現の手順（`future_key_x` を足した `.ndf/project.json` に `ndf project check`）をこのブランチで打ち、今も `stopped`・`invalid`「直してから打ち直す」になった（2026-11-24）。使える土台は「新しい版を形の違いと分け、プラグインの更新を案内する」考え方だけで、設定の版をいつ上げるか・知らない項目をどう扱うかの決定は #1706 に残る |

#1706 の再現は、この作業場所の `.ndf/project.json` のコピーに項目を 1 つ足して打った。


## 設計と違う点

| 設計 | 実装 | 理由 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 文脈を重ねる所は 2 つ（`View.context`・`machine_context`） | 3 つ。`gate/answering.py` の `_undropped` も `compose_context` を通した | 同じ重ね方が 3 か所目にあった。出力を拾う部分は `stages.recorded_outputs` にまとめた |
| スナップショットの移行は「`snapshot_from` の前」 | `command.read_current` で通し、`Current.raw` も今の形 | `snapshot_from` の呼び手はここだけ |
| `_prepare_new` が `version: 1` を書く | 新設の `_new_doc` が `write_record("context")` と `write_record("stage-snapshot")` を通す（開発ループの行も同じ） | 書く側も核で確かめる（受け入れ条件 1）。`--pace` などの引数の誤りは今までの `WorkflowDefError`（items に 1 件ずつ）を先に返すので、文言は変わらない |
| 文脈・結果の `version` の読めるバージョン（`enum: [1]`） | 2 つのスキーマは `minimum: 1` だけを持ち、上限は `internal.version()`（`internal/common.schema.json` の 1 か所）と比べる | `enum` を写すと値が 3 か所になる。`contracts.schema_errors` と `claude --json-schema` は別ファイルの `$ref` を解けない |
| 種類の名前 `result` | `KINDS` に行を足していない。`result.newer`・`result.received` が `internal.version()` と比べる | `KINDS` の版の見分けは「整数でない版は版 0」で、結果の「整数でない版は `bad_report`」と合わない。結果は移す古い形も無い |
| 代わりの結果の `detail` は誤りごとにスキーマの場所と規則 | 重複を除いて並べる。表と照らす誤り（停止理由・回答・重さ・終了コード）は件数にだけ入る | 表の誤りの文は値を含む |
| `emit` だけを変える | `ndf contracts emit --out` は、代わりの結果を標準出力にだけ出し、ファイルへは書かない | 「形が合うときだけ書く」を保つ |
| `precondition` は「今の例外の表」で | `command.STOPPABLE` と表に `InternalError` を足した。`ndf lanes` の側（`read_doc`）は `ndf.cli` の受け口が受ける | `ndf.cli` は U5 で `InternalError` を受ける |

## 利用者向けの変化

- 無し

## 移行の手順

- 無し

- [x] `plugins/ndf/bin/ndf check`・`scripts/check-lint.sh`・`scripts/check-ndf-contracts.py`（exit=0）
- [ ] pytest は CI で見る（`test.ci.only`）
