body:
## Failure and fix

Dropping a quantized vector index on a populated, sealed segment creates a replacement Flat index. The reload step removes the old raw and quantized index files, but the manifest retained the raw block. The drop succeeded, then reopening the collection failed on the missing index file.

Use the existing single-argument `remove_vector_persisted_block(column)` in `drop_vector_index()` to retire both source blocks for the target column before adding the replacement Flat block.

## Regression

`CollectionTest.DroppedQuantizedIndexReopensWithBothVectorColumns` seals a collection with two quantized vector fields and confirms that the target has both source block types. It drops the target index, reopens the collection, and checks that the same query vector finds a different expected document in each column. On `a26f8ab`, reopening failed while loading the retired raw index.

All 108 tests in `unittest.collection_test` passed on this branch. The changed C++ files passed clang-format 18.1.8.

author: nikumar1206
body:
## Context

Signing in to Loco takes more than one request. In the dashboard, the first request sends you to your identity provider and a second request finishes when you come back. `loco login` hands the CLI a one-time code that the CLI trades for tokens. `loco login --device` shows a short code you approve in the browser while the CLI keeps asking "done yet?".

Between those requests the API has to remember a little state: which browser started the sign-in, which code belongs to which user, whether the device was approved. By default the API kept that state in its own memory.

When two copies of the API run behind the gateway, each request can land on either copy. If the sign-in starts on one copy and finishes on the other, the second copy has never heard of it, and the sign-in fails. So the API could only run one copy safely.

This PR keeps that state in the database every copy already shares. Any copy can now finish a sign-in that another copy started, so the chart can run more than one API copy; #3402 makes two the default.

## Root cause

`CACHE_TYPE` defaulted to `in-memory`, a cache inside each API process. Web login state, CLI loopback codes, device codes, user codes and the device poll throttle all lived there, so a second replica could not see entries the first one wrote.

## Changes

- New table `auth_states` (key, value, start time, expiry), added to `00003_user_scopes.sql` in place, so an existing database needs a reset to get it. Reads ignore expired rows, and the token cleanup loop (`LOCO_TOKEN_CLEANUP_INTERVAL`, every minute) deletes them. The table is unlogged: sign-ins in progress are lost if the database restarts after a crash or fails over, and users start them again.
- The auth service stores its entries through a small store over that table:
  - Starting a dashboard or device sign-in (`StartWebLogin`, `StartDeviceLogin`) is one statement that stores every entry of the new sign-in with one start time. A device sign-in has two entries, its user code and its device row, which count and are deleted as one sign-in. An expired key can be reused, and a live one is stored once.
  - At most 1,000 sign-ins are in progress. Starting one more deletes the oldest in the same statement, so starting a sign-in never fails for lack of room. A sign-in deleted this way has to start again; a device login deleted this way polls as expired.
  - Approval rewrites a device row as an ordinary entry, so an approved login is never deleted early. Entries for a signed-in caller (approvals, loopback codes) and the poll throttle always store.
  - `Take` is `DELETE ... RETURNING`, so a single-use entry is taken, and read, by exactly one request across all replicas.
- Device sign-in:
  - User codes are stored under their SHA-256 hash, like loopback and device codes, and the device grant does not carry the user code.
  - A device login keeps the first 256 bytes of its `User-Agent`.
  - A failed approval, including a failed read of the device row, puts the user code back into its sign-in with the time it had left and reports `Unavailable`, so the approval can be retried.
  - A poll that cannot record itself returns `Unavailable`, so the poll interval holds.
  - `PollDeviceLogin` reports `Unavailable` when taking an approved device code fails in the store, and "expired" only when the code is gone.
- Removes Valkey and the cache settings. `CACHE_TYPE`, `CACHE_ADDR` and the Valkey option go away; every replica uses PostgreSQL, so there is no other backend to choose. The auth service was the only user of `api/pkg/cache`, so the package, its in-memory and Valkey backends, the ristretto and valkey-go dependencies, the Valkey service in the API test jobs, and the chart's references to `CACHE_TYPE` go too. The API environment reference describes how sign-ins in progress are kept.

## Evidence

`TestSignInFinishesOnAnotherReplica` starts a second auth service on the same database, built the way the API process builds one, and runs every flow across the two: web sign-in starts on one and completes on the other, a loopback code issued by one is exchanged on the other, and a device login started on one is polled, described, approved and finished across both. It also checks that a callback, code or approval cannot be reused on the first replica after the other consumed it, and that the poll throttle applies across replicas.

On `origin/main`, with the default in-memory store per instance, all three flows fail:

```
--- FAIL: TestSignInFinishesOnAnotherReplica (8.52s)
    --- FAIL: TestSignInFinishesOnAnotherReplica/web (0.01s)
        auth_replicas_db_test.go:47: complete web login on the other replica: unauthenticated: Could not sign you in
    --- FAIL: TestSignInFinishesOnAnotherReplica/loopback (0.04s)
        auth_replicas_db_test.go:69: exchange on the other replica: unauthenticated: this sign-in code is invalid or has expired; run loco login again
    --- FAIL: TestSignInFinishesOnAnotherReplica/device (0.00s)
        auth_replicas_db_test.go:84: poll on the other replica: <nil> not_found: this device code has expired; run loco login --device again
FAIL
```

With this PR:

```
--- PASS: TestDeviceLoginsStayWithinTheStoreBound (0.48s)
--- PASS: TestAuthStateStartStoresOnce (0.50s)
--- PASS: TestCLIDeviceApprovalRetriesAfterUnavailable (0.51s)
--- PASS: TestSignInFinishesOnAnotherReplica (0.52s)
--- PASS: TestAuthStateStartEvictsTheOldestSignIns (0.52s)
--- PASS: TestAuthStateStartsConcurrentlyAtTheCap (0.52s)
--- PASS: TestAuthStateTakeSucceedsOnce (0.53s)
--- PASS: TestDeviceLoginDescribesTheRequestingDevice (0.53s)
--- PASS: TestCLIDeviceApprovalRetriesAfterAFailedRead (0.54s)
--- PASS: TestDevicePollFailsClosedWhenItCannotRecordThePoll (0.54s)
--- PASS: TestDeviceLoginKeepsTheStartOfALongUserAgent (0.54s)
--- PASS: TestAuthStateExpires (0.54s)
ok  	github.com/team-loco/loco/api/service	0.938s
```

- `TestAuthStateTakeSucceedsOnce` and `TestAuthStateStartStoresOnce` run 32 concurrent calls against one key and require exactly one to succeed.
- `TestAuthStateStartEvictsTheOldestSignIns` fills a store with a bound of 3 sign-ins, the oldest with two entries. A fourth start succeeds and deletes both entries of the oldest; an entry written by `Set` stays; an entry taken and put back keeps its sign-in's place and is deleted as the oldest.
- `TestAuthStateStartsConcurrentlyAtTheCap` runs 16 workers of 10 starts each on a full store with a bound of 20. Every start succeeds, and right after the burst at most 20 + 16 sign-ins remain, counted by distinct start time: each concurrent start can miss rows the others have not committed yet.
- `TestDeviceLoginsStayWithinTheStoreBound` runs 10 device starts against a bound of 4, then checks exactly 4 user codes and 4 device rows remain and the oldest device login polls as expired.
- `TestCLIDeviceApprovalRetriesAfterUnavailable`, `TestCLIDeviceApprovalRetriesAfterAFailedRead` and `TestDevicePollFailsClosedWhenItCannotRecordThePoll` cover a failed approval write or read followed by a successful retry (the restored user code keeps its expiry), and a poll that cannot record itself.
- `TestDeviceLoginKeepsTheStartOfALongUserAgent` starts a device login with a 128 KB `User-Agent` and reads back at most 256 bytes of valid UTF-8.
- `TestAuthStateExpires` checks expired entries cannot be read or taken, can be stored again, and are deleted by the cleanup query while live ones stay.
- Cost of a start at a full table, measured with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` and `\timing` on local PostgreSQL 18 against an unlogged `auth_states` holding 1,000 device sign-ins (2,000 rows): 0.58 ms execution for the first start, which deleted both entries of the oldest sign-in, then 0.39 to 0.48 ms per start. Afterwards the table held 1,000 sign-ins in 2,000 rows.

## Validation

- `go test ./service/... . ./tvm/ ./migrations/ ./db/...` in `api/` against local PostgreSQL, with the unlogged table created through the test template database: pass.
- `mise run lint:go api`: 0

body:
## P6.2 — Service Worker update audit

### Proven gap
`js/sw-register.js` decided whether the app was busy by looking **only at `document.activeElement`**. If a user typed into the inline cash-transfer amount field and then moved focus to the still-empty notes field (or a button/select), a new deployment would pass `appIsBusy()`, and the 5-second retry would call `location.reload()` — silently discarding the unsaved amount. A new E2E test reproduced this on desktop and mobile: before the fix the page marker was `undefined` after 6 seconds and the field value was lost.

### Fix
`appIsBusy()` now scans all visible, enabled, non-readonly text-like inputs and textareas for a non-empty value. Checkboxes, radios, buttons, hidden fields and `.hidden`/`[hidden]` containers are excluded so idle updates still apply normally. A new Node regression locks in the broader guard. The update card is still shown whenever input is detected, so the user can choose when to reload.

- `e2e/service-worker-update.spec.js`: 8/8 on desktop and mobile (failing before the fix, passing after).

author: rubo77
body:
A rate-limited response (HTTP 429) from my.tado.com carries an empty body. `request()` previously returned `{}` in that case, so callers crashed later with a confusing `KeyError` (`'homes'` in `_get_id()`), which is regularly mistaken for an authentication problem - see for example home-assistant/core#148095.

Changes:

- Raise `requests.HTTPError` for a 429 with an empty body, including the `RateLimit` header in the message
- Extract the quota header parsing into `_store_rate_limit()` and also run it for the 429 path, so `rate_limit_info` stays useful for backoff decisions
- Harden `_get_id()`: accept a bare list of homes or a dict with a `homes` key, cast the id to `int`, and raise a `TadoException` on unexpected formats

Tests added for the 429 path and the list-form `/me` response. All 46 tests pass locally (`python -m pytest`), black/pylint clean.

Note: master/0.19 already handles this via `TadoRateLimitException` + `_store_rate_limit` - this is the equivalent fix for the 0.18 line that Home Assistant currently pins (`python-tado==0.18.16`).

author: dbczumar
body:
## Related issue

No tracked GitHub issue. Reported by a user of a host-sharded (multi-replica) deployment: a session's sidebar row said "Needs response", but opening it showed nothing to answer.

## Summary

The page asked the wrong replica what the session was waiting on. When its stream then reached the right replica, nothing asked again, so the approval never appeared.

- **Cause.** On a host-sharded deployment, a session's parked approvals live only in the memory of the replica that holds its host's tunnel. A host whose tunnel connected without a slice key lives on the default replica, but the page keys the session's requests by host id, which routes them to another replica. `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` answers 200 from any replica, so the bind snapshot came back with empty `pending_elicitations`. The stream was refused with `wrong_replica` and retried without a key, which reaches the right replica. The stream doesn't replay a prompt published before it subscribed, so the chat never got a card. The sidebar count is mirrored across replicas, so it kept showing "Needs response".
- **Why the existing recovery missed it.** `startStreamPump` already reconciles on the first connect when a session's host changes mid-bind. A keyless re-address to the same host (`markHostKeyless`) didn't notify anyone, so the bind snapshot from the wrong replica stood.
- **Fix.**
  - `markHostKeyless` and `clearHostKeyless` notify host-change subscribers when the demotion actually changes.
  - When the open's own host is demoted, the pump marks the bind as re-addressed. It doesn't abort the open, which re-addresses itself.
  - The first connection then runs the existing reconnect reconcile. It re-reads the snapshot from the replica the stream reached and appends the missing approval card.

```
page ─ keyed by host ─▶ replica B   GET snapshot → 200, pending_elicitations: []
page ─ keyed by host ─▶ replica B   GET stream   → 400 wrong_replica
page ─ no key ────────▶ replica A   GET stream   → 200          (prompt parked on A)
before: nothing re-reads the snapshot → no card
after:  first connect reconciles → GET snapshot (no key) on A → card appended
```

## Test Plan

- **Unit, `web/src/store/chatStore.test.ts`** (routing-host rebind): new test `shows a prompt parked on the replica its keyless re-address reaches`.
  - A host-keyed open is refused with `wrong_replica` naming the key it sent, and only a keyless snapshot lists the prompt.
  - It fails on `main` (no snapshot read after the keyless open) and passes with the fix.
  - `routeKeyedStreamOpens` gained two options for this, `refuseKeyedOpensFor` and `keylessSnapshotExtras`.
- **Unit, `web/src/lib/sessionHost.test.ts`**: a demotion notifies subscribers once per actual change.
- **E2E, `tests/e2e_ui/start_session/test_managed_first_message_routing.py`**: new test `test_fresh_page_shows_approval_parked_on_hosts_replica`, on the existing rig of two real replicas behind a slice-keyed ingress.
  - Setup: a create without a host id puts the host on replica A. A recorded permission prompt is parked on A's hook, then a fresh page opens the session.
  - From the ingress log, it asserts the routing preconditions: B served a snapshot without the prompt, the keyed stream was refused, and the keyless stream connected on A.
  - It then asserts the approval card renders, Approve returns `accept` to the hook, and the badge clears.
  - On `main` it fails waiting for the card; with the fix it passes.
  - It's a separate E2E because the bug only shows across the replica and transport boundary, which the unit test models with mocks.
- **Suites:** `pnpm exec vitest run src/store/` (983 passed). The `sessionHost`, `identity`, `identity.managedRouting` and `TerminalView` suites also pass (254 tests).

## Demo

- [x] Visual demo attached below
- [ ] Non-visual evidence provided below or in Test Plan
- [ ] Not applicable — no behavioral change

All three captures come from the E2E run on real replicas.

**Before (`main`):** the row says "Needs response" and the Inbox counts 1, but the chat has nothing to answer.

![Before: badge without an approval card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dbczumar/omnigent/pr-assets/needs-response-badge/before-badge-no-card.png)

**After:** the same fresh page shows the parked approval.

![After: the parked approval card is shown](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dbczumar/omnigent/pr-assets/needs-response-badge/after-card-shown.png)

**After approving:** the badge clears.

![After approving: badge cleared](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dbczumar/omnigent/pr-assets/needs-response-badge/after-approved-badge-cleared.png)

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] UI / frontend change
- [ ] Refactor / chore
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Test / CI
- [ ] Breaking change

## Test coverage

- [x] Unit tests added / updated
- [ ] Integration tests added / updated
- [x] E2E tests added / updated
- [ ] Manual verification completed
- [ ] Existing tests cover this change
- [ ] Not applicable

## Coverage notes

N/A. Both behaviors are covered by automated tests above.

## Release notes

Should this change be included in the release notes? Choose exactly one.

- [ ] No — no noteworthy user-facing change.
- [x] Yes — include the entry in the Changelog section.

## Changelog

Opening a session marked "Needs response" on a multi-replica deployment now shows the approval it is waiting on.

This pull request and its description were written by Isaac.

author: aosama
body:
## Linked issue

Refs #2473

## Github Issues

- #2473, Step 7: the folder layout. This is the first part: the root `Cargo.toml` lists its members by glob.

## Problem

The root `Cargo.toml` named all 39 workspace members by hand, so every new crate meant an edit there.

## Change

- **Member globs.** `members` is now `apps/*`, `crates/*`, `verification/*` and `xtask`.
- **Exclusions.** `exclude` names the three folders under those globs that hold no crate: the two Swift apps and the shell tooling contracts.
- **The member set is unchanged:** 39 members.
- **`default-members` stays an explicit list for now** (37 members). It leaves out the two Neural Engine crates, whose hardware journeys run only by hand and in their own CI lane. A glob over `crates/*` would take the Neural Engine crate in and change what a bare `cargo test` runs. It becomes globs when the rest of Step 7 gives each layer its own folder.

## Verification

- `cargo metadata` reports the same 39 members and 37 default members as main.
- `cargo test -p xtask --tests`: 992 passed.

## What changed

`platform/scripts/access-sync-job.py`
- `realm_group_members()` (new, after `group_members`): pages `GET /admin/realms/<REALM>/groups?briefRepresentation=true&first=&max=MEMBER_PAGE` until a short page, skips `ADMIN_GROUP`, `wh-` names and names holding `,`/`:`, and fetches each remaining group with `group_members(name)`. A status other than 200 is `fail("cannot list the realm's groups (HTTP %s)")`. Subgroups are not listed (the platform's groups are top-level).
- `render_groups_txt(admin_subs, warehouse_members, realm_members=None)`: writes the admin line, then the realm's other groups by name, then the warehouse lines. `realm_members=None` renders the previous text byte for byte.
- `main()`: `realm_members = realm_group_members()` right after the declared-group loop (so every Keycloak read still happens before the first write), printed as `realm groups: N extra line(s) in the group file`, and passed through `converge_warehouses(..., realm_members)` to the `GROUP_CONFIGMAP` write.
- Module docstring: the `trino-group-file` bullet names the new lines.

`platform/scripts/tests/test_access_sync.py`
- `RenderGroupsTxtTest.test_the_group_file_carries_the_realms_other_groups`: `render_groups_txt({"sub-a"}, {"small": {"sub-b"}}, {"visitors": {"sub-c"}, "demo": {"sub-d"}, "wh-small": {"sub-x"}, "empty": set()})` is exactly `stardelt-admins:sub-a\ndemo:sub-d\nvisitors:sub-c\nwh-small:sub-b\n`.
- `FakeKeycloak` answers the group listing (`/admin/realms/stardelt/groups`, paginated) from the same `{name: [(sub, username)]}` dict; without it every `main()` test would get a 404 on the new read.
- The five `WarehouseMainTest` expectations that assert the exact `groups.txt` text now carry its realm lines (class constant `REALM_LINES`): the realm below holds `analytics`, `finops`, `stardelt-users`, which the new code writes between the admin line and the warehouses. The four `RenderGroupsTxtTest` tests are unchanged and pass.

Nothing is authorized by the new lines: no rule keys on a group yet (the bridge's `trino.stardelt.rego` keys on `identity.user`; the resource-group selectors match `wh-<name>`), so they are inert until #50's next slice uses them. No operator change (`access_sync.rs` creates `trino-group-file` empty and never writes content).

author: nickolas-chu
body:
## Cluster all reads (no 20,000-read sample); one CTSS window for both CTSS modes

### What changes
**Clustering (TC mode)**
- New `CamoTSS/utils/distinct_clustering.py`: CamoTSS's average-linkage clustering (100 bp InnerDistance) computed on distinct read positions. It gives the same clusters as `AgglomerativeClustering(linkage='average')` run on every read, so no gene is sampled any more.
- Exact ties (two merges exactly equally close, common because positions are whole numbers) are compared with integer arithmetic and broken leftmost-first. sklearn breaks them by BAM read order, so its own answer can change with read order.
- Removed: the 20,000-read stratified sample, the leftover add-back and the chunked recovery pool. Recovery now re-runs the same clustering for any gene that fails.

**CTSS (single-base TSS), both `--mode CTSS` and `--mode TC+CTSS`**
- **One sliding window for both modes:** `windowSize` consecutive bases, with empty bases counted as 0 (the old CTSS-mode window), now **including the cluster's last base**. The old code used `range(TSS_start, TSS_end)`, which stopped one base short.
  - The old TC+CTSS window used only bases that had reads, so its 15 positions could span hundreds of bp, and the last 14 read-bearing bases of each cluster were never tested.
- Reads come from `keepdict.pkl` (reads of kept clusters) instead of loading the whole `fetch_reads.pkl`.
  - With all-reads clustering these are exactly the reads inside each kept TSS's bounds.
  - On output folders made by the old sampled clustering, `keepdict.pkl` misses some reads inside the bounds, so CTSS mode run on such a folder can give lower counts than before.
- Cells per CTSS are found with numpy rather than a Python loop over the gene's reads.
- Sparse CSR output instead of a dense table.
- No stray `index` column in `var`.
- `CTSS_foldchange.pkl` is reused on a rerun only if `CTSS_foldchange_params.txt` matches: same window version, `windowSize` and number of clusters.

### Tests
Run on the human brain `fetch_reads.pkl` (45 M reads), in a local Python 3.6.9 environment with sclab's exact package versions.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent brute-force average linkage on every read (exact fractions, leftmost ties) vs new clustering | identical on all 1,127 blocks tested, including all 127 blocks where sklearn differs |
| Genes ≤ 20,000 reads, old vs new full run | identical clusters and features except at exact ties (480 of 8,603 genes) |
| Every kept TSS, cell by cell, vs all reads inside its bounds (`fetch_reads.pkl`) | 10,553 TSS, 0 mismatches |
| Reference files (`ref_gene.tsv`, `ref_TSS.tsv`) vs the original human run | identical |
| CTSS data-handling rewrite vs old code, same clusters, each mode's old window | identical CTSS, cells and counts in both modes |
| New single window: CTSS mode vs TC+CTSS mode | identical output (849 CTSS) |
| Resume | same settings → reused; `--windowSize 10` → recomputed |
| Two full new-code runs | identical TSS, counts and tables (only CSV row order differs) |

### Human brain results (TC+CTSS, `--minCount 50`, 8 processes, resumed from `fetch_reads.pkl`)

| | Old code (main, 768ee6a) | New code |
|---|---|---|
| Wall time, whole run | 1 h 17 min | **33 min** |
| Clustering step | 70.8 min | **28.8 min** |
| CTSS step | 117 s | **2 s** |
| Peak RAM, whole run (drop in WSL available memory) | 63 GB | **28 GB** |
| Disk, `count/` | 10.0 GB | **7.0 GB** |
| Genes that failed / timed out and needed recovery | 2 | 0 |
| Clusters ≥ 50 reads (before classifier) | 74,758 | 84,173 |
| Kept TSS | 10,504 | 10,553 |
| Total TSS counts | 3,678,061 | 3,686,506 |
| CTSS called (default cutoffs) | 341 (old TC+CTSS window) | 849 (single window) |

### Not changed (known issues)
- `fetch_reads.pkl` is still loaded whole by the main process (largest single process 22 GB on human, the same in both versions). For mouse (43.5 GB pickle) this is the main RAM limit.
- `before_cluster_peak.pkl` and `before_cluster_peak_Final.pkl` are identical copies (2.3 GB each on human) when no gene fails.
- `--maxReadCount` defaults to 10,000 and subsamples reads before anything else. Runs must pass a large value (e.g. 100000000).
- The last `windowSize-1` bases of each cluster cannot be tested as CTSS (no full window).

## Summary

Natural holes stay open under the streets of the ring bands and next to the paths of a village. This pull request fills them. The rules apply from the new plan version 5 (`PlanVersion.STREET_FILL`). A world of an earlier version keeps its villages.

- Each street of a ring band gets a ramp profile, as a street of the core (`StreetRamps`). A band has no plaza. Thus a first piece starts at the path across the band, or at the terrain. The junctions and the houses of the band go to the level of the profile. The path of each street fills the holes under its rows.
- Each street path, each arm and each path across a band gets sides of 2 blocks (`VillagePathPiece.SIDES`). The flat terrain in front of and behind a gate gets the same sides around its area (`TerrainPiece`). On the sides, an open hole gets dirt up to 1 block under the row. Its floor must be terrain, 10 blocks under the row or less. A hole under a roof, a floor of water, of a street or of another piece do not change.
- The sides of the flat terrain are not a part of its area. Thus the terrain adaptation and the cleared space of a gate do not change.
- New optional measure `VillageGroundGameTests.measureHolesNearTheStreets` for the capital of the reproduction.

Closes #799

## Tests

- New GameTests `StreetHoleGameTests`. 2 tests put a path and a gate front on flat ground with an open hole, a roof, water, a floor of planks and a far hole. 1 test puts a town with a hole under a band street and an open hole next to a path across the band. With the sides off, the town test fails on the open hole.
- New JUnit test `StreetRampTest.planWithNoPlazaStartsAtTheTerrain`. `VillageWallTest` checks the area, the sides and the terrain adaptation box of the gate fronts.
- Local runs: `./gradlew spotlessApply :core:test :world:build` passes. The full GameTest run passes (704 required tests).
- Measure on the reproduction: seed 2313585753942443114, capital of style base, start chunk [956, -11], plaza at 15303 64 -183. Tectonic 3.0.28 and Lithostitched 1.8.0 are in `dev/run-gametest/mods`.

| Place | Version 4 | Version 5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shaft under a band street, X 15386 to 15389, Z -176 to -173 | Path at Y 47 and 49 | Rows at Y 64, no hole |
| Small holes, X 15428 to 15432, Z -186 | Y 59 to 62 | Y 63 |
| Crevasse next to the flat terrain of the east gate, 1 to 2 blocks out | Y 55 to 57 | Y 63 |
| Same crevasse, 3 to 5 blocks out (Z -178 to -176) | Y 55 | Y 55, open |

- `measureGroundAroundThePaths` with Tectonic, the same 7 villages: 3327 path columns in the 2 versions. The steps past the edge go from 62 to 33. The 8 high steps stay. No step next to a path is lower than the path.

Not verified: the game client. The crevasse part 3 to 5 blocks from the flat terrain of the gate stays open. The bands of a new ring at runtime (`RingBands`) get no street paths.

## Checklist

- [x] The CI passes.
- [x] New text that the player sees has a key in `en_us.json` and in `fr_fr.json`. (No new text.)
- [x] A change that the player sees has an entry in `changelog/`.
- [x] The documentation is up to date (`docs/design.md`).
- [x] Tests cover the new logic (JUnit and GameTest).

author: anurag-mantri
body:
## Summary
- Complete the server foundation with PostgreSQL integration coverage in CI, GitHub OAuth flow, role permissions, host identity checks, rotating tokens and stale-host handling.
- Add a TypeScript host transport with validated protocol frames, heartbeats, reconnect handling and OS keychain host-token management.
- Add hidden-prompt, agent-scoped provider secret storage in the OS keychain.
- Add a Linux rootless Podman sandbox using a digest-pinned image, explicit non-overlapping agent workspaces, no network, bounded resources and task JSON over stdin.
- Add a local metadata-only task audit log with correlated lifecycle IDs; task prompts and provider credentials are excluded. Tasks fail closed if the start record cannot be written.
- Cancel in-flight sandbox work on disconnect or daemon shutdown; replies stay bound to the connection that received each task.

## Validation
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm build`
- `git diff --check`
- CI runs the server integration suite against PostgreSQL.

The sandbox backend is covered by mocked runtime tests. This WSL environment has no Podman binary, so a real container run was unavailable. Provider secrets remain on the host; model requests use only the fixed routes in the task-scoped broker while general container networking stays disabled. Tool execution and approvals, per-requester budgets, individual tool-action audit, and non-Linux sandbox backends remain open.

## Provider egress broker

- Added a per-task Unix-socket broker for fixed OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Chat Completions, and Anthropic Messages routes.
- Provider keys stay in the host OS keychain and are attached only to host-side requests to fixed HTTPS endpoints. The container remains on `--network=none`.
- Enforced request and response size limits, 20 requests per task, one in-flight call, a 45 second request timeout, a 4,096 output-token cap, and no redirects or streaming.
- The exported Node helper `requestProvider(route, body)` is used by the minimal TypeScript runtime. This PR does not include an end-to-end Podman run because Podman is unavailable in this WSL environment.

## TypeScript agent runtime

- Added the `swarmroom-agent` executable. It accepts one Zod-validated task on stdin, reads an agent/model/system-prompt config from the image's fixed `/etc/swarmroom/agent.json` path, and prints only the model reply.
- Supports OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Chat Completions, and Anthropic Messages through the task-scoped broker. Credentials stay on the host.
- The initial runtime has no shell or workspace tools. Runtime and provider-route tests are included; this WSL environment has no Podman for a real container test.

## Requester token budgets

- Added optional per-agent host policies with owner exemption and rolling per-task, hourly and daily limits.
- The broker reserves a conservative request-size/output-token bound before provider dispatch, then settles against provider-reported usage. It retains the reservation if usage is missing or a dispatched request fails.
- Usage is persisted locally with restrictive permissions and contains no prompts or credentials. Budget denials propagate through Podman and tell the requester to ask the agent owner to raise the limit or shorten the task.
- Policies are configured with `SWARMROOM_AGENT_BUDGETS`; existing agents remain unmetered when the variable is unset.

body:
## O que muda

- **Outros navegadores:** além do Google Chrome, a captura funciona no Microsoft Edge, no Firefox, no Chromium e no Brave. A janela ganha a linha **Navegador**, com os navegadores encontrados no computador; a escolha fica guardada no `config.json` e não muda durante a captura. Sem nenhum encontrado, fica o Chrome, como antes.
  - Chrome, Edge e Firefox: o Selenium encontra o navegador e o driver sozinho.
  - Chromium e Brave: chromedriver com o executável deles. Se não for encontrado, a captura para com uma mensagem clara, em vez de abrir o Chrome no lugar.
  - Opera e Vivaldi ficam de fora (a versão deles não segue a do Chromium, e o Selenium não acha o driver certo). Está no README.
  - O `.deb` agora recomenda qualquer um dos navegadores suportados.
- **Versão 1.1.0:** `__version__` e a seção `[1.1.0] - 2026-11-23` no CHANGELOG, com tudo o que estava em "Não lançado".

## Testes

- 119 testes e ruff passando localmente (Python 3.13, Linux).
- Testes novos em `tests/test_navegadores.py` (detecção no Linux e no Windows, qual driver abre para cada navegador, navegador não encontrado) e em `tests/test_interface.py` (seletor da janela).
- Firefox de verdade (headless), em páginas locais que imitam o Lattes: CAPTCHA resolvido → OK com nome, data e print carimbado; página de erro → "Página inesperada"; Firefox fechado no meio da captura → abre outro e continua.
- Não testados: Chrome, Edge, Chromium e Brave reais (não instalados na máquina do teste), o site real do Lattes e o Windows fora do CI.

## Depois do merge

Para gerar o `.exe`, o `.deb` e o `.tar.gz`, publicar a release com a tag `v1.1.0`. O build confere a tag com a `__version__` e usa as notas do CHANGELOG se a descrição ficar em branco.

`docs/janela.png` ainda mostra a janela sem a linha "Navegador".

author: dastratakos
body: Second of two PRs that fix the iOS @mention menu. The first, [#10608](https://github.com/ReviewStage/vespin/pull/10608), took the filtering off the keystroke path. > **Stacked:** this branch merges in [#10537](https://github.com/ReviewStage/vespin/pull/10537) (and the [#10522](https://github.com/ReviewStage/vespin/pull/10522) under it), since both change `GlassBar`/`DockedFoot` where the float goes. Until they land, the diff below includes their commits. Auto-merge stays off until they merge and the simulator recording is checked. ## The glitches it fixes - **The transcript and the field jumped on every key.** `MentionSuggestions` stood inside the composer's glass head. As the list filtered, the bar resized, the dock measured its room again (`DockMeasure` → `useDockRoom`), and the transcript's foot inset moved. - **Rows were drawn again at the cap.** `BarHead` measured itself in JS and swapped its `VStack` for a `ScrollView` past 35% of the window, which remounted every row, and the frame before the swap was drawn at full height. - **The capsules stepped aside** when an `@` was typed, which moved the transcript once more on open and again on close. ## What changes - **`GlassBar`/`Composer` take a `float`.** It's a SwiftUI piece in a glass of its own (`BarFloat`) standing over the bar, outside the view the dock measures, so nothing under it moves as it comes, goes or filters. It's its own `Host`, so the bar's field is never re-parented or drawn again (the keyboard stays). On the agent page the row of capsules keeps its room under the float, hidden and not pressable, instead of stepping aside. At a SwiftUI column's foot (`ComposerFoot`, an iPad's split view) the float stands over the composer in the column. - **One scroll, sized natively.** `MentionSuggestions` is now a `ScrollView` whose frame is capped at `useFloatRoom()` (the window less the keyboard, the bar and the screen's bar, between 100 and 300 pt) and sized to its rows with `fixedSize`. It hugs short lists and scrolls long ones in the same frame the words land in, with no JS measuring round trip and no view swap. The crumb stands still above the rows, and a drag scrolls the rows without dismissing the keyboard. - **List-row metrics:** a 44 pt minimum and the lead mark (face, status ring, harness, or glyph) centered in the app's 20 pt lead column. Under it, a regular-weight body title over a muted subheadline line, as Mail's recipient suggestions stand. Group headers are footnote semibold, with a grouped list's gap between them. Picking a row keeps its selection haptic. - The description editors (`DocumentPage`, `MentionDock`, `MentionFoot`) draw the same list. There it stays in the dock's bar, since floating it would cover the caret. - **Placement:** floating, as Messages, Slack and the desktop's popover do. It's the only placement that keeps the content and the field still while typing. ## Tests - Ran turbo `typecheck` for `@repo/mobile` (it covers `@repo/ui-native`), plus oxlint, biome, `press-guard-check`, and `style-guard` on the changed files. - No unit test: this is layout, which the package's rules leave to the simulator flows. - Before/after recordings come from the Mac simulator queue on the Inbox fixture. JS only, so no native build. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: jerryjwres-hue
body:
## Summary

Existing Maotai assets (C8B master, B1 scene, identity lock v2, FLUX.2 Klein LoRA v2) can now be registered in Core, looked up by **full** SHA-256, and gated by Owner approval. Everything reuses the existing `artifacts` table, `/studio/assets/import` intake and `approvals` table. There is no new table, column, approval system or schema version: `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 24.

Baseline: PR #330 HEAD `d17316aed25d2685f3a094da827d85244de14d40`. No video generation; nothing here queues work or authorizes a GPU post.

## How the kinds map onto the existing data

| kind | existing role / artifact_type | byte provenance |
|---|---|---|
| character_master | `character` / `storypack_character` | `CORE_HASHED_MANAGED_COPY` (bytes copied through the existing import and hashed by Core) |
| scene_master | `scene` / `storypack_scene` | same as above |
| identity_lock | `style` / `storypack_style` | same as above |
| lora | `lora` / `storypack_lora` | `WINDOWS_CLIENT_CLAIM_NOT_CORE_HASHED` (no bytes; `stored_object_hash` is NULL) |
| workflow | `workflow` / `storypack_workflow` | same as lora |

Mac Core cannot read Windows `D:`. A Windows-claim record stores only the SHA-256 that Windows reports, plus Windows evidence (method, time, verifier, bare file name, never a path). The API never reports these bytes as Core-verified (`core_verified_bytes=false`).

## Endpoints

All endpoints use the existing device Bearer.

- `POST /studio/assets/windows-evidence`: registers a Windows-verified digest for `lora` or `workflow`. Image and text kinds are refused with `ASSET_KIND_REQUIRES_CORE_COPY` and must go through the existing byte import.
- `GET /studio/assets/by-sha256?sha256=<64 hex>[&project_id=]`: returns the real artifact IDs. A prefix is rejected with 422, and an empty result invents nothing.
- `POST /studio/assets/{artifact_id}/owner-approval-request`: opens one task-less **Pending** approval of type `storypack.asset_owner_approval.v1`. The approval scope binds artifact_id, sha256, kind, size, media type, byte provenance and the Windows evidence. Repeat requests are idempotent. Nothing in this PR can approve; only the existing digest-bound Control Center decision (`/approvals/{id}/decision`) can.
- `GET /studio/assets/{artifact_id}/production-eligibility`: eligible only with a currently valid Approved scope that matches the row, plus an intact Core copy for Core-copy kinds. It always reports `requires_windows_byte_check_before_use=true` and `gpu_post_authorized=false`.

## StoryPack preview

The preview adds new fields per ref and leaves old fields with their old meaning:
- `missing_reason`: `REF_IS_NOT_A_CORE_ARTIFACT_ID` or `ARTIFACT_NOT_REGISTERED`
- `expected_asset_kind`
- `kind_check`: `KIND_MATCHES_SLOT`, `ARTIFACT_KIND_MISMATCH` or `RECORD_NOT_FOUND`
- `byte_provenance`
- `owner_approval_status`

`owner_approval_verified` is true only when a valid approval exists. `usable_for_generation` stays false. Shot fingerprints and Owner-subject digests are unchanged, because they read only the existing fields.

The Control Center summary now also shows `asset_kind` and `byte_provenance`.

## Tests

- New: `tests/integration/test_storypack_existing_asset_intake.py`, 20 tests. Covers:
  - kind mapping without new tables and without a schema bump
  - Windows claim CREATED / REPLAY / conflict
  - eight rejection cases, including a Windows path in the evidence and a short SHA
  - full-SHA lookup
  - unapproved, pending, rejected and approved transitions
  - wrong expected SHA
  - a tampered Core copy revoking eligibility
  - a Windows claim requiring evidence
  - an unknown artifact
  - preview missing reasons with no ID creation
  - a wrong kind in a slot
  - a legacy-row compatibility case
  - the Control Center summary
- Written test-first: all 19 initial tests failed before the implementation. The summary test was added later and also failed first.
- Local, Python 3.12.3, Linux: `pytest tests` → **2075 passed, 5 skipped**. The skips are native Windows/macOS-only tests.
- `ruff check` is clean on the new files. `studio.py` keeps its 3 pre-existing findings unchanged.
- Native CI: this test file is added to `p0-296-real23-storypack-studio.yml` (macos-15).

## Remaining blockers for StoryPack asset intake (not solved here)

1. **The Windows client still has to upload the real bytes and open the approval requests.** C8B (`c6d7e556…`), B1 (`c89f7c8d…`) and identity lock v2 (`63b4b8ba…`) are not in any Core database yet: no real files were uploaded. The Windows client must send these copies through `/studio/assets/import`, register LoRA v2 (`5972e7f7…`) through `/studio/assets/windows-evidence`, and then the Owner must approve each one in the Control Center.
2. **The 11-21 StoryPack uses names, not IDs.** It references `MASTER_body_C8B_v1` and similar names instead of `asset-<64 hex>` IDs, so preview reports `REF_IS_NOT_A_CORE_ARTIFACT_ID`. The pack must be revised to use the IDs returned after registration. Its output profile is `p0_landscape` while every verified asset is 9:16, which is an Owner decision.
3. **Only reference eligibility is solved.** `CANONICAL_23_PRODUCTION_BRIDGE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (the StoryPack → frozen Plan compiler) is P0-2. Wiring eligibility into Plan compilation and into the Windows pre-GPU byte re-check is not done here.
4. **Owner identity is the existing Control Center model.** Any authenticated device can call `/approvals/{id}/decision`. That is the current approval model, and this PR does not change it.

No changes to GPU HOLD, ComfyUI, LTX, training, generation or private material uploads.

author: egolearner
body:
## Failure and fix

1. **Document decoding.** `Doc::deserialize(data, size)` ignored the supplied byte count when reading fields and variable-length values. A short record could be accepted and the decoder could read outside the supplied range. Validate field tags, lengths and element counts against the remaining bytes before decoding. Complete documents keep their existing encoding.
2. **Legacy WAL writes and recovery.** Append accepted empty and oversized payloads and could report success when an automatic flush failed. Recovery treated a damaged complete frame as end-of-file and could leave subsequent appends behind an incomplete tail. Enforce the existing 4 MiB limit on writes, propagate flush errors, and distinguish EOF, incomplete tails, and corrupt frames. Writable recovery checks the WAL before mutating the persistent primary-key map, trims only an incomplete tail, and reports checksum or document errors. Read-only open preserves the WAL.

## Regression

- `DocDetailedTest.SerializedPayloadRequiresCompleteFields` checks every logical prefix length against a fully backed document, then checks an exact round trip and trailing bytes.
- `WalFileTest.AppendRejectsUnreadableSizesAndRoundTripsLimit` and `AppendReportsAutomaticFlushFailure` exercise the write boundary and injected flush error. `RepairsIncompleteLengthChecksumAndPayload` covers partial frame headers and payloads.
- The three `LegacyWalRecoveryTest` cases use a scalar collection. They verify read-only preservation, recovery followed by a readable append, rejection of complete frames with a bad checksum, and rejection of undecodable documents with a valid checksum. They also check that a failed open leaves the primary-key map usable.

The new document, append and collection cases reproduced the failures on `a26f8ab`. This change reads and writes the existing WAL format.

On this branch, all 28 document tests, 15 WAL file tests, and 110 collection tests passed. The changed C++ files passed clang-format 18.1.8.

The existing segment recovery and read-only-after-recovery tests also passed in both parameter configurations (4 additional cases).

author: neffer77
body:
## Add a Saga: a chapter of the story told as each realm's boss falls

Before: the opening said why mathematics hurts a dragon, and then the story stopped. Beating a realm's boss paid gold and opened the next realm, and nothing said what had happened or what came next.

After: beating a realm's boss for the first time tells that realm's chapter on the victory screen, between the rewards and the way on, beside the boss drawn in its own colours. Each chapter is three sentences: what the boss was in its own mathematics, how the blow that beat it worked (the Determinant Golem falls because a matrix sent to zero cannot be undone), and what waits in the next realm. A rematch or a plain foe tells nothing. A 📜 Saga button on the map, and one in the Tome, open a page with the opening first and every chapter read, while the rest stay held back with only where to read them, counted 1 of 8 and so on. Nothing is saved: the page reads which bosses are beaten.

How: a Saga object with eight chapters, a screen off the map, and one card in Battle.win for a boss's first fall. `npm test` checks each chapter is three sentences about its own boss, names the mathematics that beat it and points to the next realm, and checks the page, the locked chapters, the count and the victory card. A new play suite beats the first boss with real answers on a phone-sized screen and reads the chapter there and on the page.

Break tests: 8 of 8 caught (a chapter given away before its boss falls, a rematch telling it again, a realm's first foe telling it, the count running one ahead, the boss drawn as a shadow, the victory never drawing the boss, the opening left off the page, and the map with no way to the Saga).

author: lucasthevenet
body:
Part of #274.

## Why

A `Field.entity` holds whatever id was written, and its entity may be gone. It read as `Entity`, so `get`, `has`, `set`, `sources` and `Commands` all took a stale id as if its entity were still there, and nothing failed. Now the field reads as `Entity.Ref`, which no world call takes. `world.live(ref)` returns the `Entity` while it is alive, and `undefined` after a despawn, including after another entity takes the slot.

## What changed

- `Entity.Ref` is a namespace type merged onto `Entity` in `ecs/component.ts`: `number & { _brand: "Entity" | "Entity.Ref" }`. An `Entity` is a `Ref`, but a `Ref` is not an `Entity`. So writes to an entity field take an `Entity`, a copied `Ref` or a `Spawned` id with no separate input type, and every read (`each`, `world.get`) yields a `Ref`. The root entry's `type Entity` export carries `Entity.Ref` with it. I checked this by compiling a consumer against the built `dist`.
- `live(ref): Entity | undefined` is on `EcsWorld`, `ReadingWorld` (the world a system is handed and the one `app.read(World)` hands out) and `Read` in `services/handed.ts`. It returns `Entity | undefined`, like `placed(id)` and `get`.
- There is no `refEntity` helper. Since `Entity` is a subtype of `Ref`, nothing converts that way. `live` builds its `Entity` with `makeEntity(index, gens[index])` from the slot itself, so the change adds no cast anywhere.
- `isAlive`, `entityIndex` and `entityGeneration` take an `Entity.Ref`, so they work on both kinds of id.
- Relation `target`s stay `Entity`, because the world keeps them live. `Entity` itself is unchanged, as item F of #274 covers making it opaque.

**Breaking**: a value read from a `Field.entity` is an `Entity.Ref`. A game that passed it to the world now calls `world.live(hunter.target)` first and checks for `undefined`. The changeset `.changeset/a-stored-id-is-a-ref.md` says so.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm check`: exit 0 (formatting is clean and Oxlint passes).

body:
Closes #300

## What
- **`/name <handle>`**, **`/name`** (show), **`/name --clear`**; **`--name HANDLE`** at launch (with `--resume`, renames the resumed session). Handle: lowercase letters, digits, `-`, ≤32 chars, not `sess-…`.
- **Storage:** a `name` record in the session log (last wins), folded into the session index (`Summary.name`); restored on `/resume`, `--resume`, `/relaunch` and `/update`. Named sessions are kept by `session_retention_days` like titled ones.
- **Uniqueness:** new `nano/handle.d` registry (`<peers dir>/<handle>.name` → session id, liveness via the session log's flock). A handle held by a running session is refused (naming the holder); a stopped session's handle is reusable.
- **Resolution:** `session_send` `to`, history tools' `session`, `--resume` and `/resume` try handle (running holder first, then newest stopped) → exact id → unique id prefix → title. A handle beats a colliding title.
- **Visibility:** status bar `@handle`, `/session`, banner/exit message (`--resume <handle>` when unique on disk), peer label `[from perf · title]`, `sessions_list` `[name: …]`, system prompt tells the agent its handle, Herdr pane label + `name` token.
- **ACP:** `session/set_name` (`{name}`; null clears), `name` in `_meta` of `session/new`/`session/load`; `--name` applies to ACP sessions.
- README: `/name`, `--name`, resolution order, two-agents-by-name example, ACP method.

## Tests
New `agent_name_test.d` (validation, persistence across resume, clear, uniqueness, running-first resolution, `session_send` by handle beating a title, labels, resume hint), plus tests in `handle.d`, `cross_session.d`, `session_index.d`, `acp.d`, `status.d`, `herdr.d`, `peers.d`, `system_prompt.d`, `app.d` arg parsing.

`scripts/ci.sh all` passes (run with `NANO_TEST_BUDGET_SCALE=10`: the host had load ~6 from parallel runs, which pushed unrelated modules like `nano.frame` over their time limits; all 124 modules pass).

Budgets: no budget raised (catch(Exception) count unchanged — new code catches `FileException`/`UTFException`/`JSONException`). New modules `nano.handle` and `nano.agent_name_test` are listed in `scripts/serial-tests` (flock probes / `NANO_CODER_PEERS`).

**Not done here:** checking in a real terminal/Herdr pane — the status-bar segment and Herdr label are covered by unit tests only; a reviewer should eyeball `/name` in a terminal and a Herdr pane.

author: andyrewlee
body:
## Stack

Merge bottom-up. Base: #46 (`context`). The OAuth and OpenAPI work (#83, #87, #88) follows as a second stack on this core.

1. #79 tool calls on the session log
2. #80 code mode
3. #81 vaults and credentials
4. 👉 #82 MCP servers, admission plan, tool registry
5. #84 approvals and client tools, pause inside the turn
6. #121 durable script pauses
7. #122 dashboard: tool calls and answers
8. #123 dashboard: vaults, servers and tools

---

This PR is part of the rebuilt tools stack. After six review rounds found about 70 bugs, the stack was redesigned around three rules:

- **Pi owns execution state.** Waiting calls are Pi's own parked tasks; nothing mirrors them.
- **Pi's task id is the identity of a call.** Public ids are `tu_<task id>`.
- **A pause stays inside the turn.**

Code mode is the main tool surface.

## Summary

MCP servers end to end, plus the two pieces the rest of the stack builds on: one admission plan per session and one tool registry.

- **Agent:** `mcp_servers: [{ type: "url", name, url }]`, a field of the agent version, stored atomically with it. Main's `ChangeMintsNextVersionOrNoOps` and `UnchangedConfigMintsNothing` now also compare `mcp_servers`, which makes them stricter.
- **One admission plan:** `makeSessionPlanner` resolves the agent version, the checked environment version and every server binding once. HTTP create and automations both use it.
  - A retried create replays its first admission under the same command id (#114) instead of planning again.
  - Admission refuses with 409 if the environment changed after planning.
- **Credential binding:** session create takes `vault_ids` and `mcp_server_credentials`.
  - An explicit binding wins.
  - Otherwise exactly one credential matching the server's URL binds, and several are refused, naming the server.
  - With none, the server is called without a credential.
- **One registry:** names are `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. Server names may not contain `__` or start or end with `_`, so no two servers can produce the same name. A long name gets a stable alias: as much of the name as fits, plus a 10-character hash. Dispatch, deferral and events all come from it.
- **Transport:**
  - **Credentialed servers** go through `Connection.forward`, which sends only to the stored URL, follows no redirects, and bounds each request at 60 s and 4 MiB. One scrubber removes every encoding of the secret from bodies, structured content, errors and all returned headers.
  - **Servers without a credential** are fetched directly by the session.
  - **One MCP client per session per server,** with modern version negotiation and legacy fallback. A failed connect is dropped, so the next call retries.
- **Tools:** each server is a deferred Pi extension, callable from scripts. The tool-list cache has a byte budget, and a server whose list doesn't fit is unavailable on its own. Events are `agent.mcp_tool_use` / `agent.mcp_tool_result`.

## Verification

- Each slice was built and verified on its own: typecheck, generate:check, format, lint; the SDK, API, local-Worker and dashboard suites; and the domain suite with every proof.
- The assembled stack was re-checked commit by commit for #79–#81, all green. The run was stopped there to push, so CI is the per-commit check for the rest.
- Proofs at the top, run alone: Sessions 182 s (limit 600), Checkfu 225 s (limit 300).
- `persisted:check` is red only because no baseline has been cut, as on main.
- Not deployed to Cloudflare; Worker behaviour verified under local workerd.
- The dashboard has not been clicked through in a running stack yet.

body:
## What changed

- New package `src/physgate/build/bom/` with the sheet schema, the verdict rules and the command.
- One registration line in `src/physgate/cli.py`, plus its import.
- `bom` added to the subcommand list in `ui/src/rules/terminal-commands.json`. That list is held equal to the command's own subcommands, so that no screen shows a terminal command.
- Nothing in `orchestrator/`, `contracts/`, `state/` or the UI's code is edited.

**The command:** `physgate bom check <run> [--sheet FILE] [--quantities FILE] [--json]` reads the run's `events.jsonl` and writes nothing.

**Lines:** the plan's parts that a person answered "find".
- The choice comes from the release line through `parts_choices`; the domain and label come from the plan's component list, in plan order.
- These are not a bill of materials a design produced.
- A run with no parts decision has no lines (exit 4), and no lines is not a pass.
- A run that asks and is not released is refused (exit 2). So is an empty event log (exit 2).
- A last line cut mid-write is left out, as the run's reader leaves it out, and the output says so (`torn_last_line` in `--json`).
- `bom_lines` is not used: it reads the graph's electrical component nodes, which recorded runs do not have.

**Sheet:** `example_sheet.fixture.json`.
- Its header must say `kind: "example fixture"`.
- Each entry gives the exact node ids it answers, a maker and the maker's part number, and up to five facts: availability, unit price, minimum order quantity, order multiple, lead time to Norway with its scope.
- Every number is `{value, unit}`; a bare number is a schema error.
- A price or a lead time of zero is refused as a slip.
- Every fact carries a source note: `example`, or `read` with a place and a date.
- In the committed sheet every figure is an example value, starred in the table and flagged `example_value` in `--json`.
- One real maker's part number (from the reference brief's plan label) stands beside an invented, starred price. The header and the footnote say that every figure is an example.

**Verdict per line:** `passes`, `incomplete` or `fails`.
- **Incomplete, never a pass:** the part is not in the sheet; a fact is missing; the lead time is generic ("unverifiable for Norway"); or no quantity is stated ("quantity needed not recorded: the minimum-order rule is not judged").
- **Fails:** a lead time above four weeks to Norway; a minimum order above five times the quantity needed; a part that is not purchasable. Exactly four weeks and exactly five times pass.
- **Exit status:** 0 every line passes, 1 any line fails, 2 refused, 3 none fails and some are incomplete, 4 no lines.

**`--quantities`:** a person's stated quantity needed per node id, `{value, unit: "1"}`. It is recorded in the output as the operator's input, with its unit. A quantity for a node that is no line is refused.

## What is proven and how

- `tests/unit/bom/`: 67 rows. They are green with `tests/unit/ui` (852 passed on the laptop's test slot), and `./scripts/check.sh types lint` is green.
- **Exit codes:** held as the numbers 0 to 4.
- **The shipped sheet:** its own entries are run on lines carrying their ids, and each verdict its header promises is produced. The default command answers from the sheet on a run built by the tests.
- **Read only:** the command writes nothing under its run, a temporary home or its working directory.
- **No network:** it runs with `socket.socket`, `create_connection`, `getaddrinfo` and `socketpair` patched to raise. No function, class or method is named for ordering, and no module imports a network library (ARCH-121).
- **Mutants:** `scripts/mutation/bom_check_mutants.json` has 37 entries, and `check_entry_files.py` is clean. 21 guard mutants were run as the red proof and every one was killed by an assertion, with both baselines green. The rest of the list is left to be scheduled.

## What is not proven / left out

- This is shown, not measured: every figure in the sheet is an example value, not distributor data.
- **Left out:**
  - a live distributor: it needs credentials, and which distributor to use is not chosen here;
  - the orchestrator sending a failing line back to a role;
  - the measurement the risk table asks for.
- The minimum-order rule cannot be judged on a recorded run, because no run records a quantity needed.
- A sheet of read figures cannot be loaded yet: the header must call it an example fixture.
- Tests live in `tests/unit/bom/`, not `tests/unit/build/`, because pytest's `norecursedirs` skips every directory named `build`.
- No UI screen.

## Purpose

The source review found no grant-lifetime bypass: the checker rejects grants in return types, struct fields, enum payloads, constants and collections; grants and their saved policy arguments are GC-managed pointer-bearing objects. The remaining concern was whether a live local grant and its argument graph remain rooted across collection.

## Change

- Add `tests/gc/grant_roots.cap`: obtain a grant, perform 2,000 allocation-heavy iterations, then call the protected function.
- Add the expected output and run the fixture with `CAPSTAN_GC_STRESS=1`, forcing collection on every allocation.
- Keep this test separate from the ordinary grant argument-role and policy-recheck tests.

This is a regression for the conservative stack-root / heap object graph assumption. It is not evidence that a grant bypass was found.

## Validation

The normal conformance suite and the new GC-stress execution must pass on all supported CI platforms.

author: gyutae-kim
body:
## 요약

SKP 앱 README에 남은 코어 요청(3D 좌표축 표시가 세계 원점에만 그려져 옮기거나 돌린 그리기 축의 자리·방향을 보이지 못함 — 코어에 축 틀을 주는 길이 없음)을 새 공개 API 하나로 풉니다.
`setAxesFrame({ origin, x, y } | null)`을 주면 격자 X·Y축선을 그 원점을 지나 그 방향으로 그립니다. 주지 않거나 `null`이면 0.100.0과 같습니다(그린 도형·GL 호출·알림).

먼저 이미 풀렸는지 읽었습니다: 코어에는 축 틀·축 원점을 주는 API가 없었습니다(0.65.0 절은 앱이 선분 묶음으로 그리라고 두었고, 앱은 그 길을 쓰지 않았습니다).

## 바뀐 것

- `Viewer3d.setAxesFrame(frame: AxesFrame | null): boolean`, getter `axesFrame`, 형 `AxesFrame { origin, x, y }`(배열·형식 배열의 앞 세 값 — 입구에서 내보냄)
  - 축선 = 원점을 지나는 그 방향 직선을 격자 사각 기둥(x·y 범위)과 원점 높이 ± 격자 한 변으로 자른 선분. 원점 높이에 그립니다(격자 면에 내리지 않음). 세계 축을 격자 높이에 주면 0.100.0 선분과 같은 규칙
  - 틀이 있으면 x = 0·y = 0 격자선도 그립니다(세계 원점 축선이 없으므로)
  - 축선 끝점이 보이는 범위 밖일 때만 가까운·먼 면을 넓힙니다(안이면 카메라 틀·고르기·측정 값이 틀 없을 때와 비트까지 같음)
  - `y`가 `x`에 직교하지 않으면 그람-슈미트로 맞춥니다(Z = X × Y는 받지 않음). 쓸 수 없는 틀(객체가 아님, 유한한 수 셋이 아닌 원점·방향, 좌표 한도 밖 원점, 길이 0·넘치는 방향, `x`와 나란한 `y`)은 `false`(앞 틀 그대로 — `setMeasureInferenceLock` 꼴)
  - 틀이 없을 때 `null`은 아무것도 하지 않습니다(격자를 다시 만들지 않음)
- 순수 `gridLines(g, origin?, frame?)` 셋째 인자, `axesFrameOf`·`axesFrameLines`(`opencad-viewer3d/grid`)
- 판단: 왼쪽 아래 축 표시는 세계 축 그대로(뷰 큐브·표준 뷰와 같은 세계 — 틀을 따르면 큐브와 어긋남. SketchUp 꼴을 원하면 앱이 `setAxesVisible(false)`). 측정(축 추론·잠금·축 다리·찍은 값·`onMeasure`)과 고르기는 바꾸지 않습니다 — 틀 방향으로 재려면 기존 `setMeasureInferenceLock({ direction })`
- 판 0.101.0, README 0.101.0 절(읽은 표·새 API·판단·크기·확인·남은 한계·앱이 할 일)과 맨 앞 요약

## 확인

- 새 시험 `tests/v01010axes.test.ts` 18개(순수 8 · 뷰어 10 — 가짜 DOM·가짜 WebGL). 0.100.0 src로 14개 실패(API 없음·셋째 인자를 읽지 않음)
- 새 API를 부르지 않는 정상 길 탐색(104걸음, 저장소에 넣지 않음): GL 그리기·덧그림 호출·알림·상태 해시가 0.100.0 src와 107줄 모두 같음
- typecheck 통과. 새 시험·탐색·`misc`·`origin` 4파일 35개, `v0590axis`·`v0920args`·`v0500input`·`v0940contract` 4파일 171개 통과
- 크기: 코어 조각 460,184 (156,179) → 462,025 (156,826) B(+1,841 / gzip +647). 묶어 그리기·면 미리 강조 조각·첫 화면 입구 그대로
- 부하로 생략 — CI가 전체 시험·화소를 합니다. 실제 GPU·브라우저로 틀 축선을 보지 못했습니다(가짜 WebGL 그리기 기록·끝점으로만 확인)

## 위험

- 바뀐 기본 동작은 없습니다. 기존 화소 장면은 새 API를 부르지 않으므로 `pixels-changed` 라벨 없이 통과해야 합니다
- 새 API를 부른 뒤에만 그림이 달라집니다: 격자 축선 자리·방향, x = 0·y = 0 격자선, 축선이 보이는 범위 밖이면 가까운·먼 면

## 남은 일

- Z축선 없음(0.100.0도 없음), −쪽 점선 없음, 격자와 함께만 보임, 격자 자체는 세계 축에 나란함
- 틀 원점이 격자 사각형 밖이면 축선이 짧거나 없음(격자 범위 규칙)
- 실제 브라우저·GPU에서 보기

## 앱이 할 일

- SKP: 판 올림(코어 병합 커밋 전체 SHA). 그리기 축이 바뀔 때마다(문서를 열 때, 그리기 축을 기억하는 장면을 고를 때) `viewer.setAxesFrame(doc.drawAxes ?? null)` — `{ origin, x, y, z }`를 그대로 주면 됩니다(`z`는 읽지 않음, `null`이면 세계 축). `origin`은 코어에 준 장면과 같은 좌표. 그 뒤 README의 「코어에 축 틀을 주는 길이 없음」 문장을 걷습니다
- NC·STEP: 판 올림만(부르지 않으면 바뀌는 것이 없음)
- 앱 가짜 WebGL 하네스의 GL 호출 수·그린 도형은 0.100.0과 같아야 합니다(`setAxesFrame`을 부르는 하네스만 다름)

author: gfreund123
body:
## Second checkpoint — primitive nonuniform substitutions

**Head:** ba58227c5a047ff3859a148a5fdaac4fd1451e4c. The theorem now covers **every nonperiodic fixed word of every primitive binary substitution**, including nonuniform ones (e.g. Fibonacci), in addition to all binary uniform substitutions from checkpoint 1.

[Full extension proof](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ba58227c5a047ff3859a148a5fdaac4fd1451e4c/research/mahler-physical-scripts-20261124/PRIMITIVE_MORPHISMS.md) · [Additional exact controls](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/ba58227c5a047ff3859a148a5fdaac4fd1451e4c/research/mahler-physical-scripts-20261124/PRIMITIVE_CHECKS.md)

- Exact regularity for unequal image lengths: the Mahler coefficient vanishes iff the two periodic image words coincide. That would force the fixed word itself to be periodic.
- Irrational Perron weight: one leading monomial dominates along the moving rational point. Rational Perron weight: the transverse monomial is governed exactly by the secondary eigenvalue; degenerate cases reduce to a rational monomial curve.
- New weighted D-finite lemma: for any aperiodic binary word and positive integral clock weights p,q, the series G_1(a z^p,b z^q) is transcendental for all nonzero rational a,b. Finite normalized boundary states turn any hypothetical polynomial recurrence into eventual periodicity.
- Executed 11,532 periodic-image regularity controls (including 1,176 proper-prefix cases) and 163 exact transverse eigenvalue identities. No Lean compilation or full validator run; written theorem remains proposed.
- Concurrent PR188/189 descriptions were refreshed and pinned. Neither supplies a universal substitution structure for ordinary escape.

**Collatz remains OPEN.** This draft builds on PR182's actual scalar and L/P physical return language, and PR187's fixed-source repeat obstruction. It directly excludes rational realization of all non-eventually-periodic binary uniform substitution fixed-point scripts (not just balanced scripts, or scripts of subexponential height), over any two distinct equal-odd-length gap blocks.

## The mathematical result

For the complete physical inverse affine maps f_i(t)=α_i t+β_i, write
G_i(X,Y)=Σ_{j:s_j=i} X^{#0 before j}Y^{#1 before j}.
Then (1-X)G_0+(1-Y)G_1=1, and the physical completion is a nonconstant rational affine function of G_1(α_0,α_1). A binary uniform substitution induces an exact two-variable Mahler equation. Its coefficient is nonzero at **every** physical iterate by the earliest differing position of the substitution images.

The proof uses an elementary weighted D-finite obstruction, a Mahler auxiliary polynomial, explicit propagation of algebraic height, and nonvanishing along the rational monomial orbit. It covers the unbalanced cases and treats the degenerate ratio cases λ=0,±1 separately. Thus the unique physical odd 2-adic completion is transcendental for every such nonperiodic script, even when the prescribed real block slopes expand. No assumption of ordinary subexponential growth, probabilistic parity, or equality of real and 2-adic completions is used.

The explicit L/P example σ(0)=0^(b−1)1, σ(1)=10^(b−1) works for all b≥12 and has expansion factor 9^b/(4·8^b)>1. Every finite prefix has ordinary lifts, but no fixed rational source realizes the infinite word.

- [Written proof](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2accad955ed02f55bec507bd47e2f5f3787c8c7a/research/mahler-physical-scripts-20261124/README.md)
- [Lean finite core (uncompiled)](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2accad955ed02f55bec507bd47e2f5f3787c8c7a/research/mahler-physical-scripts-20261124/MahlerCore.lean)
- [Source audit](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2accad955ed02f55bec507bd47e2f5f3787c8c7a/research/mahler-physical-scripts-20261124/SOURCES.md)
- [Exact execution record](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/2accad955ed02f55bec507bd47e2f5f3787c8c7a/research/mahler-physical-scripts-20261124/CHECKS.md)

Exact controls completed: 13,860 finite Mahler substitution identities (each also checked weight and one-sum identity), 924 coefficient regularity checks, 924 ratio identities, 2,044 literal rational physical paths, 93 telescopes, 19 expanding parameters. Lean/Lake and a complete local checkout were unavailable: the Lean source is pending compilation and axiom audit, and the full repository validator was not run.

**Open:** arbitrary non-substitutive schedules, all positive cycles, universal triadic scalar membership, and the fixed-source merger bridge. This is an actual-source exclusion theorem, not an assertion that exceptional Collatz orbits must be substitutive. Historical priority is not claimed.

body:
## Problem

Module-loader still runs Changewrite v0.14.1, AgentSkills v0.7.0, and CodeQuality v0.7.0, so agents here miss skills and lint rules added since, and the release tooling is behind. This is one repo in the org-wide pin sync tracked in flipbook-labs/infra#47.

## Solution

This moves Changewrite to v0.16.0 in `ci.yml` and `release.yml`, AgentSkills to v0.9.0, and CodeQuality to v0.8.0. The CodeQuality pin is also hard-coded in `.lute/build.luau` and `.lute/lint.luau`, so both move with it. body:
Pursuit: design:docs-rfd-0072-auto-local-cloud-harmony:into-auto-cmux-tui-crates-cmux-cloud-start

This is RFD 0072 piece 5, "Into Auto", stacked on #51824. Its diff includes #51824 until that one lands, so review only the top commit. Quoting the task: "`place.rs` `auto()` takes the verdict as one more signal; shadow mode appends to `auto-shadow.jsonl`. The Swift sampler stops being a second source for memory and battery."

## What changes
- **acpmux** `host_pressure` (`_acpmux/status`) now carries `power` (`batteryPercent`, `onAc`, `lidClosed`) from the existing cached `host_power` reading. It is read in parallel with the host budget verdict.
- **cmux-cloud-start-core** adds `moves/place/verdict.rs`.
  - `signals(own, verdict)` builds the rule's `Signals`. Memory pressure and battery come from the verdict, and a closed lid counts as sleep. Free disk, idle time and the sleep notification are the only things the app still reads itself.
  - `judge()` runs the unchanged `auto()` and adds a **shadow** decision. The shadow is "toCloud, reason `busy`" when the verdict says the computer is over budget, the chat is on Auto, local, has work, the person is here, and Auto would otherwise stay.
  - `shadow_line()` formats the `auto-shadow.jsonl` line.
- **FFI** `cloud_move_place_auto` takes `{mode, chat, session, nowMs, own, verdict}`. It returns `do`/`reason` as before, plus `shadow` and `shadowLine`.
- **Swift** `CloudAutoSignals` no longer reads battery (IOPS) or tracks the memory level. Its memory-pressure and power sources only wake Auto to ask again. `CloudPlaceDriver.evaluate` awaits the daemon's verdict (`placeVerdict`, 5 s bound) and decides each chat on it. It hands each `shadowLine` to `placeShadow`, which appends to `<acpmux home>/auto-shadow.jsonl` off the main thread through `CloudPlaceShadowLog` (in CmuxNextCloudPlace; it starts over past 4 MiB).

## Note
The RFD names an agents'-share verdict (`reserve.rs`), which does not exist yet. This uses the existing host budget verdict, which judges the whole machine. That is why its over-budget judgment stays shadow only, as RFD stage 1 asks: nothing moves for it.

No measurement: this changes which source Auto reads, not a hot path. The Auto pass adds one `_acpmux/status` read every 30 s while an Auto chat exists. A lane VM cannot run a Mac bench.

## Tests
- `verdict/tests.rs` covers three cases: memory and battery come from the verdict (low battery wins, charging is not on battery, no verdict moves nothing), over budget is shadow only, and no shadow without a cause.
- Fleet run [45321847384](https://github.com/manaflow-ai/cmux/actions/runs/45321847384) at f2ea051d7af: cmux-cloud-start-core `moves::place` 18 passed, every cmux-layout-reducer-ffi test passed, acpmux `--lib host` 616 passed, 0 failed.
- `cmux-ci compile-check --app` at 44bfd7da6c1: CmuxNextCloudPlace and this PR's app adapter compile. Three errors remain, all in #51824's own code (`CloudHandlers+Move.swift:72`, `CloudService.swift:340`, `CloudBringBack.swift:127`), and they are listed on #51824. This PR also fixes two of #51824's compile errors: the evacuation loop's isolation-checker failure and `AgentPaneHeaderState`'s public `Data` import.
