author: waghanza
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [github.com/valyala/fasthttp](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp) | `v1.79.0` → `v1.80.0` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/go/github.com%2fvalyala%2ffasthttp/v1.80.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/go/github.com%2fvalyala%2ffasthttp/v1.79.0/v1.80.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>valyala/fasthttp (github.com/valyala/fasthttp)</summary>

### [`v1.80.0`](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/releases/tag/v1.80.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/compare/v1.79.0...v1.80.0)

`v1.80.0` fixes client connection desynchronization when skipping response bodies and preserves cache variation headers during compression. It also adds helper APIs for downstream frameworks, makes parser errors matchable, and improves redirects, compression negotiation, and repeated-header handling.

#### Security fixes and hardening

- **Skipping a response body no longer desynchronizes later requests.** Reusing a `Response` after HEAD no longer makes subsequent requests skip their bodies. When a caller explicitly skips a potentially present body, `Client` and `HostClient` close the connection instead of pooling it with unread bytes. `PipelineClient` reads and discards the body so the next pipelined response starts at the correct boundary. The caller's `SkipBody` setting is preserved. [#​2533](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2533)
- **Compression preserves every `Vary` line.** Adding `Accept-Encoding` no longer removes later `Vary` fields, such as `Vary: Cookie`. This fixes a regression that could let a shared cache reuse a response without considering all of its original variation criteria. Both `CompressHandler` and compressed static-file serving are covered. [#​2598](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2598)
- **Unsigned float parsing rejects non-finite values and negative zero.** `ParseUfloat` and the argument getters that use it now reject NaN, infinity, and `-0`. Finite formats accepted by `strconv.ParseFloat`, including a leading `+`, digit separators, and hexadecimal floats, remain supported. [#​2546](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2546)

#### Features

- **Bounded decompression helpers work directly on byte slices.** `AppendGunzipBytesWithLimit`, `AppendInflateBytesWithLimit`, `AppendUnbrotliBytesWithLimit`, and `AppendUnzstdBytesWithLimit` append decoded data while enforcing a limit on newly decoded bytes. Existing data in the destination does not count toward the limit. Exceeding the limit returns `ErrBodyTooLarge`; a non-positive limit leaves output unlimited. The zstd helper also limits decoder window size when a positive limit is supplied. [#​2520](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2520)
- **Frameworks can inspect header normalization and reuse redirect helpers.** `RequestHeader.NormalizingDisabled()` and `ResponseHeader.NormalizingDisabled()` expose the current setting. `HasNonHTTPSchemeWithoutAuthority` identifies locations such as `mailto:` and native-app callbacks, and `DefaultMaxRedirectsCount` exports the existing default of 16. `DoRedirects` continues to use the count explicitly supplied by its caller. [#​2520](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2520)
- **Unsupported methods and unknown transfer codings have matchable errors.** `errors.Is` can identify `ErrUnsupportedRequestMethod` regardless of `SecureErrorLogMessage`. The new `ErrUnknownTransferCoding` distinguishes a well-formed but unsupported transfer coding from malformed framing and also matches `ErrUnsupportedTransferEncoding`. Custom error handlers can use these distinctions to choose between 501 and 400 responses; malformed request fields and targets still take precedence over an unknown coding. [#​2594](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2594)

#### HTTP compatibility and redirects

- **Compression negotiation checks all supplied encodings.** `HasAcceptEncoding` scans every `Accept-Encoding` header line and continues after a matching `q=0` member, so a later acceptable occurrence is considered. Compressible media types are also recognized case-insensitively. [#​2600](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2600), [#​2590](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2590), [#​2606](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2606)
- **Directory redirects preserve the client-facing path.** For ordinary origin-form request targets, `FS` adds the trailing slash to the original encoded path and retains the query string. Prefix stripping and virtual-host rewriting no longer expose the internal filesystem lookup path in the redirect. [#​2551](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2551)
- **`DoRedirects` preserves URL credentials on the initial request.** Relative redirects retain URI credentials, while absolute redirects use only their own userinfo. An explicit `Authorization` header still takes precedence and follows the existing host-based forwarding rules. [#​2531](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2531)
- **URI updates separate queries from fragments.** Updating a URI with `?next=2#new` now stores `next=2` as the query and `new` as the fragment, keeping the fragment out of the HTTP request line. Explicit empty query delimiters are preserved, including a redirect target ending in `?`. Hosts with an empty port, such as `example.com:` or `[::1]:`, now receive the scheme's default port when dialing. [#​2592](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2592), [#​2603](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2603)
- **Repeated cookies and suppressed content types retain their meaning.** `ResponseHeader.PeekAll("Set-Cookie")` returns each cookie separately instead of joining them into one value; `Peek` is unchanged. Adapted `net/http` handlers that set `Content-Type` to nil or empty now send no default content type, on both buffered and flushed responses. [#​2599](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2599), [#​2556](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2556)

This release also adds a WebSocket README, reorganizes its tests, addresses intermittent CI failures, and clarifies retry callback eligibility and fragmented input to `Request.Read`.

#### What's Changed

##### Security and hardening

- fix(client): don't let SkipBody desync reused responses and connections by [@​waw666waw666](https://redirect.github.com/waw666waw666) in [#​2533](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2533)
- fix: don't drop later Vary lines when adding Accept-Encoding by [@​waw666waw666](https://redirect.github.com/waw666waw666) in [#​2598](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2598)
- fix: reject NaN, infinity and negative zero in ParseUfloat by [@​Kernel-Hunter](https://redirect.github.com/Kernel-Hunter) in [#​2546](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2546)

##### Features

- feat: add helper APIs for downstream frameworks by [@​gaby](https://redirect.github.com/gaby) in [#​2520](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2520)
- feat: make the unsupported method and unknown transfer coding errors matchable by [@​gaby](https://redirect.github.com/gaby) in [#​2594](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2594)

##### Fixes

- fix(header): keep scanning Accept-Encoding after a q=0 member by [@​CJstate](https://redirect.github.com/CJstate) in [#​2590](https://redirect.github.com/valyala/fasthttp/pull/2590)
- fix(fs): redirect a directory request to the path the client sent by [@​Dv2Corn](https://redir

author: scotteilerman
body:
# Summary
Moves the Forge wizard's blueprint Description field from the Run window subsection to the Review and export card, directly below the blueprint name, and replaces the "Generated blueprint" default with a one-line summary derived from the blueprint. The summary updates as the blueprint is edited until the user types their own, the same way the wizard already handles the derived name.

AI disclosure: Claude Code; drafted the code, tests, release note and this description

**How it works.** `build_forge_blueprint(description=None)` now derives the text with `default_blueprint_description(bp)` in `resolve.py`, next to where it derives the default name, so Python callers get the same default. The summary names the grid, its size and approximate spacing, the run window, the model preset (without `-default`), the BGC mode, the forcing preset and any CDR release, for example `wio-toy, 20x20x10 grid at ~400 km, 2012-01-02 to 2012-01-06, roms-marbl-0.13, MARBL, one alkalinity release`. It reads only the blueprint's own fields (no grid or file), so it runs on every resolve, and it leaves out any part it can't describe (a grid file's size, a spec authored from scratch) instead of failing. Past about 120 characters it drops the forcing preset, then the model preset; with a CDR release the forcing preset usually goes. Cells far from square show both spacings (`~83x500 km`). It uses an ASCII `x` because the blueprint YAML writer escapes `×` as `\xD7`.

**Wizard wiring.** `_description_touched` follows `_name_touched`. `_gather` passes `None` while the field is untouched (or cleared), `_rebuild` fills the field under `_suspend()`, and a real edit sets the flag. `self.description` left the `watched` list: its own observer sets the flag and then rebuilds, so the fill can't write over the user's first keystroke. A loaded file keeps its description unless it is the old `PLACEHOLDER_DESCRIPTION` ("Generated blueprint"), missing, or equal to its own derived text (saved without edits). In those cases it follows the inputs again. Clearing a typed description leaves the box empty with a placeholder, and the blueprint gets the summary, as Name does. Refilling the box would put text back in front of the user while they type.

**Catalog spec saves.** All five spec saves now go through `_spec_description()`: the user's typed text, or `""` while the field holds the summary. The summary describes the whole run, not one spec. With `""`, a saved ModelSpec keeps its base spec's description (`register_model_from_settings` already falls back to it). Domain, forcing, output and CDR specs are saved with an empty description. Before this, every spec saved from the wizard got "Generated blueprint"; that is where the bundled specs' "Generated blueprint" descriptions came from. Those bundled files are left as they are.

**Behavior change, not breaking.** Python callers of `build_forge_blueprint` that omit `description` now get the summary instead of "Generated blueprint". `description` is blueprint metadata and is excluded from the content hash, so hashes and provenance stamps don't change, and no golden fixture changed. The release note is an Improvement, not `breaking-python`.

**Testing.** `python -m pytest cstar/tests/unit_tests`: 10178 passed, 8 skipped, 1 xfailed after rebasing onto #955. That run came before a final change that only edits the field's glossary hint, and was not rerun. Tier 1 (`cstar/tests/integration_tests/test_fixtures.py` and `cstar/tests/integration_tests/forge`): 98 passed, 0 skipped. `pre-commit run --all-files` and `towncrier check --compare-with origin/main` pass. New tests in `test_forge_blueprint.py` cover the resolver default and each part of the summary, the wizard following edits, typed and cleared text, loaded files, and spec saves (derived text never reaches a spec; typed text does). In the running wizard I checked the field position, live updates on a date edit, typed text surviving later edits, and the tutorial file `docs/tutorials/forge_blueprint_wio_release.yaml` keeping its description on load.

**Not verified.** Tier 2 was not run; nothing in it reads the description.

## Code Review Checklist
- [x] Closes CWorthy-ocean/claude-docs#190
- [x] Release note added as `docs/changes/+wizard-description.improvement.rst`
- [x] New functionality has documentation, type hint coverage, and tests
- [x] Tests and `pre-commit run --all-files` are passing (unit suite and Tier 1; Tier 2 not run)

author: apellis
body:
For Webster, arXiv:1309.3796v2, §6.1, proof of Lemma 6.8 after (6.21), this computes the affine relation equations at a fixed bottom loading of the interval (#405).

`exit_relation_polynomial_matrix_iff` gives an exact finite polynomial matrix for arbitrary upper algebra coefficients. Each coefficient contributes its polynomial PBW tuple at the actual exit loading. `exit_polynomial_matrix_iff` gives its action on a specified list of upper words. In a chosen top-dotted PBW basis, the entry at permutation `t` and exit column `a` is the coefficient polynomial of the bare concatenated word. Arbitrary upper polynomials multiply these entries. Reconstruction of the fixed-bottom column proves the equivalence in all crossing degrees, allowing repeated colours and any symmetric parameters over a commutative ring.

`twoBlack_extreme_middle` computes a relation between distinct exits at any offset `p`. The reduced upper word `[p,p+1]` on the extreme exit `[p,p+1,p+2]` equals the middle exit `[p+1,p,p+2]` with the transported black/right-red square polynomial on top. A braid, a square, and two polynomial slides prove the formula. The integral example has two equal black labels and red/black parameter of weight one. The two columns have entries `x₀` and `1` in the middle row and vanish in all other rows, so every polynomial relation on the pair is a multiple of `(1,-x₀)`.

The general entries are defined using PBW coordinates. Computing the remaining exit syzygies and their marked lifts is still open. This PR is independent of #565.

Both native theorems and the integral fixture passed with warnings as errors. The focused transitive axiom audit checked 1,789 declarations.

author: ssjraz
body:
`spe study --baseline main --candidate HEAD --config spe.json` compares two committed versions of a trusted local HTTP service. One operator-supplied configuration defines the build, foreground server, readiness GET, expected response and measurement settings. The driver builds each distinct commit once in a private local clone and starts a fresh process group and scratch directory for every arm of every pair. [Copy-paste example](https://github.com/SsjRaz/systems-performance-engine/blob/a150a5111253bd0a9cec19c66db03701a387900d/docs/STUDY.md#try-a-controlled-regression)

The driver freezes the commit IDs and balanced order before building. The existing C++ engine performs the readiness requests, verifies a response before timing each instance, records the GET workload and analyzes the native manifest. Results include a terminal summary, a replayable JSON report, per-instance logs and the stage that failed if a study stops early.

### Measured example

The documented example ran on a local Linux x86-64 host with the three pending Meilisearch and README PRs present. Commit `840d3e5` sleeps 3 ms per lookup. Commit `f0f6474` sleeps 15 ms and returns the same answer. Each comparison used eight fresh process pairs, 24 timed requests per instance and a prespecified 10% threshold.

| Comparison | Median per-process mean, baseline → candidate | Median paired change | Exact median interval | Native verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline → delayed commit | 3.36 → 15.52 ms | +367.0% | +313.5% to +380.8% | Regression |
| Delayed commit → itself | 15.52 → 15.46 ms | −0.1% | −4.0% to +3.1% | Inconclusive |

All 768 timed GETs and 32 native response preflights succeeded across the two studies. Replaying each saved manifest reproduced its original JSON decision. These figures describe the deliberately delayed fixture on this host.

### Integration coverage

The new CLI suite exercises dirty and staged caller files, a revision-specific config that must be ignored, fresh process identities, native replay, an occupied port, a wrong HTTP 200 body, a failed build, a slow healthy readiness check, a readiness timeout, SIGINT during measurement and SIGTERM with a live build descendant. Linux adopts and reaps orphaned workers in each owned process group. The interruption test checks the worker PID and socket after cleanup in a container whose PID 1 does not reap children. The feature is based on public `main`. A local trial combining #10, its follow-up #11, #12 and this head produced tree `a34052b600d032a45e9649336cc6ac6e9b92a126` without conflicts.

All 15 CTest suites passed on that combined Linux tree in Release and ASan/UBSan, including real HTTP and HTTPS. The combined executable also replayed the #10 and #11 evidence archives. The GitHub push and pull request workflows passed both configurations on the final feature head. [Pull request CI](https://github.com/SsjRaz/systems-performance-engine/actions/runs/45320642535) · [Branch CI](https://github.com/SsjRaz/systems-performance-engine/actions/runs/45320636620)

author: sykhayyat
body:
Steps 1–3 of `decisions/2026-11-23-frontends-are-views-in-boxes.md` §5 (#118).

1. **The record.** FRONTENDS.md becomes the decision record. Note deletion is a setting, `noteDelete`: `twoStep` by default, `immediate` as the alternative.
2. **The registry** (`views.ts`, `views-builtin.ts`). It holds parts, modes, link modes and layers (resolved global < mode < scope < box), plus the scope query. The built-ins register through the same API a contribution would. Every refusal carries a reason key.
3. **Boxes hold views.** `Leaf` is `{view, link}` and replaces `role` and the prose/linked flags.
   - The head is the mode line, `scope · mode · link → leader`, and each part opens a menu. Refused combinations are shown disabled with their reason, never hidden.
   - ⊞ opens a box beside this one (scope, then mode), and the new box follows the one it was opened from.
   - Links can chain. Cycles and self-links are refused. Closing a leader hands its followers to that leader's own leader.
   - `validTree` keeps stored ids, so a tab's focused box survives a restart. It refuses duplicate ids and old role-shaped trees, and unlinks a dangling leader.

Writer mode (#238) and steps 4–5 come next, in their own PR.

**Gate:** `tsc` and `lint` are clean. The suite is 176 files, 14928 passed and 0 failed. browserlang and importui skip locally because there is no browser engine; CI's browser job runs them.


## Also on this branch: #238 option 1 and steps 4–5

The later commits landed on this branch rather than in a stacked PR:

## Stack

Merge bottom-up. Base: #46 (`context`).

1. #79 tool calls on the session log

---

## Summary

A standalone library under `apps/api/src/OpenApi/`, with no Worker, domain or handler wiring (that is in the OpenAPI-servers PR further up).

- `importOpenApi(document, { include?, exclude?, limits? })` returns a catalog of operation summaries; `catalog.descriptor(name)` builds one tool descriptor on demand (`name`, `description`, `inputSchema`, `outputSchema?`, `method`, `pathTemplate`, `readOnly`).
- `buildRequest(descriptor, args, baseUrl)` builds the HTTP request. Path arguments are percent-encoded so they cannot add segments, `..`, a query or a fragment; the URL's origin must equal the base URL's; `Authorization`, `Cookie` and declared security headers from the caller are dropped.
- `readOnly` is true only when the HTTP method fixes it (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS).
- No new dependency: Effect's `JsonSchema.fromSchemaOpenApi3_0/3_1` converts dialects. A dereferencer would inline shared schemas, which is the memory problem to avoid; descriptors share one converted copy.

**Scale (Node 24):** Checkfu's own `openapi.json` imports in 14–36 ms; a synthetic 10,000-operation, 10 MB document in under 0.8 s with a 26 MB catalog.

## Not supported

YAML, OpenAPI 3.2, Swagger 2.0 (rejected with a typed error), non-JSON bodies, cookie parameters, path `label`/`matrix` styles, nested `deepObject`, `allowReserved`.

- Every commit in the stack passes `typecheck`, `generate:check`, `format:check` and `lint` on its own.

body:
## Summary

The close-shot kit's five-finger 3D hand was too big for the painted arm it joins. The user picked size 1.1 from a comparison sheet and confirmed it at camera 1.5 m, 0.5 m and 0.3 m.

```diff
 placeMidHand (src/painted/kit/mid-hands.ts)
-  hand size = 1.5 × height / 1.75
+  hand size = 1.1 × armScale          # every adult shares one painted arm
 midCell
+  foreScale = cast armScale            # a child's close-shot forearm narrows with its hand
 hold-cup
+  mug scale 0.8, grip radius 0.032     # fits the smaller hand
 edu26/r4-hands.ts, edu33/shots/B07-SH04.ts
+  size pinned at the delivered 1.5     # these episodes render as delivered
+src/painted/kit/hand-size.ts           # handDims, measureHand, HAND_SIZE_BANDS
+scripts/hand-size.mjs                  # ratios per cast, PASS/FAIL, --json
+tests/hand-size.test.ts                # every cast × 34 MID_ACTIONS × both hands
```

`cast.ts` exports the plain arm widths as `PLAIN_ARM` (same numbers) and adds the opt-in `FigPose.foreScale`. `KIT-HAND-SIZE` is the size check still (props `size`, `foreScale`, `dist`).

`scripts/painted-kit/build-notes.md` records the measurements, the user's picks and the proposed rule text DP06 (a `CP-H` hand-size section) and DP07 (AN15). Those are `proposed` only; no rule document changes here.

## Evidence

- **Before** (adult, hand 1.5): knuckle row : wrist 1.75, hand : mitten 1.61, hand : head 0.49.
  **After** (`node scripts/hand-size.mjs`, every adult): 1.28 / 1.18 / 0.35, all PASS. Children on the narrowed forearm: boy-school 1.28, girl-school 1.28.
- Hand tests (`hand-size`, `hand-kits`, `hand-gestures`, `arm-depth`): 15 pass, 0 fail. `edu26-talk`, `edu33-guilt`, `people`: 14 pass, 0 fail. `scripts/context-map.py`: 577 modules, 0 uncovered.
- Frames viewed: 34 actions front and back at 1.1, the 1.5 / 0.5 / 0.3 m sheets, mug before and after, child candidates a, b, c. They are under `out/` in the worktree and are not in the store.
- Full `npm test` before the last edits: 400 of 404. `loudness` and `segments` fail on Node 20 (`fs.globSync` needs Node 22); the `new-shot` and `render-inputs` logs were not opened. None touch the hand code.

Not verified: the child default was not re-rendered after it became the default (candidate c used the same `foreScale` 0.75 through the same code path), and EP26 / EP33 were not re-rendered to confirm the pin.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

One constant and one default; the old look returns with `MID_HAND_SIZE = 1.5` or a size argument at a call site.

**Blast Radius:** kit

Every close-shot five-finger hand in a new shot is 0.73 × its old size, and a child's close-shot forearm is thinner. Any shot outside EP26 and EP33 that calls `placeMidHand` without a size changes on its next render. Open and unchanged here: the 3D hand's outline is heavier than the painted arm at 0.5 m and closer, `phone-look` hides the phone behind the hand, and the POV path is not in the check script.

body:
## M31.10 — email-verification security hardening (owner directive)

**Follow-up to PR #5** — PR #5 (M31) was MERGED by the owner at 2026-11-24T02:01Z (`77bd87c`), and merged PRs are immutable, so this hardening lands as a new reviewable PR on top of the exact merged state (`6dee86b`, tree-identical to `origin/main`). **Left unmerged for owner review — never self-merged.**

### Baseline
- Branch base: `6dee86b` (PR #5 head; `git diff 6dee86b origin/main` = empty)
- Endpoint commit: `be38926`

### The four requirements, implemented and regression-tested

1. **Registration REQUIRES an identity** — closes the email-verification bypass. `POST /api/auth/register` previously accepted an identity-less body, which skipped the verification lifecycle entirely (no token, trust gates never applied). Every new registration is now identity-aware: PRIVATE profile + verification token issued unconditionally. **Legacy accounts and existing user records are preserved exactly** — no backfill, no reclassification (tests assert the 400, zero rows created, and an untouched pre-M31 legacy row). Google OAuth intentionally unchanged (provider-verified emails; `tests/google-oauth.test.ts` 26/26 green).
2. **GET on the confirm route is COMPLETELY NON-MUTATING** — automated link scanners / prefetchers (SafeLinks, unfurlers) can no longer consume single-use tokens. GET = read-only state inspection + 302 into the new public `#/verify-email` page carrying the token; ONLY the explicit user confirmation (POST from that page) consumes it. Scanner-simulation regression: 3 GETs leave the token unconsumed and the user unverified; the subsequent POST verifies.
3. **Atomic consumption** — token consume (`consumedAt`) and `emailVerifiedAt` update run in ONE Prisma interactive transaction (bounded `maxWait`/`timeout`). Regression: expired tokens leave both writes untouched; 3 concurrent confirmations verify exactly once.
4. **Absolute URLs from the trusted configured origin** — links generated ONLY via `resolveShareOrigin()` (validated `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`/`VERCEL_URL`); request headers never influence the link (structural: the builder takes only the token). Unconfigured origin → honest path-only fallback + `linkAbsolute`/`originConfigured` delivery-audit markers; the GET compat redirect falls back to the request's own origin (same-host, never a foreign host). The email link now targets the confirmation page (explicit click) instead of the consuming GET.

### New surface
- `src/views/VerifyEmailView.tsx` — public, sessionless, non-mutating confirmation page; token stripped from the address bar after read; wired into `SiteShell` + `PUBLIC_ROOT_SEGMENTS` (public so an un-onboarded new account is never bounced into a setup flow).

### Verification evidence (isolated QA DB via `scripts/ops/qa-db-env.sh` guard)

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New regression suite `tests/m31-10-security-hardening.test.ts` | **15/15 pass** |
| Full per-file QA suite (111 files, per-file processes) | **1633 pass** — single timing flake `queue-reliability` (6 fail once during the run; **9/9 green across 4 isolated re-runs**; pre-existing timing sensitivity, not an M31.10 path) |
| Password login / Google OAuth / recovery / onboarding intact | `auth` 9/9 · `auth-routes` 11/11 · `recovery` 9/9 · `google-oauth` 26/26 · `trust-identity-registration` 15/15 · `trust-email-verification` 14/14 |
| TypeScript (`bunx tsc --noEmit`) | 0 errors |
| ESLint | 0 errors / 14 warnings (exact M31.8 baseline) |
| Schema parity | 104 models identical sqlite ↔ postgres |
| `prisma validate` both schemas | green (postgres validated with a postgres-protocol URL — the SQLite QA env var triggers its protocol guard, validation only) |
| Production standalone build | **exit 0** (2560MB heap cap; artifact 330M, BUILD_ID `GC0LBkQNWi5dA1duMlpzt`) |
| Secret scan + runtime-data scan on staged diff | clean |

### Honest scope notes
- The identity requirement is a **deliberate API contract change**: identity-less registration now returns 400. All QA fixtures/scripts were migrated to the new contract in this PR.
- Google-created accounts continue with `primaryIdentity = null` (legacy onboarding flow). Their emails are provider-verified by the OAuth flow itself. Adding identity selection to OAuth onboarding is an owner decision — recorded in the plan doc's M31.10 design notes.
- No production DDL/migration, no deployment, no email-provider setup, no security-default changes beyond the scoped hardening. No schema changes at all (104-model parity unchanged).

*Design decisions recorded in `docs/product/TRUST_ONBOARDING_AND_RIISHE_MULTI_AGENT_PLAN.md` (M31.10 section).*

author: fdesbiens
body:
Three `_no_output` tests for display driver paths no test reached. Test-only; each is registered in the demo list of the profiles that compile its rows.

**`guix_32bpp_rotated_pixelmap_blend_no_output`** (with `all_widgets_24xrgb_rotated_ccw`). Each blend function of the rotated 32 bpp pixelmap blend computes the rotated clip for a non-clockwise display in its `else` branch, and none of the seven ran: no test blended an uncompressed pixelmap on a 32 bpp display rotated counter-clockwise. The test draws its own pixelmaps (24xrgb, 32argb with alpha, 8-bit palette with and without a transparent index, 4444argb, 565rgb with and without alpha, compressed 24xrgb) on a 24xrgb display rotated clockwise, then counter-clockwise, at three clipped places, at brush alpha 255 (the write functions, which check the model's placement) and 157 (the blends). After every draw the whole canvas is compared with a model. It also reaches the compressed write's blended run past the rotated clip.

**`guix_partial_frame_buffer_16bpp_canvas_ops_no_output`** (with `partial_frame_buffer_16bpp`). The 16 bpp canvas copy, the 565rgb canvas blend and the 16 bpp block move return at once for a partial frame buffer canvas; the three partial canvas profiles never called them. The test reaches copy and blend through `gx_system_canvas_refresh` building a composite, with each canvas in turn given a partial buffer by `gx_canvas_memory_define`, and compares the whole composite and every canvas memory. `gx_canvas_block_move` refuses a partial canvas itself, so for one the display's block move is called directly.

**`guix_8bit_palette_rotated_aa_text_colors_16_no_output`** (with `glyph_draw_8bpp_screen_text_colors_16`). Checks that with 16 anti-aliased text colors both 8-bit palette setups install the 4-bit glyph draw; the rotated one had never run in that profile.

The first two fail when the code they cover is broken: the counter-clockwise position of one blend computed from the canvas width, the compressed blend allowed one pixel past the clip, or the three partial checks disabled.

In all 19 profiles with retries off, 1893 of 1893 tests pass. Against dev's CI no line or branch outcome falls, and the tests cover 42 lines and 15 branch outcomes no test reached.

author: wizardos-builder[bot]
body:
Refs humanitylabs-org/wizard-ux#1769

**What and why**
On a cold open the phone app did its meeting-recorder bookkeeping on the UI thread before the shell could draw: `MeetingRecorderService.recover()` in `onStart`/`onResume` opened the meeting store for the first time (reads the whole custody index plus every meeting journal) and read Android's exit records with their ANR trace, then locked the store. With a long meeting still uploading, the uploader held that same store lock while it rewrote and fsynced the whole custody index twice per acknowledged chunk, and kept re-taking it first, so the UI thread waited most of the time.

- `MizelStore.acked`: the custody receipt is written outside the store lock (custody first, then the journal, same order as before; a kill in between leaves the chunk pending and it is sent again).
- New `StartupWork`: a cold start's disk loads (the meeting store, `ProcessExits.refresh`) run on a background thread; the recorder recovery/resume after them still runs on the main thread, in order, so it stays in step with the recorder service. When already loaded, they run at once as before. Used by `MainActivity.onStart` (`recoverFromActivity`), `onResume` (`resumeUpdateFromActivity`), `ScrollCaptureDiagnostics.resumed` and `MizelUploadJob`.
- Phone 0.10.63 (versionCode 127).

Recovery mode (the other half of the report) is new behaviour and is its own feature: humanitylabs-org/wizard-ux#1775.

**Verified**
- Real `MizelStore` + `CaptureJournal` on JDK 17, a 6.4 h meeting (4,600 chunks, half still uploading, 1.3 MB custody index), uploader acking back to back, a "UI" thread doing what `recover()` does every 16 ms:
  - main: longest UI wait 1,368 ms, 10.6 s of 11.6 s spent waiting.
  - this branch: longest UI wait 13 ms, 0.3 s in total.
  - cold store open is 300-560 ms here; it now happens off the UI thread.
- New unit test `MizelTest.ackedDoesNotHoldTheStoreWhileWritingCustody` fails on main ("the store lock is free while custody works") and passes here. `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.wizards.os.mizel.*' --tests 'ai.wizards.os.audio.*' --tests ai.wizards.os.ProcessExitLogTest`: all pass. androidTest compiles.
- New emulator tests in `DeviceBridgeE2eTest` (CI's Android emulator job): `startupLoadsRunOffTheUiThread` (a 3 s load leaves the main thread free, what follows runs on main) and `longMeetingUploadsDoNotHoldTheUiThread` (the same 4,600-chunk meeting on the emulator's storage). The existing process-death resume scenario covers the deferred recover on a real open.
- `tests/home-screen-apps.test.mjs` (it runs the real `onStart`) now stubs `recoverFromActivity`; passes.
- `tests/feature-ids-in-core.test.mjs` passes (MeetingRecorderService +2 for the two `MizelHub.whenLoaded` calls; MizelUploadJob down 13 to 9).

Reuse:
- Native mic/meeting: REUSE `MeetingRecorderService` (its meeting store, custody journal and start hooks; `StartupWork` is a small helper for them, not a new component)

**Not checked**
A physical phone. No emulator on this box (no KVM); CI's emulator runs the on-device tests.

author: yanpr1332
body:
## Summary

Implements ALPHA-SYNC-002D on top of the merged owner-scoped Outbox and server protocol.

- Add a Main-process personal sync coordinator using the currently authenticated Supabase owner; Renderer cannot supply owner/device/cursor or operation envelopes.
- Add explicit per-item consent and a manual “Sync now” flow for personal tasks and manually created calendar events only.
- Push bounded Outbox batches, acknowledge exact owner-scoped operations, safely rebase in-flight local edits/deletes, and skip queue items whose consent or operation changed before upload.
- Pull ordered cursor pages and apply task/calendar snapshots locally. Persist conflicts rather than overwriting pending local edits; advance the cursor only after both stores and conflict records commit.
- Add app-shutdown handling so an in-flight request finishes before SQLite closes; unacknowledged operations remain retryable.
- Upgrade local task DB schema v8 → v9 with owner-scoped conflict records; keep manual calendar DB at v5.
- Add automated store/service/IPC/migration tests and update the acceptance/backlog documentation.

## Scope and safety

- Manual sync only. No timer or background uploader.
- Canvas, ICS, email-derived tasks, knowledge, focus sessions, study plans, and legacy ownerless queues are excluded.
- Unchecking an item stops future local uploads but does not delete an existing cloud copy.
- Conflict records are displayed, but choosing local vs cloud and recovery UX are deferred to ALPHA-SYNC-002E.
- No Supabase SQL migration was deployed and no real RLS or multi-device test was performed.

## Local verification

Please run from the repository root:

```sh
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
```

Real Supabase deployment and two-device acceptance remain explicitly out of scope for this PR.

author: r0msmith
body:
Fixes #117

## The problem

Android 11's `prebuilts/sdk` ships an `apksigner.jar` compiled for Java 9. The build container provides Java 8:

```
UnsupportedClassVersionError: com/android/apksigner/ApkSignerTool has been compiled by a
more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 53.0), this version of the
Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 52.0
```

`stderr` on that line goes to `/dev/null`, so `$digest` comes back empty and the only visible symptom is a signature mismatch, which aborts the build under `set -e`.

Android 12 and later ship a class 52 jar, which is why only 18.1 is affected:

| `prebuilts/sdk` tag | jar size | class version |
|---|---|---|
| android-11.0.0_r48 (18.1) | 434062 | 53 |
| android-12.1.0_r27 | 991274 | 52 |
| android-13.0.0_r83 | 1009547 | 52 |
| android-14.0.0_r67 | 1035139 | 52 |

## The change

Each tree ships a JDK able to run its own tools. Prefer `prebuilts/jdk/jdk11` when it is present, and fall back to `java` on `PATH` otherwise.

18.1, 20.0 and 21.0 all ship jdk11, so all three now use it. For 20.0 and 21.0 that is a change of runtime with no change of outcome, since their jar is class 52 and runs on either; both are tested below. 22.2, 23.2 and 24.0 ship no jdk11 and stay on the container's Java 8 exactly as before.

Naming jdk11 rather than searching for the newest JDK means this needs no maintenance when a tree later ships jdk26 or jdk30: those trees carry a class 52 jar that Java 8 already runs.

## Testing

Against `vendorsetup.sh` as it stands on `master`, using each branch's real `build/envsetup.sh`, its matching `build/make/shell_utils.sh`, and its real `prebuilts/sdk` jar, sourced the way `new_build.sh:472` does it (`source build/envsetup.sh > /dev/null`), in `lineageos4microg/docker-lineage-cicd:latest`.

| branch | ships jdk11 | jar class | runs under patch | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 18.1 | yes | 53 | jdk11 (11.0.4) | fails before, all 5 verify after |
| 20.0 | yes | 52 | jdk11 (11.0.13) | all 5 verify |
| 21.0 | yes | 52 | jdk11 | all 5 verify |
| 22.2 | no | 52 | java 8 | all 5 verify |
| 23.2 | no | 52 | java 8 | all 5 verify |
| 24.0 | no | 52 | java 8 | all 5 verify |

On 20.0 I confirmed the resolved interpreter is the in-tree `prebuilts/jdk/jdk11/linux-x86/bin/java` reporting 11.0.13, rather than a silent fallback to the container's 1.8.0_504.

18.1 before the change:

```
ERROR: signature mismatch for FDroid
  expected: 43238d512c1e5eb2d6569f4a3afbf5523418b82e0a3ed1552770abb9a9c9ccab
  got:      <none, unsigned or tampered>
vendor/partner_gms/vendorsetup.sh: line 1641: pop_var_context: head of shell_variables not a function context
```

18.1 after the change:

```
verified signature for FDroid
verified signature for FDroidPrivilegedExtension
verified signature for GmsCore
verified signature for FakeStore
verified signature for GsfProxy
```

All runs use master's current version codes (v0.3.18.252432).

On `line 1641` in that error: it is a line in 18.1's `build/envsetup.sh`, which is 1646 lines and calls `source_vendorsetup` at 1641. `vendorsetup.sh` is 131 lines. `pop_var_context` is what bash prints when a script sourced from inside a function exits under `set -e`, so the line number points at the caller rather than at the failing command.

I also checked the jar across releases, to confirm 18.1 is the only outlier:

| `prebuilts/sdk` tag | class version |
|---|---|
| android-11.0.0_r48 | 53 |
| android-12.1.0_r27 through android-16.0.0_r2 | 52 |

## What has not been tested

None of these are full builds; each exercises the `vendorsetup.sh` path on its own, with the branch's real `envsetup.sh` and jar but a sparse checkout rather than a synced tree. A real build on 18.1, and on one branch that newly uses jdk11 (20.0 or 21.0), would be worth having before this is trusted.

## Relationship to #118 and #119

#119 reverts the signature checking because it broke 18.1. If this fix holds up in a real build, #108 could be addressed without that revert. I have no view on the ordering; happy for this to wait behind the revert, be rebased onto it, or be closed if you would rather keep the checking out for now.

author: danielgoldbergtamu
body:
Closes #1794

## What this changes

`AuthorizationModule.forRoot` (`libs/common/nest/auth`) ran `console.log('Auth', config)` whenever `LOGGING` was set. That config includes the Auth0 management client secret, so the secret went into the log of any API started with logging on. Today that means `gisday-nest`, the one app that imports this module.

- **The new `authConfigForLog(config)`** returns every field except the secret, which it reports only as `set` or `not set`. Domain, audience, issuer and client id still appear, since they're what a person reading the log needs to confirm the settings.
- **`forRoot` logs that instead**, still only when `LOGGING` is set.

**One step outside the repository, for the maintainer.** The issue's "Done when" asks that any server that ran with `LOGGING` set have its management secret rotated. This PR can't tell whether production ever did, so that check stays open.

## Release notes

- [ ] Entry added to `docs/releases/unreleased.md`, with screenshots
- [x] Not user-visible (tests, CI, internal docs), so no entry needed

## How it was verified

- **Red first** (`a46132184`, then `b89dc3c84`, which switched the spec to Vitest's `vi`, the runner this library uses): against the unfixed module, two tests failed for the stated reason:
  - "never logs the management client secret": `expected '["Auth",{"jwt":{"audience":"https://m…' not to contain 'made-up-secret-do-not-log'`.
  - "still logs what is not secret, and whether a secret was given": no `clientSecret … set` in the output.
- "logs nothing without LOGGING" passed before the fix and after it, as it should. All values in the spec are made up.
- **Bug-fix check** (`scripts/check-in-volume.sh fix/1794-auth-config-not-logged common-nest-auth,gisday-nest`): **exit 0**, every step including `npm audit signatures`.

author: elmochilyas
body:
# Phase 44 — Operational Data Collection Center & Focused H15 Research

## 1. Summary of Deliverables

### A. Historical Discontinuity Investigation & Reconciliation Audit
- Located at `docs/phase44/historical_discontinuity_audit.md`.
- Reconciles the historical discontinuity discrepancy: the 66,464 EURUSD M1 dataset contains exactly **13 physical timestamp gaps** (9 weekend closures $\ge 48$h, 2 intraday micro-gaps of 60s, and 2 historical collection pauses) partitioning the series into **14 continuous segments**.
- Resolves the earlier authorial confusion where aggregated H1 hourly bars (~1,096 bars) were conflated with segment count.

### B. Corrected Historical Collection Coordinator
- Located at `src/iqoption_research/market_data/collection_engine.py`.
- **False Completion Prevention**: Explicit outcome states (`COMPLETED_VERIFIED`, `PARTIALLY_COLLECTED`, `CANCELLED`, `INTERRUPTED`, `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`, `FAILED`, `UNVERIFIED`). Missing data never marked completed.
- **Scheduled Weekend Closures**: Differentiates known interbank Forex closures (Friday 22:00 UTC to Sunday 22:00 UTC) from unexplained data gaps.
- **Durable Resumption**: Checkpoints track cursor at every batch boundary; resumes reconcile storage and cryptographic receipts before proceeding under explicit operator authorization.
- **Production Client Authorization Gate**: Client inspected for `assert_read_only()` and forbidden execution methods (`buy`, `sell`, `order`, etc.).
- **Authentic Broker Provenance**: Validates symbol, active ID, chronological order, non-zero prices, valid OHLC envelope, and broker receipt signatures.

### C. CLI Collection Workflow
- Located at `src/iqoption_research/cli/commands/collect_cmd.py` and `data_cmd.py`.
- Subcommands: `plan`, `run`, `status`, `cancel`, `resume`, `verify`.
- Supports `--json` output and standardized exit codes (0 for success/verified/planned, 1 for failure, 2 for cancelled/interrupted).

### D. Desktop Collection Center Workstation
- Located at `src/iqoption_research/desktop/collection_center_panel.py` and mounted in `src/iqoption_research/desktop/app.py`.
- Saved account selector from Windows Credential Vault.
- Instrument classification (Regular Forex vs OTC 24/7).
- Dual UTC & Casablanca local time (`Africa/Casablanca`, UTC+1) synchronized display.
- One-click range presets (30, 90, 180, 365 days).
- Real-time metrics grid and thread-safe background collection.
- One-click snapshot preparation and verification.

### E. Protected Data Preflight & Holdout Quarantine
- Located at `src/iqoption_research/ml/preflight.py` and integrated into `experiment_matrix.py`.
- Replaces implicit array slicing with cryptographic SHA-256 content verification and strict fail-closed boundary checking (`timestamp < 1794498000`, 2026-11-12 10:00 UTC).

### F. Focused H15 Research Engine V4
- Located at `src/iqoption_research/ml/h15_research_v4.py` and `src/iqoption_research/ml/walk_forward_v3.py`.
- Enforces model family sample sufficiency constraint: `min_samples = max(2500, n_features * 50)`.
- Enforces strictly proportional 15-bar purging and 5-bar embargo across chronological splits (Train $\to$ Purge/Embargo $\to$ Calibrate $\to$ Purge/Embargo $\to$ Validate).
- Methodological comparisons: M1 LogReg, V3 LogReg, Isotonic vs Raw, Majority Baseline, 15-Bar Momentum, 15-Bar Mean Reversion.
- 10,000-replicate day-block bootstrap confidence intervals and matched baseline superiority tests.

### G. Comprehensive Acceptance Tests & Operator Manual
- 24 unit and integration tests passing offline covering coordinator, CLI, preflight, H15 V4, audit, and e2e collection lifecycle.
- Complete operator manual in `docs/phase44/operator_manual.md`.

---

## 2. Safety Invariants
- `NO_DEMONSTRATED_EDGE` strictly maintained.
- `execution_authority = "NONE"`.
- Zero live/demo orders, zero wallet mutations.
- Offline test execution with no unauthenticated broker calls.

author: andyrewlee
body:
## Stack

Merge bottom-up. Base: #46 (`context`). The OAuth and OpenAPI work (#83, #87, #88) follows as a second stack on this core.

1. #79 tool calls on the session log
2. #80 code mode
3. #81 vaults and credentials
4. #82 MCP servers, admission plan, tool registry
5. 👉 #84 approvals and client tools, pause inside the turn
6. #121 durable script pauses
7. #122 dashboard: tool calls and answers
8. #123 dashboard: vaults, servers and tools

---

This PR is part of the rebuilt tools stack. After six review rounds found about 70 bugs, the stack was redesigned around three rules:

- **Pi owns execution state.** Waiting calls are Pi's own parked tasks; nothing mirrors them.
- **Pi's task id is the identity of a call.** Public ids are `tu_<task id>`.
- **A pause stays inside the turn.**

Code mode is the main tool surface.

## Summary

Tool approvals and client-executed (custom) tools. The pause stays inside the turn, and Pi owns the waiting calls.

- **Policy:** agent `tools: [{ type: "mcp_toolset", ... }]` with `always_allow | always_ask`, stored with the agent version and copied into the admission plan.
  - With no policy, a tool the server marks `readOnlyHint` runs and everything else asks; an explicit `always_ask` wins.
  - `evaluated_permission` goes on the use event.
- **Custom tools:** `tools: [{ type: "custom", name, description, input_schema }]`.
  - The tool parks with its arguments as Pi validated them, and `agent.custom_tool_use` carries the full arguments under its own 64 KiB limit. A call over the limit fails back to the model before parking.
  - Only calls that actually parked become requests. An `input_schema` with a `$ref` the harness can't resolve is refused at agent write.
- **Pi owns the waiting calls:**
  - A `beforeTool` gate parks the call and memos its arguments, and custom tools park themselves. Pending calls are read with `harness.inspect()`.
  - Answers are delivered with `harness.signal(taskId)`, and aborts are scoped to one run with `abortTask(run.taskId)`.
  - No waiting-call tables.
- **Domain:**
  - **Pausing:** a running turn tracks its awaiting calls. `PauseTurn` ends the segment's model request with its usage, then goes `session.status_idle` with `requires_action` and the waiting `event_ids`.
  - **One aggregate per waiting call:** `ToolConfirmation`, keyed by Pi task id. One decision creates the pending call and publishes its use event together, so a use is never visible before it can be answered.
  - **Continuing:** the last answer continues the same turn (`turn.continued`), and the turn settles once. Segments run as `<session>:turn:N:seg:k` under #111's single deadline, and a waiting turn has none.
  - **While waiting:** interrupt or archive ends the turn, and a user message gets 409.
- **API:** `user.tool_confirmation` and `user.custom_tool_result`, with typed SDK receipts. Answering a call that isn't waiting gets 409.
- **CLI:** prints a shell-quoted answer command.

## Proof rules

**Amended, as agreed:**
- `HostedViewsMatchAggregates` and `SessionViewMatchesSession`: a waiting turn shows `idle`, and turns are counted by the highest number.
- `EveryTurnSettles`: every turn settles or waits on a person.

**Added:**
- Liveness rules `APausedTurnGoesOnOnceAnswered` and `AnInterruptEndsAPausedTurn`.
- 21 rules in Sessions and 22 in Checkfu.

**Stricter:** the agent rules now also compare `tools`.

**Known limit:** the verifier's exploration never reaches a waiting turn, because only the harness can start a pause. The amended view rules are therefore checked only on turns that aren't waiting. Waiting behaviour is covered by the liveness rules and the domain stories.

## Verification

- Each slice was built and verified on its own: typecheck, generate:check, format, lint; the SDK, API, local-Worker and dashboard suites; and the domain suite with every proof.
- The assembled stack was re-checked commit by commit for #79–#81, all green. The run was stopped there to push, so CI is the per-commit check for the rest.
- Proofs at the top, run alone: Sessions 182 s (limit 600), Checkfu 225 s (limit 300).
- `persisted:check` is red only because no baseline has been cut, as on main.
- Not deployed to Cloudflare; Worker behaviour verified under local workerd.
- The dashboard has not been clicked through in a running stack yet.

author: itaigree
body:
## Why

Pelephone's DNS answers "no such name" (NXDOMAIN) for the share service on `*.workers.dev`, while Google's DNS finds it. That was confirmed on the owner's phone: with Chrome set to Google's DNS the address opens, with Pelephone's it doesn't. So for anyone on Pelephone, a share never reached the service and a short link never opened.

## What changes

- **Firestore as the store.** Shared results now go to Google Cloud Firestore (`firestore.googleapis.com`, Tel Aviv region `me-west1`). The page talks to it directly through the REST API, with the project's public web key.
- **`site/js/providers/share-store.js`:** one store with two backends.
  - Firestore when `config.firestore` is set, from the repository variables `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` and `FIREBASE_API_KEY`, which the deploy writes into `config.js`.
  - Otherwise the Cloudflare share service, as before. Until the variables are set, nothing changes.
  - A share is a document `shares/<id>` with three fields: `v`, `data` (the snapshot's JSON) and `expireAt`. Once past `expireAt` it reads as gone, because TTL deletes late.
- **`firestore.rules`:**
  - anyone can get a share by its id
  - a share can be created once, with exactly those fields and limits: `v` an int, `data` a string of at most 65536, `expireAt` within 31 days
  - no list, update or delete

  Checked in the Firestore emulator, 38 of 38 cases. That includes a trap: a chained time comparison loads without error and then refuses every write.
- **The share check and the failure reports** work with either backend. Only the Cloudflare service keeps a log.
- **The deploy log** says where shared results go.
- **README:** the Firebase setup step by step, including on a phone, plus the TTL policy, which needs the Blaze plan.
- **Privacy page:** results are stored with Google in Tel Aviv, and there's no technical log.

## Still open

Automatic deletion after 30 days: a TTL policy needs billing (the Blaze plan), at about $0.01 per 100,000 deletes. The other option is a daily GitHub job that deletes expired shares using a service account. Until one of them is in place, expired shares are hidden by the app but stay stored. The owner is choosing.

## Tests

- Unit: 167 pass, including the store with a fake `fetch`: URLs, bodies, 404, a share past `expireAt`, errors.
- Browser: 98 pass, 1 skipped as usual (the real-Google test). They run against a Firestore mock that answers as the rules do:
  - a short link is stored and opened with no search
  - sharing it on keeps the same id
  - a share past its time reads as gone
  - the share check goes through Firestore

author: miasf
body:
第2段階の前半（積分の読み取り・図の生成・近似）。数値計算そのもの（#109 #110 #111 #112 #113 #159）は 2b として別にする。

## 変更

### 計算エンジン（`core/src/equation.rs`）
- **#114**: 行のどこかに ∧・∨・¬ があると行全体を論理式として描いていたため、`∬_{\{(x,y)\mid …\land…\}}` が「条件には…」で失敗していた（値の計算 `eval_constant` は正しかった）。`@intset(…)` の中の論理記号は、行の描き方を決めるときに数えない

### 画面（`web/src/lib/latex.ts`・`App.svelte`）
- **#193**: 途中の端を 6 桁に丸めていた → 有効数字 12 桁（指数表記は使わない）
- **#195**: 近似は `\int` だけだった → `\intop`・`\smallint` も
- **#197**: 累次積分の内側を括弧で囲む `(∫_0^x y dy) dx`・`\left(…\right)` も、内側の積分として読む
- **#179**: 上下の端が逆（`∫_1^0`）の近似図は、小さいほうから大きいほうまで描き、説明に「符号を逆」と出す。端が文字なら min・max。端が等しければ値 0・図なし
- **#190**: 定義の行を変えたとき、途中までの値と近似の値も計算し直す（パラメータを変えたときと同じ）。関数が別の関数を呼ぶ場合も伝わる
- **#196**: 進み具合の変数を `1\ge x\ge 0` の逆向き、`0\le x, x\le 1` の片側ずつの書き方からも見つける
- **#199・#207**: `x_1`・`t_1` は名前として扱い、座標の x・積分の変数 t とみなさない
- **#130・#207**: `( -y\,dx + x\,dy )` の普通の括弧も `\left( … \right)` と同じく外す（値と図の両方）。`(x+1)\,dx` のような普通の括弧は外さない
- **#178**: 近似の中身の値を、字句の置き換えではなく `\left. f \right|_{t = p}`（点での値）で作る。中の `\sum_{t=1}^3` の t や `t_1` を壊さない。Σ の添字は式に出てこない名前にする
- **#194・#207**: 積分の変数と同じ名前が端や外側の積分にあるとき（`∫_0^x x^2 dx`・`∫_0^1∫_0^x x\,dx\,dx`）、中身の変数を付け替える。`∫_0^x x^2 dx` は `∫_0^x t^2 dt` と同じ扱いになる
- **#207**: z 軸に平行な線（`(0,0,t)`）の帯は、基準を e_x にする（e_z だと垂直な向きが決まらず、図が空になっていた）

## 確認

- `npm test` 全部成功、`svelte-check` エラー 0、`cargo test --release --no-fail-fast` 全部成功
- `latex.test.ts` に Issue ごとのテストを追加。修正前のコードでは失敗する（途中で例外になる所も含む）
- `notation.rs` に #114 のテスト（∧・∨・¬ の値と、画面と同じ入口で描けること。∧ はコンマで書いたものと同じ平面）
- Playwright（Chromium）で、画面の値と図:
  - #114: 半円 π/2 = 1.5708、離れた 2 つの円 2π、環 3π が表示される（修正前は「条件には…」）
  - #130: 普通の括弧・`\left(` とも 2π、逆向きは −2π
  - #178: k=j=m=p=q=10 でシンプソン則 50.5（修正前 43.5）、`∫_0^1 Σ_{t=1}^3 t dt` の近似 6、`t_1=2` の `∫_0^1 t_1 t dt` の近似 1
  - #179: `∫_1^0 t^2 dt` の近似図はシンプソン則で 14,205 三角形（正の向きと同じ）、値 −0.333333。`∫_1^1` は 0 で図なし
  - #190: `f(t)=t` → `2t` で途中の値・近似・正確な値が 0.5 → 1。`g(t)=t`・`f(t)=g(t)` の g を変えても同じ。修正前は 0.5 のまま
  - #193: 進み具合 50% で途中までの積分 2×10⁻⁷
  - #195・#199: `\intop` の近似 0.333333、`x_1=2` の `∫_0^{x_1} t^2 dt` の図と近似 2.66667
  - #207: 縦の線 `(0,0,t)`・`(0,0,−t)`・`(0,0,2t)` の帯が 48,046 三角形（修正前 0）。らせんの帯は 289 ms（修正前 266 ms。ほかの曲線の式は変えていない）。同じ名前の累次積分は、内側を y にした式と同じ図

## 見つけた別の問題（このPRでは直していない）

- `\oint_C -y\,dx + x\,dy + dz` のように**係数のない** `dz` は、括弧の有無に関係なく第3項が正しく読めない（`1\,dz` なら正しい）
- `k=j=m=p=q=10` と `\int_0^1(k+j+m+p+q+t)\,dt` の行の平面の高さが 18 になる（積分の値の表示は 50.5）。修正前から同じ
- `cargo test` の `notation::powers_of_function_calls` が、ときどき失敗する（今回は全部成功。並列のテストが定義の置き場所を共有しているためかもしれない）

body:
## Summary

When two apps define a model with the same name, `er --format dbml`, `d2`, `plantuml` and `dot` drew every relation to that name to the app that was scanned first. #223 fixed this for Mermaid only (#234). With `basket.Line`, `order.Line`, `order.Refund.line = ForeignKey(Line)` and `checkout.Receipt.line = ForeignKey("order.Line")`:

```
before:  Ref: checkout.Receipt.line > basket.Line.id [delete: cascade]
         Ref: order.Refund.line > basket.Line.id [delete: cascade]
after:   Ref: checkout.Receipt.line > order.Line.id [delete: cascade]
         Ref: order.Refund.line > order.Line.id [delete: cascade]
```

A `ForeignKey('self')` on `order.Line` pointed at `basket.Line` too.

`_collect_edges` in `er_formats.py` used a "first definition wins" map from model name to `app.Model`. It now uses the rule Mermaid uses: the app named in the reference, else the field's own app, else the first app that defines the name, and `self` is the model itself. To keep one copy of that rule, I moved Mermaid's local `target_app()` from `cli.py` into `models.py` as `related_model_app()`, and both builders call it. Mermaid output is unchanged, and diagrams without duplicate model names are unchanged in every format.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking, restores expected behaviour)

## Test plan

- New `SameNameModelEdgesAllFormatsTest` in `tests/test_er_formats.py` builds the case above (plus a bare FK inside `basket` and a `self` FK) and checks the edges in DBML, D2, PlantUML and DOT. All four tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- The Mermaid tests from #234 still pass.
- `cd cli && python -m pytest -q`: 1362 passed, 6 skipped.
- `ruff check orm_lens tests` and `mypy orm_lens` are clean.

body:
## Summary

Spec #151, "Know how every key is typed": every Keystroke of a Run is recorded in its Flight log, shown on the Debrief, folded into a saved Logbook, and read back on Analytics as the Journey.

```text
Run ──strike──▶ Keystroke ──▶ Flight log ──▶ runReport ──▶ Debrief      (#152 #153 #154)
                                  └─foldRun─▶ Logbook ──▶ journeyReport ─▶ Analytics
                                              (Run summaries 56 days,        sentence, totals, timeline  (#155 #156)
                                               lifetime, Sectors, keys)      Sector entries              (#157)
                                                                             keyboard in time, key story (#158 #159)
                                                                             Mix-ups, Shift hand, pairs  (#160)
src/analytics/   # new module beside the curriculum (ADR-0004); Biome limits its imports
```

- Debrief: one plain sentence, the Run's text shaded by time with Misses underlined, a keyboard with lists, linked hover/pin, four strips (speed, accuracy, Rhythm, Streak).
- Analytics: Journey sentence, totals row, 8-week timeline with Sector bands and days away, a keyboard that turns back in time, one key's story, Mix-ups with causes, Shift hand, Letter pairs, and a logbook of Sector entries. The old heatmap, hand balance and "Struggling reaches" are gone.
- `SAVE_VERSION` 5 → 8 (#155 → 6, #157 → 7, #159 → 8). No migration code: an older Save is discarded, an older Backup refused.
- `docs/PHILOSOPHY.md`: P10 gains the fade sentence; the Known departures row for Analytics is updated.

## Evidence

- `pnpm check`: typecheck, Biome, 1338 tests green. The `src/analytics/**` Biome import rule was proved on a scratch file.
- Real-Chromium play-checks by separate agents after #153, #154, #156, #157, #158 and #159, then a whole-app walk (five real Runs from a fresh Save, a seeded 8-week Save, a returning player, Wipe Stars, Factory Reset, Backup round-trip). Defects found were fixed on this branch; numbers were spot-checked against the Save data.
- `pnpm verify` on the final tip: `check` and 24 of 25 browser tests pass. `cosmetics.local.spec.ts:366` fails in the full parallel run and passes alone; it fails the same way on `main` on this machine (CI doesn't run the local suite). Screenshots step: 3 of 3.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way for players' data: a player's existing Save is discarded on first load (v5 → v8), and older Backups are refused. The code itself reverts with `git revert`.

**Blast Radius:** Save, Debrief, Analytics, Backup/Wipe/Reset. Game rules (scoring, Stars, unlocks, timing) are unchanged.

Merging to `main` deploys to production.

## For the owner

- You still need to look at both screens (the last box of #160).

- **Words:** on screen the Sector summaries are "entries" under "Your logbook", not "chapters" (GLOSSARY avoids "chapter").
- **Decisions the spec left open:**

  - The trickiest key needs a 10-try "now" reading.
  - Mix-up causes also include "shift" and "same hand"; Space pairs are left out of Letter pairs.
  - Keys first typed in a Free Flight are never credited to a Sector entry.

## Summary

#33 asked to measure the packed tarball against `PACKAGE_LIMITS`. Measured on main, two of the three limits were close: the total size at 91%, and `dist/scene/builder.js.map` at 97% of the single-file limit, so the next change to `builder.ts` would likely fail `package:check`. `src/` is not published, so the maps only worked by inlining every source. The owner decided to stop shipping source maps.

| | Before (main) | After | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Files | 243 | 163 | 400 |
| Unpacked bytes | 1,860,622 | 751,420 | 2,097,152 |
| Largest file | `dist/scene/builder.js.map`, 127,670 | `dist/scene/builder.js`, 60,763 | 131,072 |
| `.map` files | many | 0 | must be 0 |

The packed `.tgz` is 208,925 bytes. `PACKAGE_LIMITS` is unchanged.

**Gate/packaging change, approved by the owner in this session** (`changing-gates` § Tool configs):
- **What moved:**
  - **`tsconfig.build.json`:** `sourceMap` goes from true to false, `inlineSourceMap: false` is now explicit, `inlineSources` is removed, and `declarationMap` stays off. One comment states the decision.
  - **`scripts/check-package.mjs`, path rules:** the `dist/` allowlist now accepts only `.d.ts|.js|.json`. A new `FORBIDDEN_PATHS` entry (`/\.map$/i`) gives `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_FORBIDDEN` with the fix ("keep `sourceMap`, `inlineSourceMap` and `declarationMap` off…"). It is listed last, so a map under `src/` or `tests/` is still reported as that hazard.
  - **`scripts/check-package.mjs`, removed checks:** the map-content checks, which can no longer decide anything because any map now fails first, are removed: `findAbsoluteMapSources`, `findDanglingMapSources`, `ERR_PACKAGE_MAP_DANGLING_SOURCE` and `ERR_PACKAGE_MAP_ABSOLUTE_PATH`.
  - **`scripts/smoke-package.mjs`:** the map-leak step and `ERR_SMOKE_MAP_ABSOLUTE_PATH` are removed. They ran after the tarball-contents step, which now throws on any map.
- **Why:** to keep the package comfortably inside its limits without raising them.
- **What newly fails:** any `.map` anywhere in the tarball, in both `package:check` and `package:smoke`.
- **No longer checked:** the contents of shipped maps, since there are none.
- **Unchanged:** `PACKAGE_LIMITS`, the coverage thresholds, and every other rule. No prose doc said the package ships maps.

Closes #33

## Release impact

Release impact: no — the package is unreleased; the published JavaScript and type declarations are unchanged, and only the `.map` files are no longer included. The removed error codes belong to repository scripts, not the published surface.

## Test plan

- `tests/package.test.ts`:
  - `dist/index.js.map`, `.d.ts.map`, a nested map, `.css.map` and an upper-case `.MAP` are each rejected with exactly `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_FORBIDDEN`.
  - Only the map hazard carries a `next` fix.
  - `checkTarballContents` rejects a map.
  - A real `npm pack` with a map added fails `inspectTarball` with `[ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_FORBIDDEN]`.
  - The tests for the removed map-content functions are removed along with them.
- `/code-review medium --fix`: 4 findings.
  - **Fixed, hazard order:** a map under `src/` is now reported as the `src/` hazard.
  - **Fixed, message assertions:** two tests that asserted message wording now assert the routing via `FORBIDDEN_PATHS` instead.
  - **Fixed, embedded maps (pre-existing):** a map embedded in a `.js` file is closed off by setting `inlineSourceMap: false` explicitly.
  - **Fixed, redundant step:** the clean step in the advice is gone.
- `pnpm check`: green (3408 tests, coverage thresholds unchanged, `package:check`, smoke). The packed tarball has 0 `.map` files.

## Checklist

- [x] `pnpm check` passes
- [x] Public API changes include behavior tests, type tests, and the README example (none)
- [x] Docs affected by an observable change are updated

author: otolab
body:
## 概要

Issue 固有の GitHub・記録先の指示を共通 conductor / worker prompt から分離し、issue と workspace の両方で共通 base を使います。workspace worker の再開・復旧時にも Issue を参照しないようにします。

Fixes #824
Part of #821

## 受け入れ条件

- issue conductor / worker は共通 base と ticket モジュールを merge。run conductor は ticket を merge しません。
- run worker の初回 attach は run 用 merge を使い、Issue / PR 正本・GitHub watch を含みません。再開時は既存 ACP session の履歴を読み込み短い再開指示を送り、load 失敗後の復旧では run prompt と復旧指示を新 session に送ります。
- **dispatch の条件と実装の対応:** 常駐 worker の通常 dispatch は attach 済み session に conductor の指示本文を送り、system prompt を再生成しません。したがって「dispatch が run 用 merge を使う」という条件を文字どおり実装したのではなく、attach で run prompt を設定する現行ライフサイクルに沿っています。`buildWorkerPrompt` の run 分岐も検証していますが、現 runtime の dispatch はこの builder を使いません。適切な達成方法か独立レビューをお願いします。
- モジュール構成と merge 順を `docs/modular-prompt.md` に反映。変更前後の issue 出力と run prompt を snapshot で固定しました。

## 意図的な issue snapshot 差分

変更前の全文は `packages/core/src/prompt/testing/baselines/` に保存。共通の役割分担からマージ責務を ticket へ移し、Issue の明確化・Issue とコードの矛盾・Issue への判断報告を共通文と ticket 指示に書き分けました。GitHub 通知の hold と `github.update` の stall より高い優先度、同一復旧 poll の inform の扱いは ticket 側に保持しています。Issue / PR 正本、watch と operator の指示の優先も維持しています。merge 順により objective、terms、GitHub 監視節、worker の gh 助言の位置は変わります。run に gh 助言を含めないため、助言は ticket worker に移しました。

#828 前の履歴で旧 worker builder の Issue 混入を確認済みです。旧時点での snapshot 実行はしていません。

## 検証

- `pnpm build` 成功。
- mock ACP の runtime テストで新規 attach、保存済み session の再開、load 失敗後の新 session 復旧、handoff 確認後の dispatch を確認。通常 dispatch は同じ session に指示本文だけを送ります。mock は provider が session 履歴を永続化・復元すること自体を実証しません。
- workspace attach / dispatch builder、conductor と issue 出力の snapshot、復旧時の参照先をテスト。
- サンドボックス内の `pnpm test:all` は Unix socket の `EPERM` で中断し、制限外で再実行。
- 制限外の `pnpm test:all`: スクリプト 34 件、core 1,700 件が成功（core 1 件 skip）。operator-agent は長時間出力がなく完了前に中断したため、全体成功ではありません。
- 制限外の `pnpm test:integration`: session resume 11 件、worker model reasoning 4 件は成功を確認しましたが、残りが長時間完了せず中断。全体成功ではありません。
- 制限外の `pnpm test:e2e`: 16 件成功、3 件 skip。実 provider・認証済みモデルでの smoke は未実施。

author: oahcom
body:
## What this PR is

**Not a follow-up polish — it brings the #808 implementation up to the ruling.**

#856 (`5c64e560`, merged 2026-11-24T03:19:59Z) shipped the scope narrowing but left three things the Owner ruling (issue #808, comment `7107695221`) requires. This PR fixes all three on the same branch.

## The three defects in #856

### 1. The count was printed only when non-zero

Ruling, verbatim: *"The count must be printed even when N is 0."*

#856 used `if out_of_scope_dm10:` — so a clean increment printed no line at all, and "no stale pins" was indistinguishable from "a build that never looked". Fixed: unconditional print.

### 2. The count had no names, only a total

#856 stored `bound_errors` in the counter. Those strings carry no `rel` — `check_approval_binding` returns `"DM-10 content changed after approved_version: ..."`, and the aggregation loop is what prepends `f"{rel}: "`. So the counter could only print

```
DM-10 out-of-scope stale bindings: 3
```

The ceiling went from 11 named diagnostics to one number. An author reading it learns that debt exists but not whose, and the only way to find out is the whole-tree run this change exists to avoid.

Ruling, verbatim: *"a stale binding in a document outside that set is emitted as a **note**, and the gate prints a counted line (`DM-10 out-of-scope stale bindings: N`)"* — two things joined by `and`.

Fixed: the counter stores `f"{rel}: {err}"`, and the count is followed by one line per document:

```
DM-10 out-of-scope stale bindings: 1
  out-of-scope: 00-governance/b.md: DM-10 content changed after approved_version: ...
```

### 3. The scope test asked the wrong question

```python
if incremental and rel not in all_changed:   # was: rel not in required
```

Switched from `requirable` to `all_changed` because the question DM-10 needs to answer is *"did this increment touch this document"*, not *"is this document something the gate may require metadata on"*.

**Measured, and deliberately not oversold: this fixes no reachable bug.** `changed_paths` (`scripts/check_document_management.py:2075`) defines

```
requirable = names("--diff-filter=AMRTC")
all_changed = names()          # every status, including D
```

The two sets differ only on deletions, and a deleted path is absent from `collect_governed`'s `targets`, so it never reaches the DM-10 call. Every input that reaches that line gets the same answer either way. This is a correctness-of-intent change: `required` is DM-01's notion, and DM-10's boundary should not drift with it.

## Read points (line numbers on this branch)

| Line | Code |
|---|---|
| `scripts/check_document_management.py:1188` | `check_approval_binding` — **not modified**; its staleness judgement is identical |
| `:2153` | `out_of_scope_dm10: list[str] = []` |
| `:2191` | `if incremental and rel not in all_changed:` — the scope branch |
| `:2224` | unconditional `print(f"DM-10 out-of-scope stale bindings: ...")` |
| `:2227-2228` | `for item in out_of_scope_dm10: print(f"  out-of-scope: {item}")` |

`check_approval_binding`'s decision semantics are unchanged. Only *who pays* for its errors changed.

## Tests — 5 cases

`python3 scripts/test_check_document_management.py` → **249/249, rc=0** (baseline before the #808 work: 244).

| Test | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `test_incremental_in_scope_stale_pin_still_fails` (T81) | incremental, A changed by this increment and stale → **must** appear on **stderr**, rc=1. Proves the gate was not switched off. |
| `test_incremental_out_of_scope_stale_pin_is_counted_not_failed` (T82) | incremental, B untouched but stale → rc=0, count line exact, **exactly one** `out-of-scope:` detail naming `b.md`, and **no** `00-governance/b.md:` diagnostic on stderr. |
| `test_whole_tree_run_still_reports_every_stale_pin` (T83) | no flags, B stale → **must** appear on stderr, rc=1. Proves the whole-tree audit was not weakened. |
| `test_incremental_one_in_scope_one_out_of_scope` (T84) | A (changed, stale) + B (untouched, stale) → A on stderr, B **not** on stderr, count exactly `1`, **exactly one** `out-of-scope:` detail naming `b.md`. |
| `test_incremental_zero_out_of_scope_still_prints_the_count` (T85) | clean increment → `DM-10 out-of-scope stale bindings: 0` present, rc=0. |

T82 and T84 assert `len(details) == 1`, not just the total. A total-only assertion would pass an implementation that dumps every stale pin into the counter — which is exactly defect 2.

**Assertions distinguish the two streams.** Errors go to stderr, details to stdout. Merging them (`out + err`) cannot tell "the gate refused" from "the gate informed", because the detail quotes the same DM-10 sentence. T82 asserts `not leaked` on stderr and `len(details) == 1` on stdout separately.

## Mutation self-check — three mutations, each reverted

| Mutation | rc | Red tests |
|---|---|---|
| M1 `if incremental and rel not in all_changed and False:` (revert to unconditional reporting) | 1 | T82, T84 |
| M2 `if incremental:` (never report) | 1 | T81, T84 |
| M3 delete the `out-of-scope:` detail loop, keep the total | 1 | T82, T84 |

M3 is the one that guards defect 2: without it, a total-only implementation would be green.

Note on M2: it only touches the incremental branch, so a whole-tree run still takes the `else` arm and T83 stays green. T81 is the test that proves the gate is not switched off incrementally, and it does go red.

After reverting all three: **rc=0, 249/249**.

## Effect of the unconditional print on the suite

The count line now appears on the stdout of **every** `--require-changed` run, including all PRs' GOV-DOC-002 logs. Verified no test asserts complete stdout equality — `grep -nE "getvalue\(\)\s*==|==\s*captured_(stdout|stderr)\.getvalue"` returns nothing, so every assertion is membership/prefix based and the added line cannot flip a passing test. Full suite confirms: 249/249.

## Gate self-run

`python3 scripts/check_document_management.py --require-changed origin/main` → rc=0, and it now prints `DM-10 out-of-scope stale bindings: 0` on a clean increment.

## Scope

Two files only: `scripts/check_document_management.py` and `scripts/test_check_document_management.py`. No `.gitattributes`, no documents, no workflows.

body:
## 요약

문서가 11월 17일 상태에 머물러 있어 현재 코드와 맞지 않던 부분을 고치고, 자동 검증(CI)과 실제 앱을 브라우저로 모는 verify 스킬을 추가합니다. 앱 코드(`app/src`)는 바꾸지 않았습니다.

## 변경 사항

**1. 문서 갱신** (`docs:`)
- `구현현황.md`를 2026-11-24, `a83941c` 기준으로 다시 작성했습니다. 지금 있는 기능(협업·프로토타입·플러그인·컴포넌트 속성·변수 토큰 등), 실제 파일 수치(VNPL·커뮤니티 템플릿), 우선순위별 미비사항을 정리했습니다.
- `README.md`의 지난 설명("컴포넌트는 다음 단계", "고정 크기 초안")을 고치고 CI 배지를 달았습니다.
- `SPEC.MD`는 날짜별 기록(1.1절)을 그대로 두고 머리말·구현 요약·F-01~F-09 현재 열·M1 진행 상태·마지막 검증 기록만 갱신했습니다. M1은 1·2·3·6번 완료, 5번 부분, **4번(원본 대비 화면 비교) 미완료**로 적었습니다.

**2. CI** (`ci:`) — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `main` push와 PR마다 Ubuntu, Node 24에서 `npm ci` → typecheck → vitest → vite build → `npm audit --audit-level=high`.
- 실제 `.fig`가 필요한 통합 테스트 5개는 `FIGMA_TEST_FILE`이 없어 건너뜁니다.

**3. verify-canvas-studio 스킬** (`feat:`) — `.claude/skills/verify-canvas-studio/`
- playwright-core 1.65.0으로 **설치된 Edge/Chrome**을 띄워(브라우저 다운로드 없음) 열기 버튼·파일 선택 창·실제 다운로드 같은 사용자 경로로 편집기를 몹니다.
- 개발 서버는 포트 5179에 직접 띄우고 자기 PID만 끕니다. 여정마다 새 브라우저 컨텍스트라 사용자의 5173 서버·저장 작업을 건드리지 않습니다.
- 여정: `json-open`, `reload-persist`, `code-zip`, `fig-import`(`VERIFY_FIG_FILE` 필요). `doctor.mjs`(읽기 전용 점검), `cleanup.mjs`(남은 서버만 정리, 증거 보존).
- 기능 지도 4개, JSON 고정 문서. 증거는 `.verify-evidence/`(Git 제외, `.gitignore`에 추가).

author: tylergibbs1
body:
Ports Effect's `effect/workers/SharedMemory` (Effect #10644, carried backlog row in the 2026-11-23 catch-up) as `pyfect.workers.shared_memory`. Additive only, so it can go in a patch release.

## Mapping decision

Effect's module wraps `SharedArrayBuffer`, which only threads of one process can share; a child process gets a copy, so Effect's schema rejects it. In Python the counterpart is `multiprocessing.shared_memory`, and that one works across processes, so pyfect shares with both of its worker platforms:

- **Thread workers** get the `SharedArray` object itself.
- **Process workers**: the message is pickled, and `SharedArray.__reduce__` sends only `(kind, length, segment name)`. The worker maps the segment by name when the message arrives, so its writes land in the parent's memory. The worker maps it with `track=False`, so the worker exiting (or crashing) never frees the parent's segment.
- **Lifetime**: Python has no GC'd shared buffer like a SAB, so `make` is scoped: `Effect[SharedArray[T], SharedMemoryError, Scope]`. The scope frees the segment when it closes, whether it succeeded, failed, died or was interrupted. The creator's segment is tracked by Python's resource tracker, so if that process is SIGKILLed the tracker frees it.
- **Thread safety**: free-threaded CPython counts a buffer's views without a lock (`tests/test_memoryview_ownership.py`). So the array holds one view, made when the array is built, and no view is ever made from it after that: slices read and write one element at a time, and the array does not export a buffer.

## API

```python
from pyfect.workers import shared_memory as sm

class Fill(TypedDict):
    data: sm.SharedArray[int]
    start: int
    stop: int

class Compute(RpcGroup):
    fill = make("Fill", payload=S.Struct(Fill, data=sm.schema(sm.int32)))

@fx.fn
def program():
    data = yield from sm.make(sm.int32, 8)        # freed when the scope closes
    compute = yield from rpc_client.make(Compute)
    yield from fx.for_each([(0, 4), (4, 8)],
        lambda r: compute.fill({"data": data, "start": r[0], "stop": r[1]}),
        concurrency="unbounded")
    print(data.tolist())                          # [0, 2, 4, ..., 14], written by worker processes
```

- `make(kind, length)`, `schema(kind)` (passes through `S.to_codec_json` unchanged; rejects plain arrays, wrong kinds and copies), `is_shared(value)`, `is_available()`, `SharedMemoryError`, `SharedArray[T]` (`len`, index/slice get and set, iteration, `tolist`, `kind`, `name`).
- Kinds: `int8`, `uint8`, `int16`, `uint16`, `int32`, `uint32`, `int64`, `uint64`, `float32`, `float64` (`Kind[int]` / `Kind[float]`).

## Not ported, and why

- `Uint8ClampedArray`: Python's `array`/`memoryview` formats have no clamped kind.
- Effect's browser cross-origin-isolation check (`crossOriginIsolated`): has no counterpart. `is_available()` reports whether `multiprocessing.shared_memory` imports at all (it doesn't on Emscripten and WASI).
- Zero-copy `memoryview(array)` / `numpy.frombuffer(array)`: left out to keep the view-ownership rule above. `tolist()` copies.
- The Effect title "a child process rejects a shared array instead of copying it" holds the opposite way here. It is replaced by "worker processes write into the caller's shared array". Once the Effect pin moves to 4.1.5, that title needs an entry in `tests/_effect_title_omissions.py`; adding it now would fail the guard, since the pinned checkout doesn't have the file.

## Tests

`tests/test_workers_shared_memory.py`, with Effect's titles in the docstrings:
- SharedMemory.test.ts: reports unavailable memory (here, when `multiprocessing.shared_memory` is missing); accepts shared arrays of the requested kind; rejects unshared, wrong-kind and serialized arrays; passes values through the JSON codec untouched.
- RpcServer.test.ts: worker threads write into the caller's shared array; worker processes do too (in place of the rejection test).
- pyfect's own: a segment is freed on success, failure, defect and interrupt, and when its fiber is interrupted from outside; a worker process exiting leaves the parent's segment in place; a process SIGKILLed while holding a segment leaves none behind (its resource tracker frees it); a mapped copy that is dropped is freed; the system refusing a segment gives a `SharedMemoryError`; a negative length is refused. On Linux these check `/dev/shm`; elsewhere they check that the name can no longer be opened.

Types are pinned in `tests/type_checks.py`, variance in `tests/_variance_expected.py`, and the finalizer is listed in `tests/test_weak_tables.py`. `transferable`'s passthrough link moved to `workers/_passthrough.py` so both schemas share it, as Effect's do. There are no user callbacks, so `_call_user` doesn't apply. Added a docs section on the workers page with a process-worker snippet, and `changes/workers-shared-memory.added.md`.
