author: tuntii
body:
ROADMAP December item 2: lay out before hit-testing when a frame is pending, so a batch of mouse events does not hit the previous layout.

## What changes

- `Ui` splits a frame into **layout** (`layout_pending`) and **paint**. `dispatch` calls `layout_pending` before `MouseMove`, `MouseDown` and `Wheel` hit-test, so they hit the tree as it is now.
- `frame` still lays out what is left and then draws. It returns `true` and draws even when the events already did the layout.
- A hover change now only marks a **repaint** (`@paint_pending`), not a layout. Otherwise every hover change inside a batch of mouse moves would cost a full layout before the next event.

## Decisions

- `needs_frame?` keeps its meaning ("something must be drawn"): it is `paint_pending || needs_layout?`. Both window backends and the tests use it, so no public API changes.
- Only mouse events lay out first. Keys go to the focused widget and do not hit-test.
- `focus` and the other `Ui` methods still mark `@root.needs_frame`, as before. Narrowing them to repaint-only is possible, but it isn't needed for this fix.

## Tests

- New `test/hit_layout_test.iyi`: a widget is removed with no frame in between, and the next move and click must reach the widget that moved into its place. It **fails without this change** ("the move hits b where it is now") and passes with it. It also checks that the frame after that still draws, and that hover alone repaints.
- Local, Windows, iyi 0.22.0: `iyi test` 20/20, native smoke + todo selftest, SDL smoke + todo selftest.
- Benchmarks: "100 mouse moves" at 10,000 rows stays at 0.045 ms median, so hover still does not lay out.
- Screenshots (smoke, todo, both backends) are in this PR's CI run, as the `screenshots-<os>` artifacts.

author: the412banner
body:
## Problem
On a Samsung Galaxy S25 (SM-S931U1, Android 17, 0.7.1), the card is set as game storage at `/mnt/media_rw/4A1C-830B` and is mounted for the session. Even so, the Add game picker shows only Internal storage. The card can't be reached, so a game on it can't be added by hand.

The picker built its drive list (`pickVolumes`, `app/src/main/java/com/droiddeck/launcher/ui/ExePickerDialog.kt`) only from `GameStorage.options`. That is `Context.getExternalFilesDirs`, cut back to the volume root. When Android doesn't expose a public volume to apps (no `/storage/<uuid>`, no app-specific folder on it, as with this card and in #633), that list is empty. The file manager and the game-storage "Choose folder…" picker use `StorageRoots.list` instead. That function also reads `/storage`, `/mnt/media_rw` and `/proc/mounts`, which is how this card came out as `/mnt/media_rw/4A1C-830B`. The same `pickVolumes` list labels the card locations in the Sync folder picker.

## Fix
`pickVolumes` now uses `StorageRoots.list`, the same source the file manager uses. It keeps Internal storage first with its existing label and adds every readable volume that isn't internal storage, once each. A card that `getExternalFilesDirs` reports still appears at its `/storage/<uuid>` path, because `StorageRoots` prefers the first browsable path. No strings, settings or call sites change.

## Tests
- New `PickVolumesTest`:
  - a card reachable only through `/mnt/media_rw` is listed;
  - visible cards keep their `/storage` path and label;
  - unreadable volumes and internal-storage duplicates are left out;
  - with no card, only Internal storage is listed;
  - a mounted volume with no app folder reaches the picker through `pickVolumes(context)`.
- `PickListingTest` and the `StorageRoots` tests are unchanged and still cover the code around this change.
- No test device was available, so device verification will come from the tester's build.

Refs #633

author: hiromimie
body:
## 概要

v0.5 の M33 の段 9: FR-706 設定ファイルの自動の再読込 (Could)。07 §6 の RLD-1〜RLD-5、03 §9.5.1 の WATCH-12。

- **見るもの (RLD-1)**: ユーザー層の `config.toml`・`keymap.toml`・テーマファイル (組込みでなければ `themes/` の `*.toml`。`inherits` の親のため)・`languages/*.toml`・`--config` のファイル、ワークスペース層の `.eve/config.toml`・`.eve/keymap.toml`。
  - 置いたディレクトリを `io` のジョブ (`ResolveConfigWatch`) で canonicalize し、非再帰に監視する。
  - 解いた時点で無いディレクトリは見ない。解く時点は、起動・ルートが決まったとき・読み直しの後。
- **ディレクトリの共有**: 文書の監視の表 (`DirWatch`) に設定の印を足し、同じディレクトリの要求は 1 つにした (02 §4.4 の「数え上げは呼び出し側が持つ」)。
  - ディレクトリを外すのは、文書が無く、設定でも見なくなったときだけ。
  - 設定の監視は `file.watch.enabled` だけで決まる。`reload_on_external_change = never` では、文書の監視だけを外す。
- **契機と待ち合わせ (RLD-2)**: 文書の監視と同じ待ち合わせ (100 ms、最長 1 s。`next_deadline`) の後、`config.reload` と同じ手順で読み直す。
  - 自分の保存でも読み直す。
  - 変わった項目が無ければ何も知らせない。
- **誤り (RLD-3)**: 自動のときだけ、読む前と後の (大きさ, mtime) をジョブの中で比べる。変わっていたら当てずに、待ち合わせからやり直す。
  - 対象は、設定ファイル・キーマップ・テーマと継いだ親・`languages/` の並びと各ファイル・ワークスペース層。
  - `reload_kept` は、同じファイルの同じ内容で 1 回だけ出す。
  - 自動では、Undo の上限を下げる変化を効かせない (値と由来を前のままにする)。
- **重なり**: 読み直しの連鎖 (設定・ワークスペース層・テーマ・言語定義) の最中に来た契機は、自動も手動も落とさず、終わった後にもう 1 回読む。手動を先にする。
- **知らせ**: 診断の要約は、自動の連鎖を始める前の一覧と比べ、同じ診断は出し直さない。
  - 当てる前に表示していた警告は置き換えず、履歴に積む。
  - 前の読み直しの警告は、新しい結果で置き換える。
- **止める・縮退 (RLD-4 / RLD-5)**:
  - `file.watch.enabled = false`・`--no-config`・`--no-workspace-config`・監視できない FS (WATCH-2 の知らせは文書と共有して理由ごとに 1 回) に従う。
  - ワークスペース層は §12.3 / §12.5 の分類のまま。
  - 失効した設定だけのディレクトリの張り直しは、5 s の内には繰り返さない。

### 仕様の文言の改訂 (規則の意味は変えない)
- RLD-1 を「解いた時点で無いディレクトリは見ない」に改めた。
- RLD-1 に、テーマは `themes/` の `*.toml` を見ることを書いた。
- RLD-3 を「待ち合わせからやり直す」に改めた。
- 07 §5.2 の `file.watch.enabled` に「(文書の監視。設定ファイルの監視には効かない)」を補った。
- 段 9 の実装の細目を 07 §6 と §12.6.3 に書いた。

### レビュー
別のレビュー担当が差分を読み、6 件を指摘した。全部直した。
- 中 1 件: テーマ・言語定義・`.eve/keymap.toml` の診断の要約が、読み直しのたびに出直す。
- 軽 5 件: RLD-3 の本文、Undo の由来、`Lost` の繰り返し、手動の重なり、試験の穴。

同じ種類の穴は、診断の要約と警告のメッセージを出す呼び出し元をすべて洗って塞いだ。`.editorconfig` の読み直しの警告が上書きしていた穴も、ここで見つけて直した。

## 関連する仕様・Issue

- 07 §6 (RLD-1〜RLD-5)、07 §5.2、03 §9.5.1 (WATCH-12)、01 §5.5 の FR-706 AC-1 / AC-2
- 08 §2.6 の M33 の段 9

## 種別

- [x] feat
- [ ] fix
- [ ] spec (docs)
- [ ] chore
- [ ] spike

## チェックリスト (docs/09-testing-quality.md §8.4、docs/11-dev-workflow.md §4)

- [x] コミットに `Signed-off-by:` がある (`git commit -s`)
- [x] 変更した関数に `spec:` (節 ID) がある
- [x] 変更した Must 要件の AC に `verifies:` (AC ID) を持つテストがある (FR-706 は Could。AC-FR-706-1 / AC-2 の試験を `crates/eve-core/tests/config_auto_reload.rs` に 37 件)
- [x] ユーザーから見える挙動の変更で、シナリオテスト (v0.1 は `Harness`) を追加・更新した
- [x] core に端末や OS の概念を入れていない。OS への依存は Port の中だけにある
- [x] 文書の変更が Transaction を通っている (文書は変えない)
- [x] `unwrap` / `expect` に理由がある。外部入力でパニックしない
- [x] ログ・パニック・クラッシュログに、文書の本文・パスの全体・API キーを出していない
- [x] `unsafe` を足した場合は `// SAFETY:` と不変条件がある (足していない)
- [x] UI スレッドで I/O や全文走査をしていない (解き直し・stamp・読込はすべて `io` のジョブ)
- [x] `eve-view` を触っていない
- [x] 仕様と異なる判断をした場合、docs を直接直さず OQ の起票案を下に書いた (規則の意味は変えず、文言の明確化だけ)

## 依存を追加した場合 (docs/02-architecture.md §13.0、docs/05-platform.md §17.2)

- [x] 追加していない

## 確かめたこと

- `cargo fmt --all`、`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`。
- `cargo test -p eve-config -p eve-core -p eve-testkit -p eve-tui -p eve-host -p evoeditor` (171 の試験の実行ファイル)。
- WSL (Linux) で `config_auto_reload`・`file_watch`・`config_reload`・`workspace_config`・`editorconfig`・`language`。
- `cargo xtask spec-index --check`・`trace` (警告 0)・`check-docs`。
- 主のセッションで `config_auto_reload` (37)・`config_reload`・`editorconfig`・`file_watch`・`workspace_config` を走らせ直した。

## 補足 (残る懸念)

- 起動時の解き直しのジョブが、起動時のファイルを開くジョブより前の `io` に積まれる。`--config` が応答しないネットワークの共有の上にあると、開くのが遅れ得る。
- 張り直しを控えた (5 s の内に失効が続いた) ディレクトリは、次の読み直しまで監視しない。
- 知らせが続いて読み直しが続く間は、連鎖の前の一覧で比べ続ける。その間に一度消えて同じ内容で戻った診断は、もう一度は出ない。
- 自動で効かせなかった Undo の上限の変化は、利用者に知らせない (文言キーを足していない)。

author: beauwilliams
body:
## What

Vendors agent-cli-kit `v1.1.0-rc.3` (`51ca7dc`) and conforms to its RFC-4.

- **`describe`** declares each command's arguments, `env`, `config`, `log` and `stdin`. A test walks the argument parser's definitions and fails when they and `describe` differ.
- **Reports** carry `next_action_argv`, `fix_argv` and, on `not-run`, `error_kind`. `error` is one line. After a usage error the next action is `garita describe`.
- **A check's output** is on its entry in `checks` (`output_tail`, `output`, and garita's own `output_notable`). A failed command's finding message is one sentence.
- **stderr is empty** on every command: a usage error with or without a command, and a panic in any command, are `not-run` reports.
- **Hooks are format 2.** With `garita` missing from PATH a hook prints a `not-run` report and exits 2. Format 1 is still recognised, so `garita hooks install` upgrades it and `doctor` reports it as outdated.
- **`doctor`** no longer gives a next action that needs a shell redirection.
- **CI** runs the kit's conformance runner (`scripts/conform.sh`) at the commit in `tests/contract/VERSION`; `result` needs it.
- **Records** cite agent-cli-kit RFC-4 for the above and keep `output_notable` under garita's extended contract.

## Verified

Locally: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy with warnings denied, 393 tests, `scripts/contract-check.sh` (18 examples), `scripts/conform.sh` (pass, exit 0) and `urzua check`.

* **New Features**

author: happyseaurchin
body:
David asked (24 November 2026): *"Is there an interface that asks me for a word so it generates the right URL link to a private room?"*, then *"Go with all the recommendations."*

## What changes

In a game's open room, `<beach-here>`'s **A room for friends** used to make up a random six-letter word and go. Now it asks for one:
- **An easy word is offered:** two words and a number, e.g. `amber-heron-42`. The player can keep it or type their own.
- **The word is taken as said:** lower-cased, spaces become hyphens, and other characters are dropped, so `Friday Night!` becomes `friday-night`.
- **The link is shown as the word is typed**, e.g. `Friends join by this link: https://happyseaurchin.com/fotronic?with=friday-night`.
- **Go to that room** (or Enter) opens it. In a hosted game this navigates the top page, which the frames already allow on a tap.

It is a plain input and button, not a `<form>`, because a hosted game's page carries `form-action 'none'`. In a room reached by link, the button still shares that room's link, as before.

## Proof

- `scripts/smoke-room.cjs` gains two checks:
  - in the open room, the button offers an easy word and shows its link;
  - `Friday Night!` typed becomes `?with=friday-night`, and going there puts the page in `pool:wire:friday-night`.
- **44 checks**, all hold.
- Seen inside Fotronic's waiting room (with the plug swapped in): it wears the game's own font and colours.

No handler, salt, shape gate or wire shape is touched. `button/README.md` is updated to match.

author: ahmednuw1-lab
body:
The internet sign stayed green ("connected") with no internet.

**Why:** it trusted Android's "validated" flag. Many car boxes switch Android's own check off, so every network looks validated. After losing the network it also read the active network inside `onLost`, which can still return the network just lost.

**Fix:** CarHome checks the internet itself (an empty HTTP 204 answer, the same check Android makes, with a spare host), through the network in use, only while the sign is on screen: every 30 s, every 10 s while there is a problem.

**States:** connected (green) · phone hotspot / mobile data (blue) · slow (amber) · checking (pulsing) · sign-in or top-up page (purple, tap opens it) · no internet (red) · not connected / Wi-Fi off (grey).

- `ACCESS_WIFI_STATE` (normal, no prompt) for "Wi-Fi off"; plain HTTP allowed only for the two check hosts; privacy policy updated (EN + AR).
- 13 new unit tests; all tests pass in CI.
- Emulator shots in `carhome-shots-40`: in the "no internet" shot Android still marked the network `IS_VALIDATED`, and the sign correctly shows red.

Merging this to `main` publishes 1.3.3 (versionCode 19).

author: jeremydw
body:
Comprehensive backwards-compatible modernization of `@blinkk/degu`:

### 1. Security Fixes
- **`src/dom/dom.ts` (`addStylesToPage`)**: replaced `insertAdjacentHTML` with `document.createElement('style')` + `textContent` to prevent HTML/script injection via `</style>` breakout.
- **`src/dom/text-split2.ts`**: replaced `innerHTML` assignments with `textContent` + `\u00A0` to prevent XSS.
- **`src/dom/url-params.ts`**: blocked `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype` keys in `asObject()` (prototype pollution), safe `decodeURIComponent`, and switched `isTrue`/`getValue` to `URLSearchParams`.
- **`src/components/youtube-inline.ts`**: use `encodeURIComponent(location.origin)` instead of unencoded `location.href` (avoids leaking full path/query/tokens).
- **`src/ui/youtube-modal/youtube-modal.ts` & `src/components/youtube-modal.ts`**: `encodeURIComponent` on `videoId` and `startTime`.
- **`src/dom/pjax.ts`**: use `DOMParser().parseFromString()` instead of detached `innerHTML`.

### 2. Toolchain & Dependency Cleanup (39 → 20 `devDependencies`)
- Replaced `ava` + `ts-node` + `browser-env` + `nyc` + `@web/test-runner` + `@open-wc/testing` + `@types/mocha` with **Vitest 3** + `@vitest/coverage-v8` + `happy-dom` (all 24 test suites / 138 tests passing in <1s).
- Replaced stubbed `echo lint` / broken `gts` ESLint+Prettier with **Biome** (all 174 files formatted & lint-clean in 24ms).
- Upgraded `typescript@5.7`, `tsup@8`, `vite@6`, `typedoc@0.27`, `lit@3`, `sass@1.85`.
- Removed `fast-glob`, `js-beautify`, `concurrently`, `npm-run-all`, `esm`, `intersection-observer`, `pixi.js`, `angular` runtime devDeps, `.babelrc`, `_ava/`, `_typedoc_theme/`, and stale `yarn.lock`.

### 3. Bugs, Typos & README Badges
- Fixed `tsup.config.ts` typo (`'dat.ui'` → `'dat.gui'`), added `@github/details-dialog-element` to externals/optional peerDeps, excluded test files from published `lib/`.
- Fixed `package.json` `exports['.']` condition order (`types` before `default`).
- Fixed `dom-watcher.ts` `MediaQueryList` guard, `video.ts` `disconnectedCallback` `this.raf` guard, and `datguif.ts` error message & typing.
- Replaced dead `david-dm.org`, broken `snyk`, and unused `codecov` badges in `README.md` with working npm, GitHub Actions, and MIT badges; cleaned up `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### 4. Modernized CI & Release Automation
- Updated `test.yml` (Node 20 & 22 matrix, `npm ci`, build + typecheck + lint + coverage + examples) and `docs.yml` (GitHub Pages deploy).
- Modernized `release-please.yml` with `release-please-config.json` + `.release-please-manifest.json`, fixed `package-name: '@blinkk/degu'` (was `test-release-please`), and configured npm OIDC Trusted Publishing (`id-token: write`, `npm publish --provenance --access public`, plus `workflow_dispatch` manual publish).

author: madmax983
body:
## Summary

This is a **documentation-only** change, not a performance fix — no source code in `src/` is touched. It commits a new profiling harness and four kept callgrind/dhat logs for a finding from this round's Bolt (performance agent) pass.

- Profiled v2.40's new plain-array subscript assignment (`UPDATE t SET tags[k] = v`, `src/exec/funcs.rs::eval_array_subscript_assign`) — never profiled since v2.40 added the array function surface.
- New harness `benches/profile_array_subscript.py` (self-contained callgrind/dhat driver, same pattern as `benches/profile_jsonb_subscript.py`): a bulk UPDATE assigning one in-bounds element of an int[] column across many rows, each holding a *distinct* array, diffed against a `SET id=id` control with the same INSERT to isolate the subscript-assign-specific cost.
- **The cost is real** (11.35% of the workload's `Ir`, 12.95%/11.46% of its dhat blocks/bytes, scaling with array size) and the mechanism is concrete: in the common "subscript already in-bounds" case, the function rebuilds a second `elems` Vec and re-clones every element via a coordinate remap that's provably the identity, instead of writing the one changed element in place on the array it already cloned.
- **No fix ships**: a fast-path patch that skips the redundant rebuild measured -2.74% Ir / -2.77% allocations **against the full benchmark total** — below the impact floor's 5%/10% thresholds, because ~97% of both counters is generic per-row UPDATE machinery (parse/encode/WAL/pgstat) shared with the control and untouched by this change. Reverted.

Full writeup with profile tables, the reverted patch's own before/after numbers, and reproduction commands: #89

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build` succeeds
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` clean
- [x] `cargo test --all-features`: 1495/1495 pass (no `.rs` files touched by this PR — the fix was reverted; `git diff --stat` against `main` shows only `benches/`)
- [x] New harness verified: callgrind/dhat runs reproduce the numbers quoted in #89

author: nandaisnanda
body:
Fixes #179.

## Bug

`Sel_BW.search()` accepts seven MGWR options that it did not store in `search_params`: `init_multi`, `tol_multi`, `rss_score`, `max_iter_multi`, `multi_bw_min`, `multi_bw_max` and `bws_same_times`. `MGWRResults.spatial_variability()` replays searches with `temp_sel.search(**search_params)`, so each replay used the defaults for these options and ignored the user's settings.

Here is the Georgia data with `multi_bw_min=[60]`, `multi_bw_max=[150]`, `tol_multi=1e-4`, `max_iter_multi=50`, `rss_score=True` and `bws_same_times=3`. Bandwidths are ordered `[intercept, fb, black, rural]`.

| Search | Bandwidths |
| --- | --- |
| Original | `[92, 101, 116, 149]` |
| Replay before this PR | `[101, 101, 117, 157]` |

The replay matches the default result in `test_MGWR_AICc`, and its `rural` bandwidth exceeds the requested maximum of 150.

## Change

`search()` now stores the seven options in `search_params`. This PR leaves `spatial_variability` unchanged; #172 tracks the changes to that method.

I left out two arguments:

- `pool`: `spatial_variability` deep-copies the selector, and Python raises `NotImplementedError` when you deep-copy a pool. The argument is also deprecated and unused.
- `verbose`: it controls printing at runtime and does not affect the search result.

## Test

`test_MGWR_search_params_records_multi_options` runs a search with non-default values for six of the options and checks that:

- `search_params` holds each value, plus the `init_multi` key (left at its default)
- `search_params` omits `pool` and `verbose`
- `search(**selector.search_params)` reproduces the same bandwidths

The test fails on `main` and passes with this change. The full suite passes locally (58 tests, Python 3.15.1 on Windows). I also added a CHANGELOG entry.

## pre-commit

`ruff format` passes. `ruff check` reports 164 errors on an untouched `main` and the same 164 with this change, so I committed with `SKIP=ruff-check` and did not fix unrelated lint here.

author: cursor[bot]
body: ## Description These tests are expected to fail until the vulnerability is fixed. They do not change production code. `git_checkout` runs an unrestricted `git checkout`, and the git server image runs `git lfs install --system`, which enables LFS smudge and process filters for every repository. A branch can commit `.gitattributes` and `.lfsconfig` so checkout requests that LFS URL from the server. The tests install the same system filters, point `.lfsconfig` at a local listener, and fail when `git_checkout` contacts it. The image test fails while the Dockerfile still runs `git lfs install`. Checked the other git tools against the same repository. They did not contact the URL: `git_status`, `git_diff_unstaged`, `git_diff_staged`, `git_diff`, `git_add`, `git_commit`, `git_reset`, `git_log`, `git_create_branch`, `git_show`, and `git_branch`. ## How to run `git-lfs` must be on `PATH`. The published image installs Debian bookworm's `git-lfs` package and enables it with `git lfs install --system`. ```bash cd src/git uv sync --frozen --all-extras --dev uv run pytest tests/test_lfs_checkout_ssrf.py ``` ## Server Details - Server: git - Changes to: tests only ## Motivation and Context Locks in the behavior that checkout must not request a Git LFS URL taken from the revision being checked out, including when system LFS filters are installed. ## How Has This Been Tested? author: phongguy
body:
The second half of the metrics work. `/metrics` now also covers git traffic and pushes:

- `potluck_git_requests_total{service, outcome}`: every git request that reaches the engine (advertise, upload-pack, receive-pack), counted once as ok, busy, overran or failed.
- `potluck_git_slot_wait_seconds`: how long each request waited for a git slot, whether or not it got one.
- `potluck_pushes_total{outcome}`: accepted and refused pushes.
- `potluck_push_refusals_total{code, rule, kind}`: which rule refused a push, with the workspace kind. Past 128 distinct rules, new ones record as `other`.

How the refusals reach the server: for each receive-pack the engine creates a report file under `<data>/tmp/hook-reports/` and passes its path to git as `POTLUCK_HOOK_REPORT`. On a refusal the pre-receive hook overwrites that file with `<code> <rule>` lines (never creating it, ignoring any write failure; the message the client sees is unchanged). After git exits the server reads at most 8 KiB of it, parses at most 64 lines of known shape, deletes the file and hands the result to the push observer. Each start empties the directory. The file holds only refusal codes and rule names, never a path, ref, matched value or token. A refused push whose report is lost counts as neither refused nor accepted.

The README's metrics section lists the four new families.

Deviations from the plan:
- `acquire` now takes the git service; `advertise` and `rpc` wrap the old bodies so each request is counted in one place.
- The report parser's dead-code allowance stayed until the last task rather than the fourth, since its accessors had no caller before then.
- Both broad dead-code allowances are gone. `SignInMethod::Oidc` keeps a narrow `#[expect(dead_code)]` until the OIDC sign-in route records sign-ins; the expectation makes clippy fail the moment that variant is constructed, so it cannot outlive its reason.

Tests: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -Dwarnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass locally (169 lib, 715 integration, 6 other, 0 failed). The new end-to-end test pushes a clean commit and a commit carrying a `.env` to a server on 127.0.0.1 and checks the git, push and refusal counts on `/metrics`, and that no token, slug, user or file content leaks into the output. No podman check; nothing here touches the container.

Closes #228

author: thorwhalen
body:
Fixes #43
Fixes #44

**#43, `install_bundled`.** `source_dir` is now resolved (`expanduser().resolve()`) before linking, so a relative source (`install_bundled("data", ...)`) links to the real folder instead of writing a relative, dangling target. A dangling link at an asset's name (its target gone, e.g. a removed virtual environment) is replaced without `force`: it holds nothing that could be lost. Sibling sweep: `skill.install._create_link` raised `FileExistsError` on the same dangling-link case and now replaces it too; its sources are already absolute (`install_from_dir` resolves, `install()` uses the store path), so the relative-path half does not apply there. `uninstall` is unchanged.

**#44, the setuptools recipe.** An explicit `[tool.setuptools] packages` list turns package discovery off, so every subpackage was left out of the wheel; `[tool.setuptools.packages.find]` plus a `package-dir` mapping does not work either (setuptools ignores a mapped package that discovery does not find, so the skills are dropped instead; checked with a real build). `pyproject.toml` alone cannot do both, so the setuptools recipe is now a `setup.py` that keeps `find_packages(...)` and adds `<pkg>._skills`:

- `wheel_skills_snippet(pkg, backend="setuptools")` prints that `setup.py`; `wheel_skills_config(pkg, backend="setuptools")` now raises `ValueError` pointing at it (the dict it returned produced broken wheels). The existing test that asserted the old dict is updated accordingly.
- `check_wheel_skills` now fails when a subpackage of the repository (a tracked folder with `__init__.py`, flat or `src/` layout) is missing from the wheel; a `tests`/`test` subpackage is only a warning, since leaving it out is often deliberate.
- `skill-enable/SKILL.md` shows the new recipe and explains why the TOML-only form fails.
- New tests build a setuptools wheel with a subpackage through the sdist (as a release does) and check it, build one with the old recipe and confirm the check now fails, and strip subpackages from a hatch wheel.

Full suite with doctests: 380 passed, 1 skipped locally.

body:
<!-- factory -->

<!-- factory:information {"id":"de3d469a-ebc0-40e9-8a6a-81af3fb3903b","type":"pull-request","subject":"irasutoya-tools/irasutoya","key":"implement:81bef239-6a2f-4fd7-921b-ea46a20f6fa6@86ec70ee75f8a467@2026-11-24T00:45:49.756Z@345fba48:pull-request#0","derivedFrom":["81bef239-6a2f-4fd7-921b-ea46a20f6fa6"],"createdAt":"2026-11-24T05:47:51.411Z","data":{"title":"fix: reuse a refreshed feed count when a stale random selection retries","branch":"factory/implement-a7c083f3","base":"master"}} -->

## Problem

`Irasuto.random` retries a missing random selection by forcing a full count refresh (`load_refreshed_random_post`). If the retry happened to arrive after another caller's refresh had already completed (not while it was in flight), the old code still ignored the now-fresh cached count and kicked off a brand new, redundant `fetch_feed_count` refresh.

## Changes

- `random_entry` now returns `[entry, count]` so callers can remember which count snapshot they used to pick their index.
- `feed_count` now takes that `stale_count` instead of a boolean `refresh` flag. It still joins an in-flight refresh exactly as before. When no refresh is in flight, it reuses the cached count directly if that count is valid and different from `stale_count` (meaning someone else already refreshed it), and only registers a new refresh when the cache still holds the same stale value.
- `random` and `load_refreshed_random_post` were updated to thread the count snapshot through the retry path.
- Updated `sig/irasutoya/irasuto.rbs` signatures to match.

## Tests

Added a new spec in `spec/irasutoya/random_feed_count_spec.rb` that starts four concurrent `Irasuto.random` calls sharing a stale cached count of 10. Their empty "selected" responses are released one at a time (mirroring the issue's reproduction, where each lookup's empty response arrives only after the previous lookup has fully finished). The test asserts that exactly one count refresh request happens, and that the remaining three callers reuse the refreshed count and still resolve to the same post successfully.

I manually traced the existing specs (`spec/irasutoya/irasuto_spec.rb` and `spec/irasutoya/random_feed_count_spec.rb`) against the new code path to confirm they still pass, including the scenarios where a retry's cached count is still stale (so a refresh is correctly triggered) and the deadline-sharing/timeout specs (unaffected, since the interrupt/deadline code path itself is unchanged).

I could not run `bundle exec rspec` or `bundle exec rubocop` in this environment (no shell access), so these results are from careful manual code review rather than an actual CI run; the repo's own CI will execute both.

Closes https://github.com/irasutoya-tools/irasutoya/issues/771

author: rick7c2
body:
## Summary

- Keep serving large GETs in subranges when the catalogue is frozen. The parent looks up the requested range's extents once and checks each full ciphertext length with a metadata-only R2 HEAD, trying the cache and then the safety tier. If neither has a requested extent, or the plan exceeds a parent or child subrequest budget, it returns `503 ServiceUnavailable` with `Retry-After: 30` before any object headers or bytes.
- Frozen children also try the cache and safety tier without cold fills, read stamps, or hit-counter writes. This preserves the existing frozen non-fan-out behavior for a valid safety copy after cache eviction. Unfrozen GETs are unchanged.

## Cost and limits

- A 9 GiB request with 16 MiB extents and 1 GiB children uses 576 cache HEADs and nine child requests, plus one range query and the existing authentication and generation lookups. An 8 MiB extent layout uses 1,152 cache HEADs. The parent budgets up to two HEADs per extent if safety is needed, children, and the 1,024-retry reserve inside the existing 9,500-call envelope. It rejects an oversized plan before loading extent rows when even the minimum extent count from the enforced 16 MiB upload bound cannot fit. There is no catalogue call per extent.
- The parent counts extent overlaps separately for each child, including pieces that straddle a boundary. It reserves up to six calls per overlapping extent: HEAD and GET in both R2 tiers and one possible repeat of each GET if a produced piece was taken back when a client stalled.
- At four concurrent probes, the 576-HEAD cache-hit case has about 144 rounds of probe latency. At an illustrative 50 ms per HEAD, that adds about 7.2 s before headers (14.4 s for 1,152 extents), plus catalogue and scheduling time. Safety fallback adds a second HEAD for each cache miss. This is an estimate, not a deployed R2 latency measurement.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`
- `cargo test --locked -p velmora -p velmora-bridge`
- `cargo clippy --locked -p velmora-s3-proto -p velmora-bridge --all-targets --features velmora-bridge/testkit -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check --locked -p velmora-bridge -p velmora-s3-proto --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`
- `cargo clippy --locked -p velmora-bridge -p velmora-s3-proto --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy --locked -p velmora-s3-bridge --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings` and the CI Worker bundle build and strip check

## Risk and rollback

The new path is scoped to `CATALOG_BACKEND=d1-frozen` or `pg-frozen`, with the parent's existing fan-out setting still governing when to split. The shipped default remains `d1`. No schema, auth, token-format, or storage-format changes. Revert this PR to restore the previous frozen single-invocation behavior and its CPU limit.

HEAD verifies presence and length; it does not pin an R2 object or authenticate its contents. Fresh adaptive evictions have to claim an extent in the catalogue before deleting, so the frozen adapter blocks that claim. R2 lifecycle expiry, an administrative/out-of-band deletion, or an eviction already past its claim can still remove a local copy after HEAD. A frozen child fails closed without writes if neither tier can serve the extent; if bytes have already been sent, the stream aborts rather than completing.

## Attestation

risk_tier: T0

### Claims
- C1: A warm frozen GET returns all requested bytes through fan-out.
- C2: A frozen parent returns `503` and `Retry-After: 30` for an unavailable extent or a parent or child plan over budget, with no object body and no writes. A plan that cannot fit using the minimum extent count makes no extent query.
- C3: A frozen child uses an available local copy without writes and refuses a miss in both tiers.

### Tests
- C1 | test=crates/velmora-bridge/tests/fanout.rs::frozen_warm_get_fans_out_and_returns_the_full_body | failed_before=yes | proof=The original handler returned 200 with a single stream instead of a fan-out plan.
- C1 | test=crates/velmora-bridge/tests/fanout.rs::frozen_parent_accepts_safety_and_checks_only_requested_extents | failed_before=yes | proof=The initial change refused a safety-only extent with status 503 instead of returning a fan-out plan.
- C2 | test=crates/velmora-bridge/tests/fanout.rs::frozen_parent_refuses_a_cold_extent_in_the_last_subrange | failed_before=no | proof=The original single-stream guard already refused a missing final extent; this preserves the refusal after fan-out is restored.
- C2 | test=crates/velmora-bridge/tests/fanout.rs::frozen_parent_refuses_an_over_budget_plan_before_probing | failed_before=yes | proof=The original handler returned 200 rather than refusing an over-budget parent plan with 503.
- C2 | test=crates/velmora-bridge/tests/fanout.rs::frozen_parent_refuses_when_only_a_child_exceeds_its_budget | failed_before=yes | proof=The initial change returned 206 for an under-budget parent whose unaligned first child exceeds its own budget.
- C2 | test=crates/velmora-bridge/tests/fanout.rs::frozen_parent_refuses_a_huge_range_before_looking_up_extents | failed_before=yes | proof=The initial change tried to load extents and returned 500 against the metadata-only large-object fixture; it now returns 503 using only the normal metadata queries.
- C3 | test=crates/velmora-bridge/tests/fanout.rs::frozen_child_uses_safety_or_refuses_without_writes_after_parent_preflight | failed_before=yes | proof=The initial change returned 503 after cache eviction even though the safety copy still existed.

### High-risk checklist
- [x] The parent uses only read-only catalogue and R2 metadata calls; each child still authenticates the pieces before serving them.
- [x] Existing auth, generation pinning, grants, and unfrozen retry behavior are unchanged.
- [x] Parent and child R2 calls are budgeted; over-budget plans are refused before probing.
- [x] The frozen test doubles reject and count catalogue and blob write attempts, including write queries.
- [x] The existing catalogue opt-in remains off as shipped. General and Opus security reviews apply before merge.

author: yandalur
body:
Instructions in a packet read their sources before any write in the same packet, so a reader can leave the packet when the writer stays:

  { r2 = add(r4,r5)      // writes r2
    r6 = sub(r2,r7) }    // reads the old r2

The global scheduler rejected pullup of the sub instruction. It is now allowed.

It stays rejected when the write is forwarded, because the reader then sees the new value:

  { v2.cur = vmem(r0+#0) // forwards the loaded value
    v6 = vadd(v2,v7) }   // reads the new v2

The rules are in HexagonInstrInfo::isSafeInBundleWAR. The new -enable-def-use-same-packet=false option turns the relaxation off.

Two related fixes:
- Stall check: compare the adjusted latency (HexagonSubtarget::updateLatency), as the machine scheduler does.
- Fall-through moves: do not move a predicated instruction above the definition of its predicate in the previous block:

  bb.0: { p0 = cmp.eq(r0,#0) }
  bb.1: { if (p0) r3 = r2 }   // must stay in bb.1

isDotCurInst now recognizes every .cur load form, so none is taken for a safe write.

body:
## Scope

FE-53 S2, first internal slice. Add a canonical annual coverage result and adapt settled nominal entries to the shared annual sheet model. The coverage separates settled years, the first failed year and its localized cause, and subsequent uncomputed years. The strict projection API still fails atomically and retains its existing failure shape.

The sheet exposes provider-supplied person facts, account postings, debts and held property for supported years. Opening and closing use explicit CPI clocks, with an inflation bridge in real mode. Stable IDs and original contribution source distinguish a scheduled posting from voluntary funding even when their IDs overlap.

The results page still uses the shipped S1 projection. This slice has no FIRE/estate conclusion for the canonical path. Retirement pricing and integration are later S2/S3 work.

## Verification

- 975 Vitest tests and production build passed.
- Independently hand-calculated household fixture covers both currency modes, prior-close carry, rollback, strict compatibility, source provenance, blocked and uncomputed cells, and scheduled contribution source collisions in RRSP and FHSA.
- Thorium smoke test at 390px covered EN/FR/ZH messages on the isolated selector-to-dialog path.
- Independent viewer approved the final change, including wrapper ordering, strict results and clipped spousal contributions.

author: russianhub
body: ## 改动摘要 旁译更新清单在 Cloudflare R2 配齐之后，把安装包上传到公网直链，再用这条直链作为 `latest.json` 的主下载地址。GitHub Release 保留为 `mirrors` 兜底。官网主下载按钮继续指向清单里的 `url`；清单里出现与主链不同的 HTTPS 备用地址时，才显示「备用下载」。SHA256、大小和版本仍显示在按钮下方。 `dist/latest.json` 里的线上签名数据没有改。本 PR 不包含安装包，也不碰 `pangyi` 仓库的 Release 或标签。 ## R2 何时生效，失败时怎么退回 - **四个 Secret 都没配**：行为和现在一样。`url` 仍是 GitHub Release 直链，`mirrors` 为 `[]`。日志和 Job Summary 会说明这一点，每小时定时任务不会因此变红。 - **四个 Secret 都配齐**：除了版本变化或手动 `force`，只要当前 `latest.json` 的 `url` 还不是 `${下载基址}/` 开头，也会重新同步。这样填完 Secret 后，不必等下一个版本，就能把已经发布的 `v4.19.0` 切到 R2。 - 上传使用 `aws s3 cp`，对象键是 `pangyi-${TAG}.exe`，带上 Cloudflare R2 的 endpoint、`application/octet-stream`，以及避免 AWS CLI v2 默认 CRC 头被 R2 拒绝的四个环境变量。 - 上传之后先对公网地址做 `curl -fsI`。必须返回 HTTP 200，且 `Content-Length` 与本地安装包字节数一致，才会生成并提交 `latest.json`。直链不可达或大小不一致时，不改线上清单。 - **只配了 1～3 个 Secret**：任务失败，并列出缺失的 Secret 名称。日志不打印任何 Secret 的值。 手动 Run workflow 增加了布尔输入 `force`，默认 `false`。 ## 需要你手动配置的步骤 仓库里没有任何 Account ID、密钥或 Bucket 名称。请在 Cloudflare 和 GitHub 上自己填写。 ### Cloudflare R2 1. 创建一个存放旁译安装包的 R2 Bucket。 2. 给这个 Bucket 打开公网读取，并把自定义域名指到 `https://download.eyuxq.com`（不要末尾斜杠）。对象需要能被匿名 HEAD/GET，并且响应里带 `Content-Length`。 3. 创建一把仅限该 Bucket 对象读写的 R2 API Token，记下 Access Key ID 和 Secret Access Key。 4. 在 Cloudflare 控制台记下 Account ID。 ### GitHub 仓库 `russianhub/opensource-sites` Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions： **Secrets（四个都填，或四个都不填）** - `R2_ACCOUNT_ID` - `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID` - `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` - `R2_BUCKET` 签名仍使用已有的 `PANGYI_SIGN_KEY`。本 PR 不新增、不轮换这把私钥。 **Variables（可选）** - `PANGYI_DOWNLOAD_BASE`：公网下载基址。留空时使用 `https://download.eyuxq.com`，脚本会去掉末尾斜杠。必须是 `https://`。 配齐后，到 Actions 里手动运行 **Sync pangyi update manifest**，把 `force` 设为 true。这样会把当前最新正式版切到 R2，而不用等下一次发版。公网校验失败时，线上 `latest.json` 仍指向 GitHub Release。 ## 官网文案 「完全离线」这枚短标签保留。它已经有英文 Fully offline、俄文 Полностью офлайн，指的是输入法本体。 原来的页面没有说明更新程序会联网，所以在 SmartScreen 说明前面加了一句：输入法本体完全离线、不联网；更新提醒由独立更新程序完成，只查询版本清单，可在设置中关闭。英文和俄文使用整句翻译。当前线上清单的 `mirrors` 仍是空数组，所以「备用下载」保持隐藏，现有布局不变。 ## 假设 - `pangyi` 的正式版 tag 形如 `v4.19.0`。安装包文件名是 `pangyi-${TAG}.exe`，和清单里的 `pangyi-v${version}.exe` 一致。 - R2 自定义域名在校验时已经能对刚上传的对象返回 200 和正确的 `Content-Length`。HEAD 会重试几次，避免刚写入还不可见；最终仍失败则不改清单。 - 不在 workflow 里创建 Bucket、绑定域名或修改 Bucket 权限。这些只能在 Cloudflare 控制台完成。 - 手动运行清单脚本且不传 `DOWNLOAD_BASE` 时，脚本默认仍是原来的 `https://eyuxq.com/download`。定时 workflow 总会显式传入下载基址。 - 清单测试单独放在 `Test pangyi manifest` workflow。它不和 Pages 部署共用 `concurrency: pages`，避免 Pull Request 把正在进行的 Pages 部署取消掉。 ## 验证边界 已在本机跑通： - `python3 .github/scripts/test_pangyi_make_manifest.py`：清单的 `url`、`mirrors`、`sha256`、`size`、最多 8 行 `notes`、ed25519 签名；篡改 version、sha256 或 size 后验签失败；未设置 `MIRROR_URL` 时 `mirrors` 为 `[]`。R2 全空、部分配置、已切到 R2 的同步判断也在这里。测试用的密钥只在临时目录生成。workflow 做了 YAML 解析、`bash -n`，以及内嵌 Python 的语法检查。 - 网站现有检查：`check-russian-hub.cjs`、`audit-site.cjs`、`build-resource-directory.cjs --check`、`sync-resource-icons.cjs --check`，以及 `check-pangyi-dl.cjs`。 - 用本地页面核对了中文、英文、俄文和手机宽度。线上 `latest.json` 下，主按钮指向现有 GitHub Release 直链，备用链接隐藏。另用一份只存在于本机的清单确认：主按钮会指向 `https://download.eyuxq.com/pangyi-v4.19.0.exe`，并出现 GitHub Release 备用链接。 没有连接你的 Cloudflare R2 账号，没有实际上传安装包。`check-design.cjs` 和 `check-v3.cjs` 在改动前就已因旧版页面结构失败，它们不在 Pages 部署的检查列表里。

author: shinjuku-staition
body:
Updates the shinjuku entry to plugin commit 86cb9fef135a4011e56a287d7ea47b20bd22a17d (plugin version 0.2.0, was 0.1.1
at db1ced6). The commit range db1ced6..86cb9fe changes the plugin's own files only (README.md, launch.mjs, mcp.json,
plugin.json, skills/wallet/SKILL.md).

Plugin change:
(1) The plugin starts the Shinjuku wallet that the user installs (the npm package shinjuku) as `shinjuku mcp`
(`shinjuku.cmd mcp` on Windows), found in npm's global folders. mcp.json names no wallet version, and
the plugin never installs, downloads or updates the wallet: the launcher reads only npm's own global folders (the
user's own first, never PATH), the user's npm settings file (~/.npmrc, or the file npm_config_userconfig names) and package.json files, and makes no network connection. When the command is not
installed, the launcher answers as a small MCP server with one read-only tool (setup_wallet_first) that gives the user
the install lines. A new wallet release therefore needs no new catalog PR.
(1b) On Linux and macOS, when the wallet is found in a folder that is not npm's usual one for a plain install (for
example ~/.local), a plain update line could update another copy. Hermes does not read an MCP server's initialize
instructions, so the launcher puts the update lines for that folder at the start of one tool description in the
wallet's tools/list answer, and only in the answer to a tools/list request that Hermes sent. It checks that the new
answer is the same as the wallet's except for that one description, and passes every other byte unchanged. A folder
name that is not a plain path is never written.
(1c) skills/wallet/SKILL.md carries the wallet's own rules for an agent (the same text as the wallet's instructions to
any MCP host), since Hermes does not read those instructions.
(2) known_issues gets one line: install the wallet first (npm install -g shinjuku, then shinjuku setup), then reload the wallet in Hermes (/reload-mcp).
(3) The disclosure names the wallet as "the Shinjuku wallet the user installs (npm shinjuku), not covered by the
pinned sha", with no version number.

Disclosure changes for the current wallet (0.3.269, the stable version):
(4) the ask line now says it by rule: Hermes asks before every wallet call except the read-only ones (searches,
receipts, balance reads and the wallet's other read-only status reads), so a tool a later wallet adds is covered;
(5) Tor: on Windows and Linux x64 the wallet no longer downloads Tor from torproject.org; it runs Tor from the files
in its npm package, each checked by its pinned sha256.
(6) Paid AI: besides api.usepod.ai over Tor, the wallet's Lyber models send the prompt to Shinjuku's AI address (its
.onion, only with Tor on). Shinjuku's server asks Lyber with one Shinjuku key, so Shinjuku's server and Lyber read the
prompt; the wallet pays each answer privately.
Every other line of the disclosure is unchanged (the payment service pay.shinjukustaition.com or its .onion and its
per-payment fee; a balance read moves USDC the user added into the private balance; the keys stay in the wallet's
folder).

Precedent for (1): the listed entry canonry (sha d70ff15cc8c2e5dd342cfd1f2d8785a7addb67e0, plugins/canonry/mcp.json)
starts `canonry-mcp` from PATH with no version, and its known_issues says to install the Canonry runtime first. Rule 2
pins the plugin commit, and this entry keeps that pin; rule 3 holds, as the plugin has no updater of any kind.

author: wynandt
body:
Part of #114. #114 stays open.

## What changes

A window that started, or tried to turn the lock setting on, while another gliff window held `DisableLockWorkstation` stayed `Disabled` for the rest of its life. *Send Win+L to this machine* kept saying "another gliff window holds the Windows lock setting" after that window had exited cleanly.

- `lock_policy::State::Disabled` now carries why: `Blocked::Owner` (another client's live marker, at start or found by a turn-on) or `Blocked::Failed` (a registry error or an incomplete marker).
- `LockPolicy::recheck` runs the existing `recover` again under the mutex, at most once per `RECHECK_MS` (1 s), only for `Blocked::Owner`. Owner gone (clean exit or crash) goes to `Idle`, so the next wish for On writes the setting. Owner alive stays blocked.
- `LockGate::recheck` looks only while the gate is open and the wish is On. `Grab::apply_lock` calls it before a turn-on (focus gain, the switch), and `Grab::tick` drives it while the window has the keyboard. One log line when the window takes over. `Grab::win_l_unusable` is unchanged: the menu message clears because `is_disabled()` becomes false.
- Registry errors (`Blocked::Failed`) are still not retried. That is a separate choice.
- Docs first: `docs/settings.md`, `docs/windows-quirks.md`, `docs/state-machines.md`.

## Proof

Regression tests in `lock_policy/tests.rs`: `a_window_refused_at_start_takes_the_setting_once_the_holder_has_gone`, `a_turn_on_that_finds_another_window_holding_takes_it_once_that_window_has_gone`, `a_crashed_holder_is_recovered_on_the_next_look`, `a_live_holder_is_looked_at_again_at_most_once_a_second`, `a_registry_failure_is_not_looked_at_again`, `a_closed_gate_or_a_wish_for_off_does_not_look`.

Against main's behavior (main plus a `recheck` stub that never looks, which is what main does):

```
test lock_policy::tests::a_crashed_holder_is_recovered_on_the_next_look ... FAILED
test lock_policy::tests::a_live_holder_is_looked_at_again_at_most_once_a_second ... FAILED

  left: None

test result: FAILED. 47 passed; 4 failed
```

With this change:

```
test result: ok. 51 passed; 0 failed (lock_policy)
```

author: dirvine
body:
## Cause Under plain `cargo test`, `started_failure_and_authorization_failure_flush_logs_before_exit` shares one process with sibling tests that hit the same `error!` callsites with no subscriber. tracing-core 0.1.36 caches callsite interest for the whole process. While only one dispatcher is registered (`has_just_one`), a new callsite's interest comes from `dispatcher::get_default` on the thread that registers it (`callsite.rs` `Rebuilder::JustOne`). A sibling thread with no subscriber gets `Interest::never`, and the test's `with_default` subscriber then never sees the event. The flushed text is empty or is missing the expected line. ## Fix For the duration of the test, keep a second registered dispatcher alive: a fmt layer writing to `io::sink`, never set as anyone's default. With two live dispatchers, every interest rebuild reads the registered dispatcher list and gets `always`. A thread with no subscriber can no longer turn the callsites off. Events still go to each thread's own default, so the extra dispatcher receives nothing, and the only effect on other tests is that interest is not cached as `never` while it lives. `rebuild_interest_cache()` after installing the subscriber was considered. It is not enough because a sibling can still register the callsite after the rebuild and cache `never` again. ## Evidence (macOS, `cargo test --lib upgrade::apply::shutdown_flush_regressions`) - With the fix reverted: 2 of 3 runs FAILED with `exit preceded the failure log flush:` and empty or partial text. - With the fix: 10/10 green on the original base and 10/10 green after merging current main. - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean. Test-only, no production change; the daemon uses one global logger. Assertions are unchanged. Closes #2200 Written by ZCode (GLM), reviewed by Claude Opus 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Confidence Score: 5/5

The test-only change appears safe to merge.

Summary

Keeps a second `tracing::Dispatch` alive during the log-flush regression test. - The shutdown-flush test keeps failure logs available when sibling tests have no subscriber. No actionable issues found. Tests were not run during this review. author: noahhendrickson
body:
TestFlight build 202611232310 crashed on every launch. The phone's crash logs show a Hermes exception thrown from a Reanimated worklet on the UI runtime (called from a display link), which aborts a Release build.

The cause is `beadRingPath(progress, stretch = STRETCH)` from #418. The worklets plugin compiles it to `function beadRingPath(progress, stretch = STRETCH) { const [STRETCH, …] = this.__closure; … }`, so the default runs before `STRETCH` is unpacked from the closure and throws `ReferenceError: STRETCH is not defined`. The animated ring omitted `stretch` and hit it on its first frame. The still frame passes `0`, so it never did, and the Node unit tests run the plain function, where the default works.

The fix makes `stretch` a required argument. `BEAD_RING_STRETCH` is exported and the animated ring passes it, so the function has no default left for the bug to come back through. The drawing is unchanged.

To keep the bug from coming back anywhere else, a new fork lint rule, `t3code/no-worklet-default-params`, sits next to `no-hermes-unsupported-apis` and runs on `apps/mobile/src/**` and `apps/mobile/fork/**`. It flags a default value anywhere in a `"worklet"` function's parameters, destructured ones included. It reports the original `beadRing.ts` and is clean across the app now. The rule is registered under the manifest entry `no3y-worklet-default-params`, with fenced edits in `oxlint-plugin-t3code/index.ts` and `vite.config.ts`.

TestFlight build 202611240048 ships the first revision of this fix (8f61b546ae). The second revision doesn't change runtime behaviour.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 1 round with GPT-6.2 Sol on the first revision. Sol verdict: approved

author: technicianofthesacred
body:
**Not tested on a real card.** No VERSION bump; parked for the next card update. No partition-table change.

## Why
Two unexplained abnormal resets left only a reset reason: 2026-11-23, software panic (reason 4) right after a six-look `/api/config` save on 1.2.6; 2026-11-24, task watchdog (reason 6) after 7.57 hours on signed 1.2.5. Both came back in warm-white recovery with nothing to investigate.

## What the card now keeps
After a panic, a task or interrupt watchdog reset, or a brownout, the last three records are stored in NVS:
- reset reason, the boot count of the start-up that crashed, and its up-time;
- free memory and lowest free memory, sampled once a second;
- the path of the last request, how long before the crash it came, whether a project save was in progress, and the current pattern;
- from the panic hook: task name, fault name, core, program address and up to 16 call-trace addresses;
- the firmware version and build number, so the addresses can be decoded against the right build.

A brownout does not pass through a panic, so that record has running state and no trace. Losing power before the restart wipes the breadcrumb and leaves the reason only.

## How
- `LightweaverCrashRecord.h`: pure data and arithmetic, run on a host by `tests/crash-record.cpp`.
- `LightweaverCrashRecorder.cpp`: breadcrumb in RTC no-init memory; `-Wl,--wrap=esp_panic_handler` routes every panic through an IRAM hook that copies the evidence and always hands over to the system handler; start-up stores the record before anything else in `setup()`.
- Reports: `crash` summary on `/api/status` and `/api/firmware-info`, `capabilities.crashLog = 1`, read-only `GET /api/crash-log`.
- Only a request path is ever noted: no query string, header or body, so no credential can reach a record.

## Core dump (surveyed, not changed)
The partition table already reserves 64 KiB for a core dump and the prebuilt core already has core dump to flash enabled, yet the bench found the area empty after the panic. Why is not established. `/api/crash-log` reports whether a dump is present and its size, so the next crash answers that. Anything that needs a partition change is left for a decision.

## Measured
- Card compile succeeds. Against unmodified main: flash +6,136 bytes (2,500,421 to 2,506,557; app slot 38.2% full either way), memory +700 bytes.
- `tests/crash-record.mjs`: 6 host groups (reasons, record, rotate, persist, reports, no secrets) plus source contracts. Worst-case full report measured at 2,204 bytes against a 4,096-byte buffer.
- `test:core` 101 of 101 steps before the commit; after it, the last step (`factory-bin-freshness`) refuses any card-source commit newer than the signed binary, as expected while parked. `test:firmware-update:firmware` 5 of 5.

## Not verified
- The panic hook has never fired. That it is linked is measured (`__wrap_esp_panic_handler` in IRAM, breadcrumb in `.rtc_noinit`); that the system calls it, that the trace walk gives usable addresses, and that the breadcrumb survives a panic reset on this board need a deliberate crash on the bench. The steps are in the shared note `crash-recorder.md`.
- Whether the task-watchdog path reaches the hook on the real card.

## Not in this PR
The after-crash warm-white recovery is unchanged. Current logic and a recommendation are in the shared note.

## What this fixes

author: leelanshkharbanda
body:
## Summary

`config/runtime.exs` applied the raising `parse_port/2` helper to the optional `PHX_URL_PORT`. A typo in an optional setting aborted production boot, contradicting the file's own "bad input for optional settings must never take the node down" policy and the docs that list only `PORT` and `SECRET_KEY_BASE` as boot-fatal.

## Fix

Move the optional-port policy into a pure `Chronos.Config.UrlPort.normalize/3` helper: a valid integer `1..65535` is used as-is; unset, blank, or invalid values warn and use the documented derived default (443 when HTTPS is forced, otherwise the listen port). `PORT` still uses the raising parser and remains mandatory.

The normalizer lives in its own module so this PR does not conflict with the `Chronos.Config` module introduced by the `FORCE_SSL` fix.

## Verification

- Unit tests cover unset/blank, valid values, and four invalid values in both HTTPS and plain-HTTP modes, including the warning.
- Production config probes: `PHX_URL_PORT=notaport` now boots and reports `booted`; `PORT=notaport` still raises with the original message.
- `MIX_ENV=test mix test` — 466 passed (463 baseline + 3 regressions). `mix format --check-formatted` clean.
- Council D1 approve, D3 conditional (scope normalization to this variable), D2 reject (argued ports intentionally fail fast); final arbiter: fix now — `PHX_URL_PORT` is documented as optional, unlike `PORT`.

## Test plan

- [x] `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/chronos/config/url_port_test.exs`
- [x] Prod config probes for invalid `PHX_URL_PORT` and invalid `PORT`
- [x] `MIX_ENV=test mix test`, `mix format --check-formatted`

Lantern of Souls is a trait script: unblocked ability hits store a soul (max 3, `vars[0]`), and the next Soul Lance fires them as shards.
- **Gorrath** (`content/fighters/gorrath/`): Unbroken (one hit of 50% armour on every heavy), Chain Hook (pulls point-blank at +14), Earthsplitter shockwave, Bull Rush (2-hit armour, carries into walls), Execution Chain (command grab: unblockable, beats attacks, untechable, three slams).
- **Oath-Shade** (`content/fighters/oath_shade/`): Aldric's moves and Oathkeeper trait, Knight model with `shade = 1`. Added to `Roster` so `MatchSetup.fighter_data(&"oath_shade")` resolves.

- **Camera**: when the spot behind the fighter is inside a wall or would put a pillar between the camera and either fighter, the camera swings around until it has a clear view, then eases back.
- **Quit crash**: `FighterClips` library and `FightFx` textures were `static var` Resources, which crash on quit in Godot 4.7.2. They now live in `TreeCache` (metadata on the SceneTree).

body:
Encoding-Target: none
Fixes-Run: none

## Summary

`validation-waivers audit --scope incremental` (#1867) exists since 2026-10-15, but no RuleSpec repository can use it. This pull request removes the three reasons, for the shape of a signed encoder pull request (new module, companion test, applied manifest). The goal is a shorter `rulespec-us` pull-request check: the step "Enforce validation waiver ratchet" re-audits all 1,930 waived modules on every head and is 74% of a run (TheAxiomFoundation/.github#130, TheAxiomFoundation/rulespec-us#783).

Nothing is switched on here. The reusable workflow does not pass `--scope incremental`, and this pull request does not change it. Full scope stays the default.

Validation effect: none

The check that accepts or refuses a RuleSpec file does not change, and no fingerprint changes. Only the opt-in incremental scope changes: which waivers it re-audits. No workflow passes that flag today.

**Review round 1 is answered below; the fixes are not yet re-reviewed.** Nobody requested a review by hand; GitHub requested the code owner automatically because `cli.py` is a CODEOWNERS file.

## What blocked the incremental audit

All three were measured on `rulespec-us` main `25ddba37` (1,930 waivers, 4,888 atomic modules).

1. **Every signed pull request forced the full audit.** Any changed path under `.axiom/` was "unclassified or shared validation input", and every signed pull request adds `.axiom/encoding-manifests/<module>.json`.
2. **The selector did not finish.** One Colorado waiver was not done after 240 s under a profiler (590 s without one in the earlier analysis); the whole ledger was not done after 1,500 s. In the 240 s profile, 188 s were 7,631 symlink audits of the whole checkout (25.4 million `lstat` calls, about 25 ms per audit): the validator's resolver re-audits the checkout and re-validates its routing caches on each call, the read set called it for every target string of every file (twice per resolution root), and nothing was shared between waivers. The profiled waiver is a composition, whose read set walks the closure of every module of the country; only 565 files had been parsed. `cli.py` also ran the selector over the whole ledger in each of the 52 audit jobs, before the partition filter.
3. **One unparseable file forced the full audit for everyone (new finding).** Once the selector finished, it returned "full": three waivers (`us-ny/regulations/18-nycrr/387/12/f/3/v/a.yaml`, `.../v/b.yaml`, `us/regulations/7-cfr/273/2/j.yaml`) reach a companion file that the strict loader refuses (a YAML merge key that overrides a merged key, "found duplicate key"). The selector treated that as a failure of the whole run.

## What changes

- **Manifest classification** (`validation_waiver_scope.py`). `.axiom/encoding-manifests/<module path>.json` is a change of that module when `<module path>.yaml` is a canonical module path, the module exists as a `rulespec/v1` file, and neither file is deleted, a symlink, hard-linked or inside a configured execution input. It selects exactly what a change of its module selects. It is never inert.
- **Still the full audit**: every other `.axiom` path (in `rulespec-us` today: `toolchain.toml`, `workflow-toolchain.toml`, `pending-validation-fingerprints.json`, `target-validation-passes.json`, `reviewed-migrations.json`, `repository-structure.yaml`, `upstream-source-check-baseline.txt`, `legacy-replacements/**`; any file a repository adds there later, such as the audit cost table); a file under `encoding-manifests/` that is not `<module path>.json` (no jurisdiction, a ProgramSpec, a companion, a `.axiom`/`.github`/`programs` part inside); a manifest directory inside a jurisdiction; a manifest of another country; a manifest with no module, or with a module that is not `rulespec/v1`; and everything that forced it before (ledger, `.github/**`, `programs/**`, deleted paths, aliases, Git configuration inputs, a symlink in the checkout).
- **Selector cost.** Every repository-wide input is computed once per run (checkout admission, candidate content roots per jurisdiction, placement-search roots per jurisdiction, one parse per file). Each file's direct dependencies form one shared graph; a waiver's decision is a walk over it. The walk follows every present candidate of a target, which is a superset of the one file the validator's resolver picks. A test compares the closure with the validator's own resolvers.
- **Selection per partition** (`cli.py`). The audit job partitions the complete ledger first and selects only among the waivers it owns. Ownership still comes from the complete ledger. A selection can only narrow a partition.
- **Per-waiver fallback.** A waiver whose own read set cannot be classified (a file of its closure does not parse, an import cannot be classified, a directory sits at a dependency path) is audited on every run, with the reason in the report. Other waivers are decided from their own read sets. A filesystem error still audits every path given, and a checkout, Git or changed-path problem still forces the full audit.
- **Compositions.** A composition waiver is selected by any changed module, as before. The country-wide dependency walk that only a companion-only change needs is no longer run when a module changed.

## Soundness

The claim: a waiver that the incremental audit does not select has the same fingerprint on the head tree as on the base tree.

Evidence in this pull request:

- **Real-engine invariant tests** (`tests/test_validation_waiver_incremental_invariant.py`, CI job `real-engine`): small repositories, the full audit before and after an edit, and every waiver whose verdict changed must be selected. New edits: an applied manifest alone, and a new module with companion and manifest in a state, in a sibling state and in the federal jurisdiction. 50 pass locally and in CI (verified).
- **Resolver comparison**: the shared graph's closure equals a closure built from the validator's own resolver functions on a tree with cross-jurisdiction, transitive, absent and companion-only targets; import candidates equal the validator's for 18 spellings (verified by test).
- **Fingerprint replay on `rulespec-us`** (measured, local): 0 of 749 replayed waivers outside a selection changed.

### Replay method

The head tree is main `25ddba37`. A base tree is main with the module, companion and manifest files of past merged pull requests put back to their state before each pull request (an added file removed, a changed file restored). 80 state pull requests with one to five module files, in 44 states, each with files that main still holds unchanged: 97 modules, 264 files, 187 added and 77 changed. They are split by state into group A and group B. The selector runs on the head tree with the reverted paths; every replayed waiver outside that selection must have the same fingerprint in both trees. Fingerprints come from the entry point the audit's workers use, with encoder main `b95cfedde`, the engine and corpus release `rulespec-us` pins, and no composer.

| Base tree | Changed paths | Replayed waivers outside the selection | Changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Both groups reverted (80 pull requests) | 264 | 386: federal, and states with no pull request | 0 |
| Group A reverted (39 pull requests) | 119 | 193, in 20 states of group B | 0 |
| Group B reverted (41 pull requests) | 145 | 170, in 21 states of group A | 0 |
| No applied manifest at all (1,319 files removed) | not a selection test | 206, in 48 jurisdictions | 0 |
| Only the companions of the 80 pull requests reverted | 93 | 240 | 0 |

The replay does detect changes where the rules expect them. In the companion-only tree, 28 of the 32 replayed waivers that the rule selects have a different fingerprint, and all 28 are selected. In the group B tree, 28 replayed Arizona waivers are inside the selection and none changed (the search rule selects them because the validator indexes the new modules). author: spdrman
body:
Closes #1667

A DWG title block logo is an IMAGE entity, and the converter only counted its frame, so the converted sheet had a blank patch where the drawing has the logo. I added `PvecConversion::images(dir)`: the file the definition names is read from `dir` (by file name only, never by the path the drawing carries), decoded and written into the raster stream at the IMAGE's insertion point, pixel vectors and rotation, cut to its rectangular or polygonal clip, in the same frame as the linework next to it. It goes through the leaf's own map, so blocks, viewports and flipped sheets carry it, and the change stays out of the sheet root plot-scale work in #1665. Off by default, and then an IMAGE is still only counted. A missing, undecodable or hidden image stays a frame and its row says why.

The first commit is the thirteen red cells in `tests/pvec_1667_dwg_image.rs` (eleven were red, two are controls), the second is the fix, and #1665 is on main now, so a cell checks the raster follows the 2 : 1 plot scale together with the line next to it. One assumption I could not check against a real drawing: clip vertices are read as top-left origin, y down.

author: smiley73
body:
## Summary

`/tagteam:ship` now finds out before it starts whether Claude Code's Bash sandbox would stop it. It runs a short trial, a fraction of a second, that does what a ship needs: it makes a worktree, commits in it and starts a step. It cleans up after itself whether the trial passes or fails. This all happens before the ship creates anything, so a refused ship leaves nothing in the repository.

## What you can now do

- Run `/tagteam:ship` with no sandbox, or with one that allows what a ship needs, and nothing changes. You are asked nothing and no step is added.
- Run it under a sandbox that blocks the worktree or the commit and get one plain sentence at once. It says a ship needs the sandbox off (`{ "sandbox": { "enabled": false } }`). Nothing is left behind, where before the ship failed part-way through a run.
- Get git's own error, and no mention of the sandbox, when the trial fails for another reason such as a full disk.
- Run `/tagteam:configure` to see the same trial as one row of its preflight table. It reports the result and never stops for it.
- Read in the README what a ship needs from the sandbox. `/tagteam:plan` needs nothing from it and never runs the trial.

The ship instructions now tell the orchestrator to pass the refusal on and end. It must not rerun the ship outside the sandbox, because that would pass the trial and then fail inside the run.

## Risk

- When the trial passes but its temporary files cannot be fully removed, the message starts "The sandbox trial passed", although the instructions say to stay quiet about the sandbox in that case. The wording can confuse. The ship is not wrongly refused. It was recorded and not fixed.

- The verify command `npm test` failed, then passed when run again on the same commit (f34e18b8493e).

author: ohagmann
body:
## Problem

A DWG with BricsCAD parametric blocks loses every block parameter when OCS saves it, even with no edit at all. In BricsCAD
the references then have no parameters left: `getpropertyvalue` on a visibility parameter answers *Unknown Property*,
the Properties panel no longer lists it, and its state cannot be changed any more.

BricsCAD keeps the parameters (here: visibility states set up with `VISIBILITYSTATES`) in objects of its own classes
(`BDMDB…`, `BdmDb…`), which OCS reads as raw records (`ObjectType::Unknown`) and writes back verbatim. Those objects
read and drive the variables of the block's `ACAD_ASSOCNETWORK` (`LAMP`, `look_1`, `Unterdrücken_1`, …) by handle, and
the variables list them as reactors. `sync_native_parametric_graph`, which runs on save and on the first edit after
opening, rebuilds every scope's network from the editor's model under new handles and drops the value dependencies,
so the raw objects end up pointing at erased variables.

Measured on 408 real drawings with BricsCAD parametric blocks (a block library, templates and sheets of one project;
not shareable), each opened and saved as DWG through `--serve` without an edit. "Dangling" counts handles in the
handle streams of BricsCAD's objects that no object of the saved file has (read with libredwg):

| | dangling references | files with any | value dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|
| BricsCAD original | 0 | 0 | 14,774 |
| main | 51,045 | 244 | 0 |
| this PR | 0 | 0 | 14,774 |

## Fix

A network whose variables list a raw record as a reactor is written back as it was read, as long as the editor's model
of that scope still equals the one the network holds (`stored_network_to_keep`):

- block scope: the runtime constraint set hashes equal to the set decoded from the stored network;
- model space, where a drawing that is itself a BricsCAD parametric block keeps its parameters: in addition the
  drawing's parameter table equals what opening the drawing reads, and no swept surface is pending.

A scope the user changed is rebuilt as before. The kept networks go back under the rebuilt root network after the
rebuilt ones.

Two refactors without a change in behaviour: the per-scope part of `constraint_model_fingerprint` moves into
`hash_constraint_set` (dimension links are now hashed in id order, so two equal sets hash alike), and
`load_named_parameters_from_document` reads through the new `model_network_parameters`.

## Test

`scene::dwg_native_constraints::raw_dependents_tests`:

- a block network and a model-space network that a raw object depends on keep their handles through the sync;
- a block parameter or drawing parameter changed in the editor is still written (the network is rebuilt);
- `tests/fixtures/bricscad/visibility-states.dwg` (made in BricsCAD V26; its README says how and what it holds), synced,
  saved as DWG and reopened, keeps all 18 variables with their handles, networks and reactors, and its 6 value
  dependencies.

The three "keeps" tests fail without the fix. `cargo test --workspace` passes, apart from
`runner::tests::run_v4_delivers_document_changed_delta_to_v27_plugin`, which fails the same way on main when the whole
workspace runs in parallel and passes on its own.

## BricsCAD check

The fixture opened and saved by OCS (`--serve`, no edit), then opened in BricsCAD V26 (Linux) and asked for each
reference's states:

- main: all three references answer *Unknown Property "LAMP~MCAD"*;
- this PR: they report `On/Shown`, `Off/Shown` and `Off/Hidden` as before, and `setpropertyvalue` switches a state.

Not covered: DXF. BricsCAD does not keep these parameters through DXF itself (its own DXF of the fixture, reopened in
BricsCAD, has none), and OCS refuses DWG → DXF for drawings with these raw records unless `allow_lossy` is set.

author: prajwolrg
body:
## Description

Adds the checks that would have caught the bug #277 fixes before it reached staging. The BLS backend from #272 replays blocks that revm's default backend executed, so it has to agree with that backend on every input. Nothing tested that broadly: the comparison test in #272 never fed it a zero `Fp2`, and the official EIP-2537 vectors don't include that input either.

Stacked on #277. I'll rebase onto `main` once it merges.

- `tests/differential.rs` is the main guard. It runs all seven operations through both backends on generated input: edge values (zero, one, p - 1, p, identity, generator, points outside the subgroup, off-curve points, scalars at and above the group order) mixed with random ones. Each case has to return the same bytes or halt on both. The halt reason may differ, since it doesn't reach consensus. The checked-in proptest seed replays the zero input every run.
- `tests/eip2537_vectors.rs` runs the official EIP-2537 success and failure vectors through revm's precompile entry points, so output and gas are both checked.
- The docs commit writes the rule into the crate doc and adds the crate to `AGENTS.md`.

Start with `tests/differential.rs`.

### Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature/Enhancement (non-breaking change which adds functionality or enhances an existing one)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] New or updated tests
- [ ] Dependency Update

## Notes to Reviewers

The vectors are copied from [ethereum/EIPs at `faaa35fff856`](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/tree/faaa35fff856/assets/eip-2537). I left out `msm_G1_bls.json` and `msm_G2_bls.json` (10 MB together). The `mul_*` files are single-pair MSM inputs, and the differential suite covers multi-pair MSM. I also didn't commit the 1,036 BLS calls traced from staging (11 MB, almost all MSM). The differential suite covers the same ground.

Open gap: every check here runs the crates.io `bls12_381`. The chunk guest uses `sp1-patches/bls12_381`, which swaps in syscall-backed field arithmetic, and nothing compares that crate with the default backend. Closing this means running the differential inputs inside the zkVM, for example through `prover-perf`. That's a follow-up, not part of this PR.

Is this PR addressing any specification, design doc or external reference document?

- [x]  Yes
- [ ]  No

If yes, please add relevant links: [EIP-2537](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2537)

## Testing

I ran the new tests against the backend from before #277:

- The differential suite failed in each of 3 runs, and proptest shrank it to `map_fp2_to_g2(0, 0)`.
- The EIP-2537 vectors all passed. They can't see this bug.

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code.
- [x] I have commented my code where necessary.
- [x] I have updated the documentation if needed.
- [x] My changes do not introduce new warnings.
- [x] I have added (where necessary) tests that prove my changes are effective or that my feature works.
- [x] New and existing tests pass with my changes.
- [x] I have [disclosed my use of AI](https://github.com/alpenlabs/alpen/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-assistance-notice) in the body of this PR.

AI assistance: Claude Code wrote the tests and this description, and ran the differential checks against staging data. I reviewed the result.
