author: polionus
body:
> Opening as a Draft PR for maintainer feedback per `CONTRIBUTING.md`, since this introduces a new `data/media/` store, two teacher tools (`show_media`, `search_youtube`), and prompt updates. Happy to narrow scope, adjust contracts, or move parts into a core plugin if preferred.

### Problem
LearnHarness currently supports local image display (`show_image`), SVG figures (`visual`), interactive HTML demos (`demo`), and desktop-only file-path chips, but has no support for:
1. Direct inline image/audio/video attachments in the composer (working in both browser and desktop modes).
2. Playable audio/video or YouTube clip playback in lessons (`media-chrome` is already a dependency).
3. Grounding tutor-embedded audio/video in readable subtitles/transcripts so the agent teaches from actual spoken content rather than guessing.

### What Changed
- **Session-scoped binary media store & Range streaming** (`src/core/contracts/media.ts`, `src/store/media.ts`, `src/server/media.ts`, `app/api/chats/[id]/media/`):
  - Stores uploaded/copied binary assets deduplicated by SHA-256 under `data/media/<chatId>/<sha256>.<ext>` + metadata sidecar instead of embedding large base64 payloads in `chats/*.json`; cleaned up on `deleteChat`.
  - Serves stored assets with HTTP `Range` (`206 Partial Content`) support for audio/video scrubbing.
  - Adds `POST /api/stt/transcribe` for best-effort BYOK batch transcription (Deepgram `nova-3` → OpenAI `whisper-1`, graceful no-op when unconfigured).
- **Turn/message/view integration** (`src/core/input-events.ts`, `src/core/native-messages.ts`, `src/core/view.ts`, `src/server/chat-handler.ts`, `src/server/jobs.ts`):
  - Adds lightweight `media?: MediaAttachment[]` on `text`/`steer` inputs and app-only `lhMedia` on `LhMessage` (stripped on the provider wire by `toLlmMessages`, which injects `[Attached audio/video: ...; mediaId: ...]` + transcript).
  - Video attachments capture up to 4 keyframes client-side (`lib/client-media.ts`) via `<video>` + `<canvas>` (no `ffmpeg` required) and gracefully drop keyframes on text-only models while keeping metadata/transcript.
- **Composer & transcript UI** (`components/composer.tsx`, `components/composer-media-tray.tsx`, `components/attach-files-button.tsx`, `components/file-path-drop-zone.tsx`, `components/artifacts/media-card.tsx`, `components/chat.tsx`):
  - Clipboard image paste, web media drag-drop, and paperclip media picker (preserving existing desktop local-path chips).
  - Shared `SessionMediaPlayer` (`media-chrome`, client-only import for SSR safety) and `YouTubeMediaCard` (`youtube-nocookie.com`) with timestamp range badges and collapsible subtitles/transcript drawers.
- **Subtitle-enforced `show_media` + keyless `search_youtube`** (`src/agent/tools/show-media.ts`, `src/agent/tools/media-subtitles.ts`, `src/agent/tools/search-youtube.ts`):
  - `show_media` requires readable subtitles/transcripts across all three sources (`youtubeUrl` via Innertube captions + watch-page fallback, local `path` via sibling/explicit `.vtt`/`.srt` or STT, and session `mediaId` via cached transcript or STT), returning timestamped subtitles directly to the agent and refusing uncaptioned clips.
  - `search_youtube` searches YouTube through SSRF-guarded `safeFetch` with YouTube's Subtitles/CC filter (`sp=EgIoAQ==`) so captioned video lookup works without a web-search API key.
- **Prompts & generated plugin API docs**:
  - Updated `shared/30-learner-files.md`, `teacher/40-jobs.md`, `teacher/50-demos.md`, `researcher.ts`, added `teacher/56-media.md`, and regenerated `docs/plugin-api/` (`contracts-media.md`).

### Verification
- `npm run typecheck`: 0 errors.
- `npm run lint`: 0 errors (import boundary rules intact).
- `tests/multimedia.test.tsx`, `tests/plugin-api-reference.test.ts`, `tests/web-search.test.ts`, `tests/question-tools.test.ts`, `tests/composer-attach.test.tsx`, `tests/file-path-drop-zone.test.tsx`, `tests/file-access.test.ts`, `tests/prompt-overrides.test.ts`: all passing (mocked fetch/FS fixtures).
- Full `npm test`: 5,559 passing, 2 Windows-only skips, 1 unrelated local Node 24 failure in `tests/subscription-auth.test.ts` (CI runs Node 26).
- Live manual checks on macOS arm64: verified live `search_youtube` + Innertube English caption extraction, `npm run build` + `scripts/smoke-server.mjs`, and unsigned arm64 DMG packaging.

### Limitations / Open Questions
- Upload limit is bounded at 25 MiB to stay within Next's existing `proxyClientMaxBodySize` (26 MiB).
- YouTube caption extraction and search rely on YouTube's public Innertube/watch HTML endpoints (guarded by `safeFetch` and explicit errors if YouTube changes formats or rate-limits).
- Browser-side video keyframe extraction depends on codecs playable by Chromium/Electron; audio-only or unsupported video codecs still upload and transcribe without keyframes.
- Not yet tested on Windows/Linux installers or with live Deepgram/OpenAI batch STT keys.

author: jonasmerrell
body:
Stacked on #189 (base `android-fea-web`). Lets the phone app work on rCAD projects on GitHub.

## What it does
- **`rcad github`** (new `src/github_cli.rs`): `status`, `login-start` / `login-poll` (GitHub device flow), `logout`, `repos`, `clone`, `sync`, `resolve`. Each prints one JSON object. It reuses the editor's sign-in and git code (`vcs.rs`), so signing in from the phone signs the editor on netdash in too. With no saved token it falls back to the GitHub CLI's, as the editor does.
- **Commit and push after phone chats** (open gap 3): in a project that syncs, `rcad chat` pulls from GitHub before the request. After Claude saves, it commits the change, as the editor does after a save, and pushes it. The commit message lists the changes and ends with "From a Claude chat on the rCAD phone app: <the request>". The result shows in the chat as a notice.
- **netdash service**:
  - `GET /api/github`, `POST /api/github/login`, `/login/poll`, `/logout`, `GET /api/github/repos` (marks repos already on netdash), `POST /api/github/clone` (https URLs only, into the first project folder; an empty repo gets a new document that is committed and pushed).
  - `POST /api/doc/<id>/sync` and `/resolve`.
  - Documents carry `remote` ("owner/name").
  - The device code stays on netdash; the phone only gets the user code.
- **App**:
  - A GitHub screen, opened from the branch button on the document list or the menu. It shows the account and has "Sign in with GitHub" with a large code and a "Copy code and open GitHub" button; the screen polls by itself until you approve.
  - The repository list is searchable, rCAD projects first, and marks repos already on netdash. Repos that don't look like rCAD projects ask before netdash downloads them.
  - Documents show "GitHub owner/name".
  - The document menu has "Sync with GitHub", which asks which side to keep when both changed the same thing.

## Tested
- Receiver: `python3 -m unittest capture/receiver/test_receiver.py capture/receiver/test_projects.py`, 13 pass. The new `test_github` covers status, sign-in (device code not sent to the phone, code used once), clone (rejects file:// and `..`), the repo list marking netdash copies, an empty repo, sync, resolve and logout.
- `cargo test --release --bin rcad vcs`: 13 pass. Release build OK. The full suite was not re-run for this PR; it passed (623) on #189, and this PR touches only `claude_cli.rs`, `main.rs` and the new file.
- Against real GitHub on netdash: `rcad github status` (JonasMerrell through the gh CLI), `repos` (58) and `login-start` (code issued, not approved).
- With a local bare repo as origin (nothing pushed to real repos):
  - clone into two copies, change and `sync` in one (commit authored as the GitHub account, noreply address, pushed), then `sync` in the other (pulled);
  - both sides renaming the same Part Studio gives `diverged`, and `resolve --keep theirs` takes GitHub's;
  - an empty repo clones as empty;
  - a real `rcad chat` (Haiku) pulled 2 commits first, then committed "Plate: added variable thickness = 6 mm" with the phone note and pushed.
- Emulator: the GitHub screen shows the account and 58 repos; the confirmation for a non-rCAD repo, the sign-in code screen and cancel all work. Not tried on the emulator: approving a sign-in and opening a real GitHub rCAD project, because none of the account's repos is an rCAD project yet.
- The netdash service runs this build and the APK at http://192.168.0.247:8765/rcad.apk is this one.

body:
The four `dependabot-missing-cooldown` findings came back on the `default-days: 3` lines: the rule wants a cooldown of at least 7 days.

- uv and npm: 7 days, 14 for major versions.
- GitHub Actions and Docker: 7 days.

Security updates aren't delayed by cooldowns, so fixes for known vulnerabilities still arrive right away. Only routine version bumps wait a week, which also gives a bad or hijacked release time to be caught and pulled.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [js-yaml](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml) | dependencies | major | [`4.3.2` → `5.5.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/js-yaml/4.3.2/5.5.0) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>nodeca/js-yaml (js-yaml)</summary>

### [`v5.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#550---2026-10-16)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.4.3...5.5.0)

##### Changed

- Updated `argparse` to v3.
- Updated development dependencies.

##### Fixed

- Correct percent-encoding of shorthand and verbatim tags.
- Reject `,`, `]`, and `}` at the start of block plain scalars, [#​801](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/801).
- Report the exact position of non-printable characters in errors, [#​801](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/801).

### [`v5.4.3`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#543---2026-10-06)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.4.2...5.4.3)

##### Fixed

- Fixed loading a whitespace-only block scalar followed by a less indented
  line, [#​802](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/802).

### [`v5.4.2`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#542---2026-09-13)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.4.1...5.4.2)

##### Fixed

- `forceQuotes` no longer quotes non-string scalars, [#​798](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/798).

### [`v5.4.1`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#541---2026-08-26)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.4.0...5.4.1)

##### Changed

- Hard-limit merge sequence size to 100.

##### Security

- Count empty mappings in merge sequences toward `maxTotalMergeKeys` to limit
  CPU usage, [#​797](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/797).

### [`v5.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#540---2026-08-25)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.3.0...5.4.0)

##### Added

- Added the `scalarStyleRules` dumper option to customize string formatting.
  See [Scalar styling](docs/scalar_styling.md) for details.

##### Changed

- \[breaking] Flattened the low-level AST node style representation. Scalar
  and collection nodes now use `SCALAR_STYLE` and `COLLECTION_STYLE` values;
  explicit tags use the separate `tagged` property. Alias nodes now contain
  only `kind` and `anchor`. This only affects code that directly constructs or
  edits AST nodes.
- \[breaking] The `sortKeys` option was rewritten using AST mutation to avoid
  side effects.
- Reworked scalar style selection. This can change formatting without changing
  loaded values; in particular, whitespace-only strings are now double-quoted.

##### Fixed

- Accept a byte order mark at the start of each document in a stream, [#​791](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/791).
- Produce valid flow mappings with `quoteFlowKeys` and `flowSkipColonSpace`,
  including alias and property-only keys, [#​786](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/786).
- Preserve empty scalar items when converting block sequences to flow style.
- Do not apply the 1024-character simple-key limit to flow mapping keys.
- Count Unicode code points, rather than UTF-16 code units, for the
  1024-character simple-key limit.
- Add an explicit document-end marker after keep-chomped block scalars when
  needed to preserve trailing newlines.

### [`v5.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#530---2026-08-14)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.2.3...5.3.0)

This release focuses on reworking the documentation and making small
architectural improvements before moving forward.

##### Added

- Added completely new documentation.
- Exported `DUMP_SCHEMA`, the default schema used by the dumper.
- Added `YAMLException.throwAt()` for throwing an error at a source position.

##### Changed

- Changed flat constant exports to grouped exports: `EVENT_ID`, `SCALAR_STYLE`,
  `COLLECTION_STYLE`, and `CHOMPING_MODE`, along with their value types. The old
  exports are still preserved, but deprecated.
- Made `identify` mandatory for custom tag definitions. Use
  `identify: () => false` for load-only tags.

##### Deprecated

- Deprecated flat constant exports. Use grouped ones instead.

##### Removed

- Removed the `MERGE_KEY` export (not used anymore after last fixes).

##### Fixed

- Validate `<<` sequence items at merge time, so aliased merge sources are
  checked too.
- Resolve `<<` outside of a mapping key as the plain string `'<<'`, matching
  v4, instead of leaking an internal symbol into the result.

### [`v5.2.3`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#523---2026-08-01)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.2.2...5.2.3)

##### Fixed

- Prevent prototype fallback when resolving tags and mapping entries, [#​782](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/782).
- Resolve `!!timestamp` years 0000-0099 correctly, [#​775](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/775).
- Preserve implicit null mapping values before document markers and reject
  unpaired mapping event streams, [#​784](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/784).
- Preserve folded scalar values with tab-indented lines when round-tripping a
  parsed AST through `present()`; `dump()` and loading are unaffected, [#​780](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/780).

### [`v5.2.2`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#522---2026-07-24)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.2.1...5.2.2)

##### Fixed

- Quote flow scalars where a colon precedes a flow indicator, [#​773](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/773).

##### Security

- Avoid exponential parsing time for nested flow sequence pairs.

### [`v5.2.1`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#521---2026-07-02)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.2.0...5.2.1)

##### Fixed

- Add `Map` support to !!omap (should work when `realMapTag` used)

##### Security

- Remove quadratic complexity from !!omap `addItem`. Regression from v5
  (usually not critical, because YAML11_SCHEMA is not default anymore).

### [`v5.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#520---2026-06-26)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.1.0...5.2.0)

##### Added

- Added `maxTotalMergeKeys` (10000) loader option to limit the total number of
  keys processed by YAML merge (`<<`) across one `load()` / `loadAll()` call.
- Added `maxAliases` (-1) loader option to limit the number of YAML aliases per
  document.

##### Removed

- `maxMergeSeqLength` replaced with `maxTotalMergeKeys` for limiting YAML merge
  processing.

##### Fixed

- Round-trip of integers with exponential form (>= `1e21`)

### [`v5.1.0`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#510---2026-06-23)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/5.0.0...5.1.0)

##### Added

- Collection tags can finalize an incrementally populated carrier into a
  different result value.

##### Changed

- \[breaking] `quoteStyle` now selects the preferred quote style; use the
  restored `forceQuotes` option to force quoting non-key strings.

### [`v5.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#500---2026-06-20)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/compare/4.3.2...5.0.0)

##### Added

- Added named exports for schemas, tags, parser events and AST utilities.
- Reworked `JSON_SCHEMA` and `CORE_SCH

body:
## What changes
TP-1 of `docs/studies/TP_SCREENING_RULES.md`. The low-resolution Dig (`crates/mzlab-feat/src/legacy/lr/`) now computes rule R1, the one-ion noise floor from `mzlab_core::ionstat` (the same code as `peak noise`, schema noise-floor/1). It does this on the raw XIC of every cell that has a peak check. The result appears in three places:
- `points[].sn_floor`: S/N on the floor, one value per point;
- `rows[].checks[{id:"noise_floor", status, value, threshold, evidence, rule}]`: the B.1 contract, read on the cell the peak criterion names. `evidence` holds the peak, noise, estimator, every term and the quantum, plus a count of cells per status;
- the `noise_floor` summary block: parameters, the number of cells where the auto quantum was accepted, rows per status, and a log. The log has a head line with the automatic choice, then one line per row that warns or fails. The CLI `tp.dig_lr` prints the same lines on stderr as `note:`.

New settings and Flow params: `one_ion` (empty = auto, 0 = off, >0 = cps) and `noise_sd_weight` (default 0.5).

- **D1 (gate) is open, so the choice is conservative: evidence only.** No state, criterion, score or label reads the floor. A test checks that the output, with the floor keys removed, is unchanged under one_ion auto, 0, 1e9 and sd_weight 3.
- **D2:** `auto` is the default, as far as the study marks it decided. It changes no result, and the choice is logged with its evidence: "accepted in N of M cells".
- **`ionstat::quantum`:** consecutive differences within 1e-6 relative are deduplicated (`JITTER`). Without this, the f32-sum rounding of a Dig XIC became a false step, q came out ≈ 0 and the quantum was rejected. With it, the demo files give q = 13333.33 cps, accepted in 95 % of cells. There is a new core test, and the schema description is updated.
- **Parity:**
  - site wasm (finder-lr `api.run`) and the CLI Flow step share one `summary()`;
  - `flow_lr_floor_tests.rs` checks byte for byte that the flow output with `one_ion` set equals the page bytes;
  - it also checks that the floor of a cell equals the stdout of `mzlab-cli peak noise` on that cell's XIC;
  - `finder-lr-wasm/tests/lr_dig.rs` knows the new keys.
- **CLI for agents:** Flow params are in the regenerated `steps-cli-1.json`. The catalog row of `tp.dig_lr` is related to `peak noise`. Compact `commands --json` is unchanged in size.
- **Docs:** `docs/agenti/mzfinder-lr.md` (keys, settings, tests) and the study (Part A R1, B.2 "Today", Part C TP-1).
- **Regenerated with their tools:**
  - `docs/schemi/steps-cli-1.json`, `tools-1.json` and `tools-demo-1.json` (`MZLAB_UPDATE_STEPS=1`);
  - the LLM replay `tests/data/assist/reg/fuori_tema.jsonl` (`MZLAB_UPDATE_LLM=1`, scripted).

## Before the push
- [x] Area: I read the area file (docs/agenti/INDICE.md) and touched only what my prompt says
- [x] `origin/main` merged only on a real conflict (`tools/fondi_main.py`, never rebase); `python3 tools/pre_pr.py` green
- [x] Parity: the function exists in the site (`.wasm` + OPFS) and in the app (native + CLI) with a byte-for-byte parity test, or the real technical limit is stated below
- [x] CLI route for agents: `--json` with stable keys, distinct exit codes, data on stdout and progress on stderr, listed in the agent catalogs
- [x] English only (code, comments, docs, tests, messages, commit and PR text); user-facing text through `lang/` keys
- [x] No real data and no forbidden surnames; synthetic data only
- [x] Generated files regenerated with their tool (never by hand)
- [x] Risks: this PR does NOT touch Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, `.github/workflows/` (except `test.yml` and `stat-ci.yml`), `.wasm` files, the CSP, `crates/mzlab-desktop/` — or I listed them below

## Risks
- **Wasm size of finder-lr:**
  - Raw cargo output, measured on separate builds of main and this branch: 1,973,158 → 1,994,573 B (+1.09 %).
  - Estimated after wasm-opt: ≈ 794 KB, against the recorded 785,462 B and the cap 892,928 B. That is under the cap and under 5 %.
  - wasm-bindgen and wasm-opt are not available here, so `misura` in `tools/moduli/` is left to CI's measurement step.
- **The `ionstat` quantum jitter fix also applies to `peak noise`:** on inputs whose steps differ only by f32 rounding, the quantum can now be accepted where before it was rejected.
- **Still owner decisions:** D1 (whether the floor gates or labels anything) and D2 (whether `auto` stays the formal default).

## Business correction
MSK should recommend an evidence-supported **better alternative** to a customer's current holding, not require a near-perfect numeric quality score. The previously hard-coded `score >= 75` rejected otherwise operator-approved research items even when data and review checks passed.

## Implementation
- Keep scores finite and bounded `0 < score <= 100` as a **ranking input**, not a financial-evidence or regulatory-publication substitute.
- Keep all existing issuer, price, valuation, risk, corporate-action, 5-annual/8-quarter, current NSE session and independent audited-registry gates unchanged.
- Add an offline 5-company approval-contract regression using fictional 42–46 score rows; ensure that removing verified prices still blocks the entire report.

## Safety
Test cases use synthetic fixtures and mock reviewer approval; **do not** represent real issuer verification. This PR **does not approve any company, enable a Telegram bot, send data to customers or fix upstream bank data**. Current release registry stays `WITHHELD`. Merge only after full CI.

body:
## What & Why
Jira: BE-28

Organizers weren't told when their (simulated) payout account was ready or when paid sales for an event switched on. Customers weren't told when someone took their support case. Kazakh-speaking users got Russian emails. This PR adds the two notifications and a full set of Kazakh emails.

## Changes
- **New notification types** `payout_status` and `support_assignment`, plus `Language.KK` (registration accepts `"language": "kk"`).
- **Migration** `703f7fea8054` (revises `9a95f0f62416`):
  - adds the two `notificationtype` values (`ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS`);
  - replaces the `users.language` CHECK with ru/en/kk.
  - **Downgrade:** sets kk users back to `ru` and restores the ru/en CHECK. The enum values stay, like BE-18.
- **`payout_status`** (email + in-app to the organizer, the profile's user):
  - **`account_verified`:** when `simulate-verification` makes the verification and payout account ready. Links to `/organizer`.
  - **`sales_activated`:** when the last activation step switches paid sales on. Links to `/organizer/events/{id}`.
  - **Sent once:** both are sent only on the real change, read under the organizer/event locks, so repeating a step sends nothing.
  - **Payload:** `{stage, event_id?}`.
  - **Wording:** subject and text say «симуляция» / "simulation" in every language.
- **`support_assignment`** («Ваше обращение взяли в работу»):
  - **When:** a case goes from nobody to someone through `POST /support/cases/{id}/assign`.
  - **One notification per action** (BE-17 rule):
    - taking a case now sends `support_assignment` *instead of* the `support_status` email it used to send for open → in progress;
    - a first reply that auto-assigns sends only `support_reply`;
    - a status change that auto-assigns sends only `support_status`;
    - an admin taking over an already assigned case sends nothing.
  - **Privacy:** it says «специалист поддержки» and never includes the staff member's name or email, in the subject, text or payload `{case_id}`.
- **Kazakh emails:**
  - `templates/kk/` for every type that has ru templates, including `password_reset` and the two new ones (subject, text, HTML), plus the `base.html` footer.
  - A missing kk template falls back to ru, as before.
- **Formats:**
  - **Prices:** `5 000 ₸` with U+00A0, the same as the web's `formatKzt` and Intl ru-RU / kk-KZ.
  - **Dates:** in the venue's time zone. kk uses the web's month names: `23 қараша 2026, 18:00 (Asia/Almaty)`.
- **R-9:** publishing already needs a verified email since #35 (403 `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`). Here it's only covered by a test; draft creation stays unchecked.

## Checklist
- [x] Branch `issue/BE-28-notifications-kk`
- [x] ruff check + format clean; `alembic heads` shows one head; `alembic check` clean; upgrade → downgrade (with a kk user present) → upgrade tested
- [x] Tests: 1407 passed, plus 14 slow
- [x] API contract change: label `contract-change`
- [x] Existing tests changed on purpose:
  - `test_support_api`: taking a case now gives `support_assignment` instead of `support_status`;
  - `test_rendering`: the "unknown language" example is now `de`, since kk exists.
- [ ] **Please proofread the kk texts:** a native-speaking teammate should review `app/modules/notifications/templates/kk/` and the kk footer in `base.html`.

## How to test
```bash
uv run alembic upgrade head
uv run pytest tests/modules/notifications tests/modules/support
```
- Register with `{"email": …, "password": …, "language": "kk"}`: the verification email is in Kazakh.
- As an organizer with a paid ticket type: `POST /events/{id}/activation/simulate-verification` sends «Төлемдер қосылды (симуляция)» once. After `accept-terms` and `pay`, «Ақылы сатылым қосылды (симуляция): <event>» follows with the event link.
- Open a support case as a buyer and `POST /support/cases/{id}/assign` as the organizer: the buyer gets «Ваше обращение взяли в работу» (kk: «Өтінішіңіз жұмысқа алынды»), and nothing about who took it.

Web follow-up: send the UI language (`"kk"`) at registration, and show the two new types (`payout_status`, `support_assignment`) in the bell.

author: tomverelst
body:
Adds `gaslightmq_quick_inject`, the ⌘K sentence parser. It turns text into a rule definition and offers completions. It is a leaf crate of build step 4.

## API
- `QuickInject::read(text, &KnownNames) -> Sentence` never fails.
- A `Sentence` holds:
  - the rule it reads, if any;
  - the completions;
  - the words it could not read (`Unread`: `Unknown`, `Invalid`, `Conflict`, `Unfinished`), each with its word and span.
- `KnownNames` holds the topics, groups, clients, presets and selectors the caller knows of, so the crate stays sans-IO.
- `QuickInjectConfiguration` holds the default delay, the default throttle and the completion limit.

## Grammar
Words stand in any order, in any case, and each word is read by its form:
- **Lies:** `delay`, `throttle`, `error`, `blackhole`, `disconnect`, and the glossary words `refuse`, `silence` and `hang-up`.
- **Values:** `750ms`, `40%`, `for 20s`, `for 3 firings`, and `b2` for broker 2.
- **Names:** API and error-code names; topic patterns such as `orders.*`. Known names need no keyword.
- **Names the system does not know:** `topic X`, `group X`, `client X`, `broker X`, `preset X`, `selector X`. Quotes hold a name of several words.

`delay produce orders.* 750ms 40% order-ingest` reads as "Delay 750ms on Produce orders.* for order-ingest".

## Decisions
- No prefix guessing (`prod` → Produce): the completions do that.
- An `error` without a code is no rule yet (`Unfinished`).
- Unread words don't withhold the rule; the surface decides what to do with them.
- A name known as several kinds is read as a preset, then a selector, topic, group and client, in that order.
- Not in a sentence: the stage, jitter, count and time triggers.

The tests are tables of what a user types and the rule they get.

author: tokuji
body:
## Summary
RFC 9113 §8.3.1 defines `:path` as origin-form (`absolute-path [ "?" query ]`), or `*` for OPTIONS. Absolute-form is accepted only by HTTP/1.1 (RFC 9112 §3.2.2). Option (a) on BLA-668: a target that is neither origin-form nor `*` is refused before routing.

- **HTTP/2:** `:path` values such as `http://ignored/x`, `x`, `?q`, or `*` on a method other than OPTIONS reset the stream with `PROTOCOL_ERROR`. They used to be routed literally and answered 404. `OPTIONS *` is still accepted.
- **HTTP/1.1:** absolute-form is still rewritten to origin-form and routed. A target such as `x` or `?q` now gets 400; it used to be routed.
- **Server push:** a push path that isn't origin-form is dropped with a warning before PUSH_PROMISE is sent.

The check lives in `split_path_query`, which both transports already call; it raises `MessageError`. That function is `lru_cache`d and the check runs only on a cache miss, so a hit adds nothing. The HTTP/2 parser's two `:path` split call sites are merged into one, and HTTP/1.1 reuses its existing `MessageError` → 400 path.

Instructions per request (`sys.monitoring`, Python 3.14, reused connection):
- H1: 2627 → 2627.
- H2: 3884 → 3885 (the NOP of the parser's `try`).

Out of scope: HTTP/2 `OPTIONS *` is routed (404), while HTTP/1.1 answers it with 204. Filed as BLA-703.

## Tests
- New `tests/unit/test_h2_path_form.py`:
  - six HTTP/2 forms that must reset;
  - four forms that must be served, including `OPTIONS *` and `//x`;
  - four HTTP/1.1 targets (`x` and `?q` → 400; absolute-form and `/x` → 200).
- `tests/conformance/http2/test_http2_dispatch.py`: a push path that isn't origin-form gets no PUSH_PROMISE.
- `tests/unit/test_parser.py`: drops the case that pinned `?onlyq` as an empty path.
- The new cases fail on master. Full suite (`--run-all`): 17704 passed, 645 skipped, 1 xfailed.

Closes BLA-668.

body:
Fixes #908

## Summary
At the e2e time scale (0.1), alice's short token lived 17 s (`12 s` minimum + 5 s). The gateway refreshes at the half-life, so the refresh had about 8.5 s to land: alice's start uses part of that time, then the test's next call, the exchange, the delivery, and the reconcile pass that writes the Secret. In that pass the expiry stop runs before the refresh step. On a loaded CI cluster this missed. The instance stopped at the expiry, so every later poll saw a replaced instance and the wait could only time out after 240 s.

The short lifetime is now 2.5 × the scaled minimum (30 s, so a 15 s refresh window). The 10 min start lifetime stays. No fixed waits are added back, `enableTimeout` is unchanged, and every assertion is unchanged. The gateway behaves as designed (refresh at the half-life, stop at the expiry), so only the test changes.

**Which half failed:** I couldn't read the Tekton log from this VM because the dashboard needs a login. The mutation below reproduces the CI signature exactly: `the instance is not replaced`, subtest fails at 240.00 s. So the cause is the instance stopping at the token's expiry before a refresh reached the Secret.

## Verification
- `TestTokenExchangeEndToEnd` alone on a local kind cluster (`toolgate-908`): PASS in **73.6 s**. It took 129.5 s on master before the lifetime cut. Subtests: refresh 14.0 s, idle expiry 33.4 s, edit 16.1 s.
- Mutation: `refreshInBackground` made a no-op (`if true || ...`). The refresh subtest FAILS after 240.00 s with `the instance is not replaced` / `the Secret gets the second token before the first expires`, the same trace as CI. Reverted.
- `make fmt`, `make lint`: clean.
- Not run: under-load reproduction (the local cluster is not loaded the way CI's is) and the full e2e suite (CI runs it).

## Self-check
Test-only change. No test deleted, skipped or weakened. No assertion or timeout changed. No tracking IDs in comments. No SPEC principle touched.

## Changelog
None (test only).

author: willchan
body:
## Why
Vercel free-tier Fluid Active CPU is at 3h41m of 4h; `/api/jobs/claim` dominates. The worker polled every 10 s, 24/7 (~8,640 calls/day, nearly all empty), and each call opened a transaction, swept leases, read all queued jobs and wrote an `api_request` row.

## Changes
1. **Worker:** idle backoff. Each empty poll, Ollama outage or API error doubles the wait from `POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (10) up to the new `POLL_MAX_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (120). A job or a restart resets it. Heartbeat is unchanged.
2. **Server:** an empty claim skips the `api_request` write. Real claims and every other route are still recorded, as are errors.
3. **Server:** `claimJob` first does one indexed `SELECT … LIMIT 1` (`audit_job_status_idx`) for a queued job of a requested type (never `storage_audit`) or an expired lease. The transaction and sweep run only if it finds one, so expired leases are still released and re-claimable. No migration is needed because the index already exists.

## Tests
- Worker: backoff doubles, caps and resets; the run loop backs off while Ollama is down.
- Web: an empty claim writes no row and a real one does (fails without the fix); an expired lease is re-claimed with nothing queued; type filtering.

Docs: DESIGN §3.1 (latency middleware), §3.2, the worker loop, env vars and §10 #93. PRD is unchanged because nothing is user-visible.

Estimated reduction: about 8,640 calls/day → at most 720/day when idle (−92%). Each is now a single read, with no transaction and no telemetry write.

`make check` passed locally except `deploy-test`, because `bats` isn't installed in this container.

author: resec
body:
## Linked issue

Closes #50

## Change

- Change name under `openspec/changes/`: `fix-review-blocked-next-action`
- One-sentence summary: 最新报告为 `blocked` 且没有 finding 可处置时，`nextAction` 指向 `openspec_review action=resume review=<kind>`，不再指向会失败的 `dispose`。

## Root cause

`draftReadiness` 在 verdict 不是 `pass` 时正确地拒绝就绪，但 `nextAction` 只把「对象变化、finding 已 fixed、长度闸门、执行性预检」算作需要开新轮（`lib/review/readiness.js:91-97`）。评审无法进行时提交的 `blocked` 报告按契约不带 finding（`lib/tools/review.js:639`、`lib/review/report.js:175-181`），于是 `open` 为假、`needsRound` 也为假，落到 `openspec_review action=dispose review=<kind>`，而没有 finding 可供处置。规格里恢复路径是 `resume` 开新一轮（`change-review` 的「Resume continues a recorded review」），`dispose` 只在有 finding 为 `open` 时点名（`tool-surface` 的「Review next actions name the round entry」）。

## Scope

改动：

- `lib/review/readiness.js`：`needsRound` 纳入「最新报告 verdict 为 `blocked` 或 `changes-requested` 且没有 open finding」。有 open finding 仍是 `dispose`；无报告仍是 `wait`/`self-report`；对象变化、finding 已 fixed、长度闸门、执行性预检仍是 `resume`；`blockedReason: "stale-object"` 因对象已变本来就指向 `resume`，行为不变。
- 测试：`test/review-unit.test.mjs` 覆盖 self/reviewer × draft/apply 四种组合；`test/review-draft.test.mjs`（self draft）、`test/review-wait.test.mjs`（reviewer apply）、`test/review-reviewer.test.mjs`（reviewer draft，并给既有 stale blocked 用例补 `nextAction` 断言）走真实工具路径。
- 文档：`docs/review.md`、`README.md`、`skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md`、`skills/openspec-apply-change/SKILL.md` 写上这一步；`test/review-doc.test.mjs`、`test/skills.test.mjs` 守护对应措辞。
- `openspec/changes/fix-review-blocked-next-action/`：proposal 与 tasks（`skip_specs: true`，规格已要求该行为，只有实现落后）。

未改动：review 记录结构、报告契约与 finding 生命周期、`change-review` 与 `tool-surface` 规格（未合并也未依赖 PR #150）、依赖、workflow、hooks、`coverage.baseline.json`、`dist/`、`package-lock.json`。

## Evidence

Node v24.22.2，实现提交 `2e9938f`，tasks 记录提交 `a8158cf`。

```text
node --test test/review-unit.test.mjs test/review-draft.test.mjs test/review-wait.test.mjs test/review-reviewer.test.mjs test/review-doc.test.mjs test/skills.test.mjs
→ tests 244, pass 244, fail 0

把 lib/review/readiness.js 回退到修改前（git stash push -- lib/review/readiness.js）：
→ review-unit 1 fail（a blocked report with no finding names the next round）
→ review-draft 1 fail（a blocked draft report without findings points the next action at resume）
→ review-reviewer 1 fail（a blocked reviewer report without findings points the next action at resume）
→ review-wait 1 fail（a blocked apply submit without findings points the next action at resume）
git stash pop 后全部通过

/tmp/b3/gates.sh fix-review-blocked-next-action
→ strict validate: Change 'fix-review-blocked-next-action' is valid（skip_specs accepted）
→ npm run openspec:check: 117 passed, 0 failed
→ requirement length gate: ok
→ generated skill check: ok
→ check:pr: ok
→ npm run verify: tests 1345, pass 1345, fail 0
   plugin 覆盖率：line 98.57%，branch 93.57%，function 99.21%
   新增代码：line 100.00%，branch 100.00%，violations none
```

- Commit SHA: `2e9938f`（实现与测试）、`12b13c4`（change）、`a8158cf`（tasks 与验证记录）
- Test result: 1345/1345 通过
- Coverage summary: line 98.57% / branch 93.57% / function 99.21%；新增代码 100.00% / 100.00% / n/a

## Problem
OAuth connects (LinkedIn, meeting providers, integrations) started from a local dev server on a port other than 8080/8081 — e.g. `localhost:9000` — fail on the callback with **"Invalid or expired sign-in request."** `assertAllowedOrigin` rejects the origin captured in the signed state.

## Fix
In `src/lib/oauth-state.ts`, dev builds (`import.meta.env.DEV`) also accept `http://localhost:<port>`. Vite sets `DEV` to false in production builds, so the production allowlist (`PUBLIC_SITE_URL`) is unchanged. Optional chaining keeps the module safe outside Vite.

LinkedIn Connect on `localhost:9000` completed end-to-end after the change; before it, the callback returned 400.

author: code-acrobat
body:
## What

Security-advisory lookups are part of the proxy's curated tool surface instead of an opt-in.

- **On by default:** with `GITHUB_MCP_TOOLSETS` unset the proxy injects `default,security_advisories`. `x-mcp-toolsets` is now always injected, so a client can still narrow the list but never widen it (the absent-key "client header passes through" path is gone — that was the only way to reach upstream's bare default, and it was also the only client-controlled widening path).
- **Scope exemption, narrow on purpose:** `list_global_security_advisories` and `get_global_security_advisory` take no `owner`/`org`/`repository` argument, so `GITHUB_MCP_SCOPE` no longer refuses them — CVE triage works under an owner scope. `list_repository_security_advisories` / `list_org_repository_security_advisories` do name a subject and remain bounded like every other call.
- Rules re-stamped for the larger inventory (54 tools); README/AGENTS/skill updated.

## Why

A CVE lookup is routine work, and the proxy is *our* curation of the upstream server — a toolset nobody remembers to add is a toolset nobody has. Making it the default also means the curated surface is the same everywhere instead of depending on which env file a machine happens to carry.

## Verification

Live against the hosted endpoint, through the running proxy (54 tools registered, policy `default,actions,security_advisories`, scope active):

```
list_global_security_advisories {affects: "org.springframework:spring-core", ecosystem: "maven"}
  -> GHSA-659m-px2c-25wj (Spring Framework DoS via AntPathMatcher, CWE-1333, CVSS 3.7) + more
get_global_security_advisory {ghsaId: "GHSA-659m-px2c-25wj"}   -> full record
list_org_repository_security_advisories {org: "evil"}          -> blocked by github-mcp-proxy policy: scope: ... outside GITHUB_MCP_SCOPE
```

`--stamp` on a real install reported `inventory: +4 [get_global_security_advisory, list_global_security_advisories, list_org_repository_security_advisories, list_repository_security_advisories], -0`, 54/54, and `check` exits 0.

Offline gates: `node --check`, `--selftest` (new cases: global lookup exempt, repo/org advisory tools still subject-checked, empty scope still allows the global lookup), `tests/validate.sh`.

## Note for the reviewer

One fix rides along in `tests/e2e.sh`: `stampit` now sources the section's env file. It previously stamped under the caller's shell policy while `up` loaded the file, so the toolsets/readonly sections ran under a schema lock without any assertion noticing (they only check `tools/list`, which the lock does not block). Without that fix the new scope assertion would have failed for the wrong reason.

Merging stays a human action (still in `deny_tools`).

author: bjschnell
body:
## Problem
Tests act as a human with `setsid -f script -qec <line>`, so the daemon sees a process outside every session. When `cargo test` runs under an agent, that human's command was sometimes refused as the agent's ("adopting a session into the backlog is for the user, not claude"). It only happens locally under an agent, not on CI, but it gives agents running the suite false failures.

## Root cause
`setsid -f` forks and its parent exits. For a moment that parent has released its memory (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is empty) but its children haven't been reparented yet. A command that reaches the daemon in that window gets walked `valk → bash → script → <exiting setsid> → test binary → … → claude`, and the daemon correctly takes it for claude's. I confirmed this with a temporary trace in `Registry::caller` (not in this PR): both refused calls showed exactly that chain.

The daemon's check is right and stays as it is. Stopping the walk at a session boundary would let an agent's plain `script -qec 'valk …'` pass as human.

## Fix (tests only)
`crates/valkyrie/tests/common/mod.rs` adds `after_setsid(line) -> (String, Gate)`. The line waits for a gate file, which is written when the `Gate` drops, after `.status()` has reaped setsid's parent, so the child has already been reparented by then. The wait is a plain `timeout 30 sh -c '…'` command, because `script` runs the line with `$SHELL`. All 12 human call sites in `backlog.rs`, `context.rs`, `docs.rs` and `worktree.rs` use it. Two sites that aren't inside a closure drop the gate explicitly.

## Evidence
Stress test: `the_user_adopts_an_ad_hoc_session_into_the_backlog`, run from an agent shell with 4 CPU hogs and 80 parallel copies pinned to one CPU.
- Before: 3 of 320 refused as the agent (6 of 320 failed in all).
- After: 0 of 480 refused. The 2 failures left were "daemon did not start", the client's startup deadline under that extreme load, which is unrelated.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass, and no gate files are left behind.

## Cause
`BrandingWordmark` and `BrandingAppearance` (`apps/cockpit/src/features/settings/ui/branding-mark.tsx`) always rendered `session.tenant.display_name` as the wordmark name and document title once branding was configured. The saved branding `display_name` (`session.branding.display_name`, already part of the bootstrap payload and the generated `CockpitBootstrapResponse` type) was ignored.

## Fix
New pure model function `brandingWorkspaceName(session, installed)` in `features/settings/model/branding.ts`:
- branding configured with a non-blank saved name -> saved branding name
- configured without/blank name, or installed app -> workspace name
- otherwise -> `null`, the UI keeps `t("app.name")`

The wordmark name and document title both use it. The subtitle line and `BrandingAttribution` are unchanged.

## Tests
- `bun test src/features/settings/model/branding.test.ts`: 12 pass, 0 fail (4 new cases; the new test failed before the implementation existed)
- `bun test src/features/settings src/app src/components/cockpit/patterns/workspace-surfaces.test.tsx`: 644 pass, 1 fail. The failure is in `pattern-imports.test.ts` (`features/workflows/ui/automation-panel.tsx: heading`), which already fails on origin/main. This PR does not touch that file.
- cockpit `tsc --noEmit`, biome and the pre-push `verify` gate (36/36 invariants) pass

Refs #523

author: jalirkan
body:
## Why
When a land of a new colour arrives, the half board changes place (Araucanía + Island = Hawaii). Until now that was a cross-fade between two paintings in which nothing lined up. The owner's rule: a new mana evolves the landscape, it does not redraw it.

## What
- **places-v4** (scenery repo tags `places-v4`, `-p1`, `-p2`): every place keeps its lands left to right in one order (Island, Swamp, Plains, Forest, Mountain). Nine places were re-laid (their sites and all six stage pieces moved as painted, only the nature between repainted), five mirrored. Three four-land places keep one land out of order (Cape Town, Zanzibar, Kathmandu).
- **Spec 1.23**: on a place change the panel zooms and slides so the lands both places share travel from where they stood to where they stand, while the pictures cross-fade. The map is fitted on the largest in-order subset of shared lands whose scale is inside [0.5, 2]; other shared lands just cross-fade. Three layers while it runs (the new place settled underneath, the new place moving, the old place moving and fading), so no frame edge shows. Settled state is exactly 1.22's. Reduced motion, a shape change, or no usable subset: the plain cross-fade.
- A change straight back mid-move lets the move finish, then cross-fades back plainly.

## Checked
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (212 files, 3304 tests), `npm run build`: green.
- `npm run e2e:ambience`: 33 PASS, 0 FAIL, places-v4 served from disk; Cusco → Sicily and Araucanía → Hawaii at both shapes: tracked lands 0.0 px apart at 42% of the move, the under layer covers the half, one bare frame when settled.
- `npm run test:e2e`: 29 passed.
- On places-v4: 74 of the 75 one-land steps move (12 leave one land untracked); Valley of Mexico → Santorini is refused for scale.
- Independent review: no blocker; its two findings (scale-aware subset choice, the pop on a change straight back) are fixed here.
- Played by hand on the dev page against the published pack, desktop and phone width: Araucanía + Island moves and settles on Hawaii.

## Not checked
- Only Chromium was run. The change-straight-back hold is covered by unit and static DOM tests, not played in a browser. No phone-device performance measurement of the three masked layers. No lifecycle test of the stateful panel under a DOM with effects.

Part of the fleet-review work (gRParse #393). This PR is stacked on #44, the second document.proto sweep (gRParse #465), and has #43 merged in. Merge #43 and #44 first, then this one.

## What

The METS reader only read the `dmdSec` elements that MODS and Dublin Core share. It dropped `dc:type`, `dc:source`, `dc:format`, `dc:coverage` and `dc:relation` without saying so, so a catalogue record lost its relations and its resource type.

- `descriptive_field` now reads all five elements.
- Wire: `MetaDescriptive` gains `optional string scheme = 3` (the element's `@type` or `@xsi:type`) and `optional string language = 4` (its `xml:lang`). Both are additive, and `buf breaking` passes.
- Fold: each of these statements becomes a `DocumentMeta.dublin_core` entry, in record order, with its scheme and language. `extra` stays empty.
- docs/design.md is updated.

## Test

The tests were written first. The GBS catalogued fixture gains a `dc:type xsi:type="dcterms:DCMIType"`, a source, a format, a coverage and two relations, one of them with `xml:lang="de"`.

- `a_dmd_sec_decodes_into_the_typed_shapes_that_already_exist_for_it` now expects the six wire statements.
- The new test `a_catalogue_record_keeps_every_dublin_core_statement` expects the six `DublinCoreStatement`s.

Both tests failed before the change, because the statements were missing. The full `cargo test --locked` suite, fmt, pedantic clippy, rustdoc, `buf lint`, `buf format` and `buf breaking` all pass.

gRParse note: if gRParse vendors xml.proto, it needs the two new `MetaDescriptive` fields.

author: coopbri
body:
## Description

##### Task link: n/a

Launch hardening for authorization and billing, the workspace profile, and a dependency upgrade.

**Security fixes (launch blockers):**

- **Cross-workspace read by id.** Single-row lookups (`person(rowId:)`, `invoice(rowId:)`, every table, and the `...ById` variants) checked `organizationId` on the raw row tuple, never found it, and returned any workspace's row to any signed-in user. Verified on master with the new test. Single-row lookups are now filtered in SQL exactly like collections.
- **Creates of organization settings always failed** for real users: the mutation guard looked up the new row under `organizationSettings` while the input key is `organizationSetting`.
- **TLS verification was disabled** for every outgoing request (`NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` at the top of `server.ts`), in production too. A local stack now opts out explicitly; production ignores it.
- Sales channel `credentials` are never served through GraphQL.
- GraphQL variables and results are no longer exported to traces (they carry customer records).

**Roles (Warden):** owners and admins only for organization settings (profile), document numbering, and sales channel connections (read and write). Access tokens carry workspace ids only, so roles come from Gatekeeper userinfo (cached per user for a minute); membership still comes only from the token, and a failed lookup fails admin-only actions closed. Warden is layered on like crystal-api: it can only add denials, runs in shadow mode unless `WARDEN_ENFORCE=true`, and an unreachable Warden falls back to the JWT. Self-hosted personal workspaces are their caller's own (owner).

**Plan limits (Aether, app id `mantle`):**

- Aether answers: the workspace's plan (no billing account = free tier). Unreachable: last known plan, else fail open. Billing not configured (self-host): no limits. Limits only ever gate creates; reads, edits and deletes are never blocked.
- `max_contacts` counts every person (marking contacts internal no longer bypasses it), including moves into a full workspace. `max_invoices_per_month` counts creations from a new `usage_event` ledger, so deleting an invoice frees no slot. Checked before the write and re-counted after it (an over-limit create is undone), so concurrent creates cannot exceed it.
- Removed the `max_team_members` check on company members (it capped contacts per client company at 1 on Free). That limit is workspace seats, managed in the account hub, so Mantle reports it but does not enforce it.
- New `workspacePlan(organizationId)` query: tier, how it was resolved, limits and usage.

**Also:** workspace profile columns on `organization_settings`; inventory adjustments now move `product.current_quantity` (delete reverses; an adjustment's product and quantity can no longer be edited); test runs get their own Postgres container (fixed name/port made concurrent runs tear each other down).

**Dependencies:** Postgraphile 5.2, grafast 1.2, Drizzle 0.45.4, providers v0.4.1, OpenTelemetry 0.301 / 3.x, TypeScript 7, Biome 2.6.8, knip 6, Changesets 3. Generated schema unchanged apart from ordering; Bun pin untouched. drizzle-kit scripts run under the Bun runtime (Node could not load `@omnidotdev/providers/invoicing`).

**Migrations:** one new migration, `0029_clear_swarm` (usage ledger + profile columns), 30 total. Not squashed.

**Needed to enforce limits in production:** omnidotdev/aether-api (Mantle entitlement grant) and omnidotdev/infra (Aether/Warden env and keys). Until both land, mantle-api has no `BILLING_BASE_URL` and applies no plan limits.

Changesets: `plan-limits-and-roles` (minor), `workspace-profile` (minor), `inventory-stock-sync` (patch), `tls-verification` (patch).

## Test Steps

1. `bun test`: 145 pass. New: `workspaceIsolationAllTables` (17 tables x anonymous and another workspace: list, single row, update, delete; child-row attach; credentials; roles), `planLimits` (limits, delete-does-not-free, moves, last known plan, outage fail-open, network error, no account, unconfigured, bypass, `workspacePlan`), `wardenRoles`, `inventoryAdjustment`, extended `organizationSettings`, unit `entitlements` and `workspaceRoles`.
2. `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun biome check`, `bun knip`, `bun run build` are clean.
3. Boot with only `DATABASE_URL`: warnings for billing, Warden, Vortex, IdP webhook and flags; `/health` ok.
4. End to end with a local JWKS/userinfo stub and a slim token: a `member` is refused `createOrganizationSetting` (FORBIDDEN), an `owner` succeeds.

author: halonic-dev
body:
## What and why

T14 PR 15a (HAL-16807, plan in HAL-1307): the code editor's half of AI changes 1.2, "In a file": "green and red lines in place, with **Accept** and **Reject** per part".

`@halonicjs/studio-code-editor` gets a `review` option and two methods:

- `setReviewParts(parts)` marks each part of the assistant's changes to review: every added line on `success-soft`, the removed lines struck through in `danger` on `danger-soft` above where they were (after the text when they were the last lines), and each part as a group named by its owner ("Change 1 of 3") with its own **Accept** and **Reject**. Reject reads "Reject and delete file" on the only part of a file the assistant created (review panel note 3). The marks follow the text while the user types; a new list replaces the old one.
- `goToReviewPart(index)` puts the cursor on a part's first line, scrolls to it and focuses the editor, for the item bar's Previous and Next.
- The buttons tell the owner `(part, "accept" | "reject")`; the owner gives the words, so the editor has none of its own.

Nothing uses it yet. The file's tab wires it to the review service, the item bar (Accept file, Reject file) and the toasts in PR 15b (HAL-17298, branch `tomas/HAL-17298-file-tab-review`, stacked on this one). The split keeps each PR near the 400-line guide.

Approved sources this copies (HAL-16355): AI changes 1.2 "In a file" (HAL-3228); words Accept, Reject, "Reject and delete file" and the spoken "Change 1 of 3" from the shell's `itemReviewWords` (14a, #5528); checklist part 1, 1.5 (added lines `success-soft`, removed `danger-soft`) and 1.6 (no key decides: only a click, or Enter or Space on the focused button). No H row in the states doc section 4 covers the code editor; those rows are the chat panel.

## Requirements

- code-editor.review-parts (new)

## How tested

New `review-parts.test.ts` (jsdom, the real CodeMirror): marks and struck-through lines, the group's name and buttons, "Reject and delete file", which part and decision reach the owner, marks following an edit above them, clearing, a part removed at the end, and going to a part.

Local check: shared (adds to the editor's exported interface): `pnpm exec turbo run typecheck` on the editor, files, shell and the Studio app, the editor's tests, `biome check`, and `pnpm check` passed on `682495b4e`, rebased on `origin/main` (`dd3d6debf`). The editor stand-in in `features/files` now has `setReviewParts` and `goToReviewPart` (the first CI run failed its typecheck without them).

## Docs

None needed: the requirement records the behaviour; the editor has no user docs of its own.

## Changeset

None (no user-visible change): nothing draws the parts until PR 15b and the app's review service.

Claude Code / claude-opus-5-5

- [ ] Every commit is signed off by me (`git commit -s`) under the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/), and I have run and understood this change.

자료집 → 전투 → 도트 연출 목록(150행)과 이펙트 갤러리(48장)의 움직이는 썸네일이 **전부 계속 재생**되던 것을, 기본은 첫 칸 그림으로 두고 **마우스를 올린 것·키보드로 고른 것·선택된 행/카드만** 재생하게 바꿨다. CSS 한 곳(`src/styles/database/retro-gallery.css`)만 바뀐다. testid·DOM 은 그대로다.

움직임 줄이기 설정(`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`)에서는 예전처럼 아무것도 재생하지 않는다(재생 규칙을 `no-preference` 안에 넣었다). 그림 없는 칸(`.db-retro-thumb-missing`)도 재생하지 않는다.

## 왜 (오너 2026-11-24 앱 QA 항목 5 「도트 연출 섹션이 렉이 너무 걸림」)
계획 http://mdc2:18301/qa1124-dot-life.html. 같은 박스·같은 프로브(`measure.mjs`, headless Chromium 1440×900, `?freshProject=1`)로 잰 값:

| | 수정 전 (main db72bbc98) | 이 PR 만 | 이 PR + D2(무대 가두기) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 실행 중 CSS 애니메이션 | 150 | 1 (마우스 올리면 2) | 1 |
| 3초 트레이스 Paint / 프레임 | 127.7 | 127.5 | **4.8** |

이 PR 하나로는 페인트 수가 줄지 않는다. 무대가 매 프레임 자료집 전체를 다시 배치하면서 썸네일도 같이 다시 그리기 때문이다. 다음 PR(D2, 무대 `contain` + `translate`)과 합쳐야 128 → 4.8 이 된다. 두 PR 은 서로 의존하지 않고, 이 PR 이 없으면 D2 뒤에도 썸네일 150개가 계속 돈다.

## 위험
- 목록에서 「움직임으로 고르던」 느낌이 줄어든다 → 마우스 올림·선택 행은 그대로 움직인다(리드 결정 D4: 목록 썸네일은 정지, 큰 미리보기는 반복 재생).

No test: CSS 재생 조건만 바뀌었고 jsdom 은 CSS 애니메이션을 계산하지 않는다. 증거는 실제 Chromium 트레이스(위 표)와 1440·390 캡처다.

author: btypeace
body:
### Summary
- `src/modules/app.py` caps `log_history` at 100 entries, so reloading the Home tab displays at most 100 logs.
- However, while the Home tab remains open during a session, `log()` in `src/webapp/scripts/tabs/home.js` appended every new `.log-entry` node to `#logs` without pruning old ones and ran `filterLogs()` across all DOM nodes on every message.
- Cap `#logs` at `MAX_LOG_ENTRIES = 100` to match the backend history cap and keep live log rendering and filtering constant-time during long runs.

author: mattmoor
body:
Fixes #922
Refs #397

## What

A guard test, `sys::tests::raw_writes_only_at_listed_sites`, that turns theorem 4's "no other write reaches user memory" from an unchecked discipline into a checked one (#397, "Check that only `vspec::user` calls the raw write primitives on user memory").

Over the shipped sources (`shipped_lines`, the scan the grant tests in the same file use), every call of a raw write primitive must be in a listed function, the listed number of times:

- `core::ptr`'s `write_bytes`, `copy_nonoverlapping`, `copy`, `write`, `write_volatile`, `write_unaligned`, `swap`, `swap_nonoverlapping`, `replace`, and the pointer-method forms but `.swap(` and `.replace(` (names `Option` and the atomics share; stated as not covered);
- the wrappers `vspec::zero::zero_raw` and `vspec::user::copy_raw` (their declarations are not calls).
- a free primitive matches as a path ending in its `ptr` segment, whatever follows (call, turbofish `ptr::write_bytes::<u8>(`, or value `let f = ptr::write;`); a pointer method as a method call (`.write(`) or a qualified path (`<*mut u8>::write(`, `NonNull::write(`); the primitives' `assume_specification` lines and `use` lines are not uses.
- and a `use` item of any visibility (`pub(in ..)` included) that imports a primitive from a `ptr` path segment (`core::ptr::`, `std::ptr::`, or `ptr::` after `use core::ptr;`) by name or by glob is rejected, so a bare call (`write(p, v)`) cannot slip past.

The 14 listed functions, by the memory they write (also in the test's doc):

| memory | functions |
|---|---|
| user memory, with the block's `UserMem` | `vspec::user::zero_user`, `copy_raw`, `copy_user`; `vspec::zero::zero_raw` |
| the C caller's buffers (`c_buffer`, `c_writes`) | `api::mallctl::copy_prefix`, `store`, `store_triple` (3), `mib_out` (2) |
| metadata initialised in place through its permission | `Arena::put_stats`, `stats::zero_records`, `cgroup::untracked_in_place` (2), `Meta::alloc_zeroed` (`zero_raw` on `Meta`'s own `PointsToRaw`) |
| one huge-region byte apart from every live run (`apart_from_runs`) | `huge::kernel::write_zero` |
| the `malloc_message` static, test only | `api::jemalloc::set_message_hook_for_tests` (`#[cfg(test)]`) |

THEOREMS.md (theorem 4, user-block writes) and the guard-test table in verus/README.md cite the test.

Not covered, stated in the test's doc and in THEOREMS.md: a write through a dereferenced raw pointer in a trusted body (the methods `.swap(` and `.replace(`; `*p = v`, an atomic `(*p).store(..)` such as `vspec::atom::store_usize_at`'s to metadata words, a write to a slice from `from_raw_parts_mut`), and a use through a renamed module (`use core::ptr as p;`) or a macro.

## Checks

- `cargo test --lib raw_writes_only_at_listed_sites`: passes at the head.
- Mutants, each reverted:
  - M1: a `core::ptr::write_bytes(p, 0, 1)` added in `heap::paths::zero_slot` (an unlisted function): dies, "a raw memory write in `pub(super) unsafe fn zero_slot(`, which is not one of the listed sites".
  - M2: a second write, `(addr as *mut u8).add(1).write(0)`, in the listed `huge::kernel::write_zero`: dies, "got = 2 raw memory writes, want = 1".
  - M3: `core::ptr::write_bytes::<u8>(p, 0, 1)` added in `heap::paths::zero_slot` (turbofish form): dies, same message as M1.
  - M4: `use core::ptr::write;` with `unsafe { write(p, 0u8) }` in `zero_slot`: dies at the `use` ("imports a raw write primitive of `ptr` by name or by glob").
  - M5: a multi-line `use core::ptr::{ NonNull, copy, };` with `unsafe { copy(p, p, 1) }` in `zero_slot`: dies, same message, on the joined item.
  - M6: `use ptr::{copy, write};` (through `heap::paths`' `use core::ptr;`) with `unsafe { write::<u8>(p, 0) }` in `zero_slot`: dies at the `use`.
  - M7: `ptr::replace(p as *mut usize, 0)` in `zero_slot`: dies, same message as M1.
  - M8: `<*mut u8>::write(p, 0)` in `zero_slot` (qualified method): dies.
  - M9: `let f: unsafe fn(*mut u8, u8) = ptr::write;` in `zero_slot` (value form): dies.
  - M10: `pub(in crate::heap) use core::ptr::write;` with `write(p, 0u8)` in `zero_slot`: dies at the `use`.
  - M3 re-run against the reworked matcher at a8f3cdd7: dies.
  - M11: `use core::ptr; // for X` in `heap::paths` with `p.write(0)` in `zero_slot`: dies on the write (the `use` join drops a trailing comment, and asserts it never takes in a `fn` item).
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --lib --tests`: clean.

## Proof and runtime

Test and docs only: no proof, no exec code, no trusted item changes, so the counter does not move and there is no seams change. Codegen at 19dd5cf3 (test-only change since): `.text` IDENTICAL in all four profiles (x86_64 q16 and q8, aarch64 q16 and q8). Closes no upstream issue.

author: arif5620
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"arif5620"} -->
_Requested by **Arif** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GRLaU9bKFYQca9w2RiWnpN?thread=cmsg_01GRLaU9bKFYQca9w2RiWnpNMnE9xXu87p1mqTdbS1fVAe)_

A whole-site review pass. The design is unchanged. `npm run lint`, `tsc --noEmit` and `next build` all pass. I checked the production build in Chromium at 360, 768 and 1280px in both the light and dark themes, and no page scrolls sideways.

## Bugs
- **Listing prices were nearly invisible in light mode.** The dark text sat on a dark photo gradient. It is now white.
- **The WhatsApp label in the mobile action bar had low contrast** on the light theme. It now uses a darker green there.
- **Unknown blog URLs crashed with a 500** when the Sanity lookup failed. They now return a proper 404 and the page is marked noindex.
- **New Sanity posts never appeared until a redeploy**, because the home page, /blog, posts and the sitemap were fully static. They now refresh hourly (ISR, revalidate 3600).
- The hero's WebGL check left an extra GPU context open. It is now released right away.
- Mobile menu: Escape now closes it, the page no longer scrolls underneath it, and it reports `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.

## Mobile
- On the service-area cards, the city name and its tagline now wrap cleanly instead of colliding on narrow phones.
- The passive scroll listener on the navbar keeps scrolling smoother.

## Page speed
- The 3D city hero now loads once the browser is idle, so it doesn't delay first paint. It is skipped when the visitor has Data Saver on, and the photo stays as the fallback.
- Images are now served as AVIF or WebP (`images.formats`).
- Removed about 32 MB of unused files left over from the old portfolio (`public/projects`, `public/Blog`, `public/videos`, the default Next.js SVGs, and the old `Arif-CV.pdf`, which nothing links to).
- Removed the unused `resend` and `react-countup` packages and the unused `sanity/lib/live.ts`.

## SEO
- **New 1200×630 share card** (`app/opengraph-image.tsx`) for Facebook, WhatsApp, LinkedIn and X. Before, the square profile photo was used and got cropped.
- Blog posts now have complete Open Graph and Twitter tags (title, description, URL, publish date, image) and `BlogPosting` structured data.
- The sitemap now lists every article, including Sanity posts, with last-modified dates.
- `robots.txt` and the sitemap now take the domain from `profile.website` instead of a hard-coded copy. The value is unchanged: `https://arifsarkar.com`, which `main` already used for canonical URLs, robots and the sitemap.
- Added a `theme-color` for each theme.
- Gave the agent structured data an `@id` so articles can reference it.
- Semantic and accessibility fixes: form fields have labels and autofill hints, the toggle buttons use `aria-pressed`, icon-only stats have screen-reader text, decorative elements are hidden from screen readers, and the footer brand is no longer a stray `<h2>`.

## Cleanup
- The README now describes this project and says where to edit things.
- Added `.env.example` with the required Sanity variables.

## Still to do (content, not code)
- **Listings** in `src/data/properties.ts` are still sample data with stock photos.
- **`src/data/deals.ts`** is empty, so the deal pins on the map are hidden in production.

author: aaron-amit
body:
Order tracking now follows the client's requirements PDF.

| # | Stage (new names in bold) |
|---|---|
| 1 | In design |
| 2 | **In QA** |
| 3 | **Waiting for DWG confirmation** |
| 4 | **Waiting for estimate confirmation** |
| 5 | **Waiting for advance confirmation** |
| 6 | **In production** (new) |
| 7 | **Profile cutting** |
| 8 | Glass cutting (moved here, right after profile cutting) |
| 9 | **Profile drill** |
| 10 | **Hinge hole** |
| 11 | Assembly |
| 12 | **Packing** |
| 13 | **Route planning** (new) |
| 14 | Dispatched |
| 15 | Delivered |

"On hold for procurement" stays a hold that keeps the order's stage, not a stage of its own. A held order still can't move forward in production. Stages 6 to 13 count as production: prices and items lock from "In production" on.

## Data
- **No order changes stage.** The stored stage keys are unchanged. Only labels and order change, and two values are added.
- **Migration `0004`** rebuilds the `order_stage` type in the new order. It drops the column default before converting and sets it again afterwards. Drizzle's generated version set the default while the column was still text, which Postgres may refuse to convert.
- **Tested on a copy of the local database.** 93 orders, 4 holds and 1,058 history entries were identical before and after, and new orders still start "In design". An empty database migrates cleanly too.

## Code
- `PRODUCTION_STAGES` drives the "In production" filter and the stage track, instead of hand-written lists.
- Short labels in the track and charts strip "Waiting for" instead of the old "Awaiting".
- The stage track's columns can shrink (`minmax(0, …)`). With eight production stages, the Delivery group was pushed 96px past the edge at desktop width.
- The demo data script uses the new flow.

## Checked
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @vawe/shared test`, `pnpm build` pass.
- **API:** a demo order was moved through every stage from "In production" to "Dispatched", and each move was recorded. A held order was refused when moving forward. The production filter returns the new stages.
- **Browser at 1366px and 390px:** order page, Orders overview, the In production tab and the Overview. No horizontal overflow and no console errors.

author: avaargsh
body:
## Scope
Refs #56 — fix a deterministic false positive in the PostgreSQL runtime-role external-schema audit and add repeated PostgreSQL package stress coverage.

PostgreSQL grants EXECUTE on new functions to PUBLIC by default. A restricted application/dispatcher LOGIN can therefore see migration-owned, zero-argument, non-SECURITY-DEFINER trigger callbacks in a separate schema after PUBLIC receives USAGE. The external-schema audit previously treated those trigger-only functions as callable external capabilities and rejected an otherwise valid runtime role.

The verifier now exempts only the three known non-SECURITY-DEFINER, zero-argument functions returning pg_catalog.trigger: reject_decision_record_mutation, reject_decision_outbox_identity_mutation and reject_decision_outbox_delete. Ordinary external SECURITY INVOKER functions and SECURITY DEFINER functions remain rejected. External relations/sequences and external CREATE privileges remain checked as before.

Regression tests create a second migrated schema, grant PUBLIC USAGE, assert the three trigger callbacks are executable but do not cause false rejection, then prove both ordinary external INVOKER and SECURITY DEFINER routines are still rejected for application and dispatcher identities. A repeated restart-replay fixture now uses unique tenant/invocation/run identifiers so -count=3 runs do not collide.

CI repeats the PostgreSQL Outbox catalog-restoration scenario 20 times under race and runs the full Decision and Outbox package suites three times concurrently against PostgreSQL 16 before the full suite.

## Governance metadata
- Target branch (main or internal feature parent); exact base/head commit SHAs: main base=eb2cdf70c82aeb10863129108c6f00959ed09443; head=f2be5180bf619a1bd6c533bc89acb38c082c6ca7
- Change class (classification): internal PostgreSQL runtime-role audit logic, integration tests, and CI configuration. No migration SQL/checksum, public API, persisted schema, provider, permit, or protected-effect change.
- Affected domain / sole authoritative writer: PostgreSQL Decision runtime-role verification only. Existing migrator remains the sole schema/migration writer; this change does not add a database writer.
- Governance gate(s): #56 narrow false-positive correction and repeatable PostgreSQL test coverage. The historical intermittent Outbox trigger-restoration/catalog failure's root cause remains unproven; #56 stays open.

## Evidence (link real CI runs)
- Test/CI evidence at exact HEAD (run URL or explicit no-workflow reason): exact-head Push CI SUCCESS at https://github.com/avaargsh/agent-decision/actions/runs/45346912449. It passed PostgreSQL 16, Go race, the 20-iteration Outbox restoration test, the repeated go test -race -count=3 ./internal/decision ./internal/outbox package suites, full go test -race ./... and go vet ./.... TDD RED run 45345975275 at https://github.com/avaargsh/agent-decision/actions/runs/45345975275 failed as expected at TestRuntimeDatabaseRolePrivileges with effective access to an unreviewed external schema object when only the safe trigger callback fixture was present; exact-head GREEN is linked above.
- Authorization/recovery negative-case evidence or explained N/A: no authorization, permit, execution, recovery, or evidence-signing behavior changes. The new negative cases prove that unreviewed external INVOKER and DEFINER routines still fail closed for both runtime roles; existing lease and immutable-ledger negative tests remain in the full suite.

## Delivery / rollback
- Remaining blockers and explicit non-goals: the original intermittent Outbox restoration failure has not been reproduced by the 20-iteration or three-run package stress gates; this PR fixes a separately reproduced deterministic false positive and adds detection coverage, not the historical root cause. Production role deployment, restore/PITR and G02/G05 remain separate gates.
- Backward compatibility and rollback: no schema/migration/checksum or API changes. Revert the PR to restore the previous stricter external routine check and remove repeated CI steps if necessary.
- Main promotion vs internal-only merge decision, with rationale: promote this bounded correctness fix after exact-head PR CI and evidence declaration pass; keep #56 open for the original intermittent failure root-cause work.
- Required GitHub branch rules/required status checks verified independently (or current status UNKNOWN): repository rulesets endpoint returned an empty list; branch-protection endpoint was inaccessible (403), so status is UNKNOWN.

author: minhworker
body:
Closes #352.

## Summary

The Three.js client for Cờ Tỷ Phú, on the approved board look. Pushes are queued and played one after another (the computer's moves arrive at once), then the newest view's decision is shown.

```text
games/co-ty-phu/client/
├── main.ts        # Bridge: queue of views, init redraws, done after the end
├── decisions.ts   # decide(view, seat, names): panel for every phase (tested)
├── present.ts     # changes(before, after): dice, walk/jump, Card, Lots, money (tested)
├── scene.ts       # board, tokens, dice, Lots, Festival/Blackout, tap a Tile
├── hud.ts         # player cards, panel, Card, Tile details, end
└── print.ts, special.ts, pieces.ts, ambience.ts   # moved from prototype/
```

```text
on match:state push
  new Match → stop what plays, redraw from its view
  else queue the view
play queue
  for each view: animate changes(shown, view), faster while more wait
  present(view) → decide(view) → buttons, or Tiles to tap (Sân bay, a Card's Lot)
on over → once the end has shown, bridge.done()
```

Decisions: buy, upgrade, Takeover (with prices), Sân bay (tap a Tile), jail (roll, pay, jail-free Card), Cards with two offers, a Lot or a player, the Quiz (4 big answers, clock) and the Debt with the suggested sale and "Bán theo gợi ý". Tapping any Tile shows its price and rent per Level. Server prices are reused: `economy.ts` takes a `BoardState` (a `State` or a `View`), and `cityRent`/`stationRent` are shared with the Tile details.

`smoke:web` now runs scenarios per Game; Cờ Tỷ Phú rolls, answers its next decision and opens a Tile. CI builds the Game for it.

## Evidence

- **Before:** no client; `npm run smoke:web` covered Đặt Bom only.
  **After:**
  ```text
  OK: dat-bom drew the arena, walked from x=0.5 to 1.62 and placed a bomb at (1, 0)
  OK: co-ty-phu drew the board, rolled 4+2, then "Mua 280", and showed Sân bay
  ```
