author: noemi-agent
body:
> ℹ️ **Base branch:** target `develop`, not `main`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md#branching-model](../CONTRIBUTING.md#branching-model).

## Summary

- Adds five checks to the shared AI reviewer (`.github/workflows/ai-review.yml`): **`AI Review (premise)`**, **`AI Review (framing)`**, **`AI Review (code)`**, **`AI Review (compliance)`** and **`AI Review (all gates)`**.
- A gate check succeeds **only** when that gate's verdict is exactly `pass` in a completed, non-dry-run review of the head commit the check is reported for. `AI Review (all gates)` succeeds only when all four gate checks succeed.
- Adds `scripts/review-gate-checks.js`, which holds the decision logic, with unit tests. It is added to the carve-out.
- `scripts/review-pr.js` writes the four verdicts and the reviewed head SHA to `REVIEW_RESULT_FILE` after a completed review and a posted comment. The file contains no findings text.
- Updates `docs/AI_REVIEW_GOVERNANCE.md` (§ Per-gate checks), `docs/examples/cross-model-review-setup.md` (Part 9 check names) and the notes in `templates/ci/ai-review-caller.yml`.

## Why This Change

`AI Review (advisory)` succeeds whenever the review run completes. That includes runs where a gate failed and runs that halted for human review, for example under the carve-out. The gate verdicts appear only in the review comment, so no status check can currently enforce a rule such as "merge only after all four AI review stages pass" (NewPush D1). This change reports each verdict as its own check so that branch protection can enforce such a rule.

## Semantics

| Situation | Gate checks | `AI Review (all gates)` |
|---|---|---|
| Verdict `pass` for this head commit | success | success only if all four passed |
| Verdict `fail`, `skipped`, `OVERRIDDEN` or missing | failure | failure |
| Halted for human review (carve-out, model floor, pin not callable) | failure | failure |
| Review step error, timeout or cancellation | failure | failure |
| Review covered a different commit, or head unknown | failure | failure |
| No review ran (e.g. fork PR before the `ai-review` label) | failure | failure |
| Tooling ref without per-gate support | failure ("per-gate results are unavailable") | failure |

**A skipped, declined, failed, halted, overridden or timed-out stage is not a pass.** The gate jobs run with `if: always()`, so they never report as *skipped*; GitHub would treat a skipped required check as passing. An override never turns a gate check green.

## Backward compatibility

- The existing check names and their behaviour are unchanged: `AI Review (advisory)` and `AI Review (fork notice)`, and under fleet callers `review / AI Review (advisory)` and `review / AI Review (fork notice)`. Existing required checks and `scripts/pr-merge-gate.js` keep working.
- The new jobs need **no token permissions** (`permissions: {}`). The evaluation step runs inside the existing advisory job with the permissions it already has. Fleet callers therefore need no change to their `permissions:` block.
- No triggers, secrets or variables are added.

## Check names that D1 would require

- In `project-noemi/agents`: `AI Review (premise)`, `AI Review (framing)`, `AI Review (code)`, `AI Review (compliance)`, or `AI Review (all gates)` alone.
- In fleet repositories using `templates/ci/ai-review-caller.yml` (job `review`): `review / AI Review (premise)` … `review / AI Review (all gates)`.
- In `project-noemi/code` (caller job named `AI Review`, project-noemi/code#11): `AI Review / AI Review (premise)` … `AI Review / AI Review (all gates)`. That caller pins `e5ed8501f2cac0cd1f4aca728bc449eea5438331`, so it would need its pin moved forward once this change reaches `main`.

Making any of these checks required is a separate branch-protection decision. This pull request changes no repository settings, branch protection or required checks.

## Stacked PRs

- [x] Not part of a stack
- [ ] Ship together with #N. Merge from the bottom up into develop.

## Audience Impact

- [ ] Client / Buyer path
- [ ] MSP / MSSP path
- [ ] Builder / Accelerator path
- [x] Internal repo contract only (fleet CI checks)

## Validation

- [x] `npm run validate`: audit passes; 799 tests pass, including 15 new tests in `tests/review-gate-checks.test.js`
- [x] `npm run test:e2e`: no failures (the suite's 3 tests are skipped locally)
- [x] `node scripts/generate_all.js`: no changes to generated outputs
- [x] `actionlint` on `.github/workflows/ai-review.yml` and `templates/ci/ai-review-caller.yml`: no findings

The tests cover the following:
- exact-`pass` only
- `fail`, `skipped`, `overridden` and missing verdicts
- halts, errors, timeouts and cancellations
- stale and unknown head SHAs
- dry runs and schema mismatches
- message sanitisation
- the CLI
- the `REVIEW_RESULT_FILE` writer in `review-pr.js`
- the carve-out entry
- the workflow structure (`if: always()`, `permissions: {}`, exact job names)
- the documented check names

## Security and Secrets

- [x] No real secrets were added to the repo
- [x] Fetch-on-Demand patterns were preserved (`infisical run` / `op run`)
- [x] `.env.template` / `.env.example` files remain inventories or vault references only

## Docs and Generated Outputs

- [x] README or docs were updated when behavior changed
- [x] Generated outputs were refreshed when inputs changed (none were affected)
- [ ] Golden fixtures were updated intentionally when generated sections changed (not applicable)

## Expected result on this pull request

This pull request edits `.github/workflows/ai-review.yml` and `scripts/review-pr.js`, which are both in the carve-out, so the reviewer is expected to halt for human review without invoking a model. On `pull_request`, the reviewer scripts are checked out from `main`, which does not yet contain `scripts/review-gate-checks.js`. The new gate checks are therefore expected to report failures on this pull request. That is the intended non-pass behaviour for both a halt and a tooling ref without per-gate support.

## Human review

This change affects CI gating and the reviewer's own behaviour. The automated reviewer halts on it by design. Points for the human reviewer:

1. **Decision logic** in `scripts/review-gate-checks.js` (`evaluateGateChecks`): every path other than an exact `pass` for the expected head SHA must return a non-pass.
2. **Head binding:** the expected head is `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`. For `workflow_dispatch` it is the PR's current head from the API. A review whose fetched head differs is a non-pass. Checks from `pull_request_target` and `workflow_dispatch` runs attach to the commit GitHub assigns to those runs, the same as the existing advisory check.
3. **Fork PRs:** on the unprivileged `pull_request` run, the gate checks report failures until a maintainer-gated privileged review runs. This is deliberate, because a skipped check would count as passing, but it does add red checks to unlabelled fork PRs.
4. **Rollout:** fleet callers pick this up when the change reaches `main` (callers pinned `@main`), or when a caller pinned to a commit moves its pin. Until then, the new checks do not appear in those repositories.
5. **Out of scope, possible follow-ups:** making the new checks required (an administrator decision; `scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh` is unchanged), and teaching `scripts/pr-merge-gate.js` about the per-gate checks.

## Notes for Reviewers

Fork PRs: a maintainer adds the `ai-review` label **once**; later pushes re-run
advisory while it remains. The unprivileged "AI Review (fork notice)" check may
warn; it is not a required status check.

author: ynishi
body:
`impact --within <ref>...` tells whether a change stays inside the documents it was meant for, and `--exit-code` fails when it does not.

## Why

`impact` answers which approvals a change makes not hold, but not whether they are inside the part of the shelf the change was meant for. When changes are worked on in parallel, each in its own checkout, nothing tells a change that it reached into documents another is working on, and no check could fail on it (F-70, REQ-45).

## What changes

- **The claim** (DEC-110): a document is claimed by the change when any of these, each with its owner, says so: the change adds a cause that makes its approval not hold, or takes one away (both directions read by `impact` in one pass, `both_ways`); a decision about it changes; it comes onto or leaves the shelf; its text or what its links name changes; or a record about it (an exemption, a same-meaning record) is at one end only or differs.
- **The place** (DEC-108): the reach of the named documents is walked on the shelf at the end before, whole, so a link the change adds cannot bring a document inside. A reference that names nothing before is read at the end after.
- **The verdict** (DEC-109), built in one place: `inside`, `outside`, `unproven` with why, or `undetermined`. A file or a ledger record whose identity cannot be read, at either end, keeps the gate from passing: what it is about cannot be told, and it is not guessed. The rule and its known limits are stated once, on the module page of `within`.
- **The command:** `within` in the JSON of impact, each verdict a tagged value; `--exit-code` requires `--within` and exits 1 when anything is outside, unproven or undetermined.
- **Books:** F-70, REQ-45, DEC-108, DEC-109, DEC-110, V-134 (unit) and V-135 (e2e) are new; DEC-106 is edited; the verifications made stale are approved again.

The issue's text was brought in line with what was built (the reach before is read whole; a link the change adds does not count).

## Checks

fmt, clippy, rustdoc, the whole test suite and the books gate pass.

Closes #174
Closes #112

## What's new
- **Dashboard home style** (Settings → Home screen → Dashboard): an OpenStreetMap map on the driver's side (left by default, or right; 50/60/70% wide) with up to 3 cards beside it (speed and music by default; only the first two, bigger, while driving), a top bar (time, weather, internet sign, favourites, all apps, settings) and a row with two saved places and the next prayer while parked.
- **The map** (`ui/MapView.kt`, `MapTiles.kt`, `TileMath.kt`): no new library. Own tile cache that follows the [OSM tile policy](https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/tiles/): HTTPS, CarHome's own User-Agent, only the tiles on screen, kept at least 7 days then refreshed with `If-None-Match`/`If-Modified-Since`, 60 MB on disk, 2 downloads at a time, credit always shown. Dark (colour matrix), light, or dark after sunset. Follows the car with a heading arrow, zooms out with speed (with a dead band so it doesn't flick), drag/pinch, + / − / back to my position. Saved places (tap to navigate) and speed cameras on it.
- **Next turn** (`NavParse.kt`, `MediaService.kt`): read from Google Maps' ongoing navigation notification through the notification access CarHome already has (title = distance, text/big text = instruction, sub text = arrival, large icon = turn arrow). Shown on top of the dashboard map; tap opens Google Maps.
- **Strip over Google Maps** (`StripView.kt`, `DriveService.kt`, off by default): while Google Maps navigates and CarHome is in the background, a 216 dp strip on the left or right with back to CarHome, hide (until the route ends), speed with the road limit, and the song with its buttons. Plain Android drawing like the bubble; the bubble hides while the strip is up.
- **Custom home**: two new widgets, **Map** (2×2 to 6×4) and **Next turn** (2×1 to 3×2).
- Settings: dashboard (side, width, places row, internet sign), cards, map (colours, zoom with speed, places, cameras), while navigating (next-turn card, strip on/off, side, contents) with access rows for notifications, overlay and location.
- Strings in English and Arabic, What's new, privacy policy (map tiles, next turn, strip) in both languages.

## What this PR does

Redesigns the whole frontend to the new "Retro Campus Board" look (from the Stitch designs) and
updates the flows to match the team's latest decisions. Frontend only: no backend or API changes.

## Design

- One theme only (no dark mode). Cream, papaya, sage and bronze colors with Fraunces (headings)
  and DM Sans (body).
- Design tokens and shared classes live in `src/index.css` (`.container`, `.eyebrow`,

- New shared components: `Navbar` (hamburger on mobile), `Footer`, `PageBand`, `Icons`,
  `CategoryArt`, `SafeImage`.

## Pages

- **View Report:** new title band, search and filters, 3/2/1 column card grid, pagination.
- **Report Details:** real `/reports/:id` page with a loading skeleton, a "not found" state, a
  "couldn't load" state with Try again, and a Copy contact button. The reporter name is never
  shown.
- **Submit Report:** new layout with Lost/Found pills.
  - The date label follows the type ("Date lost" / "Date found").
  - The photo is now an optional **Photo link** (http/https, max 2048). The file upload UI is
    removed.

  - A success banner links back to View Report.
- **About:** "how it works" cards and a Contributors section with GitHub links.
- A report with no photo, or a broken photo link, shows a category illustration instead.

## Product decisions applied

These override the older docs in `docs/` (to be updated separately):

- No sign-in, profile, edit or delete.
- Photo is a link, not an upload.
- `reporterName` is required but never shown publicly.

## Cleanup

- Removed the legacy CSS variable aliases from `index.css`. Nothing in `src/` uses them anymore.
- The old `.btn` styles went away when `SubmitReport.css` was replaced.

## How to test

- [x] `npm run build` finishes without errors
- [x] View Report: search, filters, sort, Reset, pagination, empty state
- [x] Open a report from a card; check the Copy contact button and the back link
- [x] Open a bad report URL; it should show "Report not found."
- [x] Submit: empty form shows errors and jumps to the first invalid field
- [x] Submit: Found changes the date label; bad photo link and bad email show errors
- [x] Submit: a valid report appears in View Report; no reporter name appears anywhere
- [x] About: cards and GitHub links work
- [x] Checked at 1440, 768 and 390 px: no sideways scroll, tap targets about 44px, visible focus ring

## Notes for reviewers

- `uploadReportImage` in `services/reportsApi.js` is now unused. I left it for a follow-up
  cleanup with the backend owner.
- The sort labels in `reportOptions.js` still say "Newest First / Oldest First"; the design says

author: microprediction
body:
Fixes #255. Fixes #256.

**#255.** A sign-in press whose recovery check was overtaken (by a second press, or by a root change heard from another tab) returned from `notice()` without an answer, and `proceed()` treated that as checked. Now:
- `notice()` returns the promise of the latest question (`latest`).
- `proceed()` awaits until no later question has replaced it, then reads `told()`.

The older-answer protection (`asked !== asking`) is unchanged. This is the established latest-wins pattern for superseded requests: no answer is lost or reordered, and the caller waits on the one that counts.

**#256.** Records verified when an identity is opened, by discovery from a synced passkey or by its id, are now taken as the answer for that exact root and identity. This uses the same rule `notice()` applies, now `taken()`: they replace what was read before only if they leave out no notice read there (#243). The records are kept only when this tab's root is the one stored, never for a root another tab stored meanwhile. A 404 or older records served to the question that follows are therefore no answer, and the first sign-in stops with the warning.

**Tests** (P2 notice test, all gated on held requests, with no timed waits):
- Overtaken check, by a second press and by a change from another tab: nothing is reviewed or signed on the overtaken answer, the notice is shown, and the next press signs.
- Discovery and open-by-id followed by a 404 or older records: a failed check is said and nothing is signed. Two more presses show the notice and then sign.
- Found or opened again in a tab that has read the notice, with older records served at the open: they do not replace what was read.

**Mutation coverage:**
- New twins: `signin-overtaken`, `discover-unseeded`, `open-unseeded`. Retargeted: `rollback-silent`, `signin-unasked`, `unacknowledged-not-asked`. All six are caught (count 187).
- A narrow Stryker run over the changed lines left two survivors; the re-open tests now kill both.
- Stryker ranges are rebalanced and every range reads clean.

Guards: 85 pass. id tests: 89 pass. Scenarios 107 and 108 are amended.

This will be merged by a timed auto-merge (merge-green.sh) once CI is green.

author: obukhovaa
body:
For GENAI-696. In a workspace that loads many teams' skills and subagent types, every agent that has `skill` or `task` carries every one of their descriptions. GENAI-257 scoped the skill listing per agent type, but shared types serve every team, so a per-type rule can't trim them. A flow run, though, knows what it is about.

## What it adds

A top-level `listingScope` config:

```json
{
  "listingScope": {
    "skills": [".agents/skills/**", "${args.team}/skills/**"],
    "subagents": [".agents/types/**", "${args.team}/types/**"]
  }
}
```

- **Patterns** are path globs matched against an item's file location, relative to the working directory. `${args.<path>}` tokens resolve from the run's live args when each step's agent is built, so a team set by an earlier step applies from then on. A resolved value matches literally, never as glob syntax.
- **Two tiers.** Matching skills and subagent types keep their full entries. Every other permitted one is listed **by name only**, after the full entries, with a note that it can still be loaded or called by name. This mirrors how deferred tool names are announced.
- **Nothing becomes unreachable.** `skill` loads, and `task` runs, any permitted name, whichever tier lists it. `permission.skill` applies first, so a denied skill appears in neither tier.
- **Fails open.** A list with an unresolved token, or a token other than `${args.…}`, does not apply. Sessions outside a flow run, and steps on a pinned primary prefix, are never scoped. Without the config, both descriptions are byte-identical to before.
- **Propagation.** The scope rides the step context like `denyTools`: the factory keys its step cache on it, and sync, async and nested subagents inherit it.
- **Budget.** `maxListingChars` applies to full entries after reserving room for the names-only element, which is never cut.
- **Observability.** One INFO line per scoped tool gives the agent and the full and names-only counts.

OpenSpec: `openspec/changes/archive/2026-11-24-run-scoped-listings`. The new spec is `openspec/specs/run-scoped-listings/spec.md`.

## Measured on the Piano workspace

These are the real `skill` and `task` tool descriptions, built over the shared `.agents` plus 12 of the 13 registered team repos (`content` was not reachable from here), for `piano-developer` with 194 skills. Scoped means `.agents/**` plus the run's team.

| Run | `skill` | `task` | ≈ tokens | saved |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| unscoped | 103,414 ch | 11,638 ch | 28.8k | |
| composer | 39,559 ch | 8,439 ch | 12.0k | 58% |
| subscriptions | 39,260 ch | 11,644 ch | 12.7k | 55% |
| bdata | 26,339 ch | 8,304 ch | 8.7k | 69% |
| platform | 24,276 ch | 8,304 ch | 8.1k | 71% |
| reports | 27,553 ch | 8,304 ch | 9.0k | 68% |
| dexa / dmp / security / psb / ai-platform | 19.8–22.6k ch | 8,304 ch | 7.0–7.7k | 73–75% |

That is roughly 16–22k fewer tokens per scoped agent request.

## Checks

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` all pass. `gofmt` is clean.
- `make schema-check` and `go test ./cmd/schema/...` pass after regenerating `opencode-schema.json`.
- `openspec validate run-scoped-listings --strict` passes.
- **New tests:**
  - token resolution and fail-open;
  - literal values;
  - path matching;
  - context override;
  - flow wiring, including a team set by an earlier step;
  - factory seam: both tool descriptions, cache keying, and subagent and async inheritance;
  - two-tier rendering with permissions and budget;
  - byte-identity when unscoped;
  - loading a names-only skill and calling a names-only subagent by name.

author: kim-em
body:
This PR lowers the headroom that the worker slice's `memory.high` leaves for active CI. It now reserves one worst-case Lean file (the staging gate's headroom) plus 1 GiB, never less than the idle reserve. Before, it reserved the two-file headroom of CI's ordinary Lean gate. Worker admission still pauses at the two-file reserve. On chungus5 (125 GiB) the `memory.high` reserve while CI is busy drops from 20.0 GiB to 13.5 GiB.

With 40 workers at `memory.high` and 9 of 15 CI jobs busy, the two-file reserve kept about 20-26 GiB idle as MemAvailable. Meanwhile the worker slice was down to 3.2 GiB of file cache across about 15 mapped olean trees. Lean re-read oleans from disk: 77,600 file refaults/s (tauchonki: 13,900), both NVMe drives 100% busy at about 2 GB/s reads each with queue depth around 240, and IO pressure "full" at 28%. CPU was not the constraint: 50-59 of 96 cores were busy.

CI's ordinary Lean gate measures MemAvailable, which counts reclaimable worker page cache. The cache that workers keep between the one-file and two-file reserves therefore still yields to CI. `memory.high` cannot tell cache from anon, so running workers may now grow anon down to the one-file reserve. New worker rounds still pause below the two-file reserve, as before. Sizing (worker maximum, CI slots) is unchanged.

author: plong-wasin
body:
## Summary

Opening or refreshing a work item showed "Saving…" and a fresh "Last edited by <me> a few seconds ago" with nothing typed: the web editor re-emits the description document on load, and the server treated any document whose JSON differs from the stored one as an edit (new Description Version, description Activity, `updatedAt`). A document that writes the same Markdown as the stored form is not an edit.

```diff
 updateWorkItem (description given)
   written = writtenDescription(input)
+  if written.markdown equals the stored Markdown
+    skip: no version, no change, no outlinks write, stored document untouched
   snapshot a Description Version (5-minute burst)
   change: description
```

This fixes the server side for every writer (web, MCP, AI, agents). The editor's load-time save request itself is a separate web fix.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `saving a description document that writes the same Markdown changes nothing` fails on `origin/main` (checked by running the test against the old source).
  **After:** `work-items.test.ts` 22 pass, 0 fail; `bun run typecheck` clean.

```text
save description "same"
save the same text with `marks: []` (different JSON, same Markdown)
  expect updatedAt unchanged, 0 Description Versions, no new Activity
save title "Renamed" + that same description
  expect title changed, 0 Description Versions
```

- Full suite: 2063 tests, only the 2 `apps/api/test/runtimes.test.ts` timeouts that also fail on `origin/main`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No schema change.

- A save whose Markdown is unchanged but whose document carries data the written form drops (attributes) no longer updates the stored document.
- Invalid assets in such a save are still rejected, and its warnings are still returned.

**Blast Radius:** work item description saves

author: mvhenten
body:
### What?
A restore retries each pack and snapshot root download on transport errors and 5xx, with jittered exponential backoff and at most ten attempts, and asks for fresh pack URLs when one answers 401/403 or keeps failing.
### Why?
One pack GET to R2 died with "error sending request" and failed foreman turn 4b4b5c62 with SnapshotUnreadable.
### How?
Fresh pack URLs come from asking RestoreChunks again for that part; the snapshot root URL arrives only with the turn offer, so it retries on the same URL and a fresh root URL needs a new frame carrying the turn id and returning a new root URL with its expiry.

author: gustavovalverde
body:
Wave 3 PR 3A-3.

## Behavior changes

- **Unified `ZSHRNG01` sealed segments.** The signed settled-history segment format resets from the single-projection `ZSHRNG02` layout to a dual-slab file: a fixed 128-byte header (magic, network tag, artifact schema version, segment flags whose bit 0 marks the nullifier slab and whose bit 1 stays reserved for a future `shifted_epk` sidecar, interval and chain anchors, and slab/index file offsets), one slab of pre-encoded `CompactBlockShape::DEFAULT_RANGE` frames, one slab of `CompactBlockShape::DEFAULT_NULLIFIER_RANGE` frames, dual `[u32; block_count + 1]` relative offset tables, one metadata row per block (block and parent hashes, native length, and each slab's payload SHA-256), and a trailing whole-body SHA-256 digest that the signed catalog pins. Pre-`v1.0.0` disk-compatibility promise rules apply: existing `ZSHRNG02` catalogs must be republished into a fresh catalog directory.
- **`GetBlockRangeNullifiers` serves zero-copy.** The generated `CompactTxStreamer` server now routes `GetBlockRangeNullifiers` through a new `EncodedBlockRangeNullifiers` extension, mirroring the existing encoded `GetBlockRange` route, so a nullifier stream leaves the sealed slab (or the tail cache) as byte slices instead of RocksDB decode plus re-encode. Both RPCs read their slab in both directions with positional `pread` and `Bytes::slice`. Wallet and light-wallet serving answer the nullifier range; compact-blocks serving keeps `UNIMPLEMENTED`.
- **Dual-frame `ShieldedTailBuffer`.** Each cached tail row keeps both its shielded and nullifier frames, and the 64 MiB tail budget counts both. A covered nullifier range above the catalog serves from the tail without a native read.
- **Pre-Ironwood `[SAPLING, ORCHARD]` equivalence.** A range request whose pool selection omits only Ironwood encodes byte-identical blocks to the default shapes below Ironwood activation, so it serves the stored frames. After the request takes its ordinary stream slot, the listener checks the admitted activation schedule on a view that reaches the request's highest height, before the stream queues for a signed-read permit. A request at or across activation therefore reads canonical storage with the normal chunk budget from its first chunk, even when all 16 signed reads are busy. A view that stops short of the highest height, or a schedule the reader cannot read, leaves the equivalence unproven and canonical storage serves the request with its explicit pools. Track 2B's D1 evidence: on 4,096 Mainnet blocks the nullifier stream is 2,692 KiB vs the shielded 8,122 KiB (66.8% smaller), which the sealed nullifier slab now serves without per-request protobuf CPU. D6 keeps `shifted_epk` deferred past Wave 3 with only the reserved header bit.
- **Bounded publisher payload buffering.** The publisher stages each segment's nullifier slab in `.publisher-nullifiers.tmp` and streams it into the segment when the segment completes, so payload buffering does not grow with `--segment-blocks`. The offset vectors and the per-block metadata rows still grow with the segment's block count. A restarted publisher reclaims the staging file with its other temporary files.

Per-slab authentication is preserved. Portable files stream the whole file once at admission, checking each row's payload digests and chain identity. Fs-verity-protected files read only the header, offset tables, and metadata rows eagerly, and check each slab's payloads on first access. Portable files re-check every returned payload on read, so a damaged shielded frame leaves the nullifier frame of the same row serving, and tampering with the header, slabs, index, or trailer fails closed. Both offset tables must start at zero, ascend strictly, and end at their slab's exact length before any span arithmetic runs, under portable and protected admission alike.

## Scope note

The zero-copy route for `GetBlockRangeNullifiers` requires the generated server's interception, so this change also touches `crates/zinder-proto` (a new `EncodedBlockRangeNullifiers` trait plus the shared encoded streaming body) and `tools/zinder-proto-codegen` (the injection that adds the nullifiers route and trait hook). The checked-in generated server was regenerated with the pinned Buf 1.75.0 / protoc 36.2 pair.

## Compatibility risk

The `ZSHRNG02` → `ZSHRNG01` reset is a breaking disk-format change with no migration; operators republish sealed catalogs (documented in [docs/reference/lightwalletd-compatibility.md](docs/reference/lightwalletd-compatibility.md)). No canonical-store, wallet-projection, or wire-protocol bytes change. The vendored lightwalletd protos are untouched.

## Docs

- [ADR-0014](docs/adrs/0014-consumer-neutral-wallet-data-plane.md) decision 8 records the two owned projections and the Ironwood-omission equivalence.
- [ADR-0015](docs/adrs/0015-wallet-runtime-composition.md) decision 11 covers both default projections and the signed body digest.
- [ADR-0023](docs/adrs/0023-deployment-profiles.md) decision 3 notes the nullifier-range payloads the light-wallet profile serves zero-copy.
- [Lightwalletd compatibility](docs/reference/lightwalletd-compatibility.md) describes the `ZSHRNG01` layout, admission, per-slab row checks, the dual-frame tail, and which serving modes answer each range method.

## Deferred

- `shifted_epk` remains deferred (Track 2B D6); only the reserved `segment_flags` bit 1 and the header field space keep the format migration-free for a future sidecar.

body:
Before: a campaign win dropped a chest half the time, whether the fight was clean or full of misses, so accuracy earned nothing extra in loot.

After: a campaign fight won without one miss always drops a chest, and never a plain one: its find is drawn with more luck, the way a boss's is, so rare purses, feathers and gear turn up more often. The victory card says so ("✨ Clean sweep: not one miss, so a sure chest with richer odds."). A win with a miss in it drops a chest only by chance, as ever.

How: the fight's miss count, already kept, decides it, and the chest's draw takes a sweep's luck alongside a boss's. Bosses and elites already drop a sure chest, and a sweep still tips their odds. Nothing is saved.

author: paezba
body:
## Summary

Let a provider token grant send the sandbox JWT-SVID directly as the RFC 8693 `subject_token`, optionally without client authentication. This enables keyless Google Cloud access through Workload Identity Federation. A GCE metadata emulator placeholder lets unmodified Google SDKs using Application Default Credentials use the grant.

## Related Issue

Closes #5897

## Changes

- Add `subject_token.source: jwt_svid` and a `client_authentication` object (`mechanism: client_assertion | none`, optional `credential: {source: jwt_svid}`) to token grants (`ProviderCredentialTokenGrantClientAuthentication`, field 11). Omitting it keeps today's `client_assertion` behavior.
- Validate profiles at load time: `none` requires `token_exchange` with a `jwt_svid` subject and cannot be combined with `client_assertion_type`. A `jwt_svid` subject must not name a stored `credential`, and unknown sources or authentication values are rejected.
- Supervisor: dedicated supervisors exchange the JWT-SVID (requested with `jwt_svid_audience`) at `token_endpoint` without a gateway call. They send no `client_assertion` when `client_authentication.mechanism: none`.
- Gateway: shared-supervisor token grants support the same flow with the stable sandbox JWT-SVID. Previously the gateway refused them with `FailedPrecondition`. Grant-flow resolution moved to `openshell-core::oauth::TokenGrantFlow` so the supervisor and gateway share it.
- Add `gce_metadata_token` (field 13): the sandbox GCE metadata emulator serves a non-secret placeholder access token for the credential. The token grant replaces it on the credential's endpoints; requests elsewhere that carry the placeholder are refused.
- Docs: `docs/how-it-works/providers/profiles.mdx`, the `openshell-server` and `openshell-supervisor-network` READMEs, and `examples/spiffe-gcp-sts-demo`.
- Update the storage schema fingerprints in `storage_proto.rs` for the new proto fields.

## Release Notes

Provider token grants can exchange the sandbox SPIFFE JWT-SVID directly at an STS such as Google's (`subject_token.source: jwt_svid`, `client_authentication.mechanism: none`). With `gce_metadata_token: true`, Google SDKs using Application Default Credentials reach Google Cloud APIs from a sandbox without a stored key.

## Testing

- [x] Checks appropriate to the affected code and behavior pass
- [x] Unit tests added/updated (if applicable)
- [ ] E2E tests added/updated (if applicable)

- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` on `openshell-core`, `openshell-providers`, `openshell-server`, and `openshell-supervisor-network`
- `cargo test -p openshell-core -p openshell-providers`
- `cargo test -p openshell-server --tests --bins`
- `cargo test -p openshell-supervisor-network --lib`: the token grant tests pass. 8 `proxy::tests` failures on macOS also fail on `main` unchanged.
- `mise run markdown:lint`, `proto:lint`, `buf breaking` against `main`, `license:check`, `docs:nav`, `docs:build:strict`
- Not run: a live Google STS / SPIRE end-to-end call with an unmodified Google SDK. A local run of `e2e:kubernetes:shared-supervisor-spiffe` on Colima couldn't reach the host-side test fixtures, so it didn't get as far as token grants.

## Checklist

- [x] Follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] Commits are signed off (DCO)
- [x] Architecture docs updated (if applicable)

body:
Agent J, part 4. Only `compiler/` changed.

- **diff --json is complete.** compiler/diff's model now holds every field Rust's JSON has:
  - each item's old_id, label, kind, module, doc, rewritten, interface_changed, affected (with `updated`), affected_total, refs_folded, steps and verdict;
  - the lines a fold hides (`hidden`);
  - each step's `when`;
  - the range's `options` (log entries, or the git base with recent commits and branches);
  - `summary.follow_renames` is now the number of definitions that only follow a rename, as Rust's.

  The JSON is identical to Rust's on the `cli-diff_shows_changes_structurally` package (log range) and on a git range with three changes.
- **`run --trace`:** std's functions are compiled with the program, so their calls are traced (`std.time.seconds`, `std.io.Terminal.print`), and a capability shows by its name alone (`Terminal`). The trace now matches Rust's line for line, and `cli-run_mode_console_in_tests_and_trace` passes.
- **Termination:** a `for` over a lazy `map`, `filter` or `drop` of an iterator that isn't finite may not end. This is read from the code, because the solver's encoding gives such a value as a list. Proofs are unchanged: every std type implementing `Iterator` is finite, and `strata --file std verify 'std.unicode.*' --require proven` passes. `cli-finite_and_lazy_iterators` passes.
- **verify with no solver that runs** (`STRATA_SOLVER=none`): everything is fuzzed, with "no SMT solver was found (install z3)", and a `while` loop's bound is reported unchecked. The output matches Rust's, and `build-jit-verify` passes. `has_solver` now asks `--version`, as Rust's `solver()` does.

Results: 136 of my 155 cases pass, no case regresses, and bootstrap reaches a fixed point. The run before the `has_solver` fix had one regression, `cli-solver_flags_follow_the_solver`; after the fix it passes again in a targeted re-run, along with build-jit-verify, cli-verify_finds_counterexamples, cli-cross_check_catches_a_wrong_prover and cli-the_fuzzer_stops_a_slow_solver.

body:
## What

Cuts **EKA Standard 1.5** — the applicability declaration.

## Additive content (over 1.4)

A knowledge Artifact MAY declare the paths or modules its constraint binds through one optional content field, `appliesTo` (an array of repository-relative glob patterns). Declared purely additively; 1.4 is not edited.

- `specification/concepts.md` — the *Applicability Declaration* concept.
- `specification/exchange.md` — the normative field: shape, matching, retrieval contract, validation classes.

Semantics: normative for deterministic path-to-constraint retrieval (the higher-authority Artifacts whose declared scope matches a path, ordered by stratum + canonical Identity, one hop, no similarity search), advisory for knowledge (it enforces nothing itself). Absent by default; a path matching no declaration yields an empty set, never an error. A malformed pattern is a structural violation; a well-formed pattern matching no path is a warning.

## Cut

1.4 → 1.5 across the summary and the snapshot: `EKA`, `README.md`, `specification/overview.md`, `specification/versioning.md` (frozen snapshot + version bullet + axes table), `specification/exchange.md` (corpus line), `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Verification

- `grep -rn '1\.4'` remaining hits are historical only (versioning history bullet, "1.4 and earlier remain frozen", CHANGELOG `## 1.4`).
- `EKA`: header `Version 1.5`, end marker `END OF EKA STANDARD 1.5 (SUMMARY)` — release.yml consistency gate will match the `v1.5` tag.
- Backward-compatible: 1.4-and-earlier artifacts remain conformant (optional field, absent by default).

Closes #571

A Windows installer can register a custom CLI directory after AgentBro has started. Refresh now reads the current Windows environment block and searches its absolute PATH directories after the process's inherited entries. The same order applies to the PATH passed to package helper processes. Windows resolves expandable entries and combines the user's and system's saved values.

The installed-app test uses Qoder CLI as a launcher fixture. It adds a %USERPROFILE%-relative expandable entry with a Unicode directory name after the app starts. It refreshes through Agent Management, then restores the registry value and refreshes again while the executable and app process stay in place. The test preserves the native Island, Git Bash Hook, and App Paths smoke checks.

[Windows environment variables](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/environment-variables) and [CreateEnvironmentBlock](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/userenv/nf-userenv-createenvironmentblock).


The patched installation passed the same fresh-PATH fixture on Windows Server. The UI showed the new Qoder launcher, then stopped detecting it after restoring PATH while the app PID and executable stayed the same. body:
## 왜

운영 경로 시험(11/24)에서 임시 감시를 다운시켰다가 지웠더니, ops-bot은 incident를 DB에서 자동으로 닫았지만 Slack에는 다운 알림이 버튼째 남았습니다. 채널만 봐서는 회복했는지 알 수 없었습니다.

## 무엇을

자동으로 닫힌 incident의 원래 상세 알림을 `chat.update`로 고칩니다. 버튼을 없애고 닫힌 이유와 시각을 적습니다.

| 닫힌 이유 | 문구 |
|---|---|
| 외부 감시 다시 UP | 회복 확인 |
| 외부 감시 멈춤 | 감시를 멈춰 닫음 |
| 외부 감시 목록에서 사라짐 | 감시가 없어져 닫음 |
| Sentry 해결 / 무시 / 404 | Sentry에서 해결됨 / 무시됨 / 사라져 닫음 |

예: `[P1][사이트 A] 회복 확인 · 11/09 10:05` + 본문 아래 `회복 확인 · 11/09 10:05 · 자동 처리`

- **마이그레이션 6**: `slack_channel`(상세 메시지 채널 id. 묶음 메시지면 비움), `resolve_notice`(고칠 이유), `notice_tried_at`(그 메시지만 실패해 남긴 마지막 시도), 부분 색인 1개. 기존 행은 채널 id가 없어 고치지 않습니다.
- **새 collect 단계 `slack-update`**: 모든 사이트의 새 알림을 보낸 뒤 실행합니다. 실행당 사이트마다 5건까지입니다. 실패해도 heartbeat는 막지 않습니다.
- **실패 처리**
  - 인증·rate limit·Slack 장애(`internal_error` 등)·네트워크: 표시를 남기고 이번 실행을 멈춥니다(남은 사이트도).
  - 메시지·채널 없음, 내용 거절: 포기합니다.
  - 그 밖의 오류: 그 메시지만 남기고 다음 메시지로 넘어갑니다.
  - 닫힌 지 하루가 지나면 포기합니다.
- **경쟁 조건**
  - 닫을 때 보내는 중인 표(`notify_claim`)를 지우지 않습니다. 그래서 보내는 사이 닫혀도 지금 유효한 전송이 최신 메시지 위치를 기록하고, 고치기는 그 전송이 끝난 뒤에 합니다.
  - 음소거 버튼을 누르면 고치지 않습니다. 고치기 직전에 다시 읽습니다.
- **남은 한계**: 고치기 요청과 음소거 버튼 응답이 요청 하나가 오가는 사이에 겹치면, Slack에 나중에 닿은 쪽이 화면에 남습니다. 음소거는 DB에 그대로 유효합니다.
- `/ops collect` 결과에 "자동 해결로 고친 메시지" 수와 단계 이름을 더했습니다.

## 확인

- `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build` 통과(테스트 607 → 665)
- 경쟁 조건 수정은 코드를 되돌리면 해당 테스트가 실패하는 것을 확인
- Codex 리뷰 3회
  - 1차 P2 4건 반영
  - 2차 P2 4건 중 3건 반영, 1건은 위 남은 한계로 둠
  - 3차는 고칠 결함 없음. 남은 한계를 P3로 두는 판단도 타당하다고 봄. 판정은 REQUEST CHANGES지만 독립 검토 경로가 막혔다는 절차상 이유
- 아직 실제 Slack에서 확인하지 않았습니다. 머지 뒤 임시 감시로 다운→회복을 시험합니다.

author: mattzcarey
body:
Think's context now follows one rule for what the model is sent, the one Claude Code uses for its memory files and todo list:

- A block the model writes itself with `set_context` is saved at once and never sent back to it. The record of the write is the tool call and its result in the conversation: a block with a `set_context` call in the history after the newest record is one the model knows, and when the next record is written it takes that value as delivered. So a regenerated answer without the tool call is on a branch that does not know it, and gets it. Before, a writable block declared `whenChanged: "remind"` came back as a reminder on the next turn.
- A block your code writes with `this.context.setBlock()` or `appendToBlock()` (an extension's `host.setContext()` included) is a change the model did not make, so it is sent once, after the next user message, and recorded there, even when it sets the value back to what the prompt shows. Before, an ordinary block waited silently for the next refresh.
- The prompt is rebuilt from the blocks at the first turn after every compaction, when the cached prefix is gone anyway. That is where a value the model wrote first appears in the prompt, as the tool calls that wrote it fall behind the summary. Think already refreshed after `Session.compact()`; it now also does so after `addCompaction()`. ThinkHarness never did; it now refreshes from its Sessions change feed, so its own compactions, Sessions' automatic compaction and a compaction made on the raw handle are all covered.
- A new session reads the blocks fresh, as before.

Stacked on #3095.

Cost, per statement (Think, measured by wrapping `storage.sql.exec`, same history length): the write itself (`setBlock()`/`appendToBlock()`) adds one session config read and one write (the "written from code" mark) to the block row it always wrote. The turn that delivers it adds three statements, two rows read and two written, once: the latest-leaf check that decides the turn may record (1 read, the same check any reminder delivery makes), the record of the delivery (1 write, the same row a `whenChanged: "remind"` change writes), and clearing the mark (1 read, 1 write). A model write costs nothing extra: it is read from the transcript the turn already has. Turns without writes are unchanged.

Measured on a deployment (Worker `slim-context-2773`, scripted model, `probes/context/scripts/rule.mjs`, root and facet identical; before = #3095 head, after = this PR), bytes of each request not shared with the previous request:

| turn | event | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| t4 | the model wrote its plan with `set_context` at t3 | 495 (the plan comes back as a reminder) | 140 (nothing comes back) |
| t5 | your code wrote a memory block | 135 (the model is not told) | 490 (sent once, after the user message) |
| t6 | | 139 | 139 (the reminder stays in place) |
| t7 | after a compaction | prompt rebuilt, every value in it | same |

Tests (real Durable Object, real Sessions), each failing before this change: a code write is sent once, after the next user message, also when it sets the value back; a `set_context` write to a remind block is never sent back, also after a later record; a regenerated branch without the tool call gets the value; Think rebuilds the prompt at the turn after `addCompaction()`; ThinkHarness rebuilds it after its own compaction and after one made on the Sessions handle. Think and ThinkHarness suites pass; the invariant suite passes at 60 seeds. The probe above was re-run on this head: same numbers.

Docs: docs/think/context.md "What the model is sent" states the rule.

author: briandeegan82
body:
## Summary
This is the Phase 1 small-subset test for M2, not the full experiment. The `synth_lcaP` copy (LCA 1.82 δ, δ = 22 µm) was rendered on Brian's machine on 40 RobotCar plates. Each plate got 8 displacements drawn at random from ±100 µm, 319 frames in all, and the frames were scored on held-out traversals. The write-up is `results/m2_gate/M2_GATE.md`.

- **Gate B passes on displacements never seen in training.** MAE is 0.56 δ (12.3 µm) and p90 1.22 δ, under 1 δ in every displacement band and every fold. That equals the v0 leave-one-level-out MAE, so the 9-level ladder was not flattering the estimator.
- **Training on the old 9-level renders is as good as training on continuous frames.** Both give MAE 0.56 δ; continuous training has the shorter tail (p90 1.22 vs 1.37 δ).
- **Direction accuracy** is 0.984 overall. It is 1.000 above 0.5 δ and 0.844 below 0.5 δ.

## Code changes
- **`src/m2_continuous.py render`:** for each plate, seeded by plate name, draws displacements uniformly from ±`dz_max`. It builds the PSFs at those displacements with `lens_synth.render_psfs` and renders them with `render_arms.render` (pre-ISP), using the same layout and seeding as `render_robotcar`.
- **`score`:** uses 5 traversal-disjoint folds. The through-focus curve is fitted either on binned continuous training frames or, with `--ladder`, on the cached 9-level render minus the test fold's traversals.
- **Frame count:** 319 instead of 320 frames. Two draws on one plate rounded to the same 1e-4 directory, so one frame overwrote the other.

Independent of [#6](https://github.com/briandeegan82/signed-defocus/pull/6) (M3). Both are based on main.

`Inset[obj, pos, opos, size]`'s `opos` names a point of the inset **object**, but `ImageScaled[…]` and `Offset[…]` there were resolved in the enclosing picture's coordinates. A drop-shadow inset like `Inset[img, Center, Offset[{dx, dy}, ImageScaled[{0.5, 0.5}]], Scaled[{1, 1}]]` ended up far from its anchor.

Changes:
- `ImageScaled[{fx, fy}]` as `opos` is now a fraction of the object's own picture.
- `Offset[{dx, dy}, p]` as `opos` moves the object's point `p` by printer's points at the size the object is shown at. For a `Scaled` or explicit `size`, that size is taken from the enclosing frame on the second collection pass.

author: felipelapt17-maker
body:
Hoort bij #10

> **Volgorde van mergen:** bouwt voort op #31 (`feature/ride-details`), omdat de knoppen op het detailscherm staan. Merge eerst #31. Daarna toont deze PR alleen de eigen 4 commits.

## Omschrijving
De bestuurder kan zijn eigen geplande rit **aanpassen** en **annuleren**, vanaf het detailscherm van die rit. Voor het aanpassen wordt hetzelfde formulier gebruikt als bij "Rit aanbieden". Annuleren vraagt eerst om een bevestiging.

## Reden van wijziging
Plannen veranderen: een andere vertrektijd, een plaats minder of een rit die niet doorgaat. Meerijders moeten dan de juiste informatie zien.

## Uitgevoerde wijzigingen
- **`RideService.updateRide(...)`:**
  - Alleen de **bestuurder** mag een rit aanpassen, en alleen een **geplande** rit. Bij een onbekende rit krijg je een duidelijke melding.
  - De auto blijft hetzelfde.
  - De vrije plaatsen mogen niet hoger zijn dan de stoelen min de bestuurder min de **bevestigde meerijders**. Met bevestigde meerijders mag een rit ook vol zijn (0 vrije plaatsen).
  - De controles van het formulier staan nu in één methode `validate(...)`, die zowel aanbieden als aanpassen gebruiken.
- **`RideService.cancelRide(...)`:** alleen de bestuurder, alleen een geplande rit. De status wordt `geannuleerd`. De boekingen blijven bestaan, zodat meerijders bij hun boeking zien dat de rit niet doorgaat (#16).
- **`RideDao`:** `update(...)`, `updateStatus(...)` en `countConfirmedPassengers(...)`.
- **Formulier hergebruikt:** `Screen.EDIT_RIDE` gebruikt `offer-ride.fxml`. `OfferRideController.editRide(ritId)` vult het formulier, verandert de titel en de knop, en zet de auto vast. De rit en de auto's worden los op de achtergrond geladen. Het formulier wordt pas gevuld als **beide** binnen zijn.
- **Ritdetails (alleen voor de bestuurder van een geplande rit):** de knoppen "Rit aanpassen" en "Rit annuleren".
  - Bij annuleren verschijnt eerst de vraag "Weet je zeker...?" met "Ja, annuleren" en "Nee, rit behouden".
  - Na het opslaan of annuleren verschijnt een groene melding bovenaan.

## Hoe de belangrijkste code werkt
```java
// RideService.validate: hoeveel vrije plaatsen mogen er zijn?
int minSeats = takenSeats > 0 ? 0 : 1;                       // met meerijders mag de rit vol zijn
int maxSeats = car.get().passengerSeats() - takenSeats;       // stoelen - bestuurder - bevestigde meerijders
if (seats < minSeats || seats > maxSeats) { errors.put(FIELD_SEATS, ...); }
```

## Gewijzigde bestanden
| Bestand | Functie |
|---|---|
| `service/RideService.java` | `updateRide`, `cancelRide`, `maxSeatsForEdit` en gedeelde `validate` |
| `dao/RideDao.java` | `update`, `updateStatus`, `countConfirmedPassengers` |
| `controller/OfferRideController.java`, `view/offer-ride.fxml`, `navigation/Screen.java` | Aanpassen met hetzelfde formulier |
| `controller/RideDetailsController.java`, `view/ride-details.fxml` | Knoppen, bevestiging, melding |
| `test/...` (`RideServiceTest`, `RideDaoTest`, `ManageRideTest`, `FxTestHelper`) | Tests |

## Uitgevoerde tests
`mvnw.cmd clean test` geeft **223 tests, 0 mislukt, 1 overgeslagen** (de MySQL-test), BUILD SUCCESS.

| Test | Resultaat |
|---|---|
| `RideServiceTest` (aanpassen): de bestuurder past aan en de auto blijft gelijk, een ander mag het niet, een geannuleerde rit niet, het maximum na bevestigde meerijders (rit 3: max 1, 2 geweigerd, 0 toegestaan), een onbekende rit | ✅ 5 |
| `RideServiceTest` (annuleren): de bestuurder annuleert, een ander niet, niet twee keer | ✅ 3 |
| `RideDaoTest`: alleen bevestigde meerijders tellen, `updateStatus` verandert alleen die rit | ✅ 2 |
| `ManageRideTest`: de bestuurder ziet de knoppen en een ander niet, annuleren vraagt een bevestiging en is terug te draaien, bevestigen annuleert de rit, het formulier wordt gevuld en opslaan gaat terug naar de details met een melding | ✅ 5 |
| Handmatig tegen de echte MySQL-database | ⚠️ Nog niet gedaan: `database_laden.ps1` is op deze computer nog niet uitgevoerd |

## Handmatige testinstructies
1. Switch naar `feature/manage-ride`, start de app en log in als `sanne.jansen@student.example.com` / `Carpool2026`.
2. Open via Ritten zoeken de rit "Delft Station → De Haagse Hogeschool". Verwacht: de knoppen "Rit aanpassen" en "Rit annuleren".
3. Klik op "Rit aanpassen", wijzig de vertrekplaats en sla op. Verwacht: terug op de details met "Je rit is aangepast."
4. Klik op "Rit annuleren" en daarna op "Nee, rit behouden". De rit blijft gepland. Klik nog een keer en kies "Ja, annuleren". Verwacht: de badge "Geannuleerd" en de knoppen zijn weg.
5. Log in als `noah.bakker@student.example.com` en open een rit van iemand anders. Verwacht: geen knoppen om aan te passen of te annuleren.

## Bekende problemen
- Bij een rit met bevestigde meerijders kan de bestuurder het vertrekmoment nog veranderen zonder dat de meerijders een bericht krijgen. Ze zien de nieuwe tijd wel bij hun boeking. Een berichtensysteem valt buiten deze planning.

- [ ] Ik heb de gewijzigde code gelezen.

- [ ] Ik heb de functionaliteit lokaal getest.
- [ ] Ik heb de testresultaten gecontroleerd.
- [ ] Ik heb gecontroleerd op mogelijke bugs.
- [ ] Ik heb gecontroleerd of bestaande functionaliteiten nog werken.
- [ ] Ik vind de functionaliteit geschikt om te mergen.

author: excorvus
body:
# d3d12_xs: restore the console command-list IID mapping lost in a merge

Claimed in the coordination issue as: **none exists yet** — this PR is the claim, as with PR #2.
Relates to issue #47 (the boot ladder): the command-list IID wall its comments name after the
slot-26 and copy-queue stops.

AI-assisted: yes (Qwen4 Max Preview / Alibaba Token Plan).

## What and why

`3c95a4a95` ("d3d12_xs: map the console list IID in QI and CreateCommandListX") added
`runtime/shims/d3d12_xs_command_list_iid.h` — the measured console→PC IID pair for device
slot 73 — and wired it into `list_query_interface` and the slot-73 path. **The commit is an
ancestor of main, but the header is not in the tree** (`git ls-tree main --
runtime/shims/d3d12_xs_command_list_iid.h` is empty) and both wiring points forward the
requested IID unchanged again. A later merge dropped them — the same loss pattern PR #131
restored for the DirectStorage shim.

The retail executable asks slot 73 (`CreateCommandListX`) for the console command-list IID
`c3827890-4024-474c-98cf-645b51dc4874`. Unmapped, the PC `CreateCommandList` refuses it
(the Vulkan layer logs `QueryInterface: unknown IID`), the slot returns a failing HRESULT,
and the title asserts on it — a fatal `int3` right after the call, confirmed statically with
`tools/int3_cause.py` (the assert branches on the slot-73 result's sign).

## The change

- Restore the header **byte-for-byte** from `3c95a4a95` (blob `fc149cea9`); its provenance
  notes (TomBox GPL-3.0 measurement, Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0) stay intact.
- Map the requested IID through `command_list_iid_for_pc` in `list_query_interface` and in
  the slot-73 `CreateCommandList` call, adapted to the current `ListProxy`: `wrap_list` QIs
  through `list_query_interface`, so the wrapped proxy answers the console IID as well.
- `xs_proxy_mock_test`: a console-IID slot-73 case asserts the mapped PC IID
  (`ID3D12GraphicsCommandList6`) reaches `CreateCommandList` and the proxy's QI answers the
  console IID.

No behavior change for PC IIDs or IIDs outside the table (forwarded unchanged, logged once,
as the original header documents).

## Tested

Host: Windows 11, AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT, driver `32.0.32029.2010`, `LEONIDA_D3D12=vulkan`.

- `xs_proxy_mock_test` builds and exits 0 with the new case.
- `gta6rt --run` on my own 1.0.2.1 package (108/108 files SHA-256 verified), main
  `8f481cf16` + this change (the three touched files are byte-identical at `21625bca8`):
  - **Before:** 13 D3D12 calls; `CreateCommandList` refuses the console IID; the title's
    fatal assert ends the run ~2.2 s in.
  - **After:** 1,639 D3D12 calls — command lists, ~1,600 allocators, slot 25
    `GetResourceAllocationInfo`, slot 127 `CreateCommittedResource3`, SRV/RTV/UAV creation —
    before the next, unrelated assert (a bounds check on a title global; a new rung on the
    #47 ladder, not a regression).
- The restore applies cleanly on `21625bca8`; the header is byte-identical to the `3c95a4a95`
  blob. If main moves again, the two wiring points are small and local.
- Not tested: Wine, other GPUs, a full retail boot (the project does not boot yet).

## Checklist

- [x] No game data, keys or decryption in the diff, tests or this description (call shapes,
      export names and counts only; the IID is a public-interface identifier already named
      in `3c95a4a95`'s public commit message).
- [x] No new translator rule (not applicable).
- [x] Restored code keeps its original provenance comments; no GPL-incompatible code.

author: brnl-claude
body:
## Waarom
Op het cluster mislukte het ophalen zonder dat de app een fout toonde. Daar zaten drie gaten in:
- De `huizenjacht.*`-loggers hadden onder uvicorn geen handler. INFO-meldingen verdwenen daardoor, en de achtergrondlus slikte excepties stil in (`contextlib.suppress`).
- Gaf de site een pagina zonder advertentie terug, zoals een blokkade groter dan 60 kB of een andere challenge, dan telde dat als "ok" met 0 foto's. Je zag dan een lege kopie en geen foto's.
- De achtergrondlus draaide maar elke 30 minuten. Wat er gebeurde, was nergens te zien.

## Wat
- Er is een loghandler voor `huizenjacht.*`. Elke poging komt in de podlog: URL, HTTP-status, grootte en paginatitel, plus het aantal foto's gevonden en opgeslagen.
- De blokkadetekst wordt altijd herkend, ongeacht de grootte van de pagina. Een pagina zonder foto's én zonder og:title krijgt een fout (`NotAListing`). Een HTTP 4xx/5xx-antwoord geeft een nette melding.
- Mislukte foto's worden per reden geteld en in de status gemeld.
- Foto-URL's die als `/` in Nuxt-JSON staan, worden nu ook gevonden.
- De ruwe respons wordt bewaard als `raw.html`. Je kunt hem downloaden via `GET /api/houses/{id}/listing/raw` (text/plain, attachment), om hem te kunnen onderzoeken.
- De lus controleert elke 5 minuten, met 10 s vertraging na de start.
- Frontend:
  - De overlay heeft een statusbalk: opgehaald of mislukt, met de melding, "Wat de site stuurde" en "Opnieuw ophalen".
  - De huispagina toont de knop "Ophalen mislukt".
  - De overlay sluit als je naar een ander huis gaat.

## Getest
- pytest: 18 tests, waarvan 3 nieuw.
- ruff, tsc, oxlint en vitest: groen.
- Lokaal met Playwright gecontroleerd. Screenshots staan in de thread.

author: konstziv
body:
## М-3 (24.11) · Здачі й рецензії студента для автора — договір для панелі

Чотири маршрути, ключ автора (scope `prep`), як сусідні `/students`. База: a57de53. Без міграцій, без змін у `prompts/` і `config/`, без змін у шляху перевірки (`VERDICT_RULES_VERSION = 9`; оцінювач `task`/`short_task` = `ev1:e054de5f5bc7b612`, `project` = `ev1:dbcfa16ba53d80cb`, як на main). Портал студента не змінено: `portal_submissions.py` і `_portal_shared.py` ідентичні a57de53.

### Межа видимості (усі чотири маршрути)
Студент і здача належать орендареві ключа, не видалені м'яко, здача — цього студента. Будь-яке порушення — **404**. Текст однаковий для всіх випадків у межах маршруту: список — `Student not found.`; деталь, файл і переписка — `Submission not found.`. Без ключа — 401, без scope `prep` — 403 (як у сусідів).

### 1. `GET /api/v1/students/{student_id}/submissions` → `AuthorStudentSubmissions`
Параметри: `course_node_id` (необов'язковий, корінь курсу), `limit` (1–100, типово 20), `offset` (≥ 0). Найновіші першими; м'яко видалені не входять ні в сторінку, ні в `total`.
- `student` (`AuthorStudentHeader`): `student_id`, `display_name`, `login` — ті самі джерела, що в `GET /students`.
- `enrollments[]` (`AuthorStudentEnrollment`): `course_id`, `course_title`, `enrolled_at` — курси, на які студент записаний (без м'яко видалених курсів), найстаріший запис першим; не залежать від фільтра.
- `items[]` (`AuthorSubmissionListItem`), `total`, `limit`, `offset`.

Рядок здачі:
- `id` — id здачі.
- `attempt_no` — номер спроби (null до лічильника або без номера).
- `previous_submission_id` — попередня рецензована спроба цього завдання.
- `created_at` — коли здано.
- `reviewed_at` — коли записано рецензію (див. нижче), інакше null.
- `course_id`, `course_title` — курс (корінь).
- `task_document_id`, `task_title`, `task_type` — завдання (назва як у порталі: title, інакше файл, інакше `<тип> #<порядок>`).
- `status` — етап життєвого циклу.
- `presentation` — `{state, reason_code}` тією самою `curated_presentation`, що в порталі, із `awaiting_author_funds`, коли чекає юнітів автора.
- `score` — 0–100 або null.
- `passed` — з `curated_verdict`, null без вердикту.
- `rejection`, `not_opened`, `recovered_encoding` — як у порталі.
- `is_repeat_copy` — рецензія є копією попередньої тієї самої роботи (`attempt_receipt.dedup_of`).
- `review_language` — трилітерний код: з рецензії, інакше `response_language`.
- `original_filename`.

### 2. `GET /api/v1/students/{student_id}/submissions/{submission_id}` → `AuthorSubmissionDetail`
Усі поля рядка (крім `passed`) плюс:
- `student` (`AuthorSubmissionStudent`): `student_id`, `display_name`.
- `verdict` (`{passed, correctness}`), `structure` (`ReviewStructureV1` або null для старої рецензії), `review_markdown`, `delta` (для проєкту, тією ж `_delta_receipt`), `own_feedback` (`FeedbackTouch` — відгук студента на цю рецензію).
- `pass_rule` (`AuthorPassRule`): `basis`, `threshold` — записані при збиранні рецензії (`structure.verdict.rule`), не перераховуються; `required_musts` — скільки критеріїв автор зробив обов'язковими (`must_by_author`) у переліку, за яким судили (0 для гілки `no_author_musts_*`, null якщо перелік не читається). Null для тесту й старої рецензії.
- `criteria[]` (`AuthorCriterionVerdict`): `item_id`, `item_kind` (`criterion`/`point`), `text`, `weight` (`must`/`should`/`may`, null для пункту), `must_by_author`, `verdict` (`met`/`not_met`/`unconfirmed`), `quote`, `quote_line_start`, `missing`, `remark_state` (`new`/`open`/`fixed`/`broken`/null). Порядок — як у переліку (пункт одразу після свого критерію). Немає рядків — `[]`. Перелік не читається — `[]` і WARNING `author_submission_judged_list_unreadable` лише з ідентифікаторами.

Ніколи не віддається: `safety_result`, `sanity_result`, сирий `review_result`, відповіді моделей, `job_id`, ключі S3, будь-яка вартість (`billing_note` теж). Замок — тест білого списку ключів обох відповідей.

### 3. `GET /api/v1/students/{student_id}/submissions/{submission_id}/file` → `AuthorSubmissionFileLink`
`{url, expires_at}`; чинність 15 хвилин (`FILE_LINK_TTL_SEC`); `get_object` з `Content-Disposition: attachment` і ім'ям файла. 404 для тесту (там лежить не файл студента, а аркуш відповідей) і для файла поза нашим бакетом. Журнал: `author_submission_file_link` з `tenant_id`, `student_id`, `submission_id`; без посилання й без ключа.

### 4. `GET /api/v1/students/{student_id}/submissions/{submission_id}/comments` → `RemarkThreads`
Лише читання (POST → 405). Та сама схема й те саме ядро, що в порталі (`GET /portal/submissions/{id}/comments`) і в каналі школи (`GET /feedback/submissions/{id}/comments`): `reply_core.read_threads` і `to_remark_threads`; для автора інша лише перевірка доступу (межа вище).
- `accepting_replies` — чи взяла б ця рецензія репліку зараз (як у порталі; для автора це довідка, не дія).
- `threads[]` — `item_id` і `comments[]` (`id`, `submission_id`, `item_id`, `parent_id`, `author` `student`/`mentor`, `kind`, `body`, `created_at`, `answered_in_submission_id`); у порядку зауважень рецензії, найстаріший коментар першим, через усі спроби цієї версії завдання.
- Тип без реплік або без переписки — `threads: []`, як у порталі. Для тієї самої здачі відповідь дорівнює відповіді порталу студента (тест).

### Заміни назв проти переліку гайду
Немає: назви полів лишено за переліком. Додатково до переліку: `AuthorSubmissionStudent` у деталі (за вимогою), `required_musts` у `pass_rule`.

### Що з переліку не віддано і чому
Нічого з вимог. Свідомо не віддано те, що заборонено: слід перевірки, сирі рецензії, вартість, службові ідентифікатори й ключі.

### Як знайдено `reviewed_at`
Окремої колонки немає, `updated_at` змінюється й з інших причин. Береться `completed_at` задачі `homework_processing` (`submissions.job_id`), що завершилась зі статусом `complete`, і лише для здач зі статусом `completed`/`delivered`. Для відхилених, відхилених дверима, тестів без задачі й старих без задачі — null.

## Task

Issues 1 and 11 of Rohan's 24 Nov test (stage B's B2): the real model and effort are named and choosable before the first message, and stay shown while an answer runs; each answer says whether code mode was used.

Head 0a606e78d, 11 commits on main dd42de6ea. Each commit passes `cargo check --workspace --tests`.

## What changed

What a lawyer saw before: in a new conversation on a fresh data folder the model menu held one entry, "Claude's default", and the effort read "Default effort"; nothing else could be chosen until the first answer. While an answer ran, the composer showed only "Answering." and Stop. Nothing said whether an answer used code mode.

What a lawyer sees after: the real models and efforts by their real names (the default too) before any conversation, choosable then; the model and effort of the running answer on the thread's status line; a code-mode mark on each answer that ran a script (the app shows it).

- **Probe at start and after a sign-in, per signed-in agent, with no prompt, no MCP server and no plan usage:** Claude through claude-agent-acp 0.110.1's `session/options` (`mcpServers: []`); Codex through app-server `model/list` (paged, each model's reasoning efforts). The models and per-model efforts are kept in `agent-options.json`. The seed row is gone: until a probe or a session fills the list, there are no options. A failed probe is retried at the next good read, up to 3 times per start or sign-in.
- **Picks:** picks are set before the turn starts. A pick before the first message is set at the launch (`CreateThread.config`). A prompt's own picks (`SendPrompt.config`) are set on the session that runs that prompt, just before it, a newly started or switched one included, and logged on its `UserMessage` so a queued prompt keeps them across a restart. The effort pick is checked against the model pick's answer. A steer's picks are dropped.
- **TurnStarted names what the agent's answer holds.** Each TurnStarted sets the header's model and effort and clears what it leaves out. A pick that can't be used gets one notice, NoticeKind `PickNotUsed`.
- **Sign-in requeue:** `Requeue.config` keeps a turn's picks across the sign-in requeue.
- **Code mode, per turn:** `clauseo_protocol::is_code_mode_call(id)` (a tool call id starting `toolu_cc_` or `repl_`) means "a script call was seen in this turn". The host sets `TurnEnded.code_mode` at the turn's close; each answer's `StepEntry` carries it, so a reload keeps the mark; the header and thread row carry it for the running answer (set at its first script call, cleared at the next turn start).
- **Protocol (bindings regenerated):**
  - `AgentSummary.models?: AgentModels { model_option, effort_option?, models: ModelEntry[], current_model, current_effort? }`; `ModelEntry { id, name, description?, efforts?: NamedChoice[], default_effort? }`; `NamedChoice { id, name }`. `model_option`/`effort_option` are the ConfigPicks keys (Claude `model`/`effort`, Codex `model`/`reasoning_effort`).
  - `AgentSummary.models_unread: bool` (TS `models_unread?: boolean`), set while a probe has failed and no good read has followed; omitted when false.
  - `SendPrompt.config?: ConfigPicks`; `UserMessage.config?`.
  - `TurnStarted.model?`, `TurnStarted.effort?` (`NamedChoice`); `TurnEnded.code_mode?`; `StepEntry.code_mode?`; `HeaderEntry` and `ThreadSummary` carry `model?`, `effort?`, `code_mode?` (false omitted).
  - `NoticeKind::PickNotUsed` (wire `"pick_not_used"`, `{ model?, effort? }`, the display names of what the answer ran with).
  - Saved-state schema (`REDUCER_SCHEMA_VERSION`) is 16: rebased onto main 39eada1f3, after #1286 (14) and #1335 (15).
- ADR 0033: every pin bump re-checks the start-up probes (not the removed seed).

Live, no prompt, on the test sign-ins: Claude lists Opus 5.5 (current, Medium), Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.2, Haiku 5.5 and older models, each with its own efforts; Codex lists gpt-6.2-sol (current, Low, OpenAI's catalog default), gpt-6.2-astra, gpt-6.1-terra/-sol and older.

## Review fixes (r7394)

One line per fix. The test named is the one that fails when that fix is reverted. "No revert check" means the fixer's report records none.

- Picks set before the checkpoint and TurnStarted; the answer is logged first: `pickers_turn::a_turn_names_what_the_agents_answer_holds_and_a_refused_pick_is_told`.
- Unused pick gives one `PickNotUsed` notice: the same test.
- Effort checked against the model pick's answer: `pickers_turn::an_effort_pick_is_checked_against_the_model_picks_answer`.
- Probe retry, up to 3 tries, with `models_unread`: `pickers_probe_retry::a_failed_probe_marks_the_models_unread_and_the_next_read_probes_again`.
- `models_unread` clears when a session fills the models: `pickers_probe_retry::a_session_that_fills_the_models_clears_the_unread_mark` (no revert check).
- Sign-in requeue keeps the turn's picks (`Requeue.config`): `pickers_turn::a_turn_put_back_for_the_sign_in_keeps_its_picks`.
- Steer's picks dropped: `pickers_turn::a_steers_picks_never_reach_a_starting_session`.
- Header always takes the event's model and effort, so an omitted field clears it (`reducer/thread/turn.rs`): no revert check.
- Probe runs outside the limits read gate (`limits/src/readers.rs`): no revert check.
- Schema 15 to 16, with the asserts and snapshot pins updated: no revert check.

## Checks run

On main dd42de6ea + this branch, macOS. Final tree b1f5b47a. The tree hash is the same before and after the squash on the same base (both b1f5b47a).
- `cargo nextest run` protocol, acp, codex_appserver, limits, reducer, store: 1388 run, 1387 pass. The one failure, acp `helpers::a_helper_in_the_background_names_its_steps`, came from a stale fake_agent build; rerun after the build: acp 157/157.
- `cargo nextest run -p clauseo-host` filter (option|pick|model|codex|code_mode|queue|undo|sign_in|steer|notice): 497/497, fake_agent built first.
- `cargo nextest run -p clauseo-desktop bindings`: 1/1 pass (bindings regenerated, run twice after the last doc change).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo xtask check --quick --no-tests`: every check ok.
- Live probes (no prompt) against the real adapters on the test sign-ins: lists above.

## Performance

The probes run in the background at start and after a sign-in; they never delay the app's start or a conversation's launch, and a failed or slow probe keeps the cache. The probe runs outside the limits read gate.

## Deviations

- Three lints are expected with a reason, the house way (`#[expect]` plus `xtask/expect-allowlist.txt`, as `ProtectionView` does): `struct_excessive_bools` on `ThreadSummary` and `HeaderEntry` (the protocol shape keeps separate fields), `large_enum_variant` on `EnvelopeRead`.
- The model descriptions are not yet passed through #1313's `model_line` filter (marked in `agent_options/models.rs`); wired once #1313 is on main.

## Not verified

- The full host suite (only the filter above ran).
- Any live engine run against the real claude-agent-acp.
- UI words for the new fields (`PickNotUsed`, `models_unread`, the code-mode mark): the app thread's part. The app thread builds the UI against these fields.
- The probe on Windows.
- Switching agent mid-conversation (the switch itself is another stream's): the picks are applied to whichever session runs the prompt.
- A turn dequeued before it starts still leaves its `by_turn` entry until restart (as before).

## Re-review fixes (r7457), commits 027efae51 to 41a6971f5

Each test named below failed with its fix reverted.
- **Probe and sign-in** (027efae51): a hold ends a running model probe (its process tree goes with it), and no probe starts during a hold. Each probe carries a per-agent generation that a login change bumps, so an older probe's answer or failure is ignored and uses no try. Tests: host `pickers_probe_login` (two), limits `a_probe_asked_for_under_a_hold_launches_nothing`, `a_hold_ends_a_running_probe_and_its_process`.

**Summary:** A list of safety tests is kept as a master copy in the image-builder project, and this project keeps a pinned copy of it. Our copy fell behind after later additions to the master, so the nightly consistency check kept failing. This updates the copy, and teaches this project's safety hook the one new kind of case it did not yet refuse, so the refreshed tests pass.

---

Closes #715

## What changed

- `tests/fixtures/gate-refusal-corpus.json` is now byte for byte the file on `Danathar/atomic-image-builder` main (fetched with the contents API). sha256 is `8c013df1e981d6a17c6d5c8bd7d5589ff8f33fc798d9f6ce046d58d54844f6ae`, and `CANONICAL_SHA256` in `tests/test_gate_refusal_corpus.py` is updated to it.
- The previous run of this issue found the copy equal to canonical at 64246cb4...; canonical has moved since (17e17d4 and 5e6971a touched the file after the sensi copy was last synced), so the nightly mismatch is real.
- New rows (11): `path-declare`, `path-readonly`, `path-typeset-option`, `path-let`, `settings-env-let`, `config-reach-allow-let-counter`, `path-arithmetic`, `home-arithmetic`, `xdg-config-home-arithmetic-expansion`, `config-reach-allow-arithmetic-counter`, `config-reach-allow-subshell-path-word`.

## Gate change

The declare, readonly, typeset and let rows were already refused by `.claude/hooks/gate-git-file-arguments.py` (the #713 work). The three arithmetic refuse rows were not: `(( PATH = 1 )); git log -1` assigns an exported name with no `NAME=value` word, so the stand-alone assignment scan never saw it. There is no over/under-refused list for refuse rows in `tests/test_gate_refusal_corpus.py` (only `OVER_REFUSED_ROWS` for allow rows), so the gate was fixed instead.

- New `_arithmetic_assignments` runs before `_segments`. For each `((` ... `))` region (command, `$(( ))` expansion, `for ((` header) that assigns a name (`=`, `op=`, `++`, `--`; not `==`, `!=`, `<=`, `>=`), it inserts a `NAME=0 ;` segment in front of the command the region sits in. The existing `reached` logic then refuses a later git/gated command exactly as for `PATH=planted; git ...`. The region's own words are left in place so substitutions inside are still read.
- Over-refusal accepted on purpose: `( ( PATH = 1 ) )` written with a space is read as arithmetic too.
- Not covered: an arithmetic expansion inside a double-quoted word (`"$(( PATH = 1 ))"`), which the gate's quote masking hides; same blind spot class as other quoted `$(`.
- Refusal message mentions the arithmetic spelling.
- Tests: 6 refuse rows and 3 allow rows in `tests/test_git_file_argument_gate.py` (including `(( PATH == 1 ))` and `(( i = 1 ))` allowed), plus one mutation entry so removing the rewrite fails a row.

Files touched: 4. Nothing was run locally (tests, ruff and the hook were only read and reasoned about); CI is the verdict, so any lexer edge in the new function will show up there.
