author: jordanlegare
body:
## Summary

Fixes a form-layout cursor desynchronization that can suppress visible controls after a CSS-hidden wrapper.

The document builder collects form controls recursively, including controls nested inside elements with `display:none`. During rendering, those hidden wrapper subtrees were skipped without advancing the collected-control cursor. As a result, a later visible control (such as Google's `q` search field) no longer matched the cursor and was never emitted as a renderable widget.

### Changes
- Consume all collected controls belonging to a skipped `display:none` subtree.
- Preserve the rule that CSS-hidden controls are not drawn.
- Allow subsequent visible controls and submit buttons to be emitted in their original DOM order.
- Add a Google-style regression test with a hidden nested control preceding a visible `textarea[name=q]` search field and submit button.

### Validation
The pull-request CI will run formatting, all portable tests, the x86-64 UEFI target check, wolfSSL static build, and standalone EFI image verification.

Firmware runtime testing is still required to confirm the Google homepage layout on physical hardware.

author: ernest0-production
body: ## Problem On a GitLab host that requires sign-in, uploaded user avatars in a merge request's All Activity tab (and other actor chips in the detail panel) fall back to initials. Fixes #42122. ## Change REST notes already give an absolute `https:///uploads/-/system/user/avatar//`. The clients loaded it with a plain `` / `expo-image` and no GitLab credential, and GitLab had no `mediaUrl` / `fetchMedia` on `main`, so nothing could fetch it for them. - `packages/source-control-gitlab/src/shared/gitLabMedia.ts`: `gitLabMediaUrl` claims only `/uploads/-/system/user/avatar//`, wired as the GitLab definition's `mediaUrl`. - `packages/source-control-gitlab/src/server/gitLabMediaFetch.ts`: `fetchMedia` runs `glab api --hostname ` and streams the bytes back. glab sends the host's `PRIVATE-TOKEN` to a full URL on that host, not only to `/api/v4`. `GitLabCli.execute` forwards `onStdoutChunk` so binary output isn't decoded as text. - `SourceControlMediaRequest` gains an optional `cwd`, filled in by `sourceControlMediaResponse`, so the CLI-based fetch has a working directory. - Web `PullRequestActorAvatar` and mobile `PullRequestAvatar`: inside a merge request (web `PullRequestAvatarSourceContext` from the detail panel, mobile's existing `PullRequestMediaContext`), a claimed avatar loads through `SOURCE_CONTROL_MEDIA_ASSET`, as merge request images already do. If the server can't mint the asset (an older server), they fall back to the original URL. Gravatar/identicon and every unclaimed URL still load directly, and list rows outside a merge request are unchanged. Left alone: GitHub, commit authors (`decodeCommitsJson`), and project/markdown uploads (`//uploads//…`, #11412 / #23501). The web context lives in `pullRequestPresentation.tsx` because importing `PullRequestMarkdownContext` there would create an import cycle through `ChatMarkdown`. ## Scope Bug fix for #42122. One problem. No extra cleanup. ## Verification - Live, GitLab 19.4.5-ee: REST `merge_requests/:iid/notes` gives `author.avatar_url` as an absolute `/uploads/-/system/user/avatar//avatar.png`. `glab api --hostname ` returns the PNG bytes (`89 50 4E 47…`), and `GLAB_DEBUG_HTTP=1` shows a `Private-Token` header on that request. This instance also serves the file anonymously; a host that requires sign-in redirects an anonymous request to `/users/sign_in`. - Tests that fail on `main` and pass with the fix: - `vp test run packages/source-control-gitlab/src/shared/definition.test.ts`: a system avatar is claimed; Gravatar, project uploads, project avatars, and URLs with credentials are not. - `vp test run packages/source-control-gitlab/src/server/gitLabMediaFetch.test.ts`: binary avatar bytes come back intact through `glab api --hostname `. - `apps/server/src/assets/AssetAccess.test.ts` updated for the forwarded `cwd`. `vp run check:changed`: format, lint, knip, tests, and React Compiler pass. Typecheck failed on a mobile narrowing; after the fix the mobile typecheck is clean, and the rest of that run's output had only existing `TS377141` suggestions. - Not run in a real client. author: vijay-bcbp
body:
## Description

AuthZ Enrichment's side of web-shell's IAM-screens asks **AZ-2** and **AZ-3** (`frontend/web-shell-iam-screens-requests-for-iam.md`), recorded as **AE-51** (LLD rev 1.51). Several review rounds also closed older cache-race gaps on the same code path.

**AZ-2: a suspended member gets their own deny code**
- New `DENY_MEMBER_SUSPENDED` (403) for an I-8 membership with `status: "suspended"`. Before, it was `DENY_UNRESOLVABLE_SUBJECT`, the same as a non-member, so web-shell couldn't show A8's "access paused" text. Other non-active statuses are unchanged.
- `ae:neg` now stores the deny reason. A pre-upgrade `"1"`, or any other unknown value, reads as `DENY_UNRESOLVABLE_SUBJECT`.

**AZ-3: published deny-code list**
- `api/deny-codes.json` lists every `DENY_*` code with its status, problem `type`/`title`/`detail`, `retryable`, `action` and `meaning`. `TestDenyCodesJSON_MatchesDenyReasons` checks it against `domain.DenyReasons()` and the bodies `deniedResponse` actually sends. `TestDenyReasons_CoversEveryConst` checks `DenyReasons()` against the constants.

**Cache write guard (older races closed)**
- An event's eviction could be undone by an I-8/TAC-4 rebuild already in flight, which wrote its older answer back. Examples: revoked roles cached again, a `read_only` cancellation undone, a fresh grant still denied.
- New random tokens fix this: `ae:gen:{tenant}:{user}` guards `ae:ctx`, `ae:neg` and `ae:tender_acl`, and `ae:tgen:{tenant}` guards `ae:tenant`.
  - Every matching eviction replaces the token atomically with its `DEL`.
  - A rebuild reads the token before calling the sibling. That read is a plain GET once the token exists, and never happens on a fresh hit.
  - Each write is a Lua script that lands only if the token is unchanged.
  - A lost or expired token can only make a write skip.
- The tokens are part of the singleflight key, so a request that started after an eviction never shares an older in-flight answer.
- An undecodable cache entry is deleted and read as a miss. The stale `ae:ctx` is evicted on a non-member answer even when the `ae:tenant` read failed.
- New metric `iam_authz_enrichment_cache_guard_errors_total{op}` with alert `AuthzEnrichmentCacheGuardErrors`, plus a runbook entry. Startup logs an Error if Valkey won't load the guard scripts.

**Second commit:** extends the `.trivyignore` expiry for DLA-4845-1 (ca-certificates in distroless) to 2026-12-31. The entry expired on 2026-11-21, and I re-checked on 2026-11-24: the pinned distroless digest is still the newest upstream. The Dockerfile's certs stage already ships the fixed bundle.

---

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Test
- [x] Breaking change: suspended members move from `DENY_UNRESOLVABLE_SUBJECT` to `DENY_MEMBER_SUSPENDED`. It ships as MINOR only under the pre-v1 rule (VERSIONING.md).
- [ ] Event contract change (new/changed §5 consumed event)

---

## Testing
- [x] Unit tests added/updated (`make test`). `make test-ci` passes with race and coverage, and all new code is at 100%.
- [x] Integration tests updated (`make test-integration`). They passed twice in a row, which also checks repeat runs with leftover tokens.
- [x] E2E tests updated (`make test-e2e`): `TestSuspendedMember_Deny` asserts the new code and that it is served from `ae:neg` on real Valkey.
- [x] All tests passing with race detector
- [ ] Manual `grpcurl`/`grpcui` testing performed (the `Check` request/response shape is unchanged)

---

## Checklist

### Code Quality
- [x] Code is properly formatted (`make fmt-check`)
- [x] Linting passed (`make lint`)
- [x] Vet passed (`make vet`)
- [x] Arch-lint passed (`make arch-lint`)
- [x] No debug logs / commented-out code
- [x] No secrets hardcoded

### §3.1 Precedence Chain
- [x] Existing step order preserved. Suspension is decided inside step 1 (subject resolution).
- [x] Precedence covered: a suspended member of a read-only/suspended tenant still gets the step-1 reason.
- [x] `ARCHITECTURE.md` precedence table and `request-flow.mmd` updated

### Caching (§4)
- [x] New keys `ae:gen` / `ae:tgen` added to the key tables in `README.md` / `ARCHITECTURE.md` / LLD §4.1
- [x] Tokens hold no tenant data; `mfa_freshness_seconds` is still never cached
- [x] TTLs reviewed. `AE_CTX_TTL` / `AE_TENDER_ACL_TTL` / `AE_NEG_TTL` must now be positive, and `AE_STALE_IF_ERROR_MAX_AGE` not negative.

### Event Consumption (§5)
- [x] Idempotency unchanged (no consumer change). Evictions now also replace the guard token.
- [x] Eviction tests assert the token replacement

### Security
- [x] No new identity/authz input source
- [x] Client headers still cannot influence the output headers
- [x] No new claim logged

### Documentation
- [x] README updated (env-var rules, key list)
- [x] ARCHITECTURE.md updated (precedence table, cache diagrams, package node)
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` updated

---

## Related Issue
web-shell IAM-screens asks AZ-2 / AZ-3 (`frontend/web-shell-iam-screens-requests-for-iam.md`). The reply is in `frontend/web-shell-iam-screens-reply-from-authz-enrichment.md`.

---

## Deployment Notes
- **Startup now fails** if `AE_CTX_TTL`, `AE_TENDER_ACL_TTL` or `AE_NEG_TTL` is 0 or less, or `AE_STALE_IF_ERROR_MAX_AGE` is negative. The defaults are unaffected.
- **Valkey needs `@scripting`** (`EVAL`/`EVALSHA`/`SCRIPT LOAD`) for the service user. Without it, decisions stay correct but nothing is cached. The pod logs an Error at startup, and `AuthzEnrichmentCacheGuardErrors` fires.
- **Rolling deploy:** until every pod runs this version, a suspended member can get either code. Old pods also evict without replacing the token, so the write guard protects nothing until the rollout finishes. No cache flush is needed. See `docs/runbook.md`.
- New keys `ae:gen:*` / `ae:tgen:*` with a 1 h TTL, one per subject/tenant that misses the cache.

author: fchicout
body:
Closes #692

## What and why

A probe against the real Web API (`teststr`, 2026-11-24; probe items deleted afterwards): `GET /items` lists the children of a trashed item among the ordinary ones, `/items/trash` lists only the trashed parent, and `/items/<trashed parent>/children` returns them. So a backup without `--trash` wrote those children into the archive with their parent missing: orphans that inflate `counts.items` and that a restore cannot place (it lists them under `Not restored` since #681). The offline gateway behaves the same (only the parent is in `deletedItems`).

- `backup_system` without `include_trash` drops every item whose parent is not in the listing, repeating until none is left (an annotation goes with the attachment that went). With `--trash` nothing changes: parent and children are both in. A collection backup was not affected (`collections/<key>/items` excludes trashed items, children come from the listed parents) and a test pins it.
- The fake server now mirrors the real API: `/items` includes children of a trashed parent, `/items/trash` lists only items with their own `deleted` flag, `/items/<key>/children` hides an individually trashed child. This makes the existing "trash is left out by default" test fail without the fix, which is the point. The #680 round-trip tests count items Zotero *shows* (not in the trash, directly or through their parent).
- One older test listed an attachment whose parent was not in the list; it now lists the parent.
- CHANGELOG "Fixed".

Tests: no item without its parent in the archive (library and collection scope, with an annotated PDF under the trashed parent), `counts.items` equals the archive, the offline gateway with a `deletedItems` parent (out by default, in with the trash), and the filter itself on a chain of orphans.

author: ufoptg
body:
Reduces `xcl_x_ballot()` cross-half exchanges in split-wave64 (`docs/wave64-on-wave32.md`) by propagating lane-local mask liveness through 64-bit bitwise SALU ops in `x64_masks.rs`.

**Why**
- In `x64_masks.rs`, `v_cmp*` and carry outputs (`v_add_co_u32` / `v_sub*_co_u32`) already avoid a cross-half `xcl_x_ballot()` exchange (`xcl_x_ballot_local()`) when they feed only per-lane readers (`v_cndmask_b32`, `v_add_co_ci_u32`, `v_sub*_co_ci_u32`).
- However, real wave64 compute/mesh shaders frequently combine multiple compare masks with 64-bit bitwise SALU ops (`s_and_b64`, `s_or_b64`, `s_xor_b64`, `s_andn2_b64`, `s_orn2_b64`, `s_nand_b64`, `s_nor_b64`, `s_xnor_b64`, `s_not_b64`, `s_mov_b64`, `s_cselect_b64`, `s_cmov_b64`, `s_wqm_b64`) before feeding `v_cndmask_b32`. Previously, `x64_masks` treated every SALU instruction as reading its source SGPR pairs whole, forcing `xcl_x_ballot()` on all upstream compares even when neither the result mask nor `scc` was ever read whole.
- Because `xcl_x_ballot_local()` leaves each 32-lane half's own word exact (low dword on half 0, high dword on half 1) and none of these 64-bit lane-wise ops crosses the 32-lane boundary, each half produces its own exact 32-lane result word without exchanging the inputs — provided:
  1. the destination pair is not whole-live afterward (`EXEC` is always whole-live, so writes to `EXEC` stay exchanged);
  2. if the op writes `scc` (all except `s_mov_b64` / `s_cmov_b64` / `s_cselect_b64`), `scc` is dead afterward (tracked jointly in the backward liveness pass, including `LOOP_GUARD` exits and kernel-mode end readback);
  3. destination and SGPR source operands are even-aligned 64-bit pairs (so low/high half words never cross-alias), and special scalar codes `vccz` (`251`) / `execz` (`252`) still mark `VCC` / `EXEC` whole-live.

**What is in it**
- `crates/xcl/src/gpu/recomp/x64_masks.rs`: track `scc` liveness alongside whole-live SGPRs (`reads_scc`, conservative `writes_scc` matching `emit.rs`, `lane_wise_salu64`, and `flow()`), propagate non-whole-live masks through even-aligned 64-bit lane-wise SALU ops, update three existing tests that used a dead `s_mov_b64 s[2:3], vcc` as a dummy whole-reader, and add 6 unit tests covering bitwise chains, live vs overwritten `scc`, `s_and_saveexec_b64` / `EXEC` writes, `s_cselect_b64` / `s_cmov_b64`, `vccz` / odd alignment, and `LOOP_GUARD` exits reading `scc`.
- `crates/xcl/src/gpu/recomp/emit.rs`: require `n & 1 == 0` when emitting `xcl_x_ballot_local` into `Dst::S(n)` so low/high half alignment is guaranteed globally.
- `crates/xcl/src/gpu/recomp/tests.rs`: add GPU test `gpu_split_wave64_bitwise_lane_masks` verifying both 0-exchange bitwise mask chains (`s_and_b64`, `s_andn2_b64`, `s_not_b64`, `s_or_b64`, `s_mov_b64`, `s_cselect_b64` → `v_cndmask_b32`) and kept exchanges when `scc` is read (`s_and_b64` matching upper half only → `s_cselect_b32`).

**Measured impact (RTX 3060 Ti, split-wave64)**
- Across 10,490 translated wave64 compute/mesh programs from a retail shader corpus: `xcl_x_ballot()` calls drop from **210,324 → 170,561** (**−39,763 exchanges, −18.9%**).
- Cold DXC (`cs_6_6`) and NVIDIA D3D12 PSO compile benchmarks on three retail compute shaders (before `384f7f7` → after `02d65c8`):
  - Compute shader #1: `xcl_x_ballot` `513 → 433` (−15.6%), DXIL `834,160 → 803,648 B` (−3.7%), DXC `23,166 → 14,804 ms` (**−36.1%**), cold PSO `28,780 → 21,316 ms` (**−25.9%**).
  - Compute shader #2: `xcl_x_ballot` `420 → 370` (−11.9%), DXIL `512,592 → 494,064 B` (−3.6%), DXC `12,011 → 8,786 ms` (**−26.9%**), cold PSO `16,405 → 11,792 ms` (**−28.1%**).
  - Compute shader #3: `xcl_x_ballot` `135 → 75` (−44.4%), DXIL `152,752 → 130,920 B` (−14.3%), DXC `3,455 → 1,874 ms` (**−45.8%**), cold PSO `4,106 → 3,108 ms` (**−24.3%**).

**Tested**
- Hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti 8 GB (driver 32.0.16.2101), Ryzen 5 7500F, 64 GB RAM, Windows 11 Build 26300, DXC 1.9.2609.5, Rust 1.100.0 (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`), debug + release.
- `cargo test -p xcl --lib x64_masks -- --test-threads=1`: 22 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p xcl --lib gpu_split_wave64 -- --test-threads=1`: 6 passed, 0 failed (including new `gpu_split_wave64_bitwise_lane_masks`).
- `cargo test --workspace -- --test-threads=1`: 744 passed, 0 failed, 41 ignored (1 SKIPPED GPU test: `gpu::recomp::tests::gpu_wave32_program_in_wave64_hardware` (no wave64)).

**Regression run**
*(local folder name redacted to `retail-title` in both blocks; all metrics are exact output of the warm-cache 60 s runs with `XCL_NETWORK=0`)*

**Not tested**

**AI use**

Covers adopted Desktop screen and CTRL entries, synthetic Library and Outline, editing, Revision history and recovery, Knowledge, proposal approval and application, optional modules/jobs, workspace and preferences, and Publishing.

No external requests were recorded.

body:
## Correctifs trouves en production apres le deploiement de l'etape 3

### 1. Le repos du calendrier pouvait venir d'un match futur

Detecte sur Arsenal - Manchester City en production : « repos tres court
(-182.0 et -182.0 jour(s) depuis la derniere rencontre) ».

Le repos etait calcule depuis la **date maximale** du tableau des
rencontres, qui peut contenir des matchs a venir (le calendrier ESPN
d'une equipe inclut la fin de saison). Un repos negatif ne veut rien
dire, et surtout l'information future entrait dans le calcul.

Seules les rencontres **strictement anterieures** au coup d'envoi
comptent desormais. Un controle de non-regression (`scripts/step3-check.ts`)
couvre le cas.

### 2. Le bloc « validation a grande echelle » n'etait pas publie

Le generateur de la calibration le prevoyait mais ne l'ecrivait pas ; il
fallait que le rapport strict existe deja. Il le lit desormais dans
`data/backtest-report.json` et l'ecrit dans `app/lib/calibrationParams.ts`.

author: thweetkomputer
body:
Stacked on eloqdata/lavik#501. In the reported 1,280-connection SET profile, 83 of 178 sampled minor faults occurred while appending overwrite retirement receipts. This change targets repeated growth of that vector.

Each storage worker can lend one empty allocation to the first overwrite in a new staging batch. The flush snapshot and settlement coroutine retain exclusive ownership until every retirement completes. A successful settlement releases the old records' extent references and offers the empty vector for reuse. A cache miss follows the existing append path.

Idle usable capacity is admitted and charged against the worker budget, capped at 512 KiB per worker. That covers the 384 KiB of receipts for 8,192 overwrites. Existing periodic flush maintenance drops a spare after one second idle or when the worker is over its admission limit. No per-SET timer or cross-worker synchronization is added.

Focused tests cover pointer reuse, extent ownership, retained-memory accounting, bounded capacity, expiry, and admission failure. The 1,280-connection workload still needs an A/B comparison against the parent commit.

Verified on AArch64 with GCC 14 and storage test fault injection enabled. All 11 spare-buffer, storage-resume and shutdown tests passed, including retirement during overlapping flush snapshots. A two-worker SET smoke test recovered all 1,024 final 1 KiB values after 7,168 overwrites and a server restart.

author: alexandra-stoica-intern
body:
## Jira
CHAT-291

## What changed
- **The composer's @mention list no longer goes stale** when someone joins a channel after you opened it. Before, `useChannelMembers` fetched the channel's members once, when the channel opened, and nothing on the WebSocket says someone joined. A new member only appeared in the suggestions after a page reload.
- `useChannelMembers` now fetches the member list again in three cases (the three the ticket lists):
  - **A message from someone the list doesn't know.** New pure helper `unknownAuthor(message, channelId, memberIds)` in `features/messages/utils/channel-members.ts`. It ignores other channels and other events, and does nothing while the list is still loading. Each unknown author is only asked about once per channel, so a refetch that still doesn't list them (a failed request, or someone who left the team) isn't repeated on every message of theirs.
  - **A WebSocket reconnect** (`onReconnect`), which may have missed a join.
  - **Members I add or remove in Channel details → Members.** New `notifyMembersChanged` / `subscribeMembersChanged` in `features/channels/utils/members-changed.ts`, using the same listener pattern as `lib/theme.ts` and `lib/session.ts`. `useChannelSettings` calls it after `addMembers` and `removeMember`.

Web only: no API, event or backend change.

**Still open:** someone who joins but doesn't post appears after a reconnect, a reload, or a member change you make yourself, not instantly. Closing that would need a WebSocket message for membership changes from chatty-chat, which is a contract change for a separate ticket.

## How to test
1. As user A, open a channel where only A and B are members. Type `@` in the composer: only B is suggested.
2. Keep A's tab open. As user C, join the channel and send a message.
3. In A's tab, type `@` again (or keep the list open): C is suggested now, without reloading the page.
4. As A (channel owner or team admin), open Channel details → Members → Add members, and add user D. Type `@`: D is suggested right away, without D posting anything.
5. Remove D in the Members tab: D disappears from the suggestions.
6. Disconnect the network for a few seconds and reconnect: the list is fetched again (one `GET /channels/{id}/members` in the network tab).

## Checklist
- [ ] `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass (Python repos): n/a, web repo
- [x] Tests pass: `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npx vitest run` (49 files, 416 tests)
- [x] A bug fix comes with a test that fails without the fix: `channel-members.test.ts` (an unknown author is found; known authors, other channels, other events and a list still loading are ignored) and `members-changed.test.ts` (listeners are told the channel and can unsubscribe). The hook's refetch is not covered by a unit test; checked in the browser for a new author and for adding a member in the Members tab.
- [x] Docs updated (`chatty-infra/docs`) if an API, event or decision changed: n/a, no contract change
- [ ] `chatty-docs` known limitations updated if this opens or closes a gap: not done yet. "A member who joins without posting appears in @mention suggestions only after a reconnect or reload" could be added there. Say if you want it in this PR.

author: firsttris
body:
## Problem

A mail sent to a server with greylisting (here `mx03/mx04.secure-mailgate.com`: `451 … is not yet authorized to deliver mail … Please try later.`) stays in Stalwart's queue, and its submission stays `pending` until it goes out. Kontext kept showing **„Wird Di., 24. Nov., 13:38 gesendet.“** and the pill **„Geplant · 13:38“** long after 13:38. It looked as if the mail had never been sent.

## Change

- `src/jmap/submissions.ts`: fetches `deliveryStatus` with the held submissions. `delayReason` picks the receiving server's message for a recipient still queued after a temporary failure. Stalwart puts `250 2.1.5 Queued` there while a recipient is untried and the error (`Code: 451, Enhanced code: 4.7.1, Message: …`) after a 4xx (`crates/smtp/src/queue/submission.rs`, v1.1.1). `heldState` says scheduled / sending / delayed. Both are pure.
- `ScheduledNotice`: before its time as before. Past it: „Wird gerade zugestellt.“, or „Zustellung verzögert: Der Mailserver des Empfängers nimmt die Mail noch nicht an. Der Server versucht es automatisch weiter.“ with the server's answer below. „Nicht senden“ stays, since the mail can still be stopped.
- List pill: „Wird zugestellt“ instead of „Geplant · <time>“ once the time has passed.
- `useHeldMails` refetches every 30 s while any mail is held, so a delivered mail leaves the list and a delay shows up without reloading.
- Texts in `de.json` and `en.json`.

## Tests

`src/jmap/submissions.test.ts`: `delayReason` with Stalwart's real reply formats (greylisted, untried, delivered, without prefix) and `heldState` before, past and delayed. There is no e2e test: the e2e setup has no receiving server that answers 4xx, and building one is more than this change.

body:
Glass in two tiers, as Apple's small glass is clearer than its large glass.

**Thin tier** (bars, capsules, controls, which carry primary text only)
- Fill: 60% pale film in light, 66% ink film in dark, under a 10px blur (`--pl-blur-sm`) and a 180% color boost.
- Text-only buttons in a glass bar take the primary text color from the bar.
- Pressed, a thin control thickens halfway to the thick fill.

**Thick tier** (sidebars, panels, sheets, and controls with grey, pink or red text)
- Tabs, breadcrumbs, pagination, the select trigger, and tinted and destructive buttons read new strong material tokens.
- On glass, tinted and destructive faces mix 8% of their tone (21% solid), and pressing lightens them.

**Ring and selection on glass**
- `--pl-material-ring` and `--pl-material-selected`: the pink at oklch 32% in light, hot pink mixed 55% with white in dark, so they hold 3:1 on the thin fill. Increased contrast keeps its own colors.

**Light**
- Brighter rim highlight, glow and lower rim.

**Tests and stories**
- The glass legibility test in `surfaces.e2e.ts` measured role names that are not tokens (they resolved to the fallback color). It now measures `foreground`, `muted-foreground`, `accent-text`, `destructive-text`, `ring` and `selected`, composited on each ground.

author: virgilzhao
body:
## Cause

The failures on `rebuild` push runs 45389864257 and 45389921466 came from the test's tag generator, not from shared-DB ordering.

`publishPost` redacts the question and detail (`redact()` in `lib/domain/public-qa.ts`) before it reads their `#tags`. The test built its unique tags from `Date.now().toString(36)` plus `Math.random().toString(36)`, so a tag sometimes contained:

- a run of 7+ digits, which redaction reads as a phone or account number. For example, `#食mwunk1036928` was published as `#食mwunk[removed]`.
- `wx` followed by digits, which redaction reads as a WeChat ID. For example, `#rkmwunk18wx6q8busy` became `#rkmwunk18wx[removed]`.

The channel the test expected was then never made, or it was made under the shortened name. Whether a run failed depended on the clock and the random draw, so the `pull_request` runs on the same SHAs passed. The failing names in the CI logs reproduce the cut exactly.

The code is right: a phone number must not become a channel name.

## Fix (tests only)

- `tag()` now returns the prefix plus 12 random lowercase letters. With no digits in the tag, neither redaction rule can match it.
- A new test pins the behaviour: `#call…13812345678` files the post under `call…`. No channel is created with the number in its name.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- I ran the full `./scripts/test-integration.sh` twice in a row. Both runs: 186 files passed, 1 skipped (1590 tests passed, 4 skipped, the skips are pre-existing).

npm run storybook                            # Storybook has to be running

author: n-takatsu
body:
Refs #760（「公開のまま直す」のうち、HTTPのチャンネル・管理APIの11項目。ほかは別のPR）

mcp-rs本体は`with_request_handler`（直接のハンドラー）を使うので、本体の動きは変わらない。ライブラリとして`receive_message`・`receive_request_with_caller`（#749）で要求を受ける場合と、管理のAPIを使う場合の修正。

## 変更（`src/transport/http.rs`ほか）

| # | 項目 | 変更 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `is_connected()` | 待ち受けのタスクが動いている間だけ`true`。始める前・始められなかった後・止めた後は`false` |
| 2 | キューが満杯 | HTTP・WSとも、渡す前に期限（30秒）付きでキューの枠を取る。期限は枠の待ちと応答の待ちの両方に効く。HTTPは枠が空かなければ503、WSは返さずに接続を保つ |
| 3 | キャンセルされた要求 | 破棄のガードが、その要求の登録だけ（相関IDで）外す |
| 4 | 同じ`id`の2つのクライアント | 要求ごとに内部のID（`mcp-rs-N`）を`id`の代わりに入れ、`send_message`はそれで照合して、クライアントの元の`id`に戻す（`RequestId`で持てない`1.5`等も）。期限切れの後の遅い応答も、次の要求に届かない。HTTP・WSとも |
| 5 | 再び`start_server()` | 始める・止めるを直列にし、動いている間の`start_server()`はエラーで、`bound_addr()`は変えない |
| 6 | `stop()` | 待ち受けのタスクに止める合図を送り、リスナーを閉じ（ポートを放す）、HTTPの接続のタスクも終える。開いている`/ws`にはクローズフレーム（AWAY）を送る。`stop()`は待ち受けのタスクが終わるのを待つ |
| 7 | `connection_stats()`のpanic | 統計を`std::sync::Mutex`で持ち、写しを返す。大きさの計算はロックの外 |
| 8 | 2026-07-28版のHTTPステータス | チャンネル経由も`respond_with_request_handler`と同じ判定（`id`の無いエラーは400、2026-07-28版は`modern_response_status()`、ほかは200） |
| 9 | 選んだ版 | キューの要求ごとに、`MCP-Protocol-Version`で確かめた版を持つ（ヘッダーが無い・WSは`None`）。新しい`receive_request_with_context()`で受け取る |
| 10 | `TransportError`の変換 | `Error::TransportError(e) => e`を足し、元の種類を保つ。`Transport::start()`も元の種類を保つ |
| 11 | `ws://wss://` | 既に`ws://`・`wss://`で始まるURLはそのまま表示する |

### 公開のAPI
- 追加: `HttpTransport::receive_request_with_context()`（`Option<ReceivedRequest>`。`request`・`caller`・`protocol_version`。`crate::transport`から再公開）。`receive_request_with_caller`はこれを呼ぶ
- 追加: `HttpTransport::stop_server(&self)`。`Transport::stop`はこれを呼ぶ
- 動きの変更: チャンネルの要求の`id`は内部のID（文字列）になる（受け手が要求の`id`を応答にそのまま写すなら、変えなくてよい）。動いている間の`start_server()`はエラー。`is_connected()`は始めるまで`false`
- `HttpTransport`を破棄しても、サーバーは止めない（今までどおり。テストの補助が破棄して動かし続けるため）

### 残したもの（11項目の外）
- `send_message`が照合できない応答（サーバーからの通知等）は、今までどおり要求のキューに入れ、その送信は期限なしで待つ
- `stop_server()`は`/ws`の接続に閉じるよう伝えるが、そのタスクが終わるのは待たない

- CHANGELOG（Added・Changed・Fixed）

## テスト

`test_server_start_and_stop`（1・5・6）、`test_request_channel_reserves_a_slot_with_a_deadline`、`test_dropping_a_pending_channel_request_removes_only_its_registration`、`test_channel_responses_are_not_mixed_up_between_clients_using_the_same_id`（2つのAPIキー、同じid 1、逆の順に応答）、`test_connection_stats_can_be_read_from_a_tokio_task`、`test_channel_modern_responses_get_the_same_http_status`、`test_channel_requests_carry_the_protocol_version`、`test_wrapped_transport_error_keeps_its_kind`、`test_websocket_display_keeps_the_scheme`

`cargo test --lib transport`: 168件（1件無視）、`--lib mcp::server`: 57件、`--bin mcp-rs`: 5件、統合テスト（anti_replay_http・http_websocket_tls_integration・network_policy_http・no_config_startup・ids_integration）すべて成功。`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`: 警告なし

author: poppin-fumi
body:
## Summary

Until now the security check sent its `keys` section as unreadable. This PR replaces that with a read-only search on the server for private keys and secrets kept in plain text. It goes on top of `feat/security-check` (#85) and needs the `security-check-pilot` feature, like the rest of the check. The BIP-39 English word list is embedded under its MIT licence and compiled only with `security-check-pilot`.

**What it finds.** Each find is one `KeyKind`:
- `solana_keypair`: a JSON array of exactly 64 integers from 0 to 255.
- `evm_private_key`: a file whose name contains `key`, `private` or `wallet` (in any case, `.pem` excepted) and that holds only 64 hexadecimal digits, with or without `0x`.
- `mnemonic`: 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24 lower-case words from the BIP-39 English list, and nothing else.
- `unencrypted_keystore`: a JSON object with a private key field (`privateKey`, `private_key`, `privKey`, `secretKey` and similar spellings) and no `crypto` object. Encrypted Ethereum keystores and erpc's own keystore files do not count.
- `env_secret`: a line of a `.env`, `*.env` or `environment` file that sets one of these variables to a value written out. The variable's name contains `PRIVATE_KEY`, `SECRET_KEY`, `MNEMONIC`, `SEED_PHRASE`, `KEYPAIR` or `WALLET_KEY`. "Written out" means not an `op://`, `keychain:`, `keystore:` or `$` reference, and not a path starting with `/`, `~/`, `./` or `../`. A name ending in `_PATH`, `_FILE` or `_DIR` is not counted.
- `process_env_secret`: the same variables in the environment of any process that can be read.
- `history_secret`: a line of a bash, zsh or fish history that holds any of:
  - 64 hexadecimal digits in a row;
  - 87 or 88 base58 characters in a row;
  - one of those variables set to a value.

  A transaction signature, hash or digest of the same length is counted too. The docs say so.

**Roles.** The search reads the identity file each running validator was given (`--identity`) and works out its public key on the server. A keypair whose public key matches counts as `validator_identity`. Every other key is `unknown`. No RPC is used.

That identity file is the one read outside the walk's rules below: it is read where the validator reads it, through symbolic links and on any filesystem. It is read only if all of these hold:
- it is a regular file of 1 byte to 64 KiB (on Linux: opened with `O_PATH`, checked with `fstat`, reopened with `O_NONBLOCK`);
- it is not on a kernel filesystem such as procfs, sysfs, debugfs or tracefs (by `fstatfs`);
- it is owned by the validator's user (from the `Uid:` line of `/proc/<pid>/status`), unless the validator runs as root.

All of this is checked on the path-only descriptor before the file is opened to read, and it is read no further than its size. An identity file it does not read makes the search partial. So does a validator whose identity file cannot be told: Firedancer, an unreadable command line, or a path that cannot be resolved. A program merely named like a validator therefore cannot make the search open a file its user does not own.

**Where and how it reads.**
- It walks `/root`, `/home`, `/etc`, `/opt`, `/srv`, `/var/lib/docker/volumes`, `/var/lib`, `/tmp` and `/var/tmp`.
- It opens each directory and file relative to the descriptor of the directory it was listed in (rustix `openat` and `Dir`), with `O_NOFOLLOW`. A directory swapped for a link during the walk therefore leads nowhere new.
- It does not follow symbolic links. A starting directory that is itself a link is skipped and marks the search partial.
- On Linux every entry is first held with `O_PATH`, which opens no device and waits on no pipe. Its type is checked with `fstat`, and only a directory or a regular file is reopened to read, through that same descriptor, with `O_NOATIME` where the system allows it (always for root). Elsewhere, where the check does not run but the tests do, entries are opened with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`.
- It does not cross into another filesystem (compared by `st_dev`). The exception is a home directly under `/home`, which may be a filesystem of its own.
- It skips `.` and `..`, Docker's `overlay2` image layers, and every directory named `ledger`, `accounts`, `snapshots`, `rocksdb`, `chaindata`, `geth`, `nodes` or `data`.
- It reads files of up to 64 KiB, the last 1 MiB of a history, and process environments of up to 1 MiB; a larger environment is not read and marks the search partial.
- It goes at most 48 directories deep, holding one descriptor per level.
- It stops after 200,000 entries or 20 seconds, counted between entries. Every check of a file's contents takes time in proportion to its length; a test feeds it 1 MiB lines built to be slow.

**Access.** `access` comes from the permission bits and groups of the file and of every directory above it, starting at `/`:
- `world`: others may pass every directory and read the file;
- `group`: the group may read the file, and may pass every directory (through a directory's group bits if it is the same group, otherwise its others bits);
- `owner_only`: otherwise.

This is an approximation, and the docs say so: an account that owns a directory above the file is not considered, and neither are access control lists.

**Coverage.**
- `partial`: any of
  - the budget ran out, or a tree went deeper than the limit;
  - a directory, file, environment or identity file could not be read;
  - a validator's identity file could not be told;
  - a starting directory is a link;
  - a count was capped, or groups were dropped to fit.
- `unreadable`: none of the starting directories could be read.

**Key bytes and paths.**
- Contents go into one buffer that is wiped after each file.
- The keystore check skips JSON values without copying them, and the keypair is parsed into memory that is wiped.
- The request carries, for each `(kind, role, location, access)`, only a count, capped at the service's bound.
- The paths go into a separate list (`Places`) that is never serialized. The report lists them under each key finding on the operator's screen, at most ten per group and then "and N more", with control and bidirectional characters escaped.
- `--json` stays path-free.

`docs/ai.md` lists what the search reads and skips, plus the limits above. A new message (`detail.key_more`) is added in all four languages.

## Known limits

- A validator in a container or chroot has its `--identity` path looked up on the host, not under its own root. Its identity keypair then reads as `unknown` in a search reported as complete.
- An identity file owned by root, given to a validator that does not run as root, is not read; the search is reported as partial.
- The 20-second budget is counted between entries, so a read that blocks (FUSE, NFS, a process environment whose memory lock is held) is not bounded by it.
- The identity read's kernel-filesystem check is tested on its own, not through a non-empty kernel file named as a root validator's identity.
- `docs/ai.md` does not yet say that an identity file must be at least 1 byte, or list "a starting directory that is a link" among the causes of a partial search.

## Checklist

- [x] No secrets, tokens, `.env` files, 1Password vault/item identifiers, Cloudflare account identifiers or internal hostnames are included (see `docs/public-hosts.md`). Every test key, seed phrase and env line is generated when the test runs.
- [x] Nothing in this PR belongs in ELSOUL LABO's private operations documentation instead of this public repository.
- [x] No new dependencies (`Cargo.lock` is unchanged). The existing unix-only rustix dependency of `erpc` gains its `fs` feature, which adds no crate. The word list is a data file with a `REUSE.toml` entry (MIT), and its notice is also beside the `include_str!`.
- [x] Every new file has an SPDX header or a `REUSE.toml` entry.
- [x] `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (standard, node-check and security-check builds) and `cargo test --workspace` pass locally.
- [x] No w

author: dfattal
body:
**Based on main** (after the A10 squash 652db75e3); no longer stacked. Draft.

Uses the shared helpers in `comp_segments_view_size.h`:
- `_overlay_mode` (the frame-mode overlay);
- `_tile_map` (the per-view crop map);
- `_log_change` (the one change-only WARN).

`_update_for_window` is not used: Metal cuts the table in points but must evaluate it against the drawable's backing px, see below. `comp_metal_compositor_get_segment_metrics` returns true when the effective table is valid, even if the window is not split.

**Also:** the macOS service's **Metal** weave backend (`comp_multi_weave_macos_metal.m`) now does what the Vulkan backend does:
- it runs the view-size step after each segment update and publishes the effective table (`comp_multi_weave_macos_publish`);
- it hands the record the confirmed slot, so each other screen's segment is drawn in its own entry.

## What changes

**Metal segment manager** (`src/xrt/compositor/metal/comp_metal_segments.{h,m}`)
- Holds a `comp_segments_view_size` (the shared header from #2797, not forked). `comp_metal_segments_update_view_size` advances it from the point table that `comp_metal_segments_update` cuts on every weave of a placed window. It runs whether or not the frame splits, including zero-copy frames, so the size follows the window back. It writes change-only WARNs with the same wording as vk_native (`view size: the window covers ...` / `view size: the window is on the session screen ...`), so one grep works on both platforms.
- `comp_metal_segments_record`: each non-primary segment is cropped in **its own screen's entry** for the app's slot (`comp_segments_view_size_segment_grid`). Segment tile v takes the session's view v. Its DP is told the entry through `set_output_entry`, only when the entry changes. The primary keeps the session grid.

**Metal compositor** (`comp_metal_compositor.m`)
- Publishes the effective table in `xrt_segment_metrics::table`. The state tracker's enumerate and `XrEventDataRenderingModeTableChangedDXR` already read it for Metal (#2797's `locate_fetch_segment_metrics`).
- Overlays the table on the frame's mode in the commit, so the atlas is laid out from the table the app was told. Legacy apps are untouched.
- Grows the atlas and depth once to the **instance's** worst case (`xrt_system_compositor_info::atlas_*_pixels`, covering every claimed screen) when the screen list arrives. Until now they were sized from the head display's modes only.

**DP ABI**: `xrt_display_processor_metal::set_output_entry` is appended after `get_eye_positions_at` (ADR-020, no ABI bump). It is announced by `XRT_DP_METAL_HAS_OUTPUT_ENTRY` and called through a size-gated wrapper. **sim_display's Metal DP** implements it: a screen-bound sim DP draws its screen's entry ("Same as 2D", "Anaglyph", ...) whatever the process-wide output says.

**Points vs backing px (the #2791 bug class).** The table is still cut in points. Every pixel quantity is in the **drawable's** backing px:
- Each segment's canvas and crop are its point rect × (drawable px / window pt), never × its own screen's scale.
- The effective table is evaluated against the drawable size. Evaluated in points on a 2x panel, the clamp to the instance's worst case would pass a window whose atlas overflows it.

The pure part is in `metal/comp_metal_segments_geom.h`: cut, canvas in drawable px, the view-size step and the crop plan. It is unit-tested by `tests_comp_metal_segments_geom` for a 2x Retina + 1x external pair (straddle with either majority, wholly on the external with Anaglyph, the drawable-px clamp).

**Not segmented on macOS, so unchanged:** the in-process Vulkan (MoltenVK) compositor (`VK_NATIVE_HAVE_SEGMENTS` is Linux/Windows only) and the GL compositor (`comp_gl_segments` is Windows only). They publish no table, and the session screen's table stands as before. The macOS service's Metal weave backend now runs the view-size step too (see above).

## Tests
- New: `tests_comp_metal_segments_geom`.
- Updated: `tests_dp_eye_positions_at` (Metal vtable layout).
- Run locally on Linux: `tests_comp_metal_segments_geom`, `tests_u_screen_modes`, `tests_dp_eye_positions_at`, `tests_comp_segments`, all passing.
- The Metal / ObjC code cannot be built on Linux: macOS CI is the compile gate.

## Manual test (Mac, built-in Retina + one external display)
See the report in the PR thread / hub. Short version: sim-display on both screens; `displayxr-cli dp mode set anaglyph --screen <external key>`; run `cube_handle_metal_macos` on the Retina panel, then on the external display, then straddling; grep `view size:` / `rendering-mode table changed` / `draws entry`; capture with `/tmp/dxr_atlas_trigger` and `$TMPDIR/displayxr_segments_trigger`.

body:
## Summary
- The current Yandex connect flow first calls GET /models. That endpoint is a model-metadata/list operation and can return 403 even though the service account has permission to generate text.
- Add a small test request through the same chat-completions path used for chat.
- Use this request when connecting/checking Yandex AI Studio.
- Avoid polling GET /models for Yandex connection status; keep the existing model-list behavior for generic OpenAI-compatible providers.

## Why
The documented minimum permissions for text generation are API key scope `yc.ai.languageModels.execute` and service-account role `ai.languageModels.user`. Listing model metadata is a separate permission area. This change validates the operation the user actually needs rather than requiring extra listing rights.

## Validation
- Frontend build and Python runtime CI.
- Live Yandex API request requires the user's own key and is not run in CI.

author: karanmrn
body: ## Problem A send could check its recipient, pause during a handle rename, then recreate the retired conversation pair. Other late messaging writes could also escape the rename's row rewrites. Closes #3144. ## Change Migration 0266 guards pairs, group seats, deletion markers, poll votes, message senders and notification recipients at the database boundary. The trigger holds profile SHARE locks until commit and rejects retired aliases with SQLSTATE `23514`. An earlier insert makes rename wait and carry its row. A later insert waits for rename and refuses the stale handle. Inserts acquire live-author locks before profile locks. Updates check only newly introduced handle values. They do not acquire auth locks after rename already owns its profile, which avoids an auth/profile lock inversion. The existing store refuses failed writes without using its memory fallback. The rollback removes the guards without changing data. No production migration was applied. The captain must authorise and apply 0266 separately. ## How I checked it - `npm test -- __tests__/handleRenameMessagingMigrationEffective.test.ts __tests__/migrationVersions.test.ts`: **16 tests passed**. - Effective PostgreSQL coverage includes stale upserts after rename, all six messaging lanes, uppercase aliases, handle updates, retained transaction locks, auth/profile lock order, current writes, subsequent renames and rollback. - `npm run verify:no-mistakes:changed`: lint, route type generation, scoped typecheck and related-test discovery passed. The full RLS stage was still running when this PR opened. - `git diff --check`: passed. ## What I could not check The full local verification pipeline and PR CI had not finished when this PR opened. Production behaviour remains unchanged until the captain applies the migration. No UI code changed. ## Pseudocode ```text Read the handles introduced by this write. Resolve current and retired aliases to stable profile IDs. For inserts, lock live authors first. Lock the profiles FOR SHARE in stable ID order. Read current handles after the locks are acquired. Reject any introduced retired alias. Otherwise write the row and hold the locks until commit. ``` ## Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Messaging write] --> B[Resolve stable profile IDs] B --> C{Insert?} C -->|Yes| D[Lock live authors] C -->|No| E[Lock profiles FOR SHARE] D --> E E --> F{Introduced handle is current?} F -->|No| G[Refuse stale write] F -->|Yes| H[Write and commit] R[Rename locks profile FOR UPDATE] <-->|Conflicting transaction locks| E R --> S[Move messaging rows to current handle] ``` ## TDD proof 1. `4740a74469`: committed the failing stale-recipient regression before the fix. The PostgreSQL reproduction failed with `true !== false` because the stale upsert succeeded. 2. `26939993bd`: added the migration and rollback. `b5f0414dc0` connected the migration and expanded the effective proofs. The original reproduction then refused the stale pair. 3. `a74ecec3c7`: added a second regression after reproducing an auth/profile lock inversion, corrected that lock order, and verified the final **16/16 green** run. ## Summary

Removes the 2-second background system-locale polling thread and browser timer interval from `waterui-locale` and replaces them with platform locale-change signals across Apple, Windows, Linux, Android, and web.

- **`waterui-locale`**: Removes `regional::start_auto_refresh` and `regional::start_auto_refresh_default`, drops the unused `wasm-bindgen` / `web-sys` target dependencies, and exposes `regional::refresh_system_locale()` and `regional::update_system_locale_tag(...)` for backend notification hooks while keeping explicit `set_locale_tag` overrides authoritative.

author: 0815games
body:
## Worum es geht

Zwei Lücken aus der RAD-Analyse. Die Frage war: was tut RAD eigentlich im Spiel — und die Antwort war „zu wenig, und die Quellen sind dünn". Rohfleisch war dabei der auffälligste Punkt.

## Rohfleisch wird essbar

Sieben Fleischsorten lagen als `type: "component"` im Katalog — ungenießbar. Gemessen: `useItem` tat bei Kakerlakenfleisch exakt nichts, weder Heilung noch RAD.

Jetzt trägt jedes rohe Stück ein `raw`-Feld. Der Unterschied zum gebratenen ist der Punkt:

| Roh | +HP | +RAD | Gebraten | +HP | +RAD |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Kakerlakenfleisch | 8 | 6 | Gegrillte Kakerlake | 15 | 2 |
| Rattenfleisch | 12 | 9 | Ratten-Steak | 25 | 3 |
| Skorpiondrüse | 22 | 14 | Skorpion-Überraschung | 45 | 5 |
| Yao Guai Rippchen | 30 | 16 | Yao Guai Steak | 50 | 6 |

Roh heilt knapp die Hälfte und verstrahlt das Drei- bis Vierfache. Bei vollen HP wird das Essen verweigert, statt unnötig zu verstrahlen.

**Dabei aufgefallen:** Hundefleisch und Yao-Guai-Rippchen hatten gar kein Kochrezept. Roh essbar, gebraten unerreichbar — eine Sackgasse. Beide Rezepte sind ergänzt, und ein Test prüft jetzt, dass jede Rohware ein Gegenstück hat.

## Lagerschrank

Das Camp war eine Basisfunktion: schlafen, kochen, ausbauen. Der Schrank ist der erste echte Ausbau — und er löst das eigentliche Problem des Lagers. Das Inventar ist eng (10 + STR + Rucksack); wer unterwegs Beute sammelt, musste bisher wegwerfen. Einlagerstätte gab es keine.

- 10 Plätze auf Stufe 1, +5 je Stufe (55 auf Stufe 10) — wächst mit dem Upgrade, das es schon gab
- Einlagern nimmt Ware aus dem Rucksack, Entnehmen legt sie zurück
- Gleiche Ware landet im selben Fach
- Beim Einpacken reist der Inhalt mit, beim nächsten Aufbau ist er wieder da

## Nebenbei korrigiert

Der Balancing-Bericht schrieb zu den Buff-Items weiter „Effekte noch WIP" — falsch, seit B3 in #418 behoben ist. Korrigiert. Der neue Abschnitt „Roh oder gebraten" stellt beide Varianten gegenüber.

**Tests: 107 grün, 0 rot** (vorher 93). 14 neue in `tests/proviant.test.mjs`.

Version 14.0.2.

## Nicht enthalten

RAD als Ortsphänomen. Keine Zone und kein Wetter erzeugt Strahlung — die Glühende See ist reine Optik, der Strahlungssturm bewegt nur Partikel. Vorschlag mit Zahlen steht in `docs/BALANCE_BEFUNDE.md` unter „Noch offen"; das wäre der nächste Schritt, wenn du willst.

author: iyinusa
body:
This pins codearchy at `eff35be`, which brings in CodeArchy/codearchy#46–#48: authorship from git, the lens and Inspector section, and the host-agnostic ledger. It gives web users the authorship features through the Companion.

## Changes
- **Lens and Inspector:** connected to the Companion, the Map's **Authorship lens** and the Inspector's **Authorship section** work. They come with the shared UI; `CompanionEngine` already answers `authorshipStatus` and `authorship`.
- **Code viewer gutter:** a thin bar beside **AI-written (orange)** and **reviewed (blue)** lines. These are the same validated colours as the Map. The hover gives the tool and the evidence (a commit, recorded by a person, or captured in an editor).
- **Code viewer toolbar,** for the selected lines:
  - **Mark as reviewed**, and **Correct** (written by a person, by an AI tool, or unknown);
  - line counts and the current selection.

  Marks go to the Companion's ledger in its own data folder, **never into the files**. The Inspector and lens refresh from the Companion's change event.
- **Viewer behaviour:**
  - it's read-only but **selectable**, so the actions have lines to work on;
  - the gutter is **reconfigured in place** with a CodeMirror compartment. The smoke caught the first version rebuilding the editor on every update, which collapsed the selection to one line.
- **Without the Companion:** nothing changes. The browser-only engine has no git history, so these features don't appear.

## Smoke
The smoke runs against the real `codearchy serve`, with a throwaway `HOME` so its ledger never touches a real home folder. In each engine it:
1. selects the Authorship lens and waits for a node's badge;
2. opens `rb/lib/billing.rb` through search and the Inspector;
3. selects lines 1–2, checking the "Lines 1–2" label;
4. corrects them to AI, and the orange gutter appears;
5. marks them as reviewed, and the blue gutter appears with "Marked 2 lines as reviewed";
6. resets them to unknown, and the gutter clears.

A screenshot (AI and reviewed lines, the toolbar, and the Inspector's live Authorship section) was checked locally.

## Notes
- The lockfile is unchanged.
- `apps/site` is untouched.
- I didn't deploy anything.
- I ran the smoke locally, and all the authorship steps passed in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit. The run then stopped at the AI step that expects Ollama to be unreachable, because a local Ollama is running on this machine. CI has no local Ollama and runs the whole smoke.

python -m pytest
ruff check .

Then benchmark the COPY and VALUES paths against the same disposable PostgreSQL source/destination pair, including INSERT_ONLY, UPSERT, row-error isolation, restart recovery, and cancellation. Record sustained logical MB/s end-to-end; 10 MB/s is a target, not a claim of measured performance.

author: pawel-olejniczak
body:
## Summary

`min_tokens`, `logit_bias` and `min_p` were silently ignored on HPU. Requests that set them returned 200 with the output they would have had without them: `min_tokens` requests finished early on EOS, `logit_bias` did nothing, and `min_p` did not filter.

The V1 sampler applies these three only through the builtin logits processors (`MinTokensLogitsProcessor`, `LogitBiasLogitsProcessor`, `MinPLogitsProcessor`). The processors keep per-request state by persistent-batch row and learn about requests only from the batch update (rows added, removed and moved) that the input batch hands to `update_state()`. The HPU `InputBatch` built the processors but never recorded a batch update and never called `update_state()` (the old "follow upstream PR#16728" TODO), so their `apply()` was a no-op on every step.

### Changes

- **Record the batch update** in `InputBatch` as upstream does: `add_request` registers the row with its sampling params, prompt ids and the request's own output list (min_tokens reads its length every step); `remove_request` registers the removal; `swap_states` and `condense` register their moves. The runner picks the row for an added request itself, filling removed rows first, so a refilled row is taken out of the removed list (the processors apply additions before removals).
- **Apply it at the right point.** HPU reorders the batch in `sample_tokens` (decodes first, multi-token decodes last, prompts by context), after the sampling metadata refresh in `_update_states` where upstream applies the update. The new `InputBatch.update_logitsprocs()` runs after the last reorder and before the first sampler call, and again at the start of `_update_states` for a step that never reached sampling (no scheduled tokens), so two steps' changes are never merged out of order. It calls `update_state()` every step, as upstream, because min_tokens drops a request that reached its minimum only on that call.
- **Map sampling rows to batch rows.** HPU samples decodes and prefills in separate calls, each padded by repeating its first request, so logits row `i` is not batch row `i`. `make_selective_sampling_metadata` already knows the batch row of every sampling row; it now passes the active processors wrapped (`vllm_gaudi/v1/sample/hpu_logits_processors.py`). The wrapper copies the call's rows to their batch rows of a `[num_reqs, vocab]` buffer, applies the processor, and copies them back; padding rows are left as they are. When the call's rows are exactly the batch rows it runs in place. For speculative decoding, min_tokens on the draft rows is rekeyed from batch rows to the call's rows. The wrapper's `apply` is excluded from `torch.compile`, as `apply_logits_processors` already is, since its index tensors vary in length.
- **No cost when unused.** With none of the three parameters in the batch the sampler gets no processors at all: no copies, no device sync, nothing new in the compiled region.
- **Warmup batch.** When the largest decode bucket exceeds `max_num_seqs` (for example with speculative decoding), warmup builds a larger `InputBatch`, and that batch keeps serving afterwards unless it is restored. Its processors are now built for its own row count. Before, min_p sized its per-row state for `max_num_seqs`, so once `update_state()` ran, warmup's dummy rows past that index raised `IndexError` at engine start.
- **Remove dead code:** the input batch's own `min_p` tensors, which were filled and copied to the device but never read (the sampler applies min_p only through `MinPLogitsProcessor`).

Behaviour change worth a release note: clients that already set `min_p`, `logit_bias` or `min_tokens` now get what they asked for, so their outputs change.

Not in scope: custom `--logits-processors` stay refused on HPU (vendoring patch P7). This change is necessary for lifting that, not sufficient.

## Test plan

Gaudi 3, 2 cards, vLLM `43c1db8c9f` (the commit current `main` targets). Control arm: `main` at the parent of this commit, same machine.

- [x] New e2e test `tests/full_tests/test_logits_processor_params.py` (`run_logits_processor_params_test`), sync and async scheduling, Qwen3-0.6B. One case per parameter, each on a mixed batch: odd rows carry the parameter, even rows do not, with `max_num_seqs` below the number of prompts and different row lengths, so requests are admitted while others decode, prefills share steps with decodes, and rows move. Each case asserts its control first (min_tokens: greedy stops early without it; logit_bias: the biased token is not generated without it; min_p: sampling at temperature 1 differs from greedy without it), and the rows without the parameter must match a reference run token for token. On `main` all 6 cases fail on the parameter assertion, with every control passing; with this PR all 6 pass.
- [x] Reproduction from the issue, single request, sync and async: on `main`, `min_tokens=32` returns the same 10 tokens ending in EOS as the request without it, and `+100` logit bias is ignored. With this PR, 39 tokens with EOS only at the end, and the biased token every step.
- [x] Smoke checks outside the e2e test, Qwen3-0.6B, mixed batch of 8 with `max_num_seqs=4`:
  - compiled sampler (`enforce_eager=False`): min_tokens, logit_bias and min_p all applied;
  - ngram speculative decoding with 2 draft tokens, sync and async: min_tokens applied (rows that stop after 2 tokens without it reach their minimum); `main` ignores it;
  - warmup with a decode bucket larger than `max_num_seqs` (`VLLM_BUCKETING_STRATEGY=lin VLLM_DECODE_BS_BUCKET_MAX=16`, compile mode): engine start and min_tokens fine. Negative control: the same change without the warmup-batch fix dies at engine start with `IndexError: index 4 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 4`.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit_tests`: the same 6 failures on both arms (`test_fsdpa_slicing` accuracy cases that also fail on `main` on our test machines), no new failures.
- [x] e2e on this PR: `run_async_penalty_consistency_test`, `run_structured_output_test`, `run_preemption_test`, `run_row_order_test`, `run_load_generate_{a,b,c}_parallel` pass. `run_spec_decode_parallel` fails on both arms with an identical EAGLE3 acceptance rate, below the threshold on our Gaudi 3 machines; it is the known drop from #1973 and passes in CI on Gaudi 2.
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual` (mypy included) passes.
- [x] Decode throughput with none of the three parameters in use (Qwen3-0.6B, eager, offline, 64 requests of 128 tokens): 8 fresh starts per arm on one machine in counterbalanced order, token totals identical on every run. The difference is inside the noise band, no effect detected; the band, from 8 same-code start pairs, is wide on this setup (about 8%). The added work per step with none of them in use is a few Python list operations.

author: gvsccrc-it
body:
## Summary

Closes #546; the rest of that ticket merged in #576.

**What changes:** `compose.yaml` sets `pids_limit: 16384`, by the owner's decision on the ticket. Without a limit, a runaway process could exhaust the host.

**Why 16,384:** the limit counts threads. One server-side motion detector's FFmpeg runs about 21, a recording FFmpeg 3, a converting one about 22 (measured). So 200 cameras with server-side motion detection would pass the 4,096 first suggested, and a process that cannot start a thread stops recording.

**Other files**
- `docs/production-checklist.md`: `pids_limit` is now "in place", and the old 1,024 example is removed.
- `docs/handoff.md` is updated.

## Evidence

- `tests/test_connection_guard.py` checks the compose file sets 16,384. It also checks that is at least 200 cameras × (21 + 3) threads plus 1,024 for everything else. This test used to assert the limit was absent while the decision was pending.
- `tests/test_production_checklist.py` passes with the row now "in place".
- `tests/test_build_inputs.py` passes.
- `docker compose -f compose.yaml config -q` accepts the file.

## Not covered

- **The thread counts are from earlier measurements on 4 cores.** A host with many more cores may run more FFmpeg threads per process.
- **Not tried on the live server.** If recording ever fails to start with a "resource temporarily unavailable" error at a very large site, this limit is the first thing to raise.

author: cryptoxdog
body:
The pip-audit job resolves its locked set from `uv.lock` or a root `requirements.txt` only. A pip-tools repository keeps one hash-locked file per environment under `requirements/` and has neither, so **any** change to `pyproject.toml` — including every version bump — ends in:

```
pip-audit: a Python project with no uv.lock or requirements.txt has no locked set to audit; the audit is incomplete
```

It fails closed on a fully locked repository. Because the required Organization CI workflow is this file on `main`, no release-preparation pull request in such a repository can merge (Gate_SDK #87 is blocked on exactly this).

Each `requirements/*.lock` is a fully pinned set, compiled against the others so a shared package carries one version. They are audited together through the existing multi-file `--no-deps` path, exactly as the uv exports above are. The failure message now names the third accepted layout.

`nightly-sink.yml` and `promotion-canary.yml` are regenerated by their tools (`render`), and the byte-for-byte generation tests pass: 190 passed, 1 skipped.

body:
When a title is switched from Series X (`anaconda`) to Series S (`lockhart`) in the same data folder, `<data>\cache\uma_coherent.txt` still holds Series X's larger coherent-heap measurement and `note_coherent_need` never lowers it. On an 8 GB VRAM + 16 GB RAM Windows host this keeps the coherent window pinned at 4095 MiB (increasing non-local GPU memory usage under WDDM) even when the Series S profile only needs ~3407 MiB. Giving Series S its own `<data>\cache\uma_coherent_lockhart.txt` lets each console profile size its coherent window independently. Part of #333.

**What is in it**
- `crates/xcl/src/gpu/uma.rs`:
  - `coherent_file_for(data_dir, series_s)`: selects `uma_coherent_lockhart.txt` when `config().is_series_s()` is true and keeps `uma_coherent.txt` for Series X.
  - `coherent_hint_from(path, free)` and `record_coherent_need(path, bytes)`: helpers extracted from `coherent_hint` / `note_coherent_need` using saturating addition before clamping to `MAX_SIZE`.
  - Unit test `series_s_coherent_cache_is_separate_from_series_x`: verifies separate cache filenames, independent coherent window sizing (`4,804,771,840` B -> `MAX_SIZE` for Series X vs `3,036,545,024` B -> `3,573,415,936` B for Series S), monotonicity within a file, and the `NEEDS_FOR_COHERENT_HEAPS` low-commit fallback.

**Tested**

author: arlirad
body:
## Summary

Give `SIGAIO` its own ordinary signal ID `16`, leaving `SIGIO`/`SIGPOLL` at `29`. Previously `SIGAIO` was a libc alias of `SIGIO` (both `29`) and the kernel enum had `io = 29` with no definition for ID 16.

Base: `ea1fc1bd` (`origin/main` has since advanced only by the unrelated strftime PR #129; no signal overlap).

## ID16 collision proof

Before this change, ID 16 was undefined and unused:

- Kernel enum skipped it: `term = 15`, `chld = 17`.
- libc had no `SIGAIO 16`; `SIGAIO` was `#define SIGAIO SIGIO` (29).
- Both validity predicates explicitly rejected it: kernel `valid_signal(...) && value != 16`, libc `... && signal_number != 16`.
- `kernel/tests/mapping_test.cpp` asserted `mapper<signal_number>::from(16)` was rejected.
- No consumer, handler, header, test, or LTP case used ID 16.
- ID 16 was never an alias: commit `3e0b28db` added the explicit exclusion without defining an occupier.

This PR removes the exclusion only so ID 16 is valid, and assigns `aio = 16` and `io = 29` distinctly.

## Semantics

`SIGAIO` is now an ordinary, maskable, catchable, ignorable signal:

- `valid_signal`, the raw mapper, `sigaction`, `sigprocmask`, `sighold`/`sigrelse`, and `sigwait*` accept ID 16.
- It has its own 32-bit mask bit (`1u << 16`) and is not in `is_uncatchable`.
- Handler and explicit-ignore dispositions are accepted.
- Default-ignore is preserved for both `SIGAIO` (16) and `SIGIO` (29).
- `init_user` proves the AIO `sigwait` path with `1u << ASTIA_SIGAIO` and now asserts the delivered signal equals `ASTIA_SIGAIO`.

## ABI

No width or layout change:

- `NSIG` and `signal_count` remain `32`.
- `sigset_t` remains `typedef unsigned int` (32-bit).
- Existing asserts still hold: signal context `160`, `astia_sigaction_t` `24`, `astia_siginfo_t` `32`.
- No new syscall; no AIO CQ/event redesign.

## Evidence

- Fresh configure + full build (`x86_64/virt`, cross userspace): exit 0.
- Focused CTest 12/12: `astia_signal_test`, `astia_mapping_test`, `astia_aio_test` + five AIO handler/readiness/socket tests, `libc_signal_api_test`, `libc_aio_test`, guest `astia_initrd_boot` (init_user AIO sigwait at `1u << 16`).
- Re-run after final edits: 6/6 focused incl. guest boot.
- ASan + UBSan (`-fsanitize=address,undefined`, leak detection on): `astia_signal_test`, `astia_mapping_test`, `astia_aio_test` 3/3 pass.
- Pinned clang-format `18.1.8` dry-run on all changed files: pass. `git diff --check`: pass.
- LTP clean checkout `3b962a950b3f37153a45bf1240d07d73ab07676e`:
  - families: `sigprocmask` 12/12, `kill` 5/5, `sigaddset` 5/5, `sigdelset` 5/5, `sigismember` 3/3, `sigemptyset` 2/2, `sigfillset` 2/2.
  - individual: `sigwait/1-1`, `sigwait/8-1`, `sigaction/1-1`, `sigaction/2-1`, `sigaction/3-1`, `sighold/1-1`, `sigrelse/1-1` all PASS.
  - `toolchain/posix-expected-failures.txt` untouched.

## Residuals

- **Linux divergence:** ID 16 is Linux `SIGSTKFLT`; using it for `SIGAIO` is Astia-specific. `SIGSTKFLT` was never defined here, and no docs are changed in this slice.
- **Uniqueness coverage:** the new test enumerates the current enum values and catches duplicate IDs today; it is not a general proof against future enum additions.
- **Formatting churn:** the pinned formatter was applied to touched files whose base predated current include/alignment rules, so whitespace/include-order hunks accompany the semantic changes.
- LTP packaging uses a prebuilt zsh binary read-only; the selected signal tests do not execute it.

No merge requested here; hosted required checks should gate merge.

author: cambridgetcg
body:
## What

- **The terminal basis says what it proves.** A decision on a `controlling_terminal` agreement now reads `agreement asserted by controlling_terminal …: the terminal path asserted a yes, which proves no terminal and no person`. A passkey act keeps the person-agreed wording. The does-not-establish list names the same-user limit. The views that show a person act or set-aside carry `basis_note`; PROTOCOL says which views do and do not. The stored basis values and the signed bytes are unchanged, and decisions already written keep their words.
- **Passkey enrolment and revocation are journaled**, as `person.passkey_enrolled` and `person.passkey_revoked` events, where the key is used: in the workspace named by an enrol command's `--workspace`, otherwise as a backfill before the key's first act in a workspace. A key whose SPKI differs from the recorded enrolment gets a new event with its own fingerprint. Revocation is recorded where an enrolment exists, with the fingerprint derived from the key. Nothing is broadcast to every workspace.
- **A terminal that takes no output** after the write-retry budget reports `tty_unavailable`, saying nothing was written, instead of an internal error. Writes on the non-blocking terminal now retry `EAGAIN` for a bounded time.

## Why

Any process running as the same user can import the store and record a `controlling_terminal` agreement with no terminal at all, or answer the CLI's prompt through a pseudo-terminal. The records were identical to a real one, so labelling that basis as the person's agreement overclaimed. Passkey enrolment was outside the hash chain, so nothing in the journal backed the key a later act is checked against.

## Limits

The design still rests on same-OS-user trust for the terminal basis. This change makes the label honest; it does not add a gate. A key revoked before any act in a workspace leaves no event there. For a before-first-act event, `enrolled_at`, `rp_id`, `origin` and `label` are the row's own claim; only the event's `occurred_at` and chain position date the journaling. An rp_id or origin change alone adds no event, though the proof names both. A voice-attestation event is not part of this change.

## Compatibility

Two new event types, covered by the forward-compat fixture: every older build pages over them and addresses them to no one. No schema, CHECK, hashing or signed-byte change. Nothing newly refuses.

## Tests

Bun 1.3.5, full suite at `--timeout 120000` on the final tree: 1156 pass, 13 skip, 0 fail (1169 tests). At the default 5 s timeout on a loaded machine one test timed out (`tests/repository.test.ts` "discovery remembers unresolvable fingerprints", a file this branch doesn't touch; it timed out on `main` under similar load too) and it passes alone. `check:mcp-bundle` passes. Mutation checks, such as matching by id only, a row-copied fingerprint, a dropped basis note and a removed set-aside backfill, were caught. The write retry was also exercised by hand on a real pseudo-terminal.

## Merge notes

Other open collab PRs touch the same files. After resolving conflicts, rebuild `dist/` with Bun 1.3.5 and re-run `check:mcp-bundle`.

- Variable-K wgrad: persistent vkq (scale planes via async VMEM, optional sum-of-squares epilogue) and vk with an
  explicit window guard (PRIMUS_TURBO_MOE_FP8BLK_WGRAD); vkp as the internal building block.
- Glue: early pool tables (routing=), dispatch gather + dual quant, SwiGLU fwd / bwd + dual quant (Gluon quant2 core
  under the gate), combine + route dW in one launch, routed + shared add in the combine (add=), d top-k weights in
  one launch, wgrads into main_grad (side stream with PRIMUS_OVERLAP); combine handles H % 1024 != 0.
- EP>1 operator on the vkq family; benchmark bench_fused_mega_moe_fp8blk_ep.py.

Measured (MI455X, DeepSeek-V4-Flash proxy, development A/B): MoE GEMMs 22.8 -> 8.4 ms per step (-15.7 ms with the
glue), k256 -0.65, vkp schedule -0.25, vkq -0.37, mxp -0.3 ms, glue fusions about -1.5 ms together. GEMM variants
bit-identical to each other; EP emulation R = 1/4/8 bit-identical to EP = 1. Whole stack: 3 interleaved pairs on MI455X (CUDA graph, 20 iterations, median of iterations 11-20, lag logging off): development branch 45.92 ms vs this stack 45.27 ms (-0.65 ms; a second session gave 45.97 vs 45.30); loss@1 11.91726, loss@20 9.871274 and grad norm 4.144 in every run. About -0.15 ms of this is the cleaned-up code itself and about -0.5 ms comes with the newer dev/mi455x_v6 base (see P-4).

Tests: tests/pytorch/ops/test_fused_mega_moe_fp8blk_gfx1250.py, test_fused_mega_moe_fp8blk_guards.py,
test_fused_mega_moe_fp8blk_ep.py, test_moe_pool_glue_gfx1250.py (63 passed (incl. the upstream mutable-global rule test) on MI455X).

author: arynbht
body:
PR 3 of the shell redesign (`proposals/shell-redesign-2026-11-24.md`, section 2 "Tasks"): a board by beat, and a task's whole record in one detail. It follows the proposal's rules: every part is read from the runtime's records (the watcher's view of the task, and this machine's judge and proof files), and nothing here writes. Merging from the shell is a later PR.

## What changed and why

### The Tasks tab: a board by beat, and the list a toggle away
- A **Board** view with columns intake → route → build → prove → judge → ship → close. Isolating counts as the build's first step and a closed task goes under close.
- Each card shows the id, title, risk, cost and rounds. It also carries a badge when the task needs you. Cards that need a person to act on the record are amber ("Needs you: Route to approve"). A shipped task whose PR waits to merge is sky ("PR #42 waiting to merge"). So a task at ship can't be mistaken for one stuck at route.
- The badge comes from the same reading as the Now view's queue: `taskSummary` carries `waiting`, from `needsYouItems`, so merge waits are included.
- The table stays as **List**. A Board/List toggle sits in the header, and the choice is kept in localStorage.
- **Decision: List is the default for now, not Board.** Three existing e2e specs (`tasks`, `task-answer`, `tasks-progress`) open the tab and go straight to the "All tasks" table. With Board as the default they fail, and fixing them means changing existing tests, which is a stop-and-ask. Flipping the default is one line (`savedView()` in `Tasks.tsx`) plus a "click List" line in those three specs. It needs your OK to touch them.

### One watcher: the Tasks tab folded into the Now hub
- `tasks.ts` no longer runs a watcher of its own. `NowHub` gained `watchTab` / `unwatchTab` / `tabViews`. The tab's repo is watched by the same watcher as the Now view and the badges, at the shown interval, so a repo is polled once. A repo only the tab shows is watched until the tab goes.
- `watchRepoTasks`, `unwatchTasks`, `openTaskPr`, `taskLedger` and `answerTask` keep their signatures as thin wrappers. `task-actions.test.ts` passes unchanged.

### Task detail
It opens from a board card, a list row, a Now item (a new "Open T-… in Tasks" button on intake, route, stop and merge items) or a Recent row. Under the existing summary (live progress, answer form, outcome) it shows these parts:
- **Card:** description, type and risk, touches, out of scope, and each acceptance criterion with its verify kind and a status: met, unmet, unverified, hand-checked or not judged. Met and unmet come from the latest judge round's review. Hand-checked means the judge asked about the criterion as unverified and a person allowed it; the note says who. Silence counts as unverified, as the judge counts it. Unverified and unmet get a filled amber or rose row and pill.
- **Route:** sectors, skills (with spine), gaps, checks, proof, budget, stop-and-ask, approved or waiting, and the router's reasons (`parseAssembly`, `routeReasons`).
- **Plan:** the build's latest plan, from the ledger's `plan` entries after the last "build started" (now the runtime's `taskPlan`).
- **Proof:** proof.json (kind, pass, lines, new tests), test-run.txt (its last 64k characters), and the screenshots.
  - Screenshots show as images with side, page, breakpoint, HTTP status, pixel size and bytes, plus the axe table.
  - Only a screenshot's file name is trusted, so nothing outside `tasks/<id>/proof/` is read. Images go over IPC as data: URLs because the CSP allows no other source.
  - UI proof carries the warning: "Rivetari's UI screenshots may show the loading state (known issue R-25): check the page loaded."
- **Judge:** every round, oldest first: tier 1's checks (pre-existing marked), protected paths and notes, then the review's blocking findings and suggestions (kind, file:line, detail, repro, fix, downgrade reason), acceptance, anything unreviewed, and the verdict. A round whose record fails its seal is kept, with the reason.
- **Pull request:** the link, as before (the main process opens the ledger's URL). When you're signed in it also shows the PR's live state (open, merged or closed, draft, mergeable) and the check runs on its head (name, status, conclusion, head SHA).
  - This uses the engine's Octokit through `githubToken()` with the signed-in token, the same path as the Now view's CI line.
  - It has a 10 s timeout, is fetched separately so the page never waits on it, and has a Refresh button. It is read-only.
- **Ledger:** unchanged.

### Runtime (changeset: `@arynbht/rivetari-runtime` minor)
- `loadJudgeRounds(repoPath, task)`: every round, each checked against the hash its own verdict sealed, with a problem per round instead of a throw. `loadJudgeRecord` now shares the seal check and behaves as before.
- `taskPlan` (was build.ts's private `plan`) and `allowedDecisions` are exported, and take only `{ entries }`, so a watcher view will do.
- `watchTasks` takes `onRead`, told after each full read and its events.
- None of the owner-merge files are touched (`ledger.ts`, `store.ts`, `ladder.ts`).

### PR 2's review suggestions
- (a) Notifications are held in a map by repo and item until clicked or until the item leaves Needs you. The hub has a new `onGone` for that, and the notice is closed then. They're no longer dropped on `close`, which fires when Windows moves a toast to the Action Center.
- (b) The AppUserModelId is read from `electron-builder.yml`'s `appId` at build time (`src/main/app-id.ts`, a Vite `?raw` import). The installer and the app share one written id. electron-builder.yml isn't a protected path, but it's only read here, not changed.
- (c) "New since launch" goes by the task's own ledger seq once the watcher has caught up. The runtime's `watchTasks` gained an `onRead` callback, told after each full read has landed. After the first one, the hub records each task's seq, and a later item is news when its task's ledger moves past that.
  - Before that read (a local-first list catching up with the branch), and for a task the full read didn't have, there's no seq to go by. The entry's time is held against the hub's start, as the existing hub test pins.
  - Review round 1 caught the first version priming from the local snapshot, which told a week-old stop from the branch as new.
- A repo only the Tasks tab keeps watched gets no badge or notification.
- (d) `onState`, `onBadges` and the Tasks push use `safeParse` and log a mismatch instead of throwing into the watcher.
- (e) `judgeFindings` uses `plain` from task-beat.

## Proof
- `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run typecheck` (root, plus the desktop's node and web configs) are green locally.
- `pnpm run test` locally: 1284/1285 passed, with coverage above the thresholds. The one failure was `packages/cli/src/commands/init-proof.test.ts` timing out while the machine slept mid-run (its duration reads 18,802,923 ms). This PR doesn't touch that file, and it passes on its own (5/5). CI is the record.
- Desktop e2e: 23/23 locally, run with `RIVETARI_CONFIG_DIR` set to an empty temp folder. The new `task-board.e2e.ts` uses a fixture repo with a task at every beat: two judge rounds, the last leaving A2 unverified; a UI proof with screenshots, axe and a test run; an assembly with skills and gaps; and a hand-checked criterion. It asserts:
  - the columns and each task's placement;
  - that the shipped and route cards look different;
  - every detail part, with the criterion statuses;
  - the R-25 warning;
  - axe at 0 serious or critical on the board and on two details.
- New unit tests: `now-hub-tab.test.ts`, `task-detail.test.ts`, `task-pr.test.ts`, `app-id.test.ts`, and runtime `judge-rounds.test.ts` and `watch-read.test.ts`. No existing test was changed.
- Screenshots and axe are in the comment below.
