author: pohsuanlai
body:
## What

An export with a reported tail (`TailPolicy::Reported`, a bounce's `BounceTail::Graph`) asks the graph what is still owed at the programme's end and again after every tail block, and spends the smallest bound it has seen.

One ask has to bound what it cannot see: an instrument whose voices are in release at the programme's end (event inputs, not idle) is charged its declared ceiling, and a reverb after it its own. A file that ends on a note-off, which is most of them, then bounces to the cap as soon as the reverb's ceiling is large.

## The rule

The tail is measured from the programme's end. After `spent` frames of it, `spent + owed now` is an upper bound on it (it also counts what sounded after the end, so it is never short). The tail is the minimum over the asks:

- the first ask is the single ask main makes, so no bounce is longer than before (a source that keeps sounding, an oscillator or a drone, leaves the first bound standing);
- once the instrument says idle the node after it is no longer fed, and the bound drops to the release as it ran plus that node's reported tail.

The graph's latency is pulled once after the last ask, as before. It reads node status and reported figures only, so a render is as deterministic as it was. A normalised export renders once and replays, so its passes agree by construction.

`drive` is one loop over a `Phase` (programme, tail with `spent` and `bound`, flush, done); the fixed-tail path keeps its block partition.

## Tests

- New, failing on main at 8,820 + 25,300 (both ceilings): `a_bounce_after_an_instrument_in_release_ends_at_the_release_and_the_reported_tail` is 8,820 + 2 × 1,024 + 300 (the instrument sounds one block and says idle in the next; the node after it then owes its report of 300).
- New: `a_node_that_never_rests_spends_the_ceiling_and_no_more` (exactly the ceiling, not a block multiple).
- Every reported-tail test from #2109 holds its figure unchanged, the session reverb test included; `export_spends_the_tail_its_nodes_report_at_the_programmes_end` is the continuous-source case (a `Const` into a node reporting 100 under 4,000: 8,820 + 100).

## Size

Source +135 −78, tests +93 −0. No public item in; `RenderPlan::of_frames` narrows to `pub(crate)` (a `pub fn` on a `pub(crate)` type). The ask costs 1.8 µs on a 9-node graph, once per tail block.

## Review

tutti-dsp: approved (tier one, the claim about the nodes' reports). Read: the diff of `tutti-export/src/render/driver.rs` whole (`drive`, `Phase`). Not read: the tests in `render.rs`, the doc hunks in `job.rs`/`graph.rs`/`bounce.rs`/`plan.rs`, the two-pass path. Nothing built or run.

One limit found in review and written on `TailPolicy::Reported`: a bound holds when each report covers its node's ring-out for the controls still to come. A report that follows a driven control at the block's value (an LFO on a decay) can be cut at the low setting; main's single ask has the same weakness at one phase. The fix is the node's (tutti-dsp, branch `dsp/driven-tail-range`: the ceiling while a control the tail reads is driven).

Gates on the merge with main: fmt, gates, doc, workspace clippy, check-features, doctests, umbrella-api, check-windows, nextest on graph/export/nodes/session/tutti (3,785 passed): all 0.

Step 3, part B (stacked on A). Tests only.

The plan was to store every message in the thread before any turn, as engenty wizards' Work does, because Mastra was said to throw a stopped turn's input away. On Mastra 1.82 the home already keeps the words: the woken turn's input is stored as Mastra accepts the signal. These tests hold that: stopped during a tool, stopped while the model writes, failed, and a message delivered into a running turn that is then stopped; every later turn reads them, and a stopped tool call never reaches the next request without its result.

Storing first is still needed where Stop drops a queue; that is in D.

The fake Ollama can now hold its answer after the first word (`hold`), fail with a status (`fail`), and counts answers the caller stopped reading (`aborted`).

body:
Lets a launcher-driven (spawn.ini) game use VERA shared control, which the engine's own rooms already have: humans who write the same explicit `[SpawnLocations]` start control one House together.

- `cncnet_spawn.rs`: in modes whose policy has `shared_start_positions` (everything but Cooperative), two or more human non-spectator participants may share an explicit start. An AI never shares one (with a human or another AI); a human never takes an AI's start; Cooperative refuses any duplicate as before.
- Checks that counted participants now count Houses: the at-least-two-playing minimum, the ≤8-houses distinct-colour check (members' colours are ignored, the leader's is the House's), mode team validation (members play the leader's team), and `check_country_limits` (leaders' countries only). Participant limits are unchanged: PlayerCount + AIPlayers ≤ 30 with a relay; no per-start cap.
- `--probe` reports `"shared_starts": true`, so a launcher can tell a build that reads shared starts; a build without the field refuses one.
- `docs/spawn.md`: a "Shared starts" section and the probe field.
- `tools/spawn`: `--starts` / `STARTS=` writes explicit starts, shared ones included.

Downstream already handled shared Houses (start count, House creation, alliances, relay certificate per source, watch staging); nothing else changed.

Tests: three new `cncnet_spawn` tests (sharing, House-counted checks, refusals); `test -p vera20k --lib app::` passes (2761). Relay e2e `PLAYERS=3 STARTS=0,0,1`: two Houses built, source 1 joins source 0's House, the member leaving keeps the House playing. Also played by hand through the lobby and launcher with two clients sharing a House.

Lobby and launcher side: YuriPlanet/vera20k-lobby-server#60 and the launcher's feature/shared-starts; they only offer sharing when the engine's probe reports `shared_starts`.

author: shad107
body:
Lot 1 de #134 : la pyramide existante passe au modèle de l'issue et de sa section 4 bis, sans changer le comportement du firmware.

## Ce qui change dans `profiles.json`

- **Les types portent leurs boutons** : commande envoyée, comportement (`up`, `stop`, `down`, `step`...) et position sur la télécommande dessinée. Ils remplacent `capture[]` et `dpad`. Le portail a un seul bouton `step` (pas à pas), comme sa télécommande.
- **Chaque profil déclare ses deux axes** : la méthode d'ajout (`copy` : on reprend la télécommande d'origine ; `enrol` : le boîtier devient une nouvelle télécommande) et le moteur (`rejeu-brut`, `keeloq`, `somfy-rts`). Le parcours d'ajout de l'interface s'en déduit, il n'est plus écrit dans le profil.
- **Chaque profil a un `id`**, un bloc `radio` et un statut de test (`tested` / `untested`, d'après l'issue).
- **Profil Franciaflex ajouté** : famille KeeLoq 0x067 comme Profalux, porteuse à relever.
- **Clés en anglais.** Les valeurs gravées dans les fiches des appareils (marques, types `volet` / `portail`) ne changent pas : aucune migration.

## Interface

- `lib/catalog.ts` vérifie le catalogue à la lecture, valeur par valeur, contre les énumérations du domaine (aucune assertion de type). Un type invalide casse le catalogue ; un profil inconnu est écarté et signalé dans la console, pour qu'un profil d'une version plus récente (moteur `io-homecontrol`) ne prive pas l'interface des autres. En mode démo, un profil écarté casse l'interface.
- Les adresses désignent un profil par son `id` (`#remotes/enrol/profalux-enrol`), plus par sa position dans la liste : ajouter un profil ne casse plus aucune adresse.
- Un profil dont le moteur n'a pas de parcours dans l'interface n'est pas proposé.

## Plugin cloud

Les commandes d'un type viennent de ses boutons. Conséquence voulue : le portail n'offre plus qu'un bouton, celui que déclare son type. Le firmware reçoit la même commande qu'avant.

## Tests

- Banc de détection (`pyramid-detect`) : traits en chemins (`radio.band`), mis à jour, **ajouté à la CI** (il n'y était pas). Témoin : ne plus écarter un profil contredit casse 4 tests.
- Plugin cloud : 26 tests verts ; nouveau test « un portail a un seul bouton ». Témoin : un bouton « Fermer » ajouté au portail le fait échouer.
- Banc `cover-attrs` contre le nouveau fichier : vert.
- Vérification de types de l'interface : sans erreur.
- Parcours dans l'interface de démo : ajout Profalux, Franciaflex et CAME par leur `id`, sans erreur console.
- **Sur matériel** : M5Stack ATOM, OTA `0.2.17-profils1test1`, les deux volets Profalux enrôlés identiques avant et après, `/profiles.json` sert les 7 profils.

## Pas dans ce lot

Les trames par bouton et les constantes de l'enrôlement (codes boutons, rafales 9 × 5, rejeu 8 × 12 ms) restent dans le C : c'est le lot 2. Puis l'`id` du profil dans la fiche de l'appareil, la garde de bande, Velux io (#118) et les contributions de profils.

author: robnielsen
body:
This updates the default Gemini model from `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` to `gemini-flash-lite-latest`.

  The current default (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, introduced in #21239 when Gemini 2.5 became unavailable to new API keys) is already out of date, as Google has since released `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. Keeping a pinned version as the default means it falls behind new releases and will eventually face the same restriction and deprecation cycle that broke `gemini-2.5-flash`.

Using Google's rolling `gemini-flash-lite-latest` alias as the default ensures that:
    - New Thing configurations work out of the box without requiring periodic binding updates to bump the default model string.
    - Things using the default automatically migrate when Google updates the Flash-Lite release.
    - Users who want predictable, pinned behavior can still explicitly set any specific model ID in the Thing configuration.

author: acerv
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"acerv"} -->
_Requested by **Cervo** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01VZUE2Hre9TwEBUgyi1K9V8?thread=cmsg_01VZUE2Hre9TwEBUgyi1K9V8FqXs1Z9hCdbrJ4qFaY7xh4)_

The last two steps of the refactoring plan. Unlike steps 1-18, both change behaviour.

## Step 19: one shutdown path for signals

Before, `SIGHUP`, `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` called `process::exit` in the terminal UI, and had no handler with `-p` or with prompts read from standard input. The commands left running were not stopped and the repositories they created were not checked.

Now a signal ends the running prompt and leaves the way quitting does: commands are stopped, the git check runs, the terminal is restored, and `kl` exits with `128 + signal`. A second signal exits at once.

- `harness-tui/src/signals.rs`: `Signals`, a cloneable handle on one listener task, which ends when every clone is dropped.
- `terminal.rs` no longer owns a signal task; `restore_terminal` runs once only.
- `lib.rs`, `drive.rs`: the idle loop, a running prompt, `/compact`, `!command`, the model listing and the thinking check all stop on a signal.
- `main.rs`: `-p` and line mode stop the prompt on a signal (`error: stopped by signal 15`), and the exit code is set in one place, `run_until_signal`.

## Step 20: requests to the worker go through a writer thread

A call wrote its request to the worker's pipe while holding the worker lock in async code. With a worker that stopped reading and a request larger than the pipe, the call could not be cancelled. A writer thread, the mirror of the reader thread, now takes requests from a queue.

## Things to know

- A request queued in the short window between the death of the worker and the reader noticing it now fails with "exited unexpectedly" instead of being sent again to a new worker. A call made after that starts a new worker as before.
- After a signal the runtime is shut down without waiting, because a read of standard input left waiting would never end.
- A signal that comes while the terminal UI starts is handled once the terminal is set up.

## Tests

- `signal_stops_the_command_and_checks_git` (terminal UI, sandboxed) and `signal_stops_the_prompt_and_checks_git` (`-p`): after `SIGTERM` the exit code is 143, the command no longer runs and its `.git` is disabled.
- `signal_ends_the_prompts_read_from_standard_input`: line mode with standard input left open.
- `call_to_a_worker_that_stopped_reading_can_be_cancelled`: a 1 MB request to a worker that never reads.
- `signals_restore_terminal` moved next to the terminal emulator in `tests/screen.rs`.

author: zir0h
body:
Two things: notifications for Teia's on-chain comments, and the result of auditing every objkt/Teia contract against objkt.com's own list.

## 1. Comments on your tokens

Teia's comments contract `KT1FXFxUcZ…` was going nowhere — the calls fell through to `DefaultIgnore` like any unknown contract interaction. All 90 comments posted so far are on the Teia FA2, so this is Teia's feature with Teia's audience.

| Who is notified | When |
|---|---|
| the artist | somebody comments on a token they created |
| the author of a comment | somebody replies to it (`parent_id` set) |

Nobody hears about their own comment, and an artist answering under their own work is not notified twice. One setting — **"Comments on your tokens"** — covers both, on by default like the other token notifications.

**The comment text is deliberately not included.** It lives on IPFS (`content` is the bytes of an `ipfs://` URI) and the notification path is the one place here that cannot wait on a gateway. The notification links to the token instead, which works by registering the comments contract in the `marketplaces` table pointing at teia.art, so the existing link machinery resolves it with no special case.

Verified end to end on staging against a real comment at level 15907681:

```
token-comment  KT1RJ6Pb…:886852  from tz2M9sX1NesK…  to tz1VHekC8LCY…
```

`tz1VHekC8LCY…` being the artist who minted it. That artist's own comments on the same token produce nothing, as intended.

Teia's poll comments (`KT1FrjJUWK…`) and channel messages (`KT19ooSLPF…`) are deliberately left alone: they belong to a poll or a channel, not to a token or a wallet, so there is nobody for this bot to route them to.

## 2. A bug found while testing it: one transfer silenced a whole block

`unpackTransfersEvents()` read `$record['parameter']['value']` on whatever sub-records an operation group contains. A plain tez transfer has no entrypoint and therefore no parameter, so that read goes through null — a notice on PHP 7.4, a warning on PHP 8, and Fat-Free turns a warning into a fatal.

The cost is not the one record. **The analyzer walks a group at a time, so the fatal ends the whole level and every group after it is never looked at.** On level 15907681 the second of three groups was an ordinary transfer: the run died there and the comment, third in line, was never analyzed. After the guard the same level yields both the transfer's own `coin-transfer` event and the comment — so this was dropping real events, not just failing noisily.

The same shape in `ObjktComV23Hunter_Auctions` is guarded too (it searches sub-records for the current bid, and an auction settlement routinely contains plain transfers). Both sites sit inside `try/catch(Exception)`, which never helped: a warning promoted by Fat-Free is not an Exception.

## 3. The contract audit

Diffed every contract this project dispatches on against objkt.com's own `marketplace_contract` list (39 contracts), then measured Teia/hic et nunc (`KT1RJ6Pb…`) activity on each one that was missing.

**The headline: objkt.com's current marketplace was missing entirely.**

| Contract | objkt's name | Teia activity | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `KT1SwbTq…` | marketplace v6.2 | **events today**, ~74,000 tez, 4.36M calls | **handled** |
| `KT1HFYHt…` | english auction v6.1 | 86 events, 1,024,460 tez, last 2026-11-23 | **handled** |
| `KT1Wvk8f…` | english auction v1 | ~500 events, last 2022 | **handled** |
| `KT1ET45v…` | dutch auction v1 | 119 events, 22,047 tez, last 2021 | **handled** |

v6.2 has *more calls than the v6.1 this project did handle*, and it went live on 2024-11-05 — so for two years every objkt listing, sale and offer made through it was invisible: no notification for a seller, a buyer, a royalty recipient or a follower. The english v6.1 address was already sitting in the `marketplaces` table, auto-created with no name, which is what an unhandled contract looks like from the inside.

All four turned out to be configuration rather than new parsers: identical entrypoints apart from gallery variants, identical parameters, identical bigmap values apart from nullable extras the packers do not read, and the same fee wallet — verified against the chain, not assumed.

`Setapp\ObjktCom_v4` also writes down the version mapping, because objkt's names and this project's do not line up (our v3 is their v6.1, our v2 is their v4). That mismatch is exactly why a missing contract was easy to miss.

**Verified end to end** by indexing two real levels and running the market analyzer:

```
level 15955108  token-purchase  token 715153   75 tez   fulfill_ask
level 15955108  token-purchase  token 223     1.5 tez   fulfill_ask
level 15954923  token-list      token 526112  5000 tez  ask
```

all attributed to `KT1SwbTq…`, where the same levels produced nothing before. A separate check covers each wiring point: every hunter subclass accepts the new contracts and resolves to the right attributes, an unrelated contract is still refused, the addresses are advertised, and every bigmap packer produces a record from values fetched off the chain.

### Still not handled, deliberately

Fourteen contracts on objkt's list have **no Teia/HEN activity at all**, so they are out of scope here: akaswap swap v1 and v2, objkt english v5 and v5.1, objkt dutch v2, the three objkt fixed-pricing handlers, objkt project offers v1, drop.art, fxhash marketplace v3, 8scribo, emprops, dogami v2. `fxhash marketplace v3` is the only one of those likely to matter to someone — it is fxhash's current marketplace, and it affects fxhash users rather than Teia ones.

One more worth knowing: **HEN v1 (`KT1Hkg5q…`) is known here only as a minter**, so its `swap`/`collect` are not handled. Swapping there stopped in 2022, but a `collect` happened as recently as 2026-06-15 and a `cancel_swap` on 2026-10-17, so a handful of purchases from old v1 swaps go unnoticed. Left alone because it needs its own handlers rather than configuration.

### What could not be exercised on staging

Auction flows past dispatch, and the reply half of the comments feature. Auction details and a parent comment's author are read from the **locally indexed** bigmaps, and staging's bigmap sync is at level 1.49M, so neither 2024-era bigmap has rows there. This is equally true of the english v6 contract that was already supported. The reply path degrades to no notification when the bigmap is absent.

## Existing deployments

Reference data is only loaded into empty tables, and there is a new column:

```sql
ALTER TABLE options_notifier
    ADD COLUMN notify_token_comment enum('yes','no') DEFAULT NULL
    AFTER notify_token_update_metadata;
```

The `marketplaces` rows for the five contracts are in the commit messages as idempotent `INSERT … ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` statements.

body:
## What changes

Only `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` in `pyproject.toml`; no test or source file is touched.

- `-ra`: the end-of-run summary lists every skipped, xfailed and xpassed test with its reason. Before, a skip showed only as an `s` in the progress line.
- Strict markers: a test using a marker that is not registered in `pyproject.toml` stops the run at collection instead of producing a warning, so a typo such as `@pytest.mark.intergration` can no longer silently drop a test out of a `-m` selection.
- `xfail_strict = true`: an xfail test that starts passing fails the run instead of being reported as XPASS.

## Why strict markers is set twice

The `dev` extra allows any pytest from 7.0, and CI installs the newest release (the last green run on main installed 9.2.0). No single spelling is enforced on every supported release, measured with a throwaway test that uses an unregistered marker:

| pytest | `strict_markers = true` (ini) | `--strict-markers` (addopts) | both |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7.4.4 | unknown-option warning, not enforced | enforced | not measured |
| 8.4.2 | unknown-option warning, not enforced | enforced | enforced, plus one warning |
| 9.0.3 | enforced | not enforced | enforced |
| 9.1.1 | enforced | enforced | enforced |
| 9.2.0 | enforced | enforced | enforced |

On pytest 7 and 8 the ini key costs one "Unknown config option" warning and is otherwise ignored.

## Checked locally

- Full suite before and after, same command as CI (`pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=80`, Windows, Python 3.12, pytest 9.1.1 from `uv.lock`): 2394 collected, 2336 passed, 58 skipped in both runs. Coverage 97.37%.
- The new summary lists 58 skips under 9 reasons (for example 29 × "Win32 cannot create these names", 10 × "Windows tells them apart by winerror", 10 × "zstd needs Python 3.14+").
- With the new config, a throwaway test (not committed) using an unregistered marker stops collection with `'slooow' not found in markers configuration option`, and an xfail test that passes fails with `[XPASS(strict)]`.
- No test in the repo uses xfail today, so `xfail_strict` changes no result yet.

Not checked locally: Linux, macOS and Python 3.10 / 3.11; CI covers those.

author: chitralverma
body:
# Which issue does this PR close?

Closes #9029.

# Rationale for this change

`hdfs-native` does not report `write_with_if_not_exists`. The NameNode can do it atomically: `create` without the overwrite flag fails when the file exists, and the check and the create are one RPC. Applications that ask for exclusive creation cannot write to HDFS today.

# What changes are included in this PR?

- `hdfs_write` creates the file without overwrite when `if_not_exists` is set, and maps `AlreadyExists` to `ConditionNotMatch`. It skips the existence check that the normal write path does first.
- The service reports `write_with_if_not_exists`. `docs.md` and `website/data/capabilities.json` list it.

The hdfs-native behavior suite against a MiniDFS cluster passes 129 tests on main and on this branch. `test_write_with_if_not_exists` covers the new path: on main it returns early because the capability is off. `test_writer_write_with_if_not_exists` still returns early, because `hdfs-native` does not report `write_can_multi`. A downstream application that creates new files with `if_not_exists` and replaces existing files also worked against MiniDFS in plain, HA, router, erasure-coding, Kerberos and KMS modes.

# Are there any user-facing changes?

`write_with(path).if_not_exists(true)` on `hdfs-native` creates the file, or fails with `ConditionNotMatch` if it exists. Before, it failed with `Unsupported`.

# Breaking changes

# AI Usage Statement

- Harness: Jcode
- Model: Claude
- Effort: default
- Role: Found the missing capability from an exclusive-create write failure, wrote the fix, and ran the behavior suite and the downstream checks above against MiniDFS. I reviewed the change and the results.

body: ## Summary Add project labels for production traces and spans so users can mark and find runs for review. ## Code changes and behavior - **Project Settings** lists label names and descriptions in the shared table. Admins and members can create labels and use the row menu to edit descriptions or confirm deletion. Names are fixed, and viewers have read access. Deleting a label removes its trace and span assignments. - **Tracing** adds a searchable checkbox picker and compact label chips below the detail header metadata. Filtered traces** The filter chip stays in the search bar and matching traces use the standard table rows. ![Filtered traces](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2e2e978-11ee-4016-983f-70339c5958d8) ## Demo Project Labels, row actions, the trace filter, and the label picker. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0fddd20b-3ead-479d-9b67-251c3a25d0f9 ## Checklist - [x] Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) - [x] Added or updated tests - [x] Included screenshots - [x] Updated API documentation --- ## Summary by cubic Adds project labels for production traces and spans so users can find annotated runs and capture regression cases from them. **Trace and dataset UI** - Project Settings lets admins and members create labels with fixed names, edit optional descriptions, and delete labels; deleting a label removes all of its assignments, and viewers have read access. - Tracing adds a searchable checkbox picker and compact label chips below the detail header metadata; members can remove their own annotations. - The trace filter matches labels on the trace or any child span and keeps the standard result rows, with label values sourced from the project catalog; the 100-trace label lookup bound is scoped to the active filters so other filters apply to the full result set. - Applies only to original customer traces and spans; detector, RCA, and evaluation traces are outside the annotation scope. **API and storage** - Adds a Postgres label catalog and durable SDK write receipts; human and SDK assignments share one labels table. - SDK writes can carry a project-scoped end-user author, and human annotations are unique per target, author, and value. - Label writes require a trace or span that exists within retention, checked via the internal endpoint before ingest. - The write-only `POST /api/v1/public/labels` uses existing project ingest keys; retries return the original ID even after deletion, and conflicting payloads return `409`. body:
## What

Fixes found while checking `/yi` before recruiting volunteers.

1. **First visit fails with "window.turnstile.render is not a function".** The page had `<div id="turnstile">`, which browsers expose as `window.turnstile`, so `session()` stopped waiting before Turnstile's async script had loaded. Reproduced on the live `/yi` page: `app.js` finished at ~190 ms, Turnstile's `api.js` at ~680 ms, and the page showed "The first word didn't load".
   - The widget's box is now `#turnstile-box`, and `session()` waits until `window.turnstile.render` is a function. After 30 s it gives up with a message, so a blocked script no longer leaves "Loading" on screen indefinitely.
   - The box sits above the word instead of below the controls, so a phone shows it without scrolling. While the check is showing, "Loading the next word…" no longer replaces the "tick the box" instruction.
2. **Skipped words were reported as "none left".** Once every word given was answered or skipped, the page said none were left, though skipped words may still be open. It now says so and offers "Show skipped words".
3. **Empty reading's note in RTL.** "Pick this if nothing is printed in the box." showed its period on the left inside the right-to-left examples box. It is now set left to right.

## Testing

- New test in `layout.test.mjs`: `session()` resolves when `window.turnstile` starts as a non-Turnstile object and the real one arrives later. It fails on `main` and passes here.
- `node --test edge/check/layout.test.mjs edge/check/worker.test.mjs edge/check/languages.test.mjs edge/check/fonts.test.mjs`: 68 pass.
- A local end-to-end run (wrangler dev with local D1/R2, Playwright Chromium at desktop, iPhone 13 and Pixel 7) found items 2 and 3. The same run checked RTL rendering, highlights, clicks, taps and keys 1–5/S/←, Back-and-change, settling with three contributors, export and stats (no contributor ids), and answers retried over a failing network. author: haaktuah
body:
Fixes #1273.

Two sync steps' mends, followed as worded, did not reach done. Each now does, with a test that follows the mend as worded and failed before the fix.

**Point 1: the queue job's step** (`scripts/steps/750-…`). The step asked only for the job `queue`. A caller written by an older kit keeps `statuses: write` in the workflow's own `permissions:`, so once `queue` was added beside the review's job, zizmor's excessive-permissions failed the workflow check. Now:
- the step also reads not done where the workflow's own `permissions:` gives a right to write (write-all, or any right set to `write`) beside two jobs, or beside one job before `queue` is added;
- its mend says to move the rights to job level, as `core/setup/template/workflows/security-review.yml.tmpl` has them;
- its stage now stages the older kit's form (the rights at the workflow's level), and its mend, as worded, moves them;
- `tests/workflows-test.mjs` renders the template, stages the miss, runs the mend as worded and runs the workflow check whole (`scripts/workflows.mjs`, zizmor and actionlint included) over the result, failing on any finding of either tool or a tool that did not run. Before the fix zizmor found excessive-permissions; now it finds nothing. `tests/steps-slots-test.mjs` reads the new case: asked with rights hoisted or with write-all, not with read-all.

**Point 2: the agent tools' step** (`scripts/steps/360-…`). Its only way out for a hook not in the kit's form was `"from": "the working tree"`, which is untrue of a hook that fetches its file from `main` in a form of its own. Now:
- `scripts/hook-source.mjs` reads exactly, from the hook's command, whether it fetches its file from main (`git show refs/remotes/origin/main:<the file>`): git where a command starts, the file from the repository's root, no redirection of its output right after the path; a command past 4,096 characters reads as fetching nothing;
- an entry may say `"from": "main"` for such a hook, and the step's listing names, for each hook, the mark its command calls for;
- `"from": "main"` on a hook whose command fetches nothing from main fails, with its mend (`"from": "the working tree"`);
- the baseline's note for a hook that stood names the mark that fits it.

`tests/agent-tools-tree-test.mjs` and `tests/agent-tools-list-test.mjs` hold a hook of each form: each gets its own mark from the step, and each, marked so, reads done. `tests/agent-tools-source-test.mjs` reads `fetchesMain` on its own.

## What the owner can try

Run `node tests/workflows-test.mjs` with zizmor at hand (`scripts/workflow-tools.sh`), and `node tests/agent-tools-list-test.mjs`. The README is current: neither step is described there.

## Readings taken

- Point 1's step reads not done for a hoisted write right even before `queue` is added, where the workflow has one job. Read so because the mend then adds the second job, and the step must not first read done and then fail the copies check.
- `"from": "main"` is the "or its equal" the issue allows. It names where the hook's file is read from, as `"from": "the working tree"` does, and is read exactly from the command, never declared alone.
- Of the 171 suites run here, zizmor and actionlint at hand, two failed, each for this session's environment alone: copy-left-out, because Betterleaks was not fetched here, as its own step says; and tools-offer, because it read the session's own ignored `.claude/settings.local.json` and a live issue's state. Neither reads a file this pull request changes. The rest passed.

## What it asks of a project

- Point 1: a project whose security-review caller keeps a right to write in the workflow's own `permissions:` is now told, by the sync's report, to move it to job level, as the kit has it, in the same pull request that adds the job `queue`. A project already at the kit's form is asked nothing new.
- Point 2: nothing. A project gains a mark it may use, `"from": "main"`, for a hook that fetches its file from main, and the sync's report names which mark fits each hook. An entry that says `"from": "the working tree"` and stood before still passes.

author: marcosmaleval-max
body:
> ⛔ **NÃO FAZER MERGE sem a decisão do Chairman.** Nada foi publicado, nada foi enviado, nenhum deploy foi feito.

## O defeito, com a evidência primária (Gmail)

### (a) Lead chegando vazio — `thread 19f885d65a6f27b6`, 22/07/2026
Três avisos de `formresponses@netlify.com` (05:47, 12:31 e 14:20 UTC), assunto "Novo orçamento pelo site — Maleval Traduções", corpo inteiro:

```
Name:

Email:

Service:

Languages:

Details:
```

Rótulo sim, valor nenhum. **Sem nome e sem e-mail: lead impossível de responder.**

**Causa raiz.** O formulário `orcamento` então publicado declarava os campos em **português** — `index.html` em `e186071`, linhas **725** (`name="nome"`), **730** (`name="servico"`), **739** (`name="idiomas"`) e **750** (`name="detalhes"`) — enquanto o registro do formulário no Netlify guardava os nomes em **inglês** (`name/email/service/languages/details`). Nenhuma chave do POST casou com o esquema do formulário, e o Netlify imprimiu cada rótulo do esquema com valor em branco.

Prova cruzada de que o diagnóstico fecha: a submissão da ISTC de 18/11 (`thread 1a1ed78d04a1516b`) veio **completa**, e os nomes dos campos foram padronizados para inglês em **`8e9f59a` (23/07/2026)** — um dia depois dos três avisos vazios.

**Mas a causa estrutural continuava viva neste branch-base:**

| verificação em `main` (`56042c1`) | resultado |
|---|---|
| campos `<select name="languages">` com `required` | **0 de 23** |
| campos `<textarea name="details">` com `required` | **0 de 24** |
| `form-name` duplicado | `orcamento` usado por `index.html` **e** `interprete-brasilia.html`, com conjuntos de campos diferentes |

Esse `form-name` duplicado é exatamente a divergência de esquema que produziu os avisos em branco de julho: dois formulários diferentes sob um mesmo registro no Netlify.

### (b) O campo de idiomas contradizendo o texto livre — `thread 1a1ed78d04a1516b`, 18/11/2026
Lead institucional real (ISTC Procurement Office, **USD 2.880 em proposta**), formulário `quote-rsi-en` de `rsi-en.html`:

- campo estruturado: `Languages: Portuguese ⇄ Spanish`
- texto livre do cliente: *"The required language combinations are: English into Spanish; English into Portuguese."*

**Causa raiz:** `rsi-en.html:397–403` (e o mesmo bloco em outras 22 páginas) — select de **escolha única**, sem `EN ⇄ FR` nem `ES ⇄ FR`, e com dois catch-all (`Other pair (on request)`, `Other combination`) que **não capturam nada**. O cliente escolheu o mais próximo e o campo passou a contradizer o pedido. **Quem lesse só o campo cotaria o par errado.**

---

## O que mudou (24 formulários de orçamento, nada fora deles)

1. **Par de idiomas obrigatório** (`required`) nos 23 formulários que o tinham.
2. **Lista do PR #3 preservada** — rótulos curtos e ordem, inclusive as entradas direcionais `Inglês → Português` e `Inglês → Espanhol` — acrescidas das **duas combinações que faltavam**: `Inglês ⇄ Francês` e `Espanhol ⇄ Francês`. Cobertura completa das 6 combinações EN·PT·ES·FR.
3. **`value` explícito e estável em cada `<option>`**, igual nas quatro línguas do site (`PT ⇄ EN`, `EN → ES`, `PT ⇄ FR`, `MULTI`, `OTHER`…). Antes o `<option>` não tinha `value`, então o que chegava ao Gmail era o **rótulo visível da página** — variando por idioma (`Português ⇄ Inglês` / `Portuguese ⇄ English` / `Portugais ⇄ Anglais`) para a mesma coisa. Agora o valor transportado não depende do rótulo.
4. **Campo de texto livre `languages_other`**, sempre visível e normalmente opcional, que se torna **obrigatório** quando o cliente escolhe `Várias combinações` ou `Outro par (sob consulta)`. É o caso ISTC: agora ele escreve `English → Spanish e English → Portuguese` e o par chega explícito.
5. **Detalhes do projeto obrigatório** nos 24 formulários.
6. **`interpretacao-eventos-nordeste.html`**: `Formato` passa a ser obrigatório e a página **ganha o campo de idiomas que não tinha**.
7. **Proteção contra envio vazio**: o honeypot `bot-field` já existia; agora um script de 25 linhas também bloqueia o submit quando o honeypot vem preenchido **ou** quando nenhum campo visível tem conteúdo (campos ocultos como `subject` não contam).
8. **`interprete-brasilia.html`** passa a ter `form-name` próprio: `orcamento-brasilia`.
9. **`index-fr.html`**: opção duplicada (`Autre paire de langues…` repetida) eliminada na reconstrução do bloco.

### Opção removida, para decisão
Saiu a opção redundante **`Outra combinação` / `Other combination` / `Otra combinación` / `Autre combinaison`**: era um **segundo** catch-all, idêntico em função a `Outro par (sob consulta)`, e essa ambiguidade é parte do que levou a ISTC a marcar o par errado. O campo de texto livre substitui as duas. Se o Chairman preferir manter as duas opções, é uma linha por arquivo.

---

## O que foi testado

Servidor estático local na própria árvore do branch, testes executados no DOM real do navegador (nenhum POST disparado, nenhum deploy):

| # | teste | resultado |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | formulário vazio → `checkValidity()` | **falso**, 1º inválido = `name` |
| 2 | nome + e-mail + formato, idiomas vazio | **falso**, 1º inválido = `languages` |
| 3 | idiomas escolhido, detalhes vazio | **falso**, 1º inválido = `details` |
| 4 | tudo preenchido | **válido**; payload leva `languages: "EN → ES"` |
| 5 | `Várias combinações` sem o texto livre | **falso**, 1º inválido = `languages_other` (`required` virou `true` sozinho) |
| 6 | `Várias combinações` com o texto livre | **válido**; payload leva `languages: "MULTI"` + `languages_other: "English → Spanish and English → Portuguese"` |
| 7 | submit de lead legítimo | **não bloqueado** |
| 8 | submit com honeypot preenchido | **bloqueado** |
| 9 | submit com payload vazio (e `subject` oculto preenchido) | **bloqueado** |
| 10 | volta a um par da lista | `languages_other.required` volta a `false` |
| 11 | console do navegador | **nenhum erro** |

Páginas exercitadas: `rsi-en.html` (a página da ISTC), `index.html` (duas formas na mesma página — o `lead-magnet` continua intacto, só `name` + `email`) e `interpretacao-eventos-nordeste.html` (o campo de idiomas novo). Verificação estática em todos os 24 arquivos: nenhum `<textarea>` sem `required`, nenhum `<select>` sem `required` (exceto `frequency`, que é qualificador opcional de propósito), nenhum `form-name` duplicado, nenhum BOM introduzido, codificação UTF-8 e finais de linha LF preservados.

**Mobile:** a largura do texto da opção mais longa foi medida com a fonte real do campo — máximo **172 px**, contra ~250 px úteis a 320 px de viewport. Não foi possível confirmar por captura de tela porque a emulação de viewport não foi aplicada no painel; vale conferir no Deploy Preview.

### O que não dá para testar sem publicar
- O e-mail de notificação de fato chegando com os valores (depende do Netlify receber um deploy).
- Um POST direto no endpoint, ignorando o navegador: nem `required` nem JS pegam isso. Hoje só o honeypot e o filtro antispam do Netlify barram. Uma validação de verdade exigiria uma Netlify Function — fora do escopo deste PR e assunto de decisão separada.

---

## O que falta o Chairman fazer

1. **Revisar este PR** e decidir sobre a opção removida (item acima).
2. **Conferir o Deploy Preview** que o Netlify cria para este PR: abrir `/rsi.html` e `/index.html`, escolher `Várias combinações` e ver o campo de texto livre virar obrigatório.
3. **Depois do merge e do deploy**, no painel do Netlify (*Forms*): o formulário `orcamento-brasilia` aparecerá como **novo** (antes as submissões de Brasília caíam em `orcamento`), e os formulários passarão a ter os campos `languages_other`. Vale conferir se o aviso por e-mail está listando os campos novos — é aí que a divergência de esquema de julho se manifestaria de novo.
4. **Nada a enviar.** Nenhum e-mail, nenhuma publicação, nenhum deploy foi feito por este PR.

author: elysiumweb
body:
## Contexte

Application du design [Elysiumweb/Elysium-design](https://github.com/Elysiumweb/Elysium-design) à l'ensemble du site.

**Le contenu, les pages, les fonctionnalités et le backend sont inchangés** : seuls la couche visuelle et les composants de présentation évoluent. Aucune route, aucun appel Firestore, aucune règle métier, aucune traduction n'a été modifiée.

## Ce que fait cette PR

### Fondations
- Palette **obsidienne + or divin** en tokens `oklch` (`src/index.css`), exposée à Tailwind via `oklch(var(--token) / <alpha-value>)` → les modificateurs d'opacité (`/50`, `/80`…) restent fonctionnels. Le site actuel était en Tailwind v3, donc la syntaxe `@theme` / `@utility` de Tailwind v4 a été traduite en `tailwind.config.js` + classes CSS.
- Polices : **Orbitron** (titres), **Chakra Petch** (labels, eyebrows), **Rajdhani** (corps) — chargées via `public/index.html`.
- Utilitaires du design system : `panel`, `text-gold` (dégradé clippé sur le texte), `text-outline`, `bg-gold`, `clip-blade` / `clip-blade-sm` (angles coupés plutôt que rayons), `shadow-gold`, `shadow-deep`, `veil`, `gold-line`, `eyebrow` ; animations `marquee`, `float-slow`, `shine`, `rise`.

### Composants signature
- `src/components/site/` : `RiseTitle`, `SectionHeading`, `PageHero`, `Container`, `Reveal` (IntersectionObserver), `TiltCard` (inclinaison pointeur + reflet doré), `SceneBackground`.
- **Emblème 3D doré en fond fixe** (three.js + `@react-three/fiber` + `@react-three/drei`), avec une pose par route (`src/three/sceneTargets.js`).
- Header refait (glass au scroll, soulignés dorés animés, CTA or/frame, menu mobile numéroté) et footer avec bandeau défilant « Not given. Earned. ».

### Pages et composants couverts
Accueil, Équipe, Staff, Fiche joueur, Résultats, Détail match, Adversaires, Calendrier, Actualités, Article, Médias, Compétitions, Stats, Boutique, Soutenir, Recrutement, Partenaires, Fiche partenaire, À propos, Presse, Support, Suivi de demande, Connexion, Profil, Admin, espace joueur (chat, planning, notes, tableau, activité), pages légales, 404, hors-ligne — ainsi que les composants partagés : fiches match, campagne de don, stepper de candidature, bannières, états loading/vide/erreur, primitives `ui/*`.

## Points d'attention pour la review

| Sujet | Détail |
| --- | --- |
| **`data-testid`** | 1224 attributs avant / 1224 après : **aucun perdu**. Un seul ajouté (`scene-background`, le fond 3D). Vérifié par diff exhaustif. |
| **Dépendances** | Ajout de `three`, `@react-three/fiber`, `@react-three/drei` uniquement (scène 3D). |
| **Performance** | `three` est isolé dans son propre chunk lazy (~992 Ko) : aucun impact sur le chemin critique. La scène ne s'initialise que si WebGL est disponible, jamais sous `prefers-reduced-motion`, et 300 ms après le premier rendu. |
| **Accessibilité** | Tous les effets s'effondrent sous `prefers-reduced-motion` ; anneau de focus doré conservé sur tous les éléments interactifs ; titres en dégradé avec repli `@supports` (couleur pleine si `background-clip: text` n'est pas supporté) ; `RiseTitle` expose le texte brut via `sr-only` + `aria-hidden` sur les lettres animées ; contrastes AA préservés. |
| **Nettoyage** | Deux classes de dégradé mal formées issues du codemod (`border-primary/30/70`, `bg-background/70/85`, `border-border/25/[0.05]`) ont été corrigées — elles ne généraient aucun style. |
| **Backend** | `functions/`, `bot/`, `firestore.rules` : **non touchés**. |

## Vérifications

- `npm run test` (Jest + jsdom) : **328 tests / 35 suites — tous verts**, dont :
  - une suite de non-régression navbar (`Navbar.skin.test.jsx`) : lien actif unique, `end` sur `/`, présence de tous les liens et test ids du menu mobile ;
  - les suites existantes MatchCard, Shop, Partners, Stats, Support, PlayerDetail, ImageUpload, RouteChunkBoundary, markdown, SEO, etc.
- `npm run build` (Craco, production) : **succès**, seules des warnings préexistantes (source map `@mediapipe/tasks-vision`).
- Test de fumée temporaire (non commité) : 27 pages montées avec le nouveau skin sans erreur d'exécution.
- Dev server : 21 routes en HTTP 200, en-têtes `Host`/`Origin` proxifiés (type `*.e2b.app`) acceptés, HMR fonctionnel.

## Documentation

- `docs/design-system.md` : tokens, recettes de classes, règles d'usage (un seul titre en dégradé par écran, or = accent, `panel` + `clip-blade` plutôt que `bg-card border-white/10`), et procédure d'ajout d'une page conforme.
- `design_guidelines.json` : mis à jour (palette oklch, typographies, surfaces, motion, accessibilité).

## Hors périmètre

- Aucun changement de contenu éditorial, de copy, de logique métier ou de sécurité.
- Les couleurs de marque tierces sont conservées telles quelles (Discord, Google, Rocket League, paliers partenaires bronze/argent).

## Comment tester

```bash
npm ci --legacy-peer-deps
npm start          # http://localhost:3000
npm test           # 328 tests
npm run build
```

Parcours à regarder en priorité : **accueil** (hero + emblème 3D), **équipe** (cartes joueurs inclinées), **résultats** (fiches match), **boutique**, **soutenir**, **recrutement**, et le **menu mobile**.

author: welpie21
body:
## Summary

The "Add PERMISSIONS clause to table" code action wrote a clause that does not parse. SurrealDB's `permissions` parser (`parser-next/src/parse/stmt/define.rs`, v4.0.1) and the grammar's `PermissionGroup` both need `FOR` before every group.

```diff
 DEFINE TABLE widget SCHEMAFULL
-  PERMISSIONS FOR select FULL, create NONE, update NONE, delete NONE;
+  PERMISSIONS FOR select FULL, FOR create, update, delete NONE;
```

Same access as before: anyone can select, nobody can create, update or delete.

The insertion point was already right. The edit goes at `table.location.range.end`, and the `DefineStatement` node ends before its `;` (the `;` is a top-level separator in the grammar), so the clause lands inside the statement. A code comment now says so.

## Evidence

- **Before:**
  ```
  $ echo 'DEFINE TABLE t PERMISSIONS FOR select FULL, create NONE, update NONE, delete NONE;' | surreal-lsp check --stdin
  x.surql:1:43 error[parse]: Invalid SurrealQL syntax near `, create NONE, update NONE, delete NONE`.
  ```
  New test `add_permissions_code_action_produces_valid_surrealql` (tests/lsp.rs) fails: the edited text holds the old clause.
  **After:** the test passes. It applies the action's real edit and checks the result, for:
  ```text
  for source in [
    DEFINE TABLE widget SCHEMAFULL;                     # trailing ;
    DEFINE TABLE widget                                 # no ; at end of file
    DEFINE TABLE widget … COMMENT 'parts'; DEFINE TABLE gadget;
    DEFINE TABLE gadget TYPE RELATION IN widget OUT widget ;   # space before ;
    DEFINE TABLE total AS SELECT count() FROM widget GROUP ALL;  # view
  ]
    edited = apply(code_action(source).edit)
    assert edited == source with clause inserted just before `;`
    assert analyze_document(edited).syntax_diagnostics is empty
  ```
  `cargo test` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** small

Changes only the text one refactor code action inserts. No wire shape, config key, diagnostic code or compat golden changes. The action is offered when `table.permissions` is empty; #70 fixes how that list is read, so this PR does not change when the action appears.

author: ryankanno
body:
Closes #230

## Why

On Linux, `github-runner.sh add` installed each runner service as the login user. Jobs, including PR code, could then read the login user's `~/.ssh/config` and open its personal SSH agent. ryankanno/event-calendar#831 has the diagnosis.

## What changes (Linux only)

- `add` installs the service as `github-runner`. It refuses when that user does not exist, and prints the `useradd` and `usermod -aG` commands.
- The default runners dir is `~github-runner/.github-action-runners`. `GITHUB_RUNNERS_DIR` still overrides it. Before the user exists, the default stays in the login home.
- Writes in the runners dir (cache, mkdir, tar, `config.sh`, `remove`'s `rm -rf`) run as `sudo -u github-runner`. The login user reads the folders through the runner user's group.
- `gh` streams the tarball with `--output -` into a file that the runner user writes.

macOS does not change.

## Host steps

Do them in this order. The new `remove` deletes as `github-runner`, and that user cannot delete folders in the login home.

1. Remove the existing runners with `github-runner.sh remove <folder>`. Do this before you create the user.
2. `sudo useradd --system --create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin github-runner`
3. `sudo usermod -aG github-runner $USER`, then log in again.
4. Run `github-runner.sh add` for each runner again.

## Known gap

After a digest mismatch, the error says "delete it to download again". On Linux the login user cannot delete that cache file, so it needs `sudo -u github-runner rm`.

## Tests

`bash tests/github-runner-test.sh`: 468 passed, 0 failed. New tests cover the install user, the refusal when the user is missing, the default folder, macOS, and the delete as the runner user.

Proves the law of total cumulance for joint cumulants of any finite order under finite moment assumptions. This is row 56 of the project's [wanted theorems](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MIqVvAgcQL72HCPZ9KDaCZXZRVxBhkrEiLX1Dr7p4Kg/edit?usp=sharing). The proof groups partitions by their union blocks and shows how the second-order case recovers the existing law of total covariance. It cites Brillinger's 1969 paper.

This submission was prepared with AI assistance. As an independent check, I used exact rational arithmetic to compare the two sides for orders one through five on a non-uniform finite distribution, with both mixed and repeated variables and four choices of conditioning (40 comparisons). The proposed ID is P575, allowing for earlier pending submissions.

## What and why

Follow-up to #217 from the 1.5.0 review, after #377. A cloned repository can commit `.mcp.json`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/giong/SKILL.md`, or a folder on the way such as `.cursor`, as a symbolic link to a file elsewhere, and git checks it out as a link. `giong ai init` (also run by `giong new`) wrote with plain `fs::write`, so it merged its text into the link's target. The content is giong's own, so the impact was small, but every other giong-cli write into a project already refuses links (#377).

- Each agent file is now written aside and renamed over it (`state::replace` from #377), so a write never follows a link, including one that appears after the check.
- A linked agent file, or a folder on the way that links outside the project, is left as it is with a `GIONG-E5036` warning that names the link; the other files are written as usual.
- Kept on purpose: `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` naming each other (a common setup). ai init writes the file they share under its own name and the link stays a link. A folder linked to another folder inside the project is fine too.
- `docs/errors/E5036.md`, the giong-cli README and the changelog entry say so.

## How it was tested

- New test `links_out_of_the_project_are_not_written_through` (Unix): `.mcp.json`, `CLAUDE.md` and `SKILL.md` linked to a file outside the project, and `.cursor` linked to a folder outside it. In each case the outside file is untouched, nothing is written in the outside folder, the link is still a link, there is an E5036 warning, and AGENTS.md is still written. A `.cursor` linked to a folder inside the project gets the rule written there, with no finding.
- `claude_md_linked_to_agents_md` (both link directions, and a link to a file not written yet) still passes: one block, the link kept, nothing written on later runs.
- `cargo test -p giong-cli`: 123 pass. clippy `-D warnings` for giong-cli is clean on the Linux, Windows and macOS targets; fmt and `release.py check` pass.
- Full `scripts/preflight.sh` at 173ce39 passes (fmt, clippy, docs, the whole workspace's tests on io_uring and on epoll, MSRV, semver), and so does `scripts/check.sh test` (release tests, 5 rounds).

## Checklist

- [x] `scripts/preflight.sh` passes (the gate, not `--quick`) before this is marked ready for review, and so does `scripts/check.sh test` when Rust changed
- [x] Every review thread is answered: fixed, then a reply `Fixed in <commit>` (which resolves it), or a reply saying why not
- [x] New behaviour has tests, including what happens when an operation is dropped mid-flight
- [x] Every new `unsafe` block has a `// SAFETY:` comment, and `scripts/valgrind.sh` and `scripts/check.sh tsan` are clean (none added)
- [x] Performance claims come with before/after numbers and the method (none made)
- [x] User-visible changes have an entry in a new file in `changelog.d/` (see its README): added to the unreleased `changelog.d/giong-cli-new-ai-fix-test.md`

Fixes #36053

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:用数据技能包写应用的 AI 助手,以前只学到「查看全部 / 修改全部」这一种放权方式,现在学到权限分三件事(能不能用这个对象、能看到哪些记录、能看到哪些字段),「这个角色能读所有字段」有专门的写法,工资、证件号这类高敏感字段要在字段上加门槛;权限文档页同步说明。
- 为什么做:属于「权限三轴」这项已裁决的工作的第二步,读全部字段的新写法已经上线,技能包和文档没跟上,AI 会照旧模型写出到 v19 要返工的权限配置。
- 出错会怎样:最坏是 AI 读到的说明不够准确,不改变任何运行行为;可以直接撤回本次合并。
- 要你做什么:这是对外发布的技能包,需要你审核批准后才能合并。

## What changes

- `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md`: the bits bullet now names the three axes (object permission, record scope, fields) and says that from v19 View All / Modify All open no field. A new section, "Field visibility and `viewAllFields`", teaches the three sensitivity tiers (ordinary: write nothing; position-dependent: `fields` rows; high-sensitivity: `requiredPermissions` on the field) and `viewAllFields: true` (a read vote on every field, never an edit vote; the set's own `readable: false` row beats it; no object access and no record; on `'*'` it also votes on a private-posture object's fields; authored in metadata, Studio has no control for it). The `requiredPermissions` paragraph now says it is strictest-wins over field rows, `viewAllFields`, View All and Modify All, and shows `maskingRule` beside it.
- `skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json`: two cases, id 36 (a read-everything auditor set written with `viewAllFields`) and id 37 (salary and ID-number fields gated with `requiredPermissions` and `maskingRule`).
- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`: new sections "The three axes", "Choosing by sensitivity" and "`viewAllFields`: a set that reads every field"; `authorization.mdx` and `permissions-matrix.mdx` each gain the "from v19" sentence where they taught View All as reaching every field.
- `packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts`: two docblock sentences, comments only (the review notes carried on the card): the `viewAllFields` no-op claim is scoped to the object entry, and the `FieldPermissionSchema` docblock names `viewAllFields` as a voter.
- Two pins for the posture-blind wildcard vote: `packages/core/src/security/superuser-field-vote-33828.test.ts` and `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/fls-own-field-mask-33828.test.ts`.
- `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: the `rules/security.md` ceiling row moves 4068 to 4292, on the ratchet header's standing-ruling path (record 6513306068, 「A:先削重复,余额按实测提高」): 274 bytes of restatement were cut first, and the row is raised by the measured remainder only, pinned at the measurement with zero headroom. The claim's amendment 1 on the card records this route.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/skills` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch.

Size readings (`node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`, tokens are `ceil(bytes / 4)`; before is the merge base `57445a6998`, after is head `f1d2ae130c`):

| | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `rules/security.md` lines | 334 | 347 |
| `rules/security.md` bytes | 16272 | 17168 |
| `rules/security.md` tokens (ceiling 4068, then 4292) | 4068 | 4292 |
| eval file lines | 361 | 381 |

| whole shipped tree tokens | 294236 | 295195 |

No `SKILL.md` is touched.

## Why

The ruling behind the card is that an AI-authored app should get the permission model right by construction. `viewAllFields` is on main, and the published data skill still taught View All / Modify All as the only wide grant, so an author granted View All to open fields. From v19 that stops working.

## Tests

Head `f1d2ae130c`.

<details><summary>Touched test files, typecheck, spec artifacts</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/security/superuser-field-vote-33828.test.ts`: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 12 passed (12).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/fls-own-field-mask-33828.test.ts`: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 63 passed (63).

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`: "All 14 generated artifacts are up to date".
- All of the above ran in one locked command: `os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0`.

</details>

The two pins add coverage for behaviour that already landed with `viewAllFields`; no tested behaviour changes in this diff, so there is no ablation.

## Acceptance notes

- `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` is not touched: an open draft rewrites it.
- An open draft (#36158, a different card) moves the same ceiling row in `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`. The two conflict there; whichever lands second takes that merge and recomputes the row.
- Studio authoring of `viewAllFields` is out of scope here; the skill and the docs say the key is authored in metadata.
- The branch is 10 commits behind `origin/main` (`5727092e72`) as this opens. None of those commits touches a file of this diff.

Step 3, part C (stacked on B). No change a person sees.

- One `subscribeToThread({ withRunStatus: true })` per conversation reads every run on the thread, however it started: a message that woke the agent, a card's answer that resumed it. Runs are matched to their turn by the id Mastra names (`accepted.runId`, the parked run's id); what a run streams before its turn is known is kept for it. A run ends at its `thread-run-status`, not at the end of a stream. The subscription is let go a minute after the last turn.
- Stop is `abortThreadStream`. It does **not** clear pending signals: `clearPendingSignals` drops a message delivered into the running turn (test in B).

Checked first on Mastra 1.82: a resumed run shows on the thread subscription under its own id; a woken run runs without its own stream being read; Stop ends the model's request (the fake sees the request closed).

Mastra covers the subscription, the run status and the abort; the turn's message, cards and longer work stay the home's.

author: millennium-palestine
body:
Proposes pnp-071, the lexicographic half of a canonical-witness version of pnp-069.

pnp-069 gives some polynomial-time witness finder under P = NP. The greedy construction of pnp-058 gives more: its output is the least witness of the exact length in the lexicographic order (false < true), so a canonical witness is available once this lemma holds. pnp-071 is that lemma, stated generically in A, E and step, so it does not depend on any machine.

The statement is checked by `python3 tools/check.py statements` (151 statements elaborate). It does not decide P vs NP.

author: j-tyler
body:
## Problem

Stateful `explore --ensure-coverage` generated standalone requests across the entire spec and then discarded requests for operations already present in chains. Earlier operations could exhaust the budget before a later uncovered operation got a single request.

On `c9c31f6`, a spec with six linked operations followed by `GET /last` produced six matching chains. Neither target received `/last`, hiding a 200/409 mismatch. Moving the same operation to the front exposed the mismatch.

## Change

Select the non-excluded operations absent from generated chains before generating standalone cases. Give each selected operation up to three cases in spec order, using the existing seed and request generator. The existing command and flags apply. Stateless generation retains its existing total budget.

## Verification

- Both new regression test variants fail on the parent and pass on this branch. They cover two missing operations with different numbers of possible inputs, operation order, exclusions, fallback operation IDs, target requests, and recorded mismatches.
- The independent two-server reproduction passes with `/last` both first and last. With it last, the saved mismatch survived merge and replay. Replay reported `still_mismatch` for 200/409 and `now_match` after both targets returned 200.
- All 1,153 repository Python tests passed. `go test ./...` built the CEL evaluator package, which has no Go test files.

author: jroachgolf84
body:
## Description

DAG code running at parse time can call `get_parsing_context()` to read `dag_id` and `task_id`, but it has no way to find out which DAG bundle it is being parsed from.

This PR adds an optional `bundle_name` field to `AirflowParsingContext`, defaulting to `None` so existing positional uses keep working. The field is filled in both when the DAG processor parses a file and when a task re-parses its DAG file before running.

Like `dag_id` and `task_id`, the value stays set after parsing, so it is also available while the task runs; it is `None` on other parse paths such as `airflow dags test`, `airflow dags reserialize` and `DAG.test()`. Because `AirflowParsingContext` is a named `tuple`, code that unpacks it positionally (`dag_id, task_id = get_parsing_context()`) needs to read the fields by name instead.

## Example Use Case

```python

from airflow.sdk import Asset, AssetWatcher, get_parsing_context

bundle_name = get_parsing_context().bundle_name

asset = Asset(
    "my_asset",
    watchers=[
        AssetWatcher(
            name="my_watcher",
            trigger=MyTrigger(bundle_name=bundle_name),  # Pass in the bundle name to be used, as needed
        )
    ],
)

...

```

## Testing

These changes were tested via unit tests added to the following files. Each of these new unit tests were run via `breeze testing ...` commands:

- `airflow-core/tests/unit/dag_processing/test_processor.py`
- `task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/definitions/_internal/test_dag_parsing_context.py`
- `task-sdk/tests/task_sdk/execution_time/test_task_runner.py`

author: aionel
body:
`suggest_change` posts any non-empty comment. Nothing in the code blocks a comment that doesn't name a concrete failure.

This PR adds a required `failurePath`: the input or condition that triggers the problem, and what goes wrong. If it is blank or under 20 characters, the tool throws, posts nothing, and tells the model to provide one or drop the comment. The field is validated and never posted.

The idea comes from an engineer who reports that this check cut their AI reviewer's false positives to near zero: https://www.reddit.com/r/LLMDevs/comments/1v5dveb/my_ai_code_reviewer_was_useless_until_i_made_it/. That's one person's report. I haven't measured it on Shippie. The eval proposed in #471 could.

author: mnoah1
body:
## Why?
- Internally, we currently have each instance perform its own polling and metrics emission.  Since this is a periodic task, it runs on every instance and produces excessive API usage and unnecessary metric emission.
- Instead, this PR moves the existing logic into an open source controller, which can then be driven by the message queue
- Will allow us to to have the task execute about once per minute - after each completion, the message is held for up to one minute

## What?

- Seed one durable metrics task per queue. Workers share the task across replicas and reschedule it every minute.
- Fail startup if task seeding fails or exceeds 30 seconds. Each sample has a 45-second timeout.

## Test Plan

- Run `./tool/bazel test //stovepipe/controller/periodicmetrics:go_default_test //stovepipe/core/messagequeue:go_default_test //service/stovepipe/server:go_default_test` to check metric values, task cadence, and startup timeout handling.
- Run the focused MySQL queue integration cases for deduplication, shared workers, postponement, and crash recovery.

## Revert Plan

- Revert this PR to stop the periodic metrics worker.

author: cambridgetcg
body:
## What

- **The inbox shows a note's scope lines.** A marked note's `Purpose:` and `Extent:` are carried on `collab_inbox` items and in `about` threads (`purpose`, `extent`). They were written into the record but dropped from the JSON a reader sees.
- **A rejection reaches the sessions that decided.** `proposal.rejected` also addresses each session that recorded a decision on that proposal, so their waits ring. The person's agreement, set-asides and the knock set are unchanged.
- **`collab_take` accepts an optional `base`** (a full commit id), which becomes the new task's `expected_base_sha`. Before creating, the take reads the session worktree's HEAD and refuses with `expected_base_mismatch` (writing nothing) when it is not that commit. The base is checked again on every claim (a retake after `request_changes` included), recovery and handoff acceptance; the remedies and docs say so and offer a new task from the current HEAD.

## Why

A delegate reading its inbox did not see the scope its parent wrote into the note. A delegate waiting on a decision it had recorded was not rung when that decision was rejected; only the author was. And a take could not pin the commit its work starts from, which `collab_task_create` could.

## Compatibility

Additive. No schema, hashing, enum, event-type or payload change. The only new refusal is a malformed or mismatched `base`, on new input.

## Tests

Bun 1.3.5, full suite on the final commit: 1148 pass, 13 skip, 0 fail. Two earlier full runs were not clean under load: one had two 5 s timeouts in tests this branch does not touch (both also timed out on `main` under the same load), and one stopped making progress and was killed without a cause found; the full run right after it was clean. `check:mcp-bundle` passes. The take schema is exercised through the registered tool schema, and the missing-`base` and wrong-`base` cases are pinned. Mutation checks were caught.

## Merge notes

Other open collab PRs touch the same files. After resolving conflicts, rebuild `dist/` with Bun 1.3.5 and re-run `check:mcp-bundle`.

author: slatteryannie-web
body:
From a piece she owns, or a wish she's thinking of buying, to a draft look built around it. Built from Annie's handoff of 24 Nov, with her correction the same day: wishes are styled too. Plan and decisions: `platform/docs/plans/2026-11-24-style-a-piece-draft-look.md`.

## What she sees
- **The sparkle:** it sits bottom right on a piece's page, once Robes has read the piece, and on a wish's page. It hides while any other sheet on the page is open.
- **The bar:** tapping the sparkle opens the draft look's own bar, with the piece as a chip ("Camel shacket", "Outerwear · Anine Bing", ×), and "Style it for…".
  - From a piece she owns, Wardrobe and Shop are both on.
  - From a wish, Wardrobe alone is on, so she sees the wish with what she already owns. If she owns nothing yet, Shop is on instead.
- **Closing:** × or a tap outside the bar closes it, and nothing is made.
- **Sending:** Send (the button or Return), with words or none, opens the draft look dressing one look around the piece or wish. An empty send reads "Style my camel shacket" in the conversation.
- **Saving:** ✓ saves with "Saved to your lookbook." and goes back to the piece or wish.
- **Leaving:** × asks as today (Discard · Keep editing · Keep for later). Discard also goes back to the piece or wish.

## The anchor rule
- **Starting:** `looks.prompt` takes `anchorPieceId` or `anchorWishId`, never both. The job loads the piece or wish as hers; someone else's, or a wish she has already bought, is `not_found`.
- **The prompt:** style-piece v13 names it as THE KEY PIECE with its photo attached. A wish is described as one she's thinking of buying, styled with the pieces she owns. Without either, the prompt is v12 byte for byte.
- **Where it's stored:**
  - A piece she owns becomes the look's anchor.
  - A wish rides the look as a "piece to find" marked `anchor`, already filed to her wishlist, so it is never filed twice.
  - The look's style-piece set stores either one as `key`, so Restyle it all keeps it.
  - A brief too vague to style never drops either one.
- **Holding it:** the `anchor` mark is set only by the server. Saving a rack from the app keeps it, and a request can never set it. `look-ask` holds the anchor from the database whatever the request says, so a typed swap or a reason chip never takes it off.

- No retry when the anchor is missing; it is added to the look instead.
- A one-line toast, then back to the piece.
- The old Create › Style a piece door and the "Robes suggested" rail stay for a follow-up.
- The anchor is locked against typed changes and left out of the Which piece? chips.
- Wishes are styled too, with her wardrobe.

- **Both sources off:** turning off the last one switches the other on, as `toggleSource` does everywhere, rather than doing nothing.
- **Save toast:** it uses the words a saved suggestion already shows ("Saved to your lookbook.").
- **Default prompt:** an empty send from a wish also reads "Style my {name}".

author: simcity400
body:
Review rv14 found that each log product paged first and the client then filtered, reordered, counted and merged by read hour, using the union of a group's tags. That caused S1–S4 and S11: native and derived rows were paged apart, an empty window appeared while matching rows existed, chip counts covered only the visible rows, an event of 120 showed in a range of 140–150, and a country joining at 200 contributed its rows from 100.

**What was built**
- `dashboard_query::log::occurrence`: one indexed query for every log. Each occurrence has a stable id, an occurrence date, the hour it was observed, a kind, dated country roles, dated states, optional figures and search text.
  - A request filters in this order: nothing observed after the cutoff, the occurrence range, the dated selection, kinds, search, then states at the hour. Only after that does it count, order (live first, by date, or by a figure) and slice.
  - The reply has the window, the total, chip counts over the matching population, gaps cut at the hour and placed by ordinal, and the next change.
  - Six tests.
- `dashboard_base::products::occurrences`:
  - shared sort, counts and cutoff;
  - `occurrence_panel`, which reuses a reply until its `nextChange`, so quiet hours read nothing.
- The selection uses #588's `GroupSelection`. A request carries `countries` or `group`, never both. `group_members` gains `runs` (which `members_at` now uses) and `dated`, so each row is matched at its own role dates and unknown membership becomes a gap.
- `event-feed-tail`, `decisions-tail` and `event-choices-tail` now come from one per-branch index:
  - The event feed merges native, derived and family rows (wars, factions, subjects, projects, strikes) in one order and one total.
  - A chosen option is joined onto its fired event.
  - Decision and choice statuses are computed in Rust at the hour, including the recorded Completed and Aborted lifecycle and breaks in the recording.
  - A family that refuses becomes a named notice instead of hiding the other rows.
  - Feed notices are dated through the hour.
- `log-tail` replies `counts` (was `facetTotals`).

**Deleted**
- `feed/scope.rs` (the scope index and the retired cursor window, S17)
- the `event-feed-span` product
- the feed `scope` on `log-counts`
- `LogFacetTotal`
- UI: the span, facet, `rowMatches` and `cardFacets` helpers, client status and country filtering, live-row reordering, and the aux kinds request in the three projections

**UI kept to the minimum for the new reply shape** (the logs family agent takes it over):
- `LogTailQuery.ask` carries product predicates.
- `occurrenceSelection(ctx)` builds the selection.
- `rowSource` reads `counts` and places gaps by `before`.
- The three projections render the window verbatim, and decisions take the running count from `counts`.

**Inherited, not from this branch:** the `dashboard` contract test fails on `decorated-divisions` `countries[].firstHour`, and a `dashboard-world` flag test needs a game install.

The market ledger moves onto the same form in the next PR.

author: reversteam
body:
## Problème

Le harnais natif ne déclarait que [Once, Session] dans ses permission_scopes : le scope Always (« ne plus jamais demander », règle persistée au-delà de la session) était refusé (Unsupported{permission_scope}). Le natif ne garde les approbations qu'en mémoire (approved, scope Session).

## Correctif

Un trait PermissionRuleStore injecté par l'hôte, en miroir exact de TranscriptStore :

- native/rules.rs — trait PermissionRuleStore (load / insert / remove) + MemoryRuleStore (défaut, en mémoire).
- native/mod.rs — NativeProvider porte rules + with_rule_store ; capacité Always déclarée ; les clés persistées sont chargées à l'ouverture.
- native/session.rs — answer_permission à Allow{Always} insère la clé dans approved ET dans le store ; CoreParts.initial_approved seed le approved de la session.

Clé = celle de l'approbation de session (nom d'outil, ou consent_key pour un consentement N23b). L'hôte fournit la persistance réelle (fichier/BDD) ; la lib ne touche jamais un vrai disque.

## Tests

- 111 tests unitaires native:: verts (dont rules::tests).
- 123 tests native_harness verts, dont un nouveau an_always_approval_is_honored_by_a_new_session (2 sessions sur le même store : session 1 → ask + Always, session 2 → aucune ask, appel exécuté).
- native_conformance 4/4 verts.
- clippy --all-targets -D warnings vert.

Décision PO : PERM-ALWAYS-NATIVE.

author: acdlite
body:
Scaffolding for an experiment: the native RSC runtime, a highly experimental runtime for rendering React Server Components on the server. None of it is usable yet.

A page with `experimental_nativeRscRuntime = true` now gets its own Turbopack entry instead of a build error. The template imports nothing from App Router: only the renderer's precompiled bundles (the SSR one through the `next-ssr` transition, so it resolves React for Fizz), the root layout, and the page. It has no request handler yet: serving the page is a later step, which adds the bridge.

The first phase supports only one shape of route, a page directly inside the root layout, so the wiring can land before any features do. Other file structure and segment exports are left out on purpose, and a route that uses them is a build error, never a fallback to App Router: `next dev`, `runtime = 'edge'`, a root layout inside a route group, segments between the root layout and the page, parallel routes, including a page that's only in a slot, `error`/`loading`/`template`/ `not-found` and the other special files, metadata files anywhere in the route's tree, including `favicon` and a root `sitemap`, and `metadata`/`viewport` exports and their `generate…` functions (now recorded by segment config parsing), `ensureStatic`, and `instant`. So are client components and CSS: the endpoint already computes a page's client references, and a page on the runtime with any, including a `"use client"` root layout or page, is an error at the page. Each error points at the file that causes it, and one build reports them all. Server actions aren't checked: nothing serves these pages yet, and the bridge, when it does, answers a POST with a 405 before the page renders. The checks are coarse by design; later steps lift them one at a time as the runtime supports each feature, so the e2e suite checks them together in one build rather than one build each.

`next build` doesn't prerender these pages, also on purpose for the first phase. The build reads the export from the page's static info, with layout inheritance, the way it reads `runtime`, and tells the static worker the page is dynamic without loading it, as it does for Go route handlers.

author: johnqin-llm
body:
Scope: Primus-Turbo fp8_block MegaMoE quantization (follow-up on top of the T-1..T-3 stack). Two persistent Gluon
kernels that write the bytes of the kernels they replace:
- swiglu_fp8blk_fwd_kernel.swf_gl: SwiGLU forward + 1x128 dual FP8 quant (vs the Triton _swiglu_fwd_dual_kernel);
- swiglu_fp8blk_bwd_kernel.swb_gl: SwiGLU backward + dual quant of d(gate | up) + d(weight) partials (vs quant2 swb_q2).
SwiGLU computed once in an 8x8-per-lane layout, outputs quantized from registers, qT via LDS fp8 transposes, sigmoid
as v_exp + v_rcp + one Newton step (bit-equal to tl.sigmoid for every bf16 gate value of the default activation).
Taken by swiglu_{fwd,bwd}_dual_blk only under the Gluon gate with the default activation, compact column scales, x4
row scales and 128-multiple shapes; otherwise the previous kernels run.

Measured (MI455X, pool 28672 / 32768 rows, I = 2048): fwd 53.9 -> 33.7 us, bwd 96.5-100.1 -> 73.7-75.0 us; e2e on the
development branch 44.95 -> 44.63 ms (-0.32, 3 pairs), checksum 961/961; on the stack top 45.03 vs 45.23 ms (-0.20 ms, 3 interleaved pairs), checksum 961/961 identical (compiled-code hash: only the two replaced kernels change).

author: matthias
body:
Step 3, part D (stacked on C): a message for after the answer. iOS is in the next PR.

- Protocol: `SendMessage.later`, `Message.queued` (`docs/protocol.md`).
- Home: while a reply is written, a `later` message is stored in the thread first, then waits in Mastra's queue (`queueSignal`) as a signal that is not stored; the message has `queued: true` until its turn starts. The next turn of longer work (`go_on`) waits in the same queue, so the person's message is answered first and the work goes on after it. Stop drops what waits (`cancelQueuedMessages`, owner = the conversation); the words stay and the next turn reads them. A home that starts again clears `queued`.
- A subscription's client reads the stored message as the new one (`clientPrompt` skips the marked signal).
- Web: ⌘↩ (Ctrl+↩) while an answer is under way sends for after it; the placeholder says so; a waiting message shows "After the answer".

Tests: in order after the running turn; at once with no reply written; Stop drops the wait and the next turn reads the message; before the next turn of longer work.

Not checked in a browser.
