body:
## Summary

Ports PR #8's analysis stats panel (Android) to the web app. Tapping the percentage on the "finding faces" screen now opens a structured panel instead of one text line: Detect and Wait as big tiles, Frame, Resolution and Sampling as smaller ones, each with a chart of the last 60 samples (about 1 s apart; smooth monotone curves for times, steps for resolution and sampling). Values are the current per-second ones, not run averages. An (i) on each tile explains it. "More details" slides open (Backend, Detectors, Fine/Coarse pass, GPU time, GPU check, Crop checks, Decode wait, Scene cuts, Merge). Copy puts an agent-readable report on the clipboard (web version, browser, cores/memory/WebGPU adapter, video, every value with now/avg/min/max). Hebrew and English, light and dark, phone and desktop.

Metric mapping from Android: Detect = ms per detection; Wait = ms per frame waiting for a free detector (CPU workers); Frame = analysis-thread ms per frame without the waits; Resolution = the fine pass's side in px; Sampling = detections per second (the web's rate, Android's "every N frames"); Workers = detectors / cores; Fine/Coarse = the web's two passes (coarse also shows the share of detections that ran it); GPU time = WebGPU inference per detection (shown only on WebGPU); Crop checks = the crop re-check's ms. Not faked: YuNet and GPU queue do not exist on the web and are left out; the web's own extras (GPU-vs-CPU check, decode wait, scene cuts, merge) are shown instead.

Only `web/` and `ci/web-tests.sh` change: `analyze.worker.ts` posts structured stats (history kept in a new `lib/analysis-stats.ts`), a new `ui/AnalysisStatsPanel.tsx`, `Analyzing.tsx`, styles, i18n, and a Playwright test `tests/stats.cjs` (shard 1) that opens the panel mid-analysis, sees the chart change, opens details and an (i), and checks the copied report.

author: hwinther
body:
Adds the optional package `wsh-qemu-rdp`: qemu-rdp from Marc-André Lureau's qemu-display (pinned at 8ac3da9, qemu-rdp 0.1.1, the last commit whose crates all come from crates.io; crates vendored at build time, built offline with `--locked` and Debian 13's rustc-web), plus the unit `wsh-qemu-rdp@<vmid>`, which serves a VM's D-Bus display (`vga: ...,display=dbus`, stage 3a) over RDP with rdpsnd sound.

- The unit is bound to the VM's bus (`wsh-dbus-display@<vmid>`): once enabled (`systemctl enable --now wsh-qemu-rdp@<vmid>`) it starts and stops with the VM. It runs as `wsh-qemu-rdp` (group `wsh-display`) under systemd sandboxing.
- `/etc/wsh-qemu-rdp/<vmid>.conf` (0600) is written at first start: 127.0.0.1, port 20000 + VMID, user `rdp` with a generated password. NLA only; a self-signed node certificate (fingerprint in the journal) unless `CERT`/`KEY` are set. Credentials reach qemu-rdp through a 0400 file, never the command line.
- Our patches to qemu-rdp: workspace trimmed to qemu-rdp, the commit in `--version`, a credentials file and an optional bus name (the VM's bus policy only lets root own a name), relative mouse motion for PS/2 and Sun mice (upstream sent absolute positions only).
- qemu-server: `-audiodev dbus` gets `out.frequency=48000`. qemu-rdp only has 48 kHz formats and dropped QEMU's default 44.1 kHz stream; Opus/Moonlight are 48 kHz too. Changes 3a's command line (cfg2cmd expectations updated).
- CI (`wsh-qemu-rdp.yml`, `packages/wsh-qemu-rdp/test.sh`, path-filtered like wsh-openglide, not a required check): wisp guests on x86 (std VGA, AC97, PS/2) and the SS-5 (cg3, CS4231) with the published pve-qemu-kvm 11.1.3-4+wsh17, through FreeRDP 3.15 on Xvfb: login (wrong password refused), picture against the QMP screendump (mean difference 0, ~0.2 s after the guest drew it), resize 640x480 → 720x400 → 1280x800, keyboard (15-17 ms), mouse buttons and motion, and a 440 Hz tone through rdpsnd (2.0 s x86, 1.8 s SS-5). The same checks pass through PVE (`qm start`) in the lab; 284 cfg2cmd tests and the D-Bus display unit tests pass; lintian clean at warning level.
- Known limits: no clipboard (the bus policy rejects QEMU's calls to the client); enablement is per node (after a migration enable it on the new node); qemu-rdp HEAD (zbus 6) isn't used because its IronRDP comes from git.
- Docs: Display reference, "RDP (qemu-rdp)"; README; ROADMAP Stage 3b.

Not verified: Windows Remote Desktop and Remmina as clients, a real network, frame rates under load or on a GPU, absolute pointers and client-requested sizes, and a full Actions run of the new workflow.

author: 0x464e
body:
This is follow-up on #400, it fixes four remaining issues with the custom maps/friend lobbies:  
<sup>See https://github.com/Ezz-lol/boiii-free/pull/400#issuecomment-6977188959 as well for more context of this PR</sup>

- ImGui workshop download prompt can be invisible
- Joining a lobby can put you in a (near) infinite loading loop
- Map's preview icon doesn't get updated after an in-lobby download of a missing custom map
- Failed/stopped in-lobby download of a custom map can't be retried

Once again, the ImGui rendering fix in https://github.com/0x464e/boiii-free/commit/088d325ee16e4206039156576d4d1187b473ec54 is fully AI generated and I have nothing to say about the code. I'm happy to revert that commit or move it to a different PR if needed. Then it can be investigated separately if you wish. I am myself not particularly interested in studying the rendering code and understanding where it goes wrong. Though I'm happy to test different builds if needed.  
All I can say about the issue is that with current upstream beta, on my desktop PC I never see the prompt pop up, no matter if I'm in fullscreen, windowed, borderless etc. But on my laptop I do see the pop-up with current upstream beta.  
Testing an exe built with this PRs code my desktop PC is able to see the download prompt pop-up, and the laptop I also still able to see it as it was before.

Here is again an AI generated summary of the code changes per commit to help with review:

<details>
  <summary>In-depth explanation of commits (click to open)</summary>

### [`088d325e`](https://github.com/0x464e/boiii-free/commit/088d325ee16e4206039156576d4d1187b473ec54) `fix(overlay): render ImGui on the game swap chain`

The overlay used to create a temporary software swap chain and hook the `Present` function it found there. If the game's swap chain used a different function address, the confirmation could be queued successfully without ever being drawn.

`flip_model.cpp` now installs the hook on the chain the game actually creates, whether it's a stock chain or a flip-model chain. The hook saves the original methods per vtable so each chain can call its own implementation. Test presents pass through without drawing, and the flip-model tearing and resize adjustments apply to the converted chain.

When there's UI to draw, the overlay binds the game's back buffer explicitly, renders ImGui, and restores the previous color and depth targets. The temporary references to the back buffer are released before returning so they don't interfere with resizing.

### [`174c3fb1`](https://github.com/0x464e/boiii-free/commit/174c3fb1655b64b6542a4f56a31e118e0637a0fe) `fix(friends): wait for Custom Maps to load before retrying a join`

When a guest has no active mod and joins a friend with a custom map selected, beta can retry after three seconds while `usermaps` is still loading. If the retry reaches the same mismatch, it can request the load again and repeat.

For this case, `join_lobby()` starts the Custom Maps frontend reload and checks readiness on the main thread every 250 ms. It waits for `usermaps` to be active, the mod and asset loading to settle, and the local party to be available again. It then requests fresh lobby info using the original host and token. If the transition never becomes ready, the guest sees an error after 60 seconds.

### [`1d5d5848`](https://github.com/0x464e/boiii-free/commit/1d5d5848862dcf74e9fbd8f5be0d1a1aeeefb557) `fix(lobby): refresh the selected custom map preview after installation`

The selected map ID can stay the same throughout a download, so reloading the installed content doesn't necessarily tell the UI to redraw the thumbnail.

After `userContentReload` rebuilds the local content pools, the guest checks the current private-match selection. If that map is now installed, the code refreshes its preview image and forces a notification on `lobbyRoot.selectedMapId`. This also handles the host changing the selection while the download was running by reading the current selection at reload time.

### [`abe17269`](https://github.com/0x464e/boiii-free/commit/abe172693c4f1a9a81eb397fe7ca5eb7609ba43d) `fix(lobby): re-offer failed or stopped custom map downloads`

When the host switches to a map the guest lacks, the private-match offer now checks the live lobby before displaying the prompt and again when the guest clicks **Yes**. This prevents an old offer from queuing a map after the selection has changed.

The retry watcher starts only after **Yes** successfully adds the item to the download queue. On failure or **Stop Download**, it can show one new offer while the same host and map are still selected. **No** never queues an item, so it also never starts a retry watcher.

</details>

body: ## Summary - The Rune app runs `listImportableSessions` and `importAgentSessions` for the import dialog. Before this PR, the `actionResolved` and `importProgress` effects that answer them carried no request id. When two listings or two imports ran at once, the app could not tell which call an answer belonged to. The R6a-5 review raised this as a follow-up. - The app now passes a request id with each call, and the model echoes it on every answer for that call. - This PR also confirms that the three R6a-5 review lows are fixed on `dev` (#2060), each by a test: - An import finishes only on its own index reload. See `an_import_answers_once_its_own_reload_arrives` and `each_import_answers_on_its_own_reload`. - A null page reply fails the listing. See `a_listing_answered_with_no_page_fails`. - `is_auth_retriable` checks `ACP_MULTI_AUTH` first. See `auth_retry_tests.rs`. ## Related Issue No issue. This is unit R6a-6 of the Troupe on Rune plan (`docs/rune/acp-model.md`, slice 10b). No duplicate PR exists. ## Type of Change - [x] feat: new feature ## What Changed - `acp/import.rs` adds `RequestId`. `listImportableSessions` takes it as an optional fourth argument, and `ImportRequest` takes it as `request`. Each listing, each import and each import waiting on its reload keeps its id. - `Effect::ActionResolved` and `Effect::ImportProgress` now carry `request`. The field is not serialized, because the recorder has no such id, so `out/acp/` does not change. - `import_tests.rs` adds two tests. In the first, two listings answered out of order each answer with their own id. In the second, two imports each name their id on progress and on the final answer. - A failed listing still answers with a plain `actionRejected`. `actionRejected` serves every action, and `troupe-app` matches its fields, so this PR leaves it unchanged. ## How It Was Tested - [x] `cargo test -p model` (shared target). The acp replay passed, and so did all 42 unit tests. - [x] `cargo clippy -p model --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `cargo check -p troupe-app` and `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p model` pass. - [x] Mutations: 3 run, 3 killed. Each one dropped the id from the listing answer, the progress or the reload answer. ## CI & Review Gate - [ ] All CI checks pass - [ ] Code review comments addressed - [ ] No unresolved review findings remain ## Checklist - [x] My PR title follows the conventional commit format used by this repo - [x] I linked the related issue or explained why none exists - [x] I updated docs when needed - [x] I added or updated tests when needed - [x] I verified the change does not introduce unrelated modifications - [x] I read AGENTS.md and followed the contributor guidelines - [ ] A human reviewed the complete diff before submission --- ## Summary by cubic Names each import listing and import call with a request id so the app can match each `actionResolved` and `importProgress` answer to its call when two listings or imports run at once. This addresses the follow-up raised in the R6a-5 review. - The request id is the optional fourth argument to `listImportableSessions` and the `request` field of an `importAgentSessions` call. - Every answer echoes its call's id, including imports waiting on their own index reload; imports that finish don't answer to another reload. - The id is not serialized, so `out/acp/` output is unchanged. - Adds tests confirming each listing and import answers with its own id, and that the three R6a-5 review lows stay fixed on `dev`. Written for commit d4a22c371b3c0687f92d067c2a100285971a5d6f. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Import and session-listing responses now include request identifiers, helping distinguish results when multiple operations are in progress. * **Documentation** * Clarified session-listing failure behavior and which date formats are accepted. * Documented how request identifiers appear in import and listing responses, including outcomes for failed listings and index reloads.

author: arpan404
body:
## Root cause

`8fb83c8b26` correctly retires a send the provider acknowledged as done (`apps/daemon/src/engine/restart.ts:311-315`), so it never reads "not sent". The uncertain-delivery notice at `restart.ts:317-324` only applies to an input that was handed over and never confirmed.

My first version did not reach that state. It used `harness([{ on: "send" }])`, whose empty step returns successfully (`packages/adapter-testkit/src/scripted.ts:88-101,124`), and `h.create()` flushed the send through delivery/retirement (`apps/daemon/src/engine/test-support.ts:293`, `intent-delivery.ts:113-116`), so the crash copy held a settled send, not an uncertain one.

## Change

The test holds the provider's `send` open with a deferred, records the created thread, and waits until that send is observed. Only then does it take a crash copy of the live store. The recovered intent is still handed over and unacknowledged, which is exactly the uncertain-delivery path.

Review follow-ups:
- The override holds **only the first** send (`sends === 0`); a replay of the same command goes through the scripted session, so a recovery that tried to send again cannot block `crashCopy()`'s flush forever — it surfaces as a second send and fails the `sends === 1` assertion instead.
- The hold is released in `finally`, so a failed copy cannot strand teardown.

## Red/green

- With the notice `fail(...)` at `restart.ts:321-324` removed: **fails** (no "execution is uncertain" notice).
- With it restored: **passes**, and the recovered engine never sends the input again (one observed send).

Tests: `reliability.process.test.ts` 16/16, twice; `acknowledged-response.process.test.ts` 5/5 (acknowledged sends still retire as done); `bun run typecheck`, `lint`, `fmt:check` pass.

Branch head: `0c6df01c4d`.

author: kenwilliford
body:
The docstring of `FittingService.fit_hydration` called the per-point input `R1_normalized.csv` "background-subtracted". It is not:

- `core/laser_normalization.py` reads `darkSubSpectra.csv` and scales each point by `max(pd) / pd_i`, where `pd_i` is the point's mean photodiode reading across laser shots.
- `services/preprocessing.py` writes `R1_normalized.csv` (and, with despiking, `R1_normalized_despiked.csv`) from that normalized frame. The asPLS baseline goes only to the separate `_baselined` files.
- The instrument-background subtraction (`_process_background_subtraction`) applies to the scan's mean and trimmed-mean spectra only.

This change corrects the docstring alone; no code or behavior changes.

Other wording about preprocessing that may need attention is listed here and not changed in this PR:
- `services/map_fitting.py:803`: "Preprocessing setup (laser norm, background, baseline)", although the map path applies no instrument-background subtraction to points.
- `web/frontend/src/components/ProcessingWorkbench.svelte:994`: "Dark frame subtraction (arm-stowed / fused silica)", although the step subtracts a selected instrument-background reference, which is not the detector dark frame.
- `docs/METHODS.md:931-932`: the preprocessing flowchart places baseline correction before normalization; the per-point normalized files are written before any asPLS baseline.
- `README.md:163`, `docs/architecture.md:104`, `cli/app.py:172`: batch summaries list background subtraction without saying that it applies to the scan averages only.

author: sisshiki1969
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"sisshiki1969"} -->
_Requested by **monochrome** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TYhJEdhJ7MLNGZw5E4v28J?thread=cmsg_01TYhJEdhJ7MLNGZw5E4v28JWFqXDQ3PhZdThZaNmACnkW)_

Fixes #2126

## What was wrong

prism reports thirty kinds of warning (`PM_WARN_*`). monoruby forwarded nine of them, through an allowlist of messages in `try_prism_inner`, because the Rust wrapper does not expose a diagnostic's level. The six of the issue ("statement not reached", "Float … out of range", "'+' after local variable or literal is interpreted as binary operator …", "comparison '>=' after comparison", "literal in condition", "mismatched indentations …") were simply not on the list, and neither were the rest.

## The change

The allowlist is now a table of every kind, `prism_warning_level(msg)`, with each wording and level checked against CRuby 4.0.9 (they all agree with prism 2.1.0's own table):

| level | newly forwarded |
|---|---|
| verbose (`-w`) | "statement not reached"; "Float … out of range"; "'op' after local variable or literal is interpreted as binary operator even though it seems like unary operator / argument prefix / regexp literal / string literal / here document"; "ambiguous first argument; …"; "ambiguous `*` / `**` / `&` has been interpreted as an argument prefix"; "ambiguous `/`; wrap regexp in parentheses …"; "comparison '…' after comparison"; "mismatched indentations at '…' with '…' at N"; "literal in condition" / "… in flip-flop" and their "symbol literal" variants; "invalid value for <magic comment>: …"; "'shareable_constant_value' is ignored unless in comment-only line"; "\`if\` at the end of line without an expression" |
| default | "string literal in condition" / "… in flip-flop"; "... at EOL, should be parenthesized?"; "invalid character syntax; use \C-\s"; "encountered \r in middle of line, treated as a mere space"; "shebang line ending with \r may cause problems" |

Three points needed more than a table entry:

- **"regex literal in condition" / "… in flip-flop" is one message at two levels** — default for a plain literal, verbose for an interpolated one. It was always printed, so `if /#{x}/` warned without `-w`. The node at the warning's location decides (`InterpolatedRegexpConditions`, built only when such a warning exists).
- **The shebang warning** is prism's for a main script only, under an option (`main_script`) that also makes prism search the script for its `#!ruby` line. monoruby does that search itself (`preprocess_shebang`, for `-x` and a non-ruby first `#!` line), so that function now reports the line and the parse raises the warning, through a one-shot marker like the ones `-e` and `-n` / `-p` use. A script on stdin and a `-e` script count; a loaded file does not, as in CRuby.
- "… is too big for a number variable, always nil" stays with the lowerer, which already raises it.

Two things the new warnings made visible, fixed here:

- **Each `-e` is a line of the script, the last one included**, as in CRuby. Without the final newline a `\r` closing a `-e` (a CRLF shell script) was "\r in middle of line".
- **A main script that names `TOPLEVEL_BINDING` is compiled twice**, and its warnings were printed twice; the second parse, no longer being the `-e` script, also added a regexp condition's warning. The first parse's are kept.

## Verification

- `ruby -wc` against `monoruby -wc` over 6,308 files — monoruby's `builtins/`, `stdlib/`, `gem/`, the vendored stdlib, CRuby 4.0.9's `lib/`, mspec and all of ruby/spec. Before: the six kinds of the issue missing (45 "statement not reached", 10 "Float … out of range", 8 comparisons, 6 "literal in condition", 4 binary operators, 1 indentation). After: four files differ, for two reasons that are not about which warnings are forwarded (#2191, #2192 below).
- Probe scripts for every kind, run under `-w`, `-W1`, `-W0` and no flag on both: identical.
- `monoruby -w` with thirty common libraries required prints nothing, as on CRuby; monoruby's own Ruby sources raise none of the new warnings.
- ruby/spec `language`, `command_line`, `core/kernel`, `core/warning`: 5,397 examples, the same single (unrelated) failure before and after.
- New `tests/prism_parse_warnings.rs` (12 tests): each kind at both levels, running and under `-c`; `-e`, `eval`, a loaded file, stdin, `-x`.
- Debug `cargo test`: the integration binary (2,359 tests) and the lib tests pass; the touched tests pass under `stress-spill-pool`.

## Found on the way (filed)

- #2191 — parse warnings are dropped when the parse ends in a SyntaxError
- #2192 — "assigned but unused variable" warnings of one scope come out in a different order
- #2193 — a NUL byte in a command: backticks raise RuntimeError, `system` returns nil
- #2194 — `load` with a relative path: `__FILE__` is not the path CRuby gives the file

---

Fixes #1807

### Problem
The MinGit instructions in README.adoc tell users to set "Subdirectory of extracted archive" to `mingw64\bin\git.exe`. MinGit 2.56.0 and later does not contain that path, so the automatic installation fails.

### Change

- images/mingit-for-windows-as-a-tool.png: new screenshot taken from Jenkins 2.516.3 (the plugin baseline) showing the updated settings. The download URL in the screenshot is the `www.example.com` placeholder, as requested in review, so the documentation does not point users at GitHub.com.

- Listed the contents of MinGit-2.56.1-64-bit.zip: it contains `cmd/git.exe` and `ucrt64/bin/git.exe` and has no `mingw64/bin/git.exe`.

Jenkins installed it to `tools\git\cmd\git.exe` (under the Jenkins home directory) and the executable reported `git version 2.56.1.windows.1`.

The Wave 9 plan's status line and its Level 3 section name the tasks. The generated views are updated (`LEDGER.md` does not change).
- Issues were created without the `task` label; the label is added after the merge and a green push run of `main`.

## ELZ-379, Level 3

- Contract source: the Level 3 section and "Owner answers (2026-11-24)" of `docs/plans/bot-platform-wave9.md`, written against the merged Contracts on `main` `a9b1badb`, with the in-place amendments of Level 1 and Level 2: ELZ-361 (the Repo `:timeout` Need; the Piece emits no event, and upstream Finch telemetry is the consumer's), ELZ-363 (object-rooted start schemas), ELZ-365 (`charge_closed`, `store_unavailable`), ELZ-369 (the limiter wait), ELZ-370 (the 64-token session bound, the redaction waits), ELZ-374 (LMStudio encoding, at most 4 stop sequences), ELZ-377 (no stream outlives its request), ELZ-378 (`create/3` on every charge pass, `:approval_mismatch` before `charge/3`).
- Q9 D: the payment provider is a scripted harness binding; `integration/payments` is not a dependency.
- Where it departs from the plan's sketch, each against `main`:
  - Another tenant's valid token is not refused at Elzoo's MCP server: token-verify and mcp-server check no tenant. The task asserts the scoping instead (its own bots only; `-32602` for a T1 bot by name; HTTP 404 `-32600` on a T1 legacy session).
  - A private address at send time is not sent; the same try is due again, then dead-lettered `retries_exhausted`.
  - `invalid_grant` refuses the same MCP call that triggers the refresh, with no MCP request; one refresh does reach the authorization server.
  - The tenant session is listed with `McpClient.list_tools/1`: `McpRuntime.list_tools/2` takes only a session of its own config.
  - Code mode: an undeclared function is `sandbox_refused` / `unlisted_name`; a bytecode signature is `lua_error`, since dumped bytecode cannot be carried in a JSON proposal.
  - Models run in a plain agent-loop Run, because `delivery/room` carries no images. The throttled candidate is `:tried` within the call and `:cooling_down` in a later call. Unknown usage is the routing binding's metering record.
  - Three plan negative controls cannot be performed from the harness, so the task names ones that can: webhook-out checks egress itself, so the double keeps answering public at send; `new/1` takes only `on_unknown: :stop`, so the binding relabels the unknown outcome; the compensation order is ledger-checkout's code, so a temporary, reverted Piece edit is used.
- Dependencies, for the owner to veto: the task names 61 dependencies in a table, each with the interface its harness calls (after review: ELZ-011, ELZ-028, ELZ-122, ELZ-137 and ELZ-322 added, for the admission declarations, the copied fixture's lease and Unit directory, the marked tool results and `model_totals/3`; all merged). They exclude the plan's ELZ-141 and ELZ-303 (not called), ELZ-371 and ELZ-372 (the routing candidates are the Wave 9 providers), ELZ-359 and ELZ-360 (no change under `budget_rule: :finish`) and ELZ-327 (the fixture's construction is copied, as in ELZ-349).
- `product_aims` is `["P09", "P10"]`, as for ELZ-323. A V2 job cannot name P13, a V1B product (`check-roadmap.py`: "product precedes job release").
- The plan's Limits stay. Added: Finch telemetry carries OAuth secrets and is not exercised; the 64-token bound is not reached; Effect-intent Store tables are not under row security.
- Risk: durable state, concurrency, tenant isolation, unknown outcomes, secrets, external effects, untrusted model output. The task names the full gate, the full review and the merge queue, on an a1.medium orb.

## Defect follow-ups

| Task | Issue | Defect | Level 3 depends on it? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ELZ-380 | #913 | ai-text-anthropic sends a cache breakpoint at the neutral index, so after a tool-result run it marks another message or is dropped silently | No: the routing candidates are Google and compatible, and no case sends an Anthropic cache hint |
| ELZ-381 | #914 | ai-text accepts a zero-byte image and providers send it empty (coordinator decision: refused at admission, `minLength: 1` stays) | No: the image case uses a non-empty PNG artifact |
| ELZ-382 | #912 | mcp-client enforces 64 distinct tokens per session, but its Contract does not state the bound and no test grounds it | No: the tools group sends far fewer than 64 tokens per session |
| ELZ-383 | #882 | ai-batch's Contract text says only `credentials_unavailable` is attested no-send (nine places: the three the issue lists, the `piece.json` limit and grounding claim, a README paragraph, two Adapter moduledocs and one comment) | No: ai-batch is not used |

Decision comments are recorded on #912 (published as ELZ-382: state and test the bound; a signal or eviction stays open) and #915 (declined for now, below).

Not published; the issues stay open:
- #915: model-routing's `tried` has no bound, but no Contract rule sets one and a correct host never passes more refs than the route has candidates. This is an unbounded host input, not wrong behaviour; a bound stays addable in place before the first release.
- #918: three optional NOTEs (a missing recipient test, one `piece.json` assumption line, one long README line). No wrong behaviour.
- #884: plan's grant IDs are unique per tenant only. This is a stated host limit; no ready Piece stores grants across tenants, and entitlement fails closed (`:grants`) on a repeated ID.
- #885: a backdated replacement subscription can overlap an earlier one's grants. This is a stated host Need; entitlement's `resolve/3` reports `:overlap`.
- #886: `transact/3` takes no timeout option. oauth-client and mcp-runtime state the Repo `:timeout` Need, and there is no wrong behaviour when it holds; a timeout option is an enhancement.

body:
Bug #45 from the top-50 report. `/api/library/books/` ignored every paging parameter and always returned the full 345 KB catalogue.

The whole-set response is deliberate: the shelves, the facets and the prerender read every book (see the note on `DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS` in settings). So paging is opt-in:
- No `?limit=`: the response is unchanged, a bare array of every book.
- `?limit=N&offset=M`: the response is `{count, next, previous, results}`, with N capped at 100.

A new test in `LocalizedAuthorBioTests` covers three cases: `?page`/`?page_size` still return the whole set, `limit`/`offset` slice it, and the cap holds.

author: georlan
body:
## Resumo (B11 Scale & Efficiency Engine — PR 2/6)

Correção estrutural do self-deadlock de pool em `DB_POOL_SIZE=4 / DB_MAX_OVERFLOW=0` e redução massiva de RTTs/SQL nos caminhos quentes:

- **Cura de self-deadlock e starvation (`database.py`, `orders_core.py`, `pos_adapter.py`, `web_adapter.py`)**:
  - `database.py`: substitui `run_in_threadpool(db.close)` por executor dedicado `_DB_CLOSE_EXECUTOR` (`ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)`), evitando tanto bloqueio do event loop quanto starvation sob >40 requests concorrentes.
  - `orders_core.py` (`PUT /comandas/kds/itens/prontos` e `PUT /comandas/itens/{id}/status`): passa `locked_comanda=comanda` em `_advance_kds_check_if_all_ready`, remove `db.refresh()` pós-commit e migra broadcasts para `manager.queue_committed_broadcast(db, ...)` antes do commit; troca `joinedload(Comanda.itens)` por `selectinload` em `/detalhes/todos` e `/delivery/ativos`.
  - `pos_adapter.py`: cache de `config` em `db.info`, evita re-query de `current_user`, pré-carrega relações com `selectinload`, serializa `ComandaDetail` antes do commit sem `db.refresh()` pós-commit e usa `queue_committed_broadcast` (corrigindo `rid` em `MESA_UPDATED`).
  - `web_adapter.py`: migra broadcasts pós-commit para `queue_committed_broadcast` antes do commit.
- **Outbox (`services/outbox/publisher.py`)**: elimina `SELECT` de deduplicação quando `event_id` é UUIDv4 recém-gerado.
- **Print Agents (`routes/print_agents.py`)**: pré-filtro async `_prefilter_agent_token_hash` rejeita 401 em cache antes de abrir sessão DB; `_claim_pending_jobs` verifica existência de jobs `pending` antes de rodar `_coalesce_pending_reprints` e `_can_agent_claim_generic_jobs`; `complete-batch` no-op faz 0 commits e 0 broadcasts (preservando integralmente PRs #1082/#1083/#1084).
- **Leituras, CRM, Relatórios e Cardápio Público**:
  - `online_order_control.py`: `GET /control` faz 0 commits quando não há escrita pendente.
  - `smartpos_cash_projection.py`: `selectinload(Comanda.itens)` elimina N+1.
  - `customer_crm.py`: cache de `crm_schema_available` por engine bind + push de filtro `criado_em >= sql_cutoff` para SQL.
  - `financial_product_routes.py`: agrega `Item` por `produto_id` via `SQL GROUP BY`.
  - `cardapio_digital.py`: `ETag` fraco + `If-None-Match -> 304 Not Modified` + `Cache-Control: public, max-age=15, stale-while-revalidate=60` em `GET /api/cardapio-digital/public`.

## Validação
- `pytest`: 97 passed em modo sequencial (`test_print_agents.py`, `test_smartpos_macro0_foundation_stress.py`, `test_b11_hotpath_query_reductions.py`, `test_b11_scale_runtime_efficiency.py`) + 204 passed nas suítes paralelas de pedidos, KDS, PDV, CRM, relatórios, cardápio e outbox.

author: shiroinock
body:
各リポジトリに配る `templates/*.yml` で zizmor が指摘を出していた(video-prosody-youtube の PR #11 で 5 件)のを、意図に合わせて抑えます。あわせて、lint がテンプレートを検査していなかったのを直し、配ったあとの写しも見回りで直るようにします。

## 指摘と扱い

どれも、設計としてわざとそうしているものなので、直さずに理由を書いて行内の `# zizmor: ignore[...]` で抑えます。各リポジトリに zizmor の設定ファイルを置かずに済むよう、設定ではなく行内のコメントにしています。

| 指摘 | 場所 | 理由(コメントに書いたもの) |
|---|---|---|
| `unpinned-uses` | 7 つのテンプレートの `uses: shiroinock/workflows/...@main` | 自分の共通ジョブを、わざと main で追う(固定したいリポジトリは README のとおり SHA に替える) |
| `dangerous-triggers` | `claude-fix-ci.yml` の `workflow_run` | ジョブはこのリポジトリの PR のブランチしか取らない |
| `dangerous-triggers` | `dept.yml` の `workflow_run` | ジョブの `if` が、このリポジトリの main の CI しか取らない |
| `dangerous-triggers` | `merge-reservation.yml` の `pull_request_target` | PR のコードは取ってこず、走らせない |
| `dangerous-triggers` | `claude.yml` の `issue_comment` | オーナーの @claude にしか動かない |

`claude.yml` の `issue_comment` は zizmor 1.22.0 では出ず、この flake の版(1.32.0)で出ます。ignore は起動条件の行に置き(`claude-mention.yml` などと同じ形)、どちらの版でも 0 件になるのを確かめました。

## lint

`zizmor --offline .github/workflows templates` は、ディレクトリ `templates` から何も拾っていませんでした(zizmor が workflow として集めるのは `.github/workflows` だけ)。`templates/*.yml` とファイルを並べて渡すようにしました。テンプレートも含めて 0 件です。

## 配ったあとの写し

`repo-baseline` はすでにあるファイルを書き換えないので、このままだと各リポジトリの写しには指摘が残ります。そこで、毎週の見回り(`repo-baseline`)が、すでにある写しにもテンプレートの ignore のコメントだけを足すようにしました。

- `scripts/zizmor-ignores.awk`:テンプレートと同じ共通のジョブを呼ぶ写し(`uses: shiroinock/workflows/.github/workflows/<同じ名前>.yml@` の行があるもの。ref は問わない)だけを相手にする。`/install-github-app` で入れた `claude.yml` など、別の由来のファイルには何も足さない(理由が当てはまらないため)。写しでは、テンプレートの行から ignore のコメントを除いたものと行がそっくり同じなら、その行をテンプレートの行(コメント付き)に置き換える。ほかの行は触らない。足したかどうかは終了コードで返す。`uses:` を SHA に固定したなど、リポジトリが書き換えた行はそのまま(固定していれば指摘も出ない)。何度当てても変わらない。
- 足すものがあれば、足りないテンプレートを入れるのと同じ PR(`chore/common-workflows`)に入れる。PR 本文には、足したファイルを別に並べる。
- その PR を閉じた(マージしなかった)リポジトリでは、今までどおり、そのファイルは断ったものとして二度と触らない。
- lint で、テンプレートからコメントを除いたものに awk を当ててテンプレートに戻ること、コメント付きに当てても変わらないこと、`uses:` の行を除いた(写しでない)ものには何も足さないことを確かめる。
- video-prosody-youtube の今の写し(4 ファイル)に当てると、5 件の指摘が 0 件になるのを手元で確かめました。

マージ後の次の見回り(月曜)か、`gh workflow run baseline.yml` で、各リポジトリにコメントを足す PR が出ます。`.github/workflows` を変える PR なので、Claude のレビューは走らず、手で見てマージします。

## 確かめたこと

- `nix run .`(lint)と `nix flake check`、`nix build .#repo-baseline` が通る
- `nix run nixpkgs#zizmor -- --offline templates/*.yml`(1.22.0)と flake の zizmor(1.32.0)で、テンプレートの指摘が 0 件

開いている #35・#37・#38 とは、`README.md`・`flake.nix`・`scripts/repo-baseline.sh` が重なります。触った箇所は別なので、どちらが先でも取り込みで済むはずです。

author: abdellah-khanani
body:
On top of `pr/mesh-compute-fallback` (13d3718), for Marvisak/VIctory#961. These are two bugs that only show in the title's world on a GPU without mesh shaders. I hit them on an **RX 5700 XT (RDNA1, Adrenalin 32.0.21045.29003)** with my own dump, title 1.0.2.1.

### 1. Root signatures
The fallback makes the mesh stage's parameters visible to ALL so the compute pass can see them. That is the same root signature the pixel shader uses, and both stages use the same registers (user data b0 in the same space). D3D12 refuses it:

> Shader register range of type CBV (root parameter [2], visibility PIXEL) overlaps with another shader register range (root parameter [0], visibility ALL).

**Before:** 245 world pipelines were refused, so their draws were dropped.

The fix: the draw's signature keeps the mesh stage visible to the vertex shader. The compute pass gets a signature of its own (`MeshFallback::compute_root`), with the same parameters at the same indices: the mesh stage's are visible to ALL, and the pixel stage's move to spaces nothing reads. `bind_as` sets it for the compute pass, and `mesh_indirect::signatures` makes each command signature on its own root.

**After:** 0 refused, 513 fallback pipelines made.

### 2. Scratch memory
Every fallback draw took a new region, kept until the list was reset, and every list kept its own 64 MiB chunks. Thousands of draws across dozens of lists ran the 8 GB card out of memory: 1,955 `E_OUTOFMEMORY` in one run, then `a host command list did not close`.

The fix:
- A draw's regions are reused once it has moved the chunk back to UNORDERED_ACCESS. That transition waits for the draw's reads.
- Chunks are 16 MiB and go back to a pool the lists share when a list resets.
- Past 512 MiB free, chunks are released 128 resets later.

Releasing them at once gave one GPU page fault inside a freed `mesh fallback Data` buffer. So the delay is a **workaround for a lifetime I haven't pinned down**; better ideas welcome.

**After:** 0 `E_OUTOFMEMORY`, VRAM steady around 7.5 GB.

### Result on RDNA1
With these two fixes, `VICTORY_PRESENT_1440P` (mpDom d6897fa) and the #898 skip list, the world draws through the fallback: peds, wheels, poles, wires and props show in the G-buffer. Terrain, buildings and car bodies are still missing; that looks like the untranslated culling compute programs, not the fallback.

### Checks
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: clean. `-p victory-gpu --features diagnostics`: clean.
- `cargo test -p victory-gpu`: 57 passed.
- `cargo xtask policy`: 159 files ok.
- No new unit test for the root-signature split; the existing synthetic tests don't bind a pixel shader with user data, so they can't hit it.

AI-assisted (Claude Code). Built, tested and run on my machine.

author: adebesin-cell
body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

No issue. Found while testing Academy sign-in on a Supabase dev project.

### 🧭 Context

The Academy sign-in and the staff dashboard login both ask for a 6-digit code. Supabase's default emails send a link instead, and which email goes out depends on the account:
- a new account (every first-time learner) gets **Confirm signup**
- an existing account gets **Magic Link**

On the dev project, a new learner got "Confirm your email address" with a link and no code, so they couldn't finish signing in.

Decisions taken:
- One email for both cases: a branded "Your sign-in code" email showing `{{ .Token }}`, with no link.
- Codes last 10 minutes, matching what the sign-in screen says (Supabase's default is an hour).
- The templates live in the repo, so local Supabase and hosted projects use the same email.
- Hosted projects get them through a small script that changes only these settings. `supabase config push` would also push the local site URL and everything else in `config.toml`.

### 📚 Description

- `supabase/templates/sign-in-code.html`: the email. It has the 4HerFrika name, the code in large type, "works for 10 minutes", a "didn't ask for this" line and hello@4herfrika.org. Inline styles only, so email clients keep the layout.
- `supabase/config.toml`: both templates point at that file, with the subject "`{{ .Token }}` is your 4HerFrika code", and `otp_expiry` is 600.
- `bun auth:emails --project-ref <ref>` (`scripts/apply-auth-emails.ts`): reads the subjects, templates and expiry from `config.toml`, compares them with the project, and lists what differs. It's a dry run by default. With `--apply` it updates only those fields through the Management API, then reads the project back to confirm.

Applying it to production. Point an agent at this, or run it by hand:

```
1. Create a personal access token at https://supabase.com/dashboard/account/tokens
   (it only needs to live for this one run; delete it afterwards).
2. From the repo root:
   SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=<token> bun auth:emails --project-ref <production ref>
   This only prints which settings differ. Check the list is the five mailer_* fields.
3. SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN=<token> bun auth:emails --project-ref <production ref> --apply
4. Sign in at /academy/sign-in with a new email address and confirm the email shows a 6-digit code.
```

**Needs custom SMTP or a paid plan first.** Supabase only allows template changes on projects that send through their own SMTP provider or are on a paid plan. On a free project with the default sender, the script stops with `entitlement_required`. If production doesn't have custom SMTP yet, set it up under Authentication → SMTP Settings (Resend works: host `smtp.resend.com`, port 465, user `resend`, the Resend API key as the password, and a sender on a verified 4HerFrika domain). Custom SMTP also lifts the default sender's limit of about 2 emails an hour.

Two related Supabase settings to check while you're there (dashboard → Authentication):
- **Google:** turn on the Google provider with the OAuth client ID and secret.
- **Redirect URLs:** add `https://4herfrika.org/auth/callback**` and the preview domain's `/auth/callback**` to the URL Configuration allow list.

### ✅ Testing

- `bun test scripts/apply-auth-emails.test.ts`: both templates carry the code and no link, the subjects carry the code, and the expiry matches the 10 minutes the screen promises.
- On the dev project, the default "Confirm signup" email arrived with only a link, which is the bug this fixes.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes. Biome is clean on the changed files.
- Ran `bun auth:emails --apply` against the free-tier dev project. It read the project and listed the five settings that differ, then Supabase refused the update with `entitlement_required` (no custom SMTP on that project). The update itself still needs to run on a project with custom SMTP.

author: congvc-bot-x99[bot]
body:
## What

CHE-9643, step 3 of CHE-9399 (Trash "Delete forever"). Adds `server/db/purge.ts`, the one file that removes a trashed frame's rows. No caller, no route, no migration, no schema change.

- `purgeTrashedFrame(args)`: one bounded transaction.
  1. `SET LOCAL` `statement_timeout` 10s, `lock_timeout` 5s, `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` 30s.
  2. `LOCK TABLE comments IN SHARE MODE` (waits for open comment writes, holds new ones back).
  3. Lock the frame row; `deleted_at` must equal the caller's value, else `refused/conflict`.
  4. A `comments` row with `frame_id = F` gives `refused/has_comments`.
  5. Delete write keys, asset refs, versions, then the frame; collect their ids.
  6. `stillMayPurge()` runs after the deletes: `false` gives `refused/access_lost`, `'has_comments'` gives `refused/has_comments`.
  7. `onCommitRequested(receipt)`, then COMMIT.
  - Result is `committed`, `refused`, or `unknown` (with the receipt once step 7 ran).
- `resolvePurgeOutcome(frameId)`: `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the frame row, so it waits for a purge transaction still open. Row gone gives `committed`, row there gives `rolled_back`. A failed attempt (lock timeout, lost connection) is retried; it never answers unknown.
- Kept untouched: comments, comment events, page snapshots and blobs, activity, decisions, memory references, automation approvals, tasks, components (T1u asserts the row counts).
- `tests/frameTrashPersist.test.ts`: one `ALLOWED` entry for `server/db/purge.ts`, with its reason.

## Tests

`tests/framePurgePg.test.ts`: T1u, T3u, T5u, T14b, T14c, T12a, T12b, T12c on real Postgres (`DOOP_TEST_PG_URL`, skipped without it) and T16 on PGlite.

```
DOOP_TEST_PG_URL=postgres://postgres:pw@127.0.0.1:55439/t bunx vitest run tests/framePurgePg.test.ts
```

Red (written first, no `purge.ts` yet):

```
 FAIL  tests/framePurgePg.test.ts > frame purge transaction on PostgreSQL
Error: Cannot find module '/server/db/purge.ts' imported from tests/framePurgePg.test.ts
 FAIL  tests/framePurgePg.test.ts > T16 purge on PGlite (no DATABASE_URL)
Error: Cannot find module '/server/db/purge.ts' imported from tests/framePurgePg.test.ts
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  16 skipped (16)
```

Green (Postgres 16 in a tmpfs container, then removed):

```
 ✓ T1u deletes the frame row, its versions, write keys and asset refs; the receipt lists exactly those ids; kept tables keep their rows
 ✓ T3u a deleted_at mismatch is refused as a conflict and every row is kept
 ✓ T3u a frame that is no longer in the Trash (deleted_at null) is refused as a conflict
 ✓ T5u stillMayPurge false is refused as access_lost, after the deletes, and every row is kept

 ✓ T14b a comment row with frame_id = F is refused as has_comments and every row is kept
 ✓ T14c … > commits: the purge waits on the SHARE lock, then answers refused/has_comments
 ✓ T14c … > rolls back: the purge commits
 ✓ T12a lost acknowledgement, committed: unknown with the seeded ids; the probe answers committed
 ✓ T12b lost acknowledgement, rolled back: unknown; the probe answers rolled_back; every row is kept
 ✓ T12c … > answers committed once that transaction deletes the row and commits
 ✓ T12c … > answers rolled_back once that transaction rolls back
 ✓ T12c … > tries again after a lock timeout and never answers unknown
 ✓ T16 … > a query issued from inside the open purge waits for it and runs outside it
 ✓ T16 … > commits and the probe answers committed; the three SET LOCAL settings are accepted
 ✓ T16 … > the probe answers rolled_back for a frame that is still there
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

Without `DOOP_TEST_PG_URL` (as CI runs it): `bunx vitest run tests/frameTrashPersist.test.ts tests/framePurgePg.test.ts` gives 7 passed, 13 skipped (the Postgres block skips, T16 and the delete guard run).

Also green: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format:check`.

## PGlite and `SET LOCAL`

Logged by T16: `{"statement_timeout = '10s'":true,"lock_timeout = '5s'":true,"idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = '30s'":true}`. PGlite accepts all three.

## Risks

- `SET LOCAL` limits are only proven accepted on PGlite and Postgres 16. They are not proven to bite on PGlite (single connection, no lock contention there).
- When the backend is killed mid-transaction, node-postgres emits `error` on the checked-out client. T12b adds a listener for that. The app's pool has no such listener on a checked-out client, so a later route step should check whether a killed connection during a purge can raise an uncaught exception.
- `stillMayPurge` and `onCommitRequested` are synchronous and run inside the open transaction; a caller must not do I/O in them.
- Nothing calls this yet; the route, realtime fan-out and docs come in later CHE-9399 steps.


## Round 2 (review CHANGES on 5c1c032a)

- **P1 fixed.** `server/db/index.ts` now builds the `pg.Pool` itself and listens for `error` on the pool and on every client from `connect`, so a killed backend rejects the query in flight instead of ending the process. New T12d runs the real pool in a child process (`tests/fixtures/purgeDisconnectChild.ts`, no test-only listener), kills the purge's backend while it waits on the SHARE lock (before COMMIT), and asserts exit code 0, `unknown`, probe `rolled_back`, all rows kept.
  - Red before the fix: `Unhandled 'error' event … Error: Connection terminated unexpectedly`, child exit 1.
  - Green after: `T12d … ✓`.
- **P2 fixed.** Probe retries after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 s, then every 30 s. New T12e records the probe's own timers and asserts `[1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 30000, 30000, 30000]`. Red before: `[100, 250, 500, …]`.

author: draarivpatel-ui
body:
Fixes #2023

`JsonStorage::fetch_schema` parses the table `.sql` file through `Schema::from_ddl`, but rebuilds the `Schema` with `engine: None`, discarding the `ENGINE = <name>` the file records.

`CompositeStorage` routes statements by `Schema::engine`, so a JSON table registered under a non-default engine name receives no writes: `INSERT` reports `affected: 1` with no error, and the subsequent `SELECT` returns nothing.

This carries the parsed engine through, matching storages like `RedbStorage` and `MemoryStorage` that serialize the whole `Schema` and already round-trip it.

The regression test is a new `storages/composite-storage/tests/memory_and_json.rs`, the same shape as the existing `memory_and_redb` test: a `JsonStorage` pushed behind the non-default `JSON` engine name, `CREATE TABLE ... ENGINE = JSON`, then `INSERT` and `SELECT` through the composite.

`ParquetStorage` and `MongoStorage` hardcode `engine: None` too, but their formats do not store the DDL engine today, so this change is scoped to `JsonStorage`, which does.

Verified: `cargo test -p gluesql-json-storage -p gluesql-composite-storage`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all`.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * JSON-backed tables now retain their storage engine information when their schema is loaded. Composite storage can correctly read tables assigned to JSON while continuing to use memory as the default.
* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for creating a JSON-backed table in composite storage, inserting a value, and reading it back.

author: 7ibo
body:
## Summary

A clone of this repository alone now holds every rule needed to work on it. Until now `CLAUDE.md` sent the reader to another repository for the shared rules (attribution, git, pull requests, review, quality, CI, keys, Linear). They are copied here, adapted to an editor extension published to two marketplaces.

Docs only: no change to code, `package.json` or the workflows, so the merge publishes nothing.

## Changes

- `docs/regles.md` (new, in French): the shared rules that apply here, taken from 7IBO/socle at commit `f0e3f9d` and adapted. Non-negotiable rules, git, pull requests, review, challenging a choice, code quality, writing, CI and releases, network calls and errors, keys and leaks, Linear, threads. The interface of a site, design, accessibility, web performance, SEO and the shared server are left out: they have no object in an editor extension.
- `.vscodeignore`: `docs/**` is left out of the package, so the rules never ship in the `.vsix`.
- `CLAUDE.md`: the block that pointed to 7IBO/socle becomes a short block that points to `docs/regles.md` and says this file wins where they differ. The session note now says that `../PROGRESS.md` exists only on the local workspace, and names the four repositories it covers. The line « No network code here » now says where the extension calls the network (three places) and that it sends no beat itself.
- `.claude/agents/review-code.md`, `.claude/agents/review-ops.md`: the reviewers read `docs/regles.md` instead of files of another repository.
- `.claude/settings.json`: a cloud session commits as `Thibault` instead of `7IBO`, same noreply address.

Where the code does not hold a shared rule today, the file says so with its date instead of stating the rule as true:

- `fetchBuf` (`src/dependencies.ts`) and `fetchToday` (`src/today.ts`) call the network without a deadline;
- CI runs on every push to a pull request, drafts included (no draft filter, no `timeout-minutes`);
- no check holds the rule on ticket ids in files, the file size and copy thresholds, unused exports, or the writing rules: they are checked in review.

## Verification

- `bunx @biomejs/biome@2.5.6 ci .` (the version CI pins): no finding. It covers `.claude/settings.json`.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bun run test` in a scratch copy of the first commit: types pass, 56 tests pass in 9 files.
- `bun run build` was not run: it writes the bundle, and nothing it reads changes. Left to CI.
- `.githooks/commit-msg` on the commit message, then `--ci` on the pushed commit and the branch name: pass.
- The new file holds no em dash, no emoji and no ticket id.
- Each command, path and behaviour named in `docs/regles.md` was checked against the code, `CLAUDE.md` and the two workflows.
- What the review changed: `.vscodeignore`, one line of `CLAUDE.md`, two sentences of `docs/regles.md`.

## Reviews

### Independent review, at 0d0ea41

A reviewer that did not write the change read the diff against the code and the workflows. The merge is safe: five files, `package.json`, `src/` and the workflows untouched, `.claude/settings.json` changes only the name a cloud session commits with. Its findings for this repository, most severe first, each with the answer:

1. `.vscodeignore` did not exclude `docs/`: the next version would have shipped the internal rules in the `.vsix` to both marketplaces.
   Fixed in 60ca370: `docs/**` is excluded. It triggers no release.
2. `CLAUDE.md` said « No network code here » while `docs/regles.md` rightly lists three call sites, and `CLAUDE.md` wins on conflict.
   Fixed in 60ca370: the line names the three call sites and says the extension sends no beat.
3. « In the same pull request… the contract section of the other repositories » cannot be one pull request.
   Fixed in 60ca370: one pull request in each repository.
4. The cycle said one review is enough for a docs change, the table asked for two.
   Fixed in 60ca370: one.
5. `.githooks/commit-msg`, a comment of `ci.yml` and the pull request template still name the other repository or speak of migrations and screenshots; README and `CLAUDE.md` keep dashes used as a pause; `main` is not protected.
   Not here: this change touches no hook, workflow or template. They are in the follow-up ticket of THI-2163.

## Deployment

None. The `version` of `package.json` does not change, so `release.yml` publishes nothing.

Refs: THI-2163

author: unitedmarsupials
body:
TDLib takes a report about a person (not a bot) only through the bar offering to report their private chat as spam (`chatActionBarReportSpam` or `chatActionBarReportAddBlock`): `reportChat` with no option, messages or text, which `report_dialog_from_action_bar` sends as a spam report. The chat's `can_be_reported` is false for such chats, and `messageProperties.can_report_chat` follows it, so no menu offered any report, though a spammer is exactly who needs one.

Now, while that bar is there:

* the buddy's menu (and the conversation's) has "Report…";
* the menu of their message has "Report" and their name;
* reporting a group member by themselves uses it too, instead of saying Telegram takes no report about them.

Such a stranger's chat also gets its buddy, under "Telegram: not in contacts" and not saved, as soon as TDLib tells of the chat, at login too; until now that was only when they wrote, so after a restart the chat could not be opened at all.

The test of a stranger's chat picks "Report…" and checks the request and the notice. GUITEST.md's M5 gains the case.

author: markdbodman
body:
## Summary

The ratified [install-is-the-tenant](docs/founder-kernel/wiki/principles/install-is-the-tenant.md) rule (W18, `DI-2DEB0D9B417F`) treats an unfiltered `organization.findFirst()` as a defect. A call like that hides the assumption that the install holds one organization. If a second organization ever exists, it silently returns whichever row the database happens to give it. This PR gives callers a named way to get the install's organization and stops new unfiltered calls from appearing. BI-EE2F38D5 (epic EP-413F2602, decision item BI-F238FBE4).

- **The helper.** `getInstallOrganization(db, select)` and `findInstallOrganization(db, select)` in `@dpf/db` (`packages/db/src/install-organization.ts`) return the install's one organization. `getInstallOrganization` throws `InstallOrganizationMissingError` when no organization exists. `findInstallOrganization` returns `null` instead, which suits setup and onboarding. Both throw `InstallOrganizationAmbiguousError` when more than one exists. They read with `findMany({ take: 2 })`, so a second row is detected instead of hidden.
- **The guard.** `scripts/check-no-unfiltered-organization-findfirst.mjs` flags any `.organization.findFirst(` call in non-test TypeScript under `apps/` and `packages/` whose arguments have no `where`. It handles calls split across lines and skips comments. The 135 existing calls in 122 files are recorded in `scripts/unfiltered-organization-findfirst-baseline.json`, a baseline that can only shrink (owner `platform-architecture`, expiry `2027-02-24`). A file whose count rises fails the guard. A file whose count falls must record the lower count with `--update` in the same change. The guard loop picks the guard up automatically, and its test is registered in the CI policy guards.
- **The docs.** The data-model stewardship runbook has a new section, "The install is the tenant", that covers the helper, the guard and the estate boundary.

Out of scope: moving the existing calls onto the helper (BI-40F7C033) and hardening the managed-service customer-estate boundary (design, BI-10CB7878).

## Verification

- Helper tests pass (5/5): one organization, none, two, and the nullable variant.
- Guard tests pass (7/7). The guard passes against the committed baseline, and the baseline budget check accepts it.
- `pnpm --filter @dpf/db run typecheck` is clean.
- The full local-CI gate passed at `baab3054` (evidence `cmwuynauo0bl10ert7bvdui8a`).
- This install holds exactly one Organization row (read-only count). The only other place that creates one is a temporary row inside a verification transaction, so the helper's refusal breaks no current install.

Convergence-Impact-Decision: auto-converges — packages/db/src and scripts ship with the source tree on the next standard image upgrade; the helper and guard add no install state
Docs-Impact-Decision: one guard test was added to the CI policy test list; the flagged pages describe the guard runner and gate costs in general and do not enumerate individual guard tests

author: keyehzy
body:
Region: #1239

Agent: sonnet-sweepC

Notes:
- fn_14404 is `UISpriteButton::Draw`. It loads the act (path at 0xE4) and the spr (path at 0xCC), plus an optional palette (`dynamic_cast<CPaletteRes*>` of the 0xFC path; its second half `m_palette + 0x400` replaces the sprite colours). For each clip of motion (`m_actionIndex`, `m_frame`), it centres the first clip on the button, offsets later clips from it, clips to the button rectangle and draws via `m_surface->Slot10` with the texture-cache lookup (fn_04040, falling back to fn_04035). When `m_animating` is set it advances `m_frame`, wrapping the action at the act's action count and the frame at `GetMotionCount` (fn_10570). Local status: diff 54.4%, 962 vs 961 bytes.
- An earlier comment said the sprite/act structures had no headers. The port uses the `UIEmotion.h` stand-ins (CActRes/CActMotion/CActClip/CSprRes) and the file-local image/texture/cache structs that `UINewMakeCharWnd::Draw` on main uses. The action vector at act+0x110 goes through a file-local `SpriteButtonAct : CActRes`.
- On main the header's `m_actPath`/`m_sprPath` names look swapped: 0xE4 (`m_sprPath`) is loaded as the act and 0xCC (`m_actPath`) as the sprite. The port uses the members by offset and leaves the names alone.
- No header changes.

author: sohailkhan0525
body:
Qofeno Drive's original touch buttons, crowded screens, and primitive city/cabin made the driving experience hard to use and visually inconsistent. This revision rebuilds the controls and screen flow, and replaces the main environment and vehicle visuals with original Blender-authored assets.

- Independent multi-touch steering, accelerator, brake, and handbrake; input cancellation on pause/suspend; progressive steering and speed-sensitive wheel lock; braking priority and a stopped direction selector.
- A new menu, contextual driving HUD, actual world-loading progress, scrollable settings with consistent Back behavior, keyboard/controller focus, and road-aligned navigation. Wide screens render the world across the display.
- Editable Blender sources and reproducible export scripts for the cabin, masonry buildings, storefronts, trees, and materials. Runtime assets use shared meshes/materials and distant proxies.
- Research notes explain the driving/control, UI, and art references and which decisions they informed.

### Actual game captures

![Menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SohailKhan0525/simulationgame/improve/driving-experience/docs/previews/menu.png)

![Wide cockpit and touch HUD](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SohailKhan0525/simulationgame/improve/driving-experience/docs/previews/wide-touch.png)

[Loading/settings captures and validation details](https://github.com/SohailKhan0525/simulationgame/blob/improve/driving-experience/docs/VALIDATION.md) · [Research and design decisions](https://github.com/SohailKhan0525/simulationgame/blob/improve/driving-experience/docs/EXPERIENCE_REWORK.md)

### Validation

Godot 4.5.1 import and all seven local suites pass: session 36, world 27, vehicle 15, touch input 18, handling 9, UI flow 215, plus the main-scene smoke flow. All three release-version tests pass. Native desktop captures show no script or shader errors. Test saves and settings are isolated from player data. The new CI workflow repeats these checks.

Physical Android touch feel, frame pacing, thermals, and interruption/resume still need device testing. Native captures used Mesa software rendering and do not establish mobile performance. The game remains a stylized prototype with a fictional procedural road grid; this revision does not claim photorealism. No APK release, signing change, or history migration is included.

author: codisplanfiscalai
body:
## Falha observada

O PostgreSQL aceitava conexões, mas a imagem iniciava a API antes de preparar o schema operacional. O teste Docker inicializava o schema com um comando que o Compose distribuído não executava.

## Correção

- Prepara o PostgreSQL antes de carregar a API. Aceita primeiro boot em schema vazio e reinício com histórico válido. Bloqueia schema desconhecido ou SQLite legado sem seleção explícita.
- Integra ao migrador o SQLite original, o ZIP do Escritura e o backup cifrado EIBK. O arquivo original é preservado. A recuperação em instalação já inicializada usa um novo schema, valida os dados e informa o nome para ativação explícita.
- Expõe a origem de migração no Compose e no pacote de deploy. Documenta o procedimento em `docs/POSTGRES_OPERACIONAL.md`.
- Remove a preparação externa do teste de imagem. A CI passa a testar o mesmo primeiro boot usado no Dockge.

## Validação

Com PostgreSQL 17.11 descartável e dados sintéticos, o entrypoint respondeu a `/api/health` no primeiro boot e após reiniciar. Os testes de regressão cobrem restauração ZIP e EIBK, proteção de dados existentes e rejeição de backup inválido. Também passaram 9 testes de backend de backup e 39 testes de armazenamento/deploy. O build da imagem Docker é validado no GitHub Actions.

Destino: `develop`. A publicação da imagem segue o fluxo de release do projeto.

## Arquivos no MinIO

O serviço de arquivos usa chaves por empresa, exercício, categoria e SHA-256. Com o endpoint habilitado, novas gravações e leituras passam pelo MinIO. A cópia transacional em PostgreSQL permite backup e recomposição. O migrador `python -m app.object_store --create-bucket` verifica o conteúdo por releitura e pode ser retomado. O teste de imagem sincroniza o acervo sintético do auditor duas vezes contra o MinIO. O procedimento está em `docs/POSTGRES_OPERACIONAL.md`.

author: lfdiazdev2209
body:
## KAN-143 — Protocolo diario de 5 pasos y cofre

Sustituye el Reto del Día por el protocolo de bienestar: ejercicio, dieta, vitales, emocional y cofre.

### Reglas implementadas

- **Un paso se completa una vez al día**; la operación es idempotente (segundo intento no suma).
- **Fecha local**: todo se guarda por `yyyy-mm-dd` local; a medianoche cambia el día y refresca la pantalla.
- **Sin arrastre**: los pasos de ayer no cuentan hoy (historial por fecha).
- **Cofre bloqueado** hasta completar los 4 primeros; muestra exactamente qué falta.
- **Cofre una sola vez**: al abrirlo queda en el historial del día y no se puede repetir.
- **Puntos al instante** (+10 por paso) y **bonus de secuencia** al completar los 5 (+20, incluido en el total).
- **Ejercicio reducido** cuenta como completado.
- **Estado compartido Home ↔ protocolo** mediante el mismo store (`getWellnessHomeData`).

### UI

- Pantalla `protocol` con cabecera de día/progreso/puntos, tarjetas por paso, chequeo emocional de 3 opciones, aviso de cofre bloqueado y banner de día completo.
- El Home ahora lleva a `protocol` desde el CTA y desde cada paso.
- `IonAlert` para el cofre (compacto y accesible).

### Verificación

- **2070/2070** tests; 12 nuevos de protocolo (store + componente), incluidos cambio de día 23:59→00:01, cofre bloqueado, cofre idempotente y versión reducida.
- `tsc`, `oxlint`, `i18n:check` 0; ES/EN.
- E2E 390/320: Home → protocolo → 4 pasos → cofre → 5/5 → Home 5/5. Evidencia en `.ai/operations/2026-11-24-kan143/`.

### Notas

- El bonus de secuencia se aplica al completar el 5.º paso; cuando llegue KAN-141 (cerrar el día) se moverá al cierre explícito sin cambiar el contrato del store.
- Los enlaces “Abrir módulo” apuntan a los módulos actuales hasta KAN-139/145/138.

author: halonic-dev
body:
## What and why

The board decided on HAL-17654 (24 Nov): a pull request uses our fast pool only while the pool has room, because a crowded pool is slower than GitHub's runners (a job takes about 1 min on an idle slot, 4–8 min when the CI VM's CPUs are full). A job's runner is fixed when GitHub creates it, so a first job decides once for the whole run.

- **`pick-runner` job** (`ubuntu-24.04`). It runs only for a pull request a person opened from a `halonic-com/halonic` branch while `CI_RUNNER_FAST` is set; forks and bots skip it. It mints a token from a new GitHub App that has one permission, **Organization → Self-hosted runners: Read-only**, then runs `infra/ci-runner/pick-runner.mjs`. The script counts the online, idle runners in `CI_RUNNER_FAST`'s group that carry its labels, and answers `fast` when there are at least `CI_FAST_MIN_IDLE` (14 when unset). On any doubt it answers GitHub's runners, never our pool: no token, a failed or odd API answer, a bad setting. The job never fails.
- **Who may be picked:** `CI_FAST_SCOPE` is `fast-track` (the default: labelled pull requests only) or `all`.
- **The seven `runs-on` copies:** the label condition becomes `needs.pick-runner.outputs.fast == 'true'`; the repository, author and bot conditions stay. The seven jobs need `pick-runner`; `policy-base` gets `!cancelled()`, so a skipped picker (every merge group and push) doesn't skip it.
- **The hook stays the real control:** it still requires `fast-track` unless the fast pool's own root-owned `pool.conf` says exactly `PR_SCOPE="all"`. The shipped value is `fast-track`. To widen it, the VM setting changes first, then the repo variable.
- **Two runs at once:** both can count the same idle runners. In the worst case some jobs wait in GitHub's queue for a fast slot. Nothing fails, and a run never splits between pools.

**Before merging:** the board creates the App (`halonic-ci-pick`) and sets the variable `CI_PICK_APP_CLIENT_ID` and the Actions secret `CI_PICK_APP_KEY`. Without them, every pull request, `fast-track` ones included, runs on GitHub's runners. Setup, tuning and switching off are in `infra/ci-runner/README.md` under "Pick by room".

Decision note: `decisions/mateo/HAL-17654-pick-runner.md` (unsigned; Liam signs it in review). Julian checks C1–C8 (new token).

## Requirements

- check.ci-self-hosted-routing

## How tested

- `infra/ci-runner/pick-runner.test.mjs` (new, 8 tests): the threshold, the runner count (online, not busy, every label), the scope, no API call out of scope, every API failure and bad setting answering GitHub's runners, and the step's output.
- `infra/ci-runner/fast-scope.test.mjs` (new, 4 tests): without `PR_SCOPE="all"` the label is required; with it, an unlabelled person's pull request is admitted, while bots, forks, closed and moved-on pull requests are still refused.
- The routing test: the new expression; every server job needs `pick-runner` and keeps `!cancelled()`; `pick-runner` runs only for a person's own-branch pull request, with a read-only token.
- `node --test infra/ci-runner/hook.test.mjs infra/ci-runner/pick-runner.test.mjs`: 78 pass. Routing test: 7 pass.

Local check: `pnpm check` passed on `613c156`, merged with `origin/main`, except `notes-signed` for this branch's own unsigned note.

## Docs

`infra/ci-runner/README.md` (routing, the hook, the "Pick by room" steps), the comment at the top of `ci.yml`, and the decision note.

## Changeset

None (no user-visible change).

## AI assistance used

Claude Code / claude-opus-5-5

## Sign-off

- [ ] Every commit is signed off by me (`git commit -s`) under the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/), and I have run and understood this change.

author: claude[bot]
body:
Closes #17

## What changed

**Backend (`horizon-be`)**
- `passport-google-oauth20` and `passport-github2` (pure JS) strategies, `application/auth/sso/`.
- Routes in `web/http/auth/sso.controller.ts`: `GET /auth/google`, `/auth/google/callback`, `/auth/github`, `/auth/github/callback`, and `GET /auth/sso-providers` (`{ google, github }`, which buttons to show). A provider is on only when its client ID and secret are both set (and `HORIZON_BE_PUB_HTTP_URL`); otherwise its routes answer 404.
- **OAuth state without server sessions:** `SsoStateStore` puts a random `state` in a 10-minute httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie on the API host (path `/auth`) and the callback must bring the same value back (CSRF protection for the callback).
- **Token handoff:** the callback redirects to `<site>/login#sso_token=…&nonce=…` (fragment, so not sent to servers or in Referer). The login page started the flow with a random nonce kept in `sessionStorage` and only accepts the token if the nonce matches, so a link carrying someone else's token can't sign a browser in. Errors come back as `/login?sso_error=<code>`, shown as fixed messages.
- `AuthService.sso_login`:
  1. a login linked before → its account (refused if deleted);
  2. else, **only with a verified email**, link to the account with that email (case-insensitive, exact match preferred; a deleted account's email is refused);
  3. else create an account with no password (names from the profile, welcome email sent). Creating also needs a verified email.
  - Google: `emails[].verified`. GitHub: scope `user:email` with `allRawEmails`, so `/user/emails` is fetched and only the **primary and verified** address is used (no fallback to other addresses).
  - Password login on an account with no password always fails (compares against the dummy hash); "Forgot password" can set one.
- Migration `AccountIdentity`: `account_identity` (`provider`, `provider_user_id`, `account_id`, unique on the pair, index on `account_id`), and `account.password_hash` nullable. `down` gives password-less accounts an unusable `'!'` value before restoring NOT NULL.
- `env.ts`: `HORIZON_BE_PUB_HTTP_URL`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`.

**Frontend (`horizon-fe`)**: `view/sso/` (`sso-buttons.vue`, `sso.js`); "Continue with Google / GitHub" on the login and signup pages, only for configured providers. The login page finishes the sign-in (`sso_finish`) and does a full page load to `/app`.

**Config/docs**: `.env.example`, `deploy/prod.env.example`, `deploy/compose.yaml` (passes the four values and `HORIZON_BE_PUB_HTTP_URL=https://${API_DOMAIN}` to the backend), `docs/OPERATIONS.md` (new section), `docs/HANDOFF.md` (5b).

## How it was checked
- Backend `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` (new `sso-identity.spec.ts`: verified-email rules for both providers, config, redirect URLs, nonce). All pass.
- A throwaway script against the built strategies: the start route redirects to Google with `state`, sets the cookie with the nonce; verify accepts the matching state and hands back the nonce, and rejects a missing cookie or wrong state.
- Frontend `npm run build`, `npm run lint`. Prettier check passes.
- **Not checked:** the migration was not run (no databases here), and the full round trip with real Google/GitHub apps was not run (no credentials). CI's `smoke` job runs the API smoke test.

## Done when
- [ ] Both providers work locally and in production — **not yet verifiable**: needs the OAuth apps and credentials (below).
- [x] An unverified email never links to an existing account (enforced in `google_identity`/`github_identity` + `sso_login`, unit-tested for the profile parsing).

## Owner steps on deploy
1. Create a Google OAuth client (Web application) and a GitHub OAuth App. Callbacks: `https://api.invokedb.com/auth/google/callback`, `https://api.invokedb.com/auth/github/callback`; for local, `http://127.0.0.1:8001/auth/<provider>/callback` (GitHub allows one callback per app, so a second app for local).
2. Set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` in `deploy/prod.env` (and `.env` locally); `npm run secrets:push`.
3. Run the migration (`deploy/deploy.sh migrate`) with the deploy. Without the values, the buttons just don't show.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- **Pre-registration takeover risk:** password signup doesn't verify the email, so someone could sign up with a victim's address and a password before the victim first uses Google/GitHub; the victim's verified SSO login would then link to that account, which the squatter can still enter by password. Options: verify emails on password signup, or clear the password and sessions when an SSO login first links to an account whose email was never verified. Needs a decision.
- `AuthService.authorize` and the account settings page don't say whether an account has a password; an SSO-only user may want a "set password" hint.

author: wslack
body:
## Context

`cf restage` fails on both `smeqa-staging` and `smeqa-rr` with:

```
-----> Nodejs Buildpack version 1.9.8
       **WARNING** buildpack version changed from 1.8.34 to 1.9.8
-----> Installing binaries
       engines.node (package.json): 18.20.6
       **ERROR** Unable to install node: no match found for 18.20.6 in [22.23.5 24.22.3]
Failed to compile droplet: Failed to run all supply scripts: exit status 14
```

The cloud.gov `nodejs_buildpack` no longer ships Node 18. `api/package.json` pins an exact `engines.node` of `18.20.6`. The running apps still work because they use their existing droplets (built Feb 2025 on buildpack 1.8.34), but they can't be restaged or redeployed until this is fixed.

The GitHub Actions workflows also use `actions/cache@v2`, `checkout@v2` and `setup-node@v2`. GitHub retired `cache@v2`, so I expect the deploy workflows would fail before they reach the deploy step. This was not confirmed, because the last runs are too old to view.

## Plan / changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `api/package.json` | `engines.node`: `18.20.6` -> `22.x`. A range means a buildpack patch removal won't break staging again. |
| `api/package-lock.json` | Root `engines` entry synced (it was stale at `18.20.3`) |
| `.github/workflows/push-staging.yml`, `push-prod.yml` | `checkout`, `cache` and `setup-node` `@v2` -> `@v4` |
| `docs/buildpackNodeNotes.md` | Explains why `engines.node` is a range; updates the Node versions |

Not changed: manifests, database/service bindings, migrations, application code, and the CI build Node versions (API build on 14, frontend on 16).

## Verification

Run locally on Node 22.22.1, on a copy of `api/` in `/tmp`:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm ci` (with the updated lockfile) | Pass (802 packages) |
| `npm run build` (`tsc`) | Pass |
| `require()` of 16 runtime deps (express, passport, openid-client, node-jose, pg, sequelize, connect-pg-simple, multer, etc.) | All load |
| Start the compiled `build/` after `npm ci --omit=dev` | Starts under Node 22: DB init, OpenID discovery, and all routes register |
| `npm run test:unit` | 3 of 9 suites pass (23 tests pass, 3 fail). **Same result on Node 18.20.6 and Node 22.** |

The unit test failures are pre-existing. Test fixtures are missing fields the code now requires (`isTieBreaker`, `sortOrder`, `failNor`, `pointsRequired`). They are unrelated to the Node version and are not fixed here.

## Security impact

- No change to authentication, authorization, data handling or the attack surface.
- The runtime moves from Node 18 (EOL) to the supported Node 22.
- The GitHub Actions are upgraded from retired and unmaintained versions.
- No secrets are touched. The deploy secrets are unchanged.
- The database is untouched.

## Review focus

- Node 22 compatibility of the old dependencies (`openid-client@4`, `node-jose@2`, `passport@0.4`, `sequelize@6`).
- Whether the workflows run with the Node 14/16 build steps.
- `stage` and `main` both contain a "Bump Node to 18.20.6" commit, so the later `stage` to `main` merge may hit a trivial conflict on the `engines` line.

## Follow-ups (to be tracked as issues)

- Fix the broken unit test fixtures.
- Move the CI build to a supported Node version. Node 14 and 16 are EOL, and `docs/buildpackNodeNotes.md` says Node 18 fails with type errors.
- Update the dependencies (63 `npm audit` findings, 5 critical).
- Move the dependencies to the current supported versions, and consider Node 24.

*Disclosure: this change was prepared with AI assistance (OpenCode agent) and requires human review before it is deployed to production.*

author: cameronfreer
hgamef72-jpg
body:
## Source audit findings

Recovered v1.5.77 Host source confirms the binary frame format is:
- 4-byte big-endian monitor index
- JPEG bytes

The Host currently iterates every GraphicsDevice, captures and JPEG-encodes each monitor on every loop, and ignores the CompletableFuture returned by WebSocket.sendBinary. This means it transmits all displays even though the Viewer has a selected monitor, and it can enqueue frames faster than the socket drains them.

The Android Viewer currently receives all binary frames and decodes them without checking the 4-byte monitor index. The Windows Viewer decodes synchronously in the WebSocket callback and schedules a Swing render for every decoded frame.

## Changes proposed

- Host captures only the selected display.
- Host capture width is reduced from 1280 to 960 to reduce encode/decode/network cost.
- Host uses a start-to-start 20 ms frame pacer (50 FPS target).
- Host waits for each binary send future to complete, applying backpressure and preventing unbounded outbound frame buildup.
- Windows Viewer uses a dedicated single decoder, latest-frame-wins coalescing, and one pending Swing render callback; scaling is moved off the EDT.
- Android filters frames by the verified monitor index before decoding and avoids scanning the full packet for the JPEG marker in the normal protocol path.
- Windows Viewer package starts from the original v1.5.77 package. The prior blind byte-offset patches to ViewerWindow are not applied.
- Recovery Agent / Power patch is limited to the Host package.

## Validation

The workflow downloads the v1.0.5 baseline packages, applies strict ASM pattern checks, validates portable ZIP integrity, builds and verifies the Android APK, and publishes v1.0.10.

The 50 FPS value is a pacing target, not a claim of 50 delivered FPS. Relay source is not present in this repository; Render previously logged a Node.js heap OOM, so relay-side fanout and memory behavior remains a separate unresolved dependency.
