author: kottlerg
body:
## Summary
`cargo xtask run --runs` no longer reads a harness's death as a budget HANG, a set whose runs only crashed QEMU as a pass, or another process's `ALL TESTS PASSED` line as a pass. Every pack records the test harnesses the packed image boots (`sysroot/.image-harness`); the default `--pass` is bound to that harness, svcmgr's `service died: <harness>` line before the pass marker is a FAIL that arms the fail grace window, and a set with no PASS fails whatever its QEMU-CRASH count.

Fixes #1551

## Acceptance
- [x] A boot whose svctest or usertest process dies before its marker is a FAIL within the fail
  grace window, with a reason naming the death. A host test in classified.rs covers the classify
  and the live-scan arming. (fixed by PR #1639)
- [x] A death line after the pass marker does not change a PASS (host test). (fixed by PR #1639)
- [x] `run --runs 1` whose only run is QEMU-CRASH exits non-zero; a set with one PASS and one
  QEMU-CRASH exits 0 (host tests). (fixed by PR #1639)
- [x] The default `--pass` is bound to the recorded harness. A log holding another harness's
  marker, or a bare `ALL TESTS PASSED`, is not a PASS (host test). (fixed by PR #1639)
- [x] xtask/README.md § `run` (the verdict list, lines 455-477), docs/testing.md § Reporting
  marker and § Coverage tiers (lines 1730-1735), and docs/build-system.md § Continuous Integration
  state the new verdicts. `cargo xtask lint-docs` passes. (fixed by PR #1639)
- [x] The README of svctest (Run Sequence, line 217) states that a fault in its own process ends
  the boot as a FAIL at the grace window. (fixed by PR #1639)

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo xtask lint-docs`
- [x] `cargo xtask test` (new host tests: `a_harness_death_before_its_marker_fails_the_run_naming_the_death`, `a_harness_death_before_its_marker_arms_the_grace_window`, `only_the_death_of_a_harness_of_the_image_fails_the_run`, `a_set_fails_without_a_pass_whatever_its_qemu_crashes`, `the_default_pass_marker_is_the_one_harness_of_the_image`, `the_image_harness_record_reads_back_and_an_absent_one_is_refused`, `the_image_harnesses_are_the_staged_harness_recipes_the_image_holds`; the argparse reference corpus re-blessed for the `--pass` default and help)
- [x] `cargo xtask build` (x86_64)
- [x] boot on x86_64 (`run --runs 1`): svctest, usertest and ktest, terminal pass marker observed
- [x] `cargo xtask build --arch riscv64`
- [x] boot on riscv64: svctest, usertest and ktest, terminal pass marker observed
- [x] additional component-specific checks: a temporary, uncommitted fault in svctest's own process before its marker reads FAIL within the grace window, after svcmgr's death line (x86_64 and riscv64)

## Validation
Validated head: 83f94187b (the sync of `master` at afafff56d; its incoming diff changes only Markdown in the PR's files, docs/testing.md and xtask/README.md, in sections the PR does not change, and merged without a conflict). Every run below was taken at 83f94187b; each command was admitted by the host launch rules with no grant (4 vCPUs).

- `cargo xtask test`, `cargo xtask lint-docs`: pass.
- `cargo xtask build`, x86_64 and riscv64: complete.
- usertest (`--runs 1`): PASS on x86_64 and riscv64, `[usertest] ALL TESTS PASSED`.
- ktest (`--runs 1`): PASS on x86_64 and riscv64, `[ktest] ALL TESTS PASSED`.
- The harness-death demonstration, a temporary uncommitted fault in svctest's own process before its marker, on the tree composed with PR #1644: FAIL on x86_64 with svcmgr's `service died: svctest` at guest time 2.49 s and the run ended at 15.0 s wall (timeout 900 s), and FAIL on riscv64 with the death line at 18.8 s and the run ended at 36.0 s wall; neither is a HANG.

Coverage screens on the PR's own diff: the CPU-count and memory surfaces are not touched, and no concurrency-fix purpose is stated. `xtask/src/disk.rs` is on the storage-wide device surface (docs/testing.md § Device surfaces) and its pack changes are not inert, so the four storage cells are owed on each architecture, at `--runs 1` (svctest `ci`, `--test-devices`):
- 4kn, second-disk, shared-line, oversize-block, x86_64: PASS, PASS, PASS, PASS at 83f94187b
- 4kn, second-disk, shared-line, oversize-block, riscv64: PASS, PASS, PASS, PASS at 83f94187b

The other changed files (`classified.rs`, `cli.rs`, `sysroot.rs`) are on no surface.

## Notes
- The Issue's "recorded harness" existed only as the bundle (`sysroot/.harness`, `init` or `ktest`); which of svctest, usertest and ubench an init image boots is decided by the recipes staged in `config/svcmgr/services/`. The pack now records them in `sysroot/.image-harness`, removed at the start of every pack and written after the image check, so it follows `disk.img` (a failed pack leaves no record, and `run --runs` refuses an image with none, naming the repack). It stays off the root partition like `.arch` and `.harness`.
- ubench is a third harness svcmgr launches with the same marker shape (the bench cell boots it with the default `--pass`), so the death line and the bound default cover it too.
- An image that boots no harness, or several, has no default `--pass`: `run --runs` refuses at once instead of booting to a HANG. A run with an explicit `--pass` is judged as before.
- The death line is matched as svcmgr's `[svcmgr] service died: <name>` with the name ended by the line's end or a character no service name holds, so `usertest-fixture` or another process's line is not read as the harness's death. A death before the first pass marker fails the run even when a restarted instance logs the marker later (all three recipes are `restart = never`). logd enqueues a line before it replies to the call, so the marker a harness logs before it exits precedes svcmgr's death line.
- ktest has no supervisor to log its death: its own fault stays a HANG, and docs/testing.md § Reporting marker says so.
- Consequence for CI: a validate cell (`--runs 1`) whose boot crashes QEMU now fails, by the no-PASS rule; no re-run rule is added for CI.
- One PR rather than the Issue's two: both halves change `classified.rs`, `cli.rs` and the same sections of xtask/README.md and docs/testing.md.
- Expansion: core/ktest/README.md stated the bare-substring scrape; it now states the bound marker (change propagation).

author: medalink
body:
## Why

Four gaps found while seeding mcode, a private copy of MiaAI-Lab/m3code (32,000 files, 12,800 commits), from a cloud agent session where no second agent CLI can sign in.

## What

- **`sync --prompt` / `--continue` / `--abort`.** `--prompt` merges; if anything is left it prints the sync step's prompt, leaves the merge open and exits 2. `--continue` checks for markers, runs the check, commits and pushes, or prints the problem and stays open. `--abort` resets. Other commands refuse while a sync is open. rerere bookkeeping is kept across the two calls in `.git/xtend-sync.json`.
- **`get --origin` is checked first.** `git ls-remote` runs before the clone. Unreachable: stop. Not empty: stop and say why (GitHub's README or license box), unless `--replace`, which keeps the old tip on `replaced-<branch>` and pushes with `--force-with-lease`.
- **Upstream workflows are turned off in your copy.** After `get --private`, `get --origin` and `daily on`, every workflow except `xtend.yml` gets `gh workflow disable`. Without gh or off GitHub, xTend says they are still on. In mcode, 27 inherited workflows started queuing CI on the first push.
- **`xtend update`** copies the running xtend over `.xtend/xtend.mjs` and commits it.
- README and skill cover all four.

## Tested

`npm test` passes with new e2e cases for each. Not run against real GitHub: `gh workflow disable` (the session's proxy blocks Actions endpoints).

In the document mail dialog, extra event documents never travelled with the mail and removing the main document had no effect. `POST /api/v1/mail/document-send` never listed the ATTACH-01a fields `attachDocument` and `documentIds` in its schema, and Fastify silently strips unknown body properties. The repository tests called `scheduleDocumentSend` directly, so they could not see it.

## Change
- Route schema: `attachDocument` (boolean) and `documentIds` (max 10 UUIDs, the same limit as the repository)
- New route-level integration test: a mail with only an extra document over HTTP (red before the fix)
- Correction note on ATTACH-01a in the implementation plan

## Tests
`pnpm check:local` green against `origin/main` (format, lint, types, workspace, docs, coverage with 2133 tests, build, ops, changed-code coverage).

author: johntwillemsen
body:
## Evidence and effect

Port **unchanged with original attribution** of [fxceless/victory-fork#77](https://github.com/fxceless/victory-fork/pull/77) by its original contributor (`a6388aa`). Eight deferred-material pixel shaders formerly refused with `the first half of an interpolation`. The mixed-precision FMA was unnecessarily reading the missing first-half value to preserve a high half that no later instruction reads.

- The patch allows a missing prior value to be zero-filled consistently with `write_half`, rather than refusing the whole pixel program.
- Adds a synthetic `mixlo_over_an_f16_first_interpolation_half` DXIL validation regression test.
- Original author: Windows RTX 4070 workspace tests 497 pass, 7 ignored, Clippy clean; offline corpus adds eight emitting/validating PS shaders, no other programs changed.
- Independent RTX 5070 Ti tester reports that this failure corresponds to missing walls/ceilings; with equivalent fix the room shell appeared, host draws/frame rose 6421→6831. **This is a contributor report, not a proof that every missing wall on every GPU is fixed.**

## Caution / acceptance

- [ ] Run Windows CI and regression test on *this* branch; our GitHub Actions currently have no runs.
- [ ] Inspect fallback behavior: currently `Some(Err(_))` becomes zero, rather than propagating a non-interpolation failure. This matches upstream candidate but merits review before merging.
- [ ] RTX 5090 hardware A/B from same checkpoint, with default relay and no skips. Verify geometry, material color, texture and dropped draw counts.
- [ ] Check for shader cache separation if testing with older translation runs.
- [ ] Licensing provenance audit of inherited decoder remains unresolved; this PR does not change that file.

`main` is untouched. No title code or game-derived assets committed.

body:
Question from the user: "does it always pick the right template, and does it use the templates in Azure DevOps?" In the run without team.yaml, L01 (create a story) failed 2/2 on `template-sections-in-order`: `loadStoryTemplate` only looked at `workItems.storyTemplate` and `skills/_shared/assets/story-template.md`, so a team repository with `.agents/skills/_shared/assets/story-template.md` and no team.yaml got the English built-in template.

## Order (story, Bug, Task)
1. (a) the path in team.yaml (`workItems.storyTemplate`, `workItems.templates.<Type>`; a missing Bug/Task path still fails as before)
2. (b) `.agents/skills/_shared/assets/<type>-template.md`, then `skills/_shared/assets/<type>-template.md`
3. (c) the team's work item template in Azure DevOps: `GET {org}/{project}/{team}/_apis/wit/templates?workitemtypename=<type>` (team: `azureDevOps.team` or "<project> Team"), then that template; `System.Description` (and the acceptance criteria) HTML to `## ` sections. One template: that one. Several: the only one whose name contains the type or "story"; otherwise none, and the result line says which ones exist. Only when (a) and (b) find nothing; cached in `.git/aihub/cache/devops-templates.json` for a day (a failure for ten minutes); no access or no network is skipped silently.
4. (d) built-in, with the hint `add .agents/skills/_shared/assets/<type>-template.md to use your own`.

`story context` keeps the local lookup (a, b, d) without network.

## Visible source
`story template` (first line, `--json`: `template`, `kind`, `text`), `story create`, `story refine`, `workitem create` and `pr create` end their result line with `template: <path>`, `template: Azure DevOps "<name>"` or `template: built-in (...)`. `pr create` names the PR template with `(origin/<target>)` or `(working tree)`, or `template: none (...)`.

## Pull request templates
`templateCandidates` already follows Azure DevOps (branch-specific for the target, then the default; `.azuredevops`, `.vsts`, `docs`, root). New: a case variant of the file name (`PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`, `Docs/Pull_Request_Template.md`) is found on `origin/<target>` (one `git ls-tree`, only when no exact name matched) and in the working tree. The other callers (cherry-pick, doctor, release, port) keep the exact lookup.

## Also
`lint:skills` normalised CRLF to LF before counting tokens: a Windows checkout counted `\r` and failed `start-here` at ~507 tokens where CI counted fewer.

## Tests
- New `test/work-item-template.test.ts` (12): (b) without team.yaml, (a) beats (b), `.agents` beats `skills/`, (c) from Azure DevOps and then from the cache with 0 calls, several templates with no clear one, 403 gives built-in with the hint, create/refine name the source, Bug template under `.agents`, HTML without headings ignored; PR: the target's branch-specific template wins and another branch's does not count, case variant on origin and locally, origin beats a local copy also with a case variant, the `pr create` source text.
- Changed on purpose: `story.test.ts` "story create maps template sections" expects the new `; template: built-in (...)` at the end of the line, and finds the POST call by method (the template lookup now makes a GET first when there is no local template).
- Full suite: 890 passed, 2 failed: the two sign-in tests in `perf-bar.test.ts` that fail on this machine without this change too (credential in the environment; green in CI). `lint:skills`: ok.

Speed: no timer or watcher. A repository with its own template makes no network call. Without one: at most two GETs a day per work item type. `pr create` adds one `git ls-tree` only when no exact template name exists on the target.

author: teamleaderleo
body:
When TURN relay A dies, a relay-only iPhone held on to its dead A allocation until the link's 45 s keepalive timeout, and only then redialed onto relay B. A UDP TURN allocation never reported itself dead; only a stream allocation did. Even with #54861 (the hand-over to B), cmux#53760's ios-mac relay `failover` cell resumed in about 62 s.

With this PR the session notices a silent TURN server within a bound derived from the route's smoothed RTT. It drops that allocation, allocates on the next server through #54861's path, and resumes without a redial. On the same rig, resume drops from about 62 s to 1.83-1.86 s idle and 1.25 s under duress. No run failed, redialed, duplicated or left a gap.

Stacked on #54861 (base `lane/ios-relay-failover`); retarget to `feat-cmux-next` once that lands.

Leo-Ask-Trace: ask-6242128727
Leo-Ask-Trace: ask-bb9c69b84e
Leo-Ask-Trace: ask-983c698fa4
iOS-hold: strict fix
Merge-case: strict fix. A relay-only session took about 62 s to resume after its TURN server died. Four files in cmux-mobile-link, Rust only. No transport replaced, no default flipped, no new fixed wait and no existing wait made longer.

## The detector

- **When it runs.** In `Paths::poll` (`dial/wireguard_paths.rs`), a probe can be reported lost or a route silent (unanswered past its silence window). When that route's carrier is `Carrier::Turn`, the paths record the route's smoothed RTT. `HybridUnderlay::poll_probes` (`dial/wireguard.rs`) then calls `TurnCarrier::check_server(bound)` on the current allocation.
- **What is probed.** The TURN server itself, through the allocation's own UDP socket. It gets a STUN Binding request at t=0 and a second at t=bound/2, so a single lost datagram does not kill a live server. Any datagram from the server since t=0 counts as an answer: the Binding response or relayed data. `TapConn::observe` stamps it before any STUN parsing.
- **The bound.** `bound = 2 * cmux_wg::silence_window(srtt) = max(8 * srtt, 200 ms)`. `silence_window(rtt) = max(4 * rtt, SILENCE_FLOOR = 100 ms)` is the window the multipath layer already uses. No new constant was added.
- **Where srtt comes from.** The `cmux_transport` Selector's smoothed probe RTT for that TURN route (`selector.path(id).rtt_us`, updated as `(3 * old + sample) / 4` on every probe answer). If several TURN routes went quiet in one poll, the largest is used. With no sample yet, the window is the 100 ms floor, so the bound is 200 ms.
- **When it fires.** The allocation's `dead` watch is set, its send queue closed, and the server ranked behind the others for #54861's `FAILED_SERVER_WAIT`. `Session::install_turn` now watches UDP allocations' `dead` too, not only streams'. The existing `retry_turn` → `replace_turn` path allocates on the next server (#54861's hand-over) and announces the new relayed address. Only one check runs at a time per allocation. A server that answers leaves everything untouched: a quiet route whose server is alive is the peer's or the link's matter.

## The idle gap, and the nudge

Idle used to take 4.8-5.6 s against 1.25 s under duress. Traced (local `eprintln` in an untracked rig copy), idle run, ms after TURN server A was dropped:

```
     0.0  drop_turn_A, marker written
   591.8  Mac: route to the phone's relayed address on A silent (unanswered send)
  4396.6  Mac: that route Dead
  4967.3  phone: its Turn route silent -> check_server starts (bound 585.7 ms)
  5554.1  phone: server A dead
  5555.9  phone: allocated on B, announced
  5639.9  marker arrived
```

Under duress the phone's Turn route went silent at 584.4 ms, so it was dead at 1169.2 and resumed at 1259.5. The cause: an idle relay-only phone sends nothing, and `PathWatch` arms its silence watch only after a send or a probe. The phone's current path is probed every 5 s, so its check started at its next probe tick, about 4.4 s late. The Mac, which was sending, saw the route go quiet at about 0.59 s.

The fix, no new wait: when the chosen route goes quiet (the selector's existing silence or lost verdict, reported once by `Paths::take_chosen_quiet`) and it is the peer's TURN relayed address, the session resends its latest endpoint announcement through signaling (`Session::nudge_peer`; generation 0 if it never announced). The peer has already applied it, so it only acknowledges it, inside the tunnel, on its TURN route. That send arms the peer's silence watch, and with it the server check. Traced after the fix (idle, ms): Mac nudge 582.6, phone receives it 582.7, phone Turn silent and check starts 1167.3, dead 1750.6, allocated on B 1752.2, marker 1835.0.

## Changelog

- cmux-mobile-link (`dial/turn.rs`): `TurnCarrier::check_server(bound)` probes a UDP allocation's server with STUN Binding and declares the allocation dead when nothing comes back within `bound`. Every UDP allocation now has a `dead` watch.
- cmux-mobile-link (`dial/wireguard_paths.rs`, `dial/wireguard.rs`): a TURN route that loses a probe or goes silent triggers that check, with `bound = 2 * silence_window(srtt)`.
- cmux-mobile-link (`dial/wireguard_roam.rs`): the session watches UDP allocations' `dead` as well as streams'.
- cmux-mobile-link (`dial/wireguard_paths.rs`, `dial/wireguard.rs`, `dial/wireguard_roam.rs`): when the route to the peer's TURN relayed address goes quiet, the session resends its endpoint announcement through signaling so an idle peer starts its own TURN check at once instead of at its next 5 s probe.
- Regression test `dial::wireguard_paths::tests::a_quiet_chosen_route_is_reported_once_within_its_window`: a relayed route left unanswered is reported quiet within 250 ms, exactly once.
- Regression test `dial::turn::tests::a_silent_udp_turn_server_is_declared_dead_within_its_bound`. Two UDP allocations each get `check_server(300 ms)`, one on a server that is then dropped. The dropped server's allocation must go dead no earlier than the bound and within 2x of it. The live server's allocation must stay up.

## Tests

All on a 16-core Linux lane VM.

- The new test cannot exist on base: `check_server` does not exist there, and no UDP allocation ever goes dead. It passes here. All 49 `dial::` tests pass (release, `--features testing`).
- Pair-matrix rig: `cmux-mobile-host/tests/pair_matrix_ios_mac.rs` from lane/pair-matrix at cafceb9f, with the local `Phone::drive` watch-guard fix described in #54861. That rig file is not in this PR. Relay `failover`, `resume_ms` per run:

| | idle (n=3) | duress (n=3) | fails | redials | dups / gaps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #54861 alone | 62148 / 62225 / 62176 | 62181 / 62183 / 62693 | 0/6 | 1 per run | 0 / 0 |
| #54861 + detector (dc0b72a) | 5625 / 4768 / 5623 | 1256 / 1250 / 1250 | 0/6 | 0 | 0 / 0 |
| #54861 + detector + nudge (36ee9ef) | 1828 / 1832 / 1865 | 1259 / 1253 / 1253 | 0/6 | 0 | 0 / 0 |

Every run ended on `Turn` with `link_closed: false`.

## ELI5

Your phone reaches your Mac through a relay server. When that relay quietly died, the phone didn't notice for 45 seconds, and the chat sat frozen for about a minute. Now, as soon as messages through the relay stop coming back, the phone (or the Mac, which pokes an idle phone) asks the relay "are you there?" twice. It waits only a few round trips, based on how fast that relay normally answers. If there's no reply, it switches to the backup relay right away. In our test the chat came back in under 2 seconds on a quiet machine and about 1 second on a busy one, with nothing lost or repeated.

author: taskto-admin
body:
## What

Send invites by email. When the server can email links, the invite dialog offers **Email the invite link to this address** (on by default, can be unticked); the link is still shown to copy.

- `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace}/invites` takes an optional `send_email`. The reply always has the token; with `send_email` it also has `email_sent`. A failed send doesn't undo the invite: the admin is told the email failed and sends the link by hand (the failure is logged by its step and the SMTP reply's number, never in the answer).
- Template `invite` (en, pt-BR) naming the admin and workspace, in the invited person's language if they have an account that picked one, else the workspace's default, else the admin's own, else English. The link `/invite#<token>` is built on `public_url`, never logged.
- Audit: `invite_emailed` (workspace, admin, the invite) when the SMTP server took the message, documented in `docs/audit.md`; it holds no address and no link.
- Limits: 30 emailed invitations an hour per admin (across workspaces) and 3 an hour per invited address; `429 too_many_invite_emails` with `Retry-After`, checked before the invite is made, and given back if the invite then fails (for example, the address is already a member). Invites without `send_email` aren't limited.
- Without SMTP and `public_url` nothing changes: the dialog has no checkbox, and `send_email` is refused with `409 mail_not_configured`, creating nothing.
- Settings → General → Email says when SMTP is set but `public_url` isn't (`sends_links: false`), since the links then aren't emailed.

Depends on #47 (it uses the same mail options, `public_url` rule and helpers), so until #47 merges this PR's diff also shows its commit; review only the last three commits (the invite dialog, the audit event and the language fix). The base is `main` because CI runs only for pull requests into `main`.

## How it was checked

- `internal/auth/invite_mail_test.go`: the emailed token is the invite's and works; no email without asking; refused where links can't be emailed (nothing made); a failed send keeps the invite and logs no relay text, address or token; per-address and per-admin limits (window ends; another admin unaffected; a refused request creates nothing and doesn't count); a failed invite gives its attempt back; a member, an anonymous caller and a member of another workspace can't send, and the message names the workspace it is for; the language choice.
- Web: checkbox shown only where the server emails links and sent in the request; unticking it; the failed-email notice; the old dialog everywhere else (mail not set, no public address, status unknown); the settings hint.
- `make lint`, `go test ./...`, `go test -race` on the invite tests, `pnpm --filter @taskto/web run i18n`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm run test`.

author: winify
body:
## Summary
Hardening of the GitHub workflows, driven by a zizmor + actionlint scan of `main` (3 high, 6 medium zizmor findings; 2 shellcheck infos).

- **Template injection (high):** `release.yml` interpolated `inputs.releaseType` / `inputs.distTag` into the `run:` line. They now go through `env:` and are quoted.
- **Credential persistence:** `persist-credentials: false` on lint, test and registry checkouts. The release checkout keeps credentials (release-it pushes the release commit and tag) with an inline `zizmor: ignore[artipacked]`.
- **Cache poisoning:** release no longer restores the pnpm cache; the registry workflow disables the package-manager cache.
- **Install scripts:** `--ignore-scripts` on the dev publish and on release-it's publish (`npm.publishArgs`). No `prepack`/`prepublishOnly` exists; the bundle is built in an explicit step.
- **Permissions:** `expense.yml` gets `permissions: {}` at top level and on `authorize` (it authenticates with `WDIO_BOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, not `GITHUB_TOKEN`).
- **CI gate:** new `workflows` job in `lint.yml` runs zizmor 1.33.1 (`--offline`) and actionlint 1.7.12 via digest-pinned Docker images, since third-party actions are not in the repo's allowlist.

## Test plan
- [x] `zizmor --offline .github/workflows`: no findings (1 ignored, 20 suppressed)
- [x] `actionlint`: exit 0
- [ ] `workflows` job green on this PR

body:
## What

Two public editor methods go (owner's decision, 2026-11-25).

**`Editor::replace` is deleted; `replace_or_swap` is the one replace.** No shipped crate called `replace`: the session's `Graph::replace` goes through `replace_or_swap`. The two differed in three cases. A key not in the spec: `replace` returned an error and `replace_or_swap` panicked; it now returns `CommitError::NoSuchNode` and changes nothing, so a call that names a node that does not exist fails at the call by name. A key not running yet, and a cut over another shape: `replace` refused and `replace_or_swap` swaps, which is its documented job and what the session relies on; no test pinned the refusals. `CommitError::NotRunning`, which only `replace` raised, is deleted. 66 test call sites follow the survivor with the same arguments; the missing-key assertion in `a_shape_mismatch_is_refused` now expects `NoSuchNode`.

**`Editor::leaked_items` is deleted.** Nothing read it and an app could not act on it. The condition is not silent: `Editor::collect` logs an error on the control side when the executor's apply leaked items since the last collect, with the number (the audio thread still only counts). tutti-graph gains the workspace's `tracing` dependency for it.

author: nelsongan
body:
The food map's "All time" now shows every tagged meal up to its 2,000 limit, instead of silently stopping at the newest 1,000.

**Source.** Found by the triage review of #326 (ledger row 241, queued 2026-11-22). No production error: the failure is silent. The map asks for up to 2,000 tagged meals in one request, but PostgREST answers at most 1,000 rows (`max_rows`) whatever the request's limit says, so every place visited only before the newest 1,000 tagged meals disappeared from the map and its totals. Nobody is near 1,000 tagged meals yet, so no user is affected today; the README already promises "the newest 2,000 tagged entries".

### What changed

- The map's read asks a page at a time (1,000, then the rest) until it has 2,000 or runs out, through the shared helper the diary already uses for reads past the cap.
- Meals logged in the same instant are now ordered by id too, so one page and the next cannot swap them and show a meal twice or skip one.

### Verification

- **Failing test on main:** new `located.test.ts` (3 tests) fails on main: 1,500 tagged meals come back as `Received length: 1000`, and 2,600 as 1,000 instead of 2,000. All pass with the fix, as do the existing `everyRow` callers' tests.
- **iPhone 18 Pro simulator (iOS 27.0, Simlock pool), local Supabase stack (`max_rows = 1000`, as hosted), Pro account** with 1,500 synthetic tagged meals added: the newest 1,000 at stalls in Kuala Lumpur, the older 500 at Gurney Drive, Penang, beside the account's 18 seeded tagged meals.
  - main: All time shows "18 places · 1000 meals" and no Penang place.
  - this branch: "19 places · 1518 meals", with Gurney Drive's 500 meals and its pin. The local gateway log shows three page requests (`offset=0&limit=1000`, `offset=1000&limit=1000`, `offset=1518&limit=482`).
  - The synthetic rows were deleted afterwards.
- `pnpm check` passes (1,973 jest tests, typecheck, biome).

| main | this branch |
|---|---|
| ![All time stops at 1,000 meals on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58526779-f540-40f5-bba1-6751a846ef7a) | ![All time shows all 1,518 meals and Penang](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/218f447a-b159-4305-bdc2-24d44a36c010) |

### Possible regression risks

- Opening the map now costs one more small request for everyone: the helper stops on an empty page rather than a short one (a short page cannot be trusted while the server's cap may sit below the page size), so an account with 18 tagged meals asks twice and one with 1,500 asks three times. The partial index serves each, and the result is held until a tagged meal changes.
- The shared page-at-a-time helper gained an optional limit. Without it, its other callers behave exactly as before (their tests pass).

**What the merge ships:** `apps/mobile` only, so `deploy.yml` builds and submits a new app to both stores. No backend change.

| v2-router.yml | v2-router | ⚙️ Router (v2) |
| watchdog.yml | watchdog | ⚙️ Watchdog |

## Display-name matches, and what changed
- **Controller check reader** (`github.ts` `CHECK_WORKFLOWS`) matched `run.name` against `ci`, `gates` and `drills`. It now matches the run's file (`path`) through `checkWorkflowOf`. The internal ids (`ci`, `gates`, `drills`) are unchanged, so the planner and the audit log are unaffected. This is also safer: a `pull_request` run takes its name from the PR's copy of the workflow, so any file could claim "ci". New test.
- **`workflow_run` triggers**, which can only filter by name:
  - controller: "⚙️ CI", "⚙️ Gates" and "🤖 Agent: review PR (v1)", plus the old names.
  - v2-router: "⚙️ CI", "⚙️ Gates" and the two new v2 agent names, plus the old names.
  - dependency-steward: "⚙️ CI", plus "ci".
  - watchdog: "⚙️ Controller (v1)", plus "controller".
- **`dependency-steward.yml`**: `workflow_run.name == 'ci'` is now `workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'`.
- **`repair.md` and `v2-repair.md`**: the failed-run check `.name == "ci"` is now `.path == ".github/workflows/ci.yml"`.
- **Already by file or job name (unchanged):** the v2 router (`ci.yml`, `gates.yml`), the canary, spend, caps, `gh aw logs`, the factory review's data collection, onboard's run ledger, both watchdogs (`controller` is a job name), the factory results page, the required status checks (`checks` and `gates` are job contexts), and CAO, which watches the whole repo.
- **Run-names (`display_title`) are unchanged**, including the activation canary's. queue-dispatch has no explicit `run-name`, so its run title follows the new name; nothing matches on it.

## Kept on purpose
- Every changed `workflow_run` list also keeps the old names, so runs that report them still wake the listener:
  - "ci" and "gates" (controller, v2-router, dependency-steward): PR branches cut before this merge still report these names.
  - "Review one factory PR" (controller), "Port one language (factory v2)" and "Repair one factory v2 PR" (v2-router), and "controller" (watchdog): runs started or re-run from a revision before the rename.
  - The old names can be removed once no such PR or run remains.

## Checks
- `gh aw compile` (v1.2.2) of all 9 agentic workflows: 0 warnings.
- Tests: controller 538/538 (1 new), harness 142/142. actionlint on the plain workflows reports only security-alerts' `vulnerability-alerts` scope, which main has too.
- Branch canary: PASS for implement, repair, review and triage (runs 45491241179, 45491241266, 45491241402 and 45491241260). The Actions tab only shows the new workflow names once this is on main.

## Journal
Finding: the controller matched ci, gates and drills runs by display name, which a `pull_request` run takes from the PR's own copy of the workflow. Lesson: identify workflow runs by file (`path`); keep display names for people.

body: ## Summary Follow-up after live QA on #16 (board “QA PR16 Retest”). 1. **Reactions** — Concurrent partner toggles were lost to full-bundle LWW on `boards.collections`. Dirty merges take **remote** per-item reactions so a caption edit cannot wipe a partner toggle. 2. **← Back** — Collection routes carry a `honeydropCollection` history marker; Back pops only when that marker is present, otherwise `replacePath` to the board. `popstate` reads boards / `activeBoardId` via ref; overshoot to `/` while a collection is open restores that URL (avoids boards list / “not on this device”). 3. **Lightbox** — History entry pushed in `useLayoutEffect`; × / Escape pop only when this mount owns the entry; stay-href restore if Back overshoots (covers automated open paths). ## Migration / edge — APPLY BEFORE MERGE **File:** `supabase/migrations/007_toggle_item_reaction.sql` **Mike / Supabot must apply before merge.** Without it, reaction toggles fail RPC and resync. No edge-function change. ### RPC ```text toggle_item_reaction(p_board_id uuid, p_collection_id text, p_item_id text, p_emoji text) → jsonb ``` Toggle via `auth.uid()`. Returns `{ ok, board_id, collection_id, item_id, emoji, action: "added"|"removed", reactions: [...] }`. ## Verify - `npm run lint` / `npm run build` clean (existing oxlint warnings elsewhere unchanged). - Live `?qa=1`: partners both react on the same drop — both stick without reload. - Event/idea **← Back** → board (not boards list). - Slideshow (click or programmatic) → × / Escape → still on that idea/event. ## What changes

On Android, an authored Fill with a quoted target (for example `Fill "qa-late-code" with "1234"`) that is refused `TARGET_NOT_FOUND` on a read with the app in front, before the step has sent any action of its own, now gets one more ordinary attempt. The walker writes one `retry` row ending "deciding again on a fresh read", pauses 500 ms and runs the attempts loop again with every existing guard. That next target decision is taken only on an observation with the app in front; on any other surface the first refusal goes back to recovery, as before. If that decision refuses, its refusal carries "; decided again on a fresh read". It happens at most once per step.

A Fill whose on-screen matches are all non-inputs now gets the advice to quote the text field's own testID or move this testID onto the field (all platforms).

Unchanged: Tap and Wait, iOS, stored selectors, replays and login blocks, described targets, ambiguity, steps that already sent a scroll or Fill, the launch poll, recovery and its precedence. No new refusal code, no CLI change, no new wait owner and no deadline threading.

A `<split-view>` with no `<sidebar>` has only its content pane, so on macOS it drew no divider and laid its children out as a column, with nothing to say why. Drawing two content panes as an NSSplitView would be a new feature, not a fix; this takes the issue's other option.

body:
**Stage 3 of 5** of the Item World (plan: `Plans/POKETACTICA_ITEM_WORLD_PLAN.md`; stages 1-2 merged in #1490). Item levels can now be earned.

## What it does
- **Camp → Item World.** Pick a held item from the bag, then how to dive: **Battles** (this PR) or **Mystery Maze** (stage 4, shown but not yet open).
- **A dive** runs from the item's level to its next exit floor (10, 20 … 100): a tactics battle a floor on a generated board, the exit a boss. Foes get stronger with the floor and with the item's shop price.
- **Clearing the exit banks the dive:** the item becomes that level (a new slot at 25, 50, 75 and 100), and the plush gemstones and the Stitching Kit found on the way join the collection.
- **Nothing is kept before the exit.** A lost floor ends the dive (no "Try again"). Giving a floor up keeps the dive waiting on the device; the Item World screen offers Continue or Abandon. One dive at a time, and the item can't be put on a figurine while it is dived into.
- **Deadly**, as Story and the Dungeon: a fainted figurine is gone for good. The item is never lost.

## Finds
A plain floor holds a gemstone about half the time; an exit always holds one (stronger) and a Stitching Kit, two gemstones from floor 50. Gemstone levels rise with depth: about level 2 near the top, about level 30 near the bottom. All from the dive's seed.

## Tests
- `poketactica_itemworld_test.mjs` (new, 46): floors and exits, foe levels, finds, the dive kept on the device, banking (including the item gone from the bag, and never lowering or passing 100).
- `poketactica_items_test.mjs` (82): a whole dive on the page: two floors to the exit, the bank, a lost floor, give up, continue, one-at-a-time, abandon.

author: arthware-dev
body:
## Summary

`./stack` on a fresh clone of `main` now offers a release first. `main` is work in progress. The installer offers the
newest pre-release (recommended for new installs) and the newest final release. It switches the checkout to the chosen
tag and runs the installer of that release. `stack update` then moves from release to release.

A script install (`./stack install --family <file> --yes`) installs the checkout as it is. A clone on a tag or on
another branch installs as before. An install that is already set up does not change.

## Tests

| Behavior | Proof |
|---|---|
| 1. A clone of `main` hears that `main` is work in progress, and gets the newest releases | `test_a_clone_of_main_is_offered_the_newest_releases_first` |
| 2. A picked release is checked out, and its installer runs | `test_a_picked_release_is_checked_out_and_its_installer_runs` |
| 3. A final release newer than every pre-release is the only release offered | `test_a_final_release_newer_than_every_prerelease_is_the_only_release_offered`, `test_the_examples_of_the_offer_hold` |
| 4. "Stay on main" installs `main` | `test_staying_on_main_installs_main_and_says_what_update_offers` |
| 5. A clone on a tag or on another branch is asked nothing | `test_a_clone_on_a_tag_is_asked_nothing_about_releases`, `test_a_clone_on_main_exactly_at_a_tag_is_asked_nothing`, `test_a_clone_on_another_branch_is_asked_nothing_about_releases` |
| 6. A script install neither asks nor switches | `test_a_script_install_neither_asks_nor_switches` |
| 7. A clone without tags goes on as it is | `test_a_clone_without_tags_says_it_found_no_release_and_goes_on` |
| 8. An install that is set up, or that stopped halfway, is asked nothing | `test_an_install_that_is_set_up_is_asked_nothing_and_stays`, `test_an_install_that_stopped_halfway_is_asked_nothing_and_stays` |
| A checkout with local edits is not switched | `test_a_checkout_with_local_edits_is_not_switched` |
| A release whose installer cannot start says how to go back | `test_a_release_whose_installer_cannot_start_says_how_to_go_back` |

The tests run `./stack install` as a process in a temporary git repository with tags.

author: a2f0
body:
## Summary

The browser recovery-QR scanner decoded camera frames silently: until a code was read, nothing showed whether one was even in view. This shows live feedback while scanning.

- The decoder already reports where it found a code (`pointsOnDetect` in `qr` 0.7.2, already a dependency), including for codes it cannot read yet. The camera loop now passes each unfinished frame's code outline to the scanner. Pixels are still zeroed after each decode, and the decoded value never enters scan state.
- `RecoveryKeyScanOverlay` draws an SVG over the video: viewfinder corners and the located code's outline. Its `viewBox` is the decoded frame, and it scales like the `object-fit: contain` video, so decoder coordinates line up without any conversion. The preview takes the stream's aspect ratio, so a portrait phone stream fills the frame instead of being pillarboxed.
- Each state has a visual hint: "Starting the camera...", "Point your camera at your recovery QR code.", "QR code found. Hold steady while it is read.", plus the existing rejected-code and camera-failure alerts. The hint is deliberately not a live region: a code drifting in and out of focus would make it chatter, while failures and rejections still announce as alerts.
- The camera asks for `1280x720` (as `ideal`, so it never fails). A dense recovery QR (45–53 modules) then keeps more pixels per module; frames are still scaled to at most 960px before decoding.
- Between frames the loop waits at least as long as the last decode took (80 ms minimum), so a slow phone never spends more than half its main thread scanning.

Behaviour change: the "not a valid recovery key" alert used to stay until Cancel. It now clears 2 s after the wrong code leaves view, and the scanner returns to "Point your camera…".

Native shells (iOS/Android) still use photo capture here. Moving them to this live scanner is a follow-up PR.

## State machine

`recoveryKeyScanState.ts` replaces the old `error` string, which was set from two places (an invalid decode and a camera failure).

States: `starting`, `searching {frame}`, `located {frame, outline, seenAt}`, `rejected {frame, outline?, seenAt, rejectedAt}`, `failed {message}`.
Events: `frame {width, height, at, outline?, rejected}`, `fail {message}`.

| From | Event | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| any but `failed` | `fail` | `failed` |
| `failed` | anything | `failed` (the first camera error wins) |
| any live state | frame with a rejected code | `rejected` |
| `rejected`, under 2 s since rejection | frame with a code | `rejected`, outline follows the code |
| `rejected`, under 2 s since rejection | empty frame | `rejected`; outline cleared after 500 ms unseen, or at once if the frame size changed |
| `starting` / `searching` / `located`, or `rejected` after 2 s | frame with a code | `located` |
| `located`, under 500 ms since last seen, same frame size | empty frame | `located` (same state) |
| otherwise | empty frame | `searching` (same object when the size is unchanged, so no re-render) |

Removed combinations: a rejection message shown alongside a camera failure, and frames still in flight overwriting a camera error. The hold windows stop the outline and the rejection alert from flickering when a code drops out of focus for a frame or two.

Left alone: `RecoveryKeyScanControl`'s `scanning` (a single boolean), and the camera's `stopped` flag (a one-way cleanup guard with one writer).

## Validation

- `bun run check:package app`: 4459 pass, 0 fail.
- New `recoveryKeyScanState.test.ts` covers every transition (rotation during a hold included), the same-state cases, flicker hold, and a failure that frames cannot hide. The two rotation rows fail against the version without the rotation fix.
- The new component tests cover searching, located (a test-kit code whose finder patterns are intact but whose data is scrambled), rejected, starting, and a camera failure. A 480x320 frame with the code off-centre checks that the overlay `viewBox`, the preview's aspect ratio, and the outline agree. That test fails if the `viewBox` axes are swapped.
- The new camera tests cover frame reporting, outline coordinates on a wide frame, a decode callback that closes the scan, and that an accepted frame is not reported as feedback.
- Playwright `recovery-qr` and `onboarding-recovery-qr` pass in Chromium. Local screenshots at 390x844 confirmed the outline sits on the code in the located and rejected states, and that the viewfinder stays visible over a white frame.
- `bun tsc --build`, `bun run check:fast`, and `lint:source-shape --staged` pass.

## Review

Codex was out of usage credits and OpenCode (DeepSeek) had insufficient balance, so the independent review used a separate Claude Code CLI session: same model family, separate session. Four rounds returned MINOR with no blockers. Fixed in response: a stale outline on rotation, the pixel stroke widths' justification comment, live-region chatter, the bounds of the test kit's scramble, wide-frame coverage, and frames reported after the scan closed.

Not taken:
- Drawing a just-swapped-in correct code green during the 2 s rejection hold. A correct code ends the scan as soon as it is read, and splitting the outline from the alert would bring back flicker for a wrong code at borderline focus.
- A fake-timer test for the adaptive gap between scans, and a downscale (>960px) camera fixture. The test kit's `getImageData` mock does not follow canvas size, so that path is covered by the Playwright specs rather than unit tests.

author: arimendelow
body:
Ari asked that the agents working on his interfaces know the bar by instinct, without being reminded. Design craft holds the bar (#3551); this gets a short statement of it to the agents in the repositories Ouro Current keeps, and keeps it current without anyone remembering.

On an update pull request, Ouro Current brings these lines into the repository's `AGENTS.md`, between `<!-- ouro-ui:bar -->` markers:[^update]

```md
**The bar, for people and agents alike** ([design craft](https://ui.ouroboros.bot/docs/design-craft/#the-bar)): would the people who made the Mac and the iPhone ship it? Whenever you scope or design something a person or an agent meets (a screen, a menu, a setting, a command, an action, a tool, a line of output):

1. Start from the jobs people do, in their words. Read a reference product's items, a service's functions or an API's fields as evidence of jobs, never as the list to build.
2. Make the first cut restraint: for each thing, name the job it serves and ask what breaks if it goes; if nothing does, leave it out and say why. Give each job one way in, not one per item or function, and extend the one that exists before adding another.
3. Build what is left well, the basics people use daily among it, for the person and for agents, with a result that says what it did.
4. Write how fresh people or fresh agents doing a real job will prove it, and rerun them after each small change.
```

- Why steps rather than a statement: in the bar evaluation (#3551), fresh agents given the bar as a statement planned as they did without it; given it as these steps, they started from jobs, cut with reasons and planned the proof more often.
- Why `AGENTS.md`: coding agents load it in their sessions without a hook or an install. Why Ouro Current: it already opens a pull request per release in the products that take Ouro from their releases, so a new product gets the lines on its first update, and a change to them reaches the products on their next.
- The block goes after the paragraph that points at ourostack's Interfaces follow Ouro UI rule, or at the end, and changes in place when `agents.mjs` does.[^place] The rest of `AGENTS.md` stays the repository's.
- A repository with an AGENTS.md byte budget in `.github/agents-md-budget.json`, as `spoonjoy/spoonjoy-v2` has, gets it moved by the block's bytes alone, so its own text keeps the room it had.[^update]
- `ignore: ["AGENTS.md"]` in `.github/ouro-current.json` leaves the file alone, and a repository without `AGENTS.md` gets none.[^update]

[^place]: test:scripts/current/current.test.mjs::AGENTS.md gets the bar beside its pointer to Interfaces follow Ouro UI, or at the end, and a stale block is replaced in place verify:testExists(scripts/current/current.test.mjs::AGENTS.md gets the bar beside its pointer to Interfaces follow Ouro UI, or at the end, and a stale block is replaced in place)
[^update]: test:scripts/current/current.test.mjs::an update brings the bar into AGENTS.md and moves its byte budget by the block alone, unless the repository ignores AGENTS.md verify:testExists(scripts/current/current.test.mjs::an update brings the bar into AGENTS.md and moves its byte budget by the block alone, unless the repository ignores AGENTS.md)

Relates to #3545.

author: florianklueckmann
body:
Ticket: https://fvs.youtrack.cloud/issue/T3B-112 (evidence is attached there).

## Problem

A Bot could prepare for an event only through one routine per event, set up on request. Asked once to "watch for upcoming sessions", it had no way to check on its own and stay silent when there was nothing to say: every routine run is a result card, an unread conversation and an alert.

## Fix

A standing assignment is one recurring **No changes** routine marked as a **watch** (`watch` on the routine's Bot target, set by the Bot through `schedule_task`). No new object and no new integration.

- Each unattended run ends its result with a report line: nothing new, or the occasion it posts about with its open questions.
- When the run ends, the server decides from that report and from what the routine already posted (`bot_watch_posts`, bots migration 026). A watch posts **once per occasion**; a second check on the same occasion is quiet whatever the model writes.
- A post is the ordinary routine result: a card in the Bot's conversation, the conversation unread, one alert through the existing alert budget.
- A quiet run shows nothing: no card (left out of the task list on every client, old ones included), no unread mark, no early Home check, no push, no web or desktop completion notification, and its work thread is archived.
- A run without a readable report shows like any routine result. A run the user starts with Run now always shows.
- Only No changes runs are watches, so the existing seal applies unchanged: read-only sandbox on Codex, no shell on Claude, and only read-only tools of the MCP connections granted to the Bot. Switching the routine to Changes allowed makes it an ordinary routine.

Nothing in the product code knows about D&D; the session case lives in the eval fixtures.

## Hit every surface

- **Providers:** Codex and Claude run No changes, so both run watches; measured on Codex only. Pi has no No changes routines, so no watch.
- **Clients:** no new control. The task list and alerts come from the server, so web, desktop and mobile get quiet runs for free. Web and desktop hold a watch run's local completion notification until the server settled it. The routine form does not show the flag yet and keeps it on save.
- **Agents:** `schedule_task` and its update take `watch`; `list_scheduled_tasks` returns it.
- **Reverse states:** pause or delete the routine in Settings → Bots, or ask the Bot. The routine is listed there like any other.
- **Contracts:** `ScheduledTaskBotTarget.watch`, `BotTaskSummary.watch`, `thread.archive.ifLatestRunId`, all optional.
- **Docs:** "Standing assignments" in `docs/user/bots.md`.

## Proof

- New server tests fail on `t3bot` and pass here (`BotTaskService.test.ts`, `BotWatch.test.ts`, the relay budget test, the notification coordinator test).
- `evals/bot-preparation`, GPT-6 Luna at medium, 3 samples per case: 18/18 on this change; the quiet cases are 0/3 on `t3bot` with the same brief as a plain routine.
- A runtime transcript from an isolated dev home: one assignment, one post, then two quiet checks.
- `vp run check:changed origin/t3bot` is green.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 5 rounds with gpt-6.2-sol on high. Sol verdict: changes requested in the last round for one finding (two dates colliding in the occasion key), fixed with a regression test and not re-reviewed. One earlier finding is declined as a follow-up on the ticket.

body: ## Complexity 🌱 Trivial: plan documents only (`.plan/active/bridge-pr-monitor/`). ## What Adds the durable plan for moving the PR monitor into the Sesori bridge and grouping the Sesori MCP server's tools: - `PLAN.md`: 17 steps in phase 1. - A tool-group interface package and a grouped MCP server, with an on/off toggle per group. - A durable tool host. - A PR monitor package (`gh`) ported from plugin v0.10.0, with one poll per PR fanned out to every watching session, resume after a restart, readiness and auto-merge, and `configure_pr_monitor`. - Skills plus a `get_guide` fallback on every harness with a seam. - The session mark and composer chip, the watched-PR list (option B), and OpenCode support. - Regression docs, then verification. - `PR_MONITOR_SPEC.md`: the plugin behaviour the port must keep. - `TRACKER.md`: the step table. ## Why The plugin monitor stops on a Sesori restart, a lost session or a lost network connection, and it behaves differently on each harness. A bridge-owned monitor delivers Sesori Automation messages on every harness and survives restarts. Tool groups give future Sesori tool plugins one interface, per-group gating, and leaner agent context. ## Risk and test focus None at runtime: this PR changes no code. Review the step boundaries and the owner decisions recorded in `PLAN.md`. The architecture plan review findings (13) are already applied. This PR is docs-only: it adds `.plan/active/bridge-pr-monitor/PLAN.md`, `PR_MONITOR_SPEC.md`, and `TRACKER.md`, with no code or runtime impact. **What the plan covers** - 17 phase-1 steps: a tool-group interface package, a grouped MCP server with per-group toggles, a durable tool host, the PR monitor ported from plugin v0.10.0 (`gh`-based polling, fan-out to watching sessions, restart resume, readiness and auto-merge, `configure_pr_monitor`), skills with a `get_guide` fallback, the session mark and composer chip, the watched-PR list, and OpenCode support. - `PR_MONITOR_SPEC.md` records the plugin behavior the port must keep; `TRACKER.md` tracks step status. - Review focus is the step boundaries and owner decisions in `PLAN.md`; the 13 architecture-review findings are already applied, and one item (the OpenCode mechanism for step 15) is deliberately left open pending research. body:
Closes #1914. ADR 056, S2.

## What moved
- The previews and fixtures of `SchoolScreen.kt`, `words/LessonWordsScreen.kt` and `text/SchoolTextScreen.kt` (`PreviewHoldoutChecksSlot` included) moved to `<Screen>ScreenPreview.kt` beside each screen. The three screen composables are now `internal`; the previews stay `private`.
- `SchoolLanguages` went to its own `SchoolLanguages.kt`, still `internal`: two screens' previews read it, detekt's `Filename` rule refuses it as the only non-private class of `SchoolScreenPreview.kt`, and keeping it there left that file at 257 lines, over the 250 limit.

## Left for S4 (sizes)
No `baseline.txt` line is deleted, since both baselined screens stay over 250:
- `file-lines feature/school/src/main/kotlin/com/emm/mygame/feature/school/SchoolScreen.kt` (288 lines)
- `file-lines feature/school/src/main/kotlin/com/emm/mygame/feature/school/words/LessonWordsScreen.kt` (275 lines)

## Files in the diff
No file moved whole, so `git diff -M90%` shows no `R`:
- `M`: the three `*Screen.kt`, previews removed, unused imports dropped, `fun` turned `internal`.
- `A`: the three `*ScreenPreview.kt` and `SchoolLanguages.kt`.

## Proof
Per screen, the lines removed from `*Screen.kt` equal the lines of the new files, apart from `package`, `import`, blank lines and the `fun` line turning `internal`. The comparison is sorted, because `SchoolLanguages` left the middle of the block:

```bash
D=apps/android/feature/school/src/main/kotlin/com/emm/mygame/feature/school
strip() { rg -I -v '^(package|import) |^$' "$@"; }
for s in SchoolScreen words/LessonWordsScreen text/SchoolTextScreen; do
  new=($D/${s}Preview.kt); [ $s = SchoolScreen ] && new+=($D/SchoolLanguages.kt)
  diff <(git diff -U0 origin/trunk -- $D/$s.kt | rg '^-[^-]' | rg -v '^-(package|import) ' | sed 's/^-//' | rg -v '^(fun|internal fun) \w+Screen\(' | sort) \
       <(strip "${new[@]}" | sort) > /dev/null && echo "ok $s" || echo "FAIL $s"
done
```

Prints `ok SchoolScreen`, `ok words/LessonWordsScreen`, `ok text/SchoolTextScreen`.

Order check for the extracted class:

```bash
D=apps/android/feature/school/src/main/kotlin/com/emm/mygame/feature/school
removed() { git diff -U0 origin/trunk -- $D/SchoolScreen.kt | rg '^-[^-]' | rg -v '^-(package|import) ' | sed 's/^-//' | rg -v '^(fun|internal fun) SchoolScreen\('; }
body() { rg -v '^(package|import) |^$' "$1"; }
diff <(removed | awk '/^internal class SchoolLanguages/{f=1} /^private fun PreviewHoldoutChecksSlot/{f=0} f && !/^@Composable/') <(body $D/SchoolLanguages.kt) && echo ok languages
```

Prints `ok languages`.

## Evidence

author: bonustrack
body:
Most of our Goldsky bill is repeats. Blue and green indexers, delegates, schnaps-api and futarchy-api fetch the same blocks (`eth_getBlockByNumber`, then `eth_getLogs` by block hash), and Base has made 5 blocks a second since 5 Nov. This keeps answers that can never change in brovider's memory and serves the repeats from there.

### What gets cached
- By hash, always: `eth_getLogs` with `blockHash`, `eth_getBlockByHash`, `eth_call`/`eth_getBalance`/... with an EIP-1898 `{ blockHash }` (not with `requireCanonical: true`). Empty `getLogs` results are not stored.
- By block number (`eth_getBlockByNumber`, `eth_getLogs` with an exact range, `eth_call`, `eth_getBalance`, `eth_getCode`, `eth_getStorageAt`, `eth_getTransactionCount`): only once the block is `RPC_CACHE_DEPTH` (32, Polygon 256) behind the highest block seen in answers passing through. No extra calls to find the head.
- Never: `latest`/`pending`/`safe`/`finalized`, `eth_blockNumber`, errors, `null`, non-200, anything over 2 MB.

LRU in a `Map`, bounded in bytes (`RPC_CACHE_MB`, 512), a hit moves the entry to most recent.

### Not slower
- Non-cacheable requests keep the existing proxy path untouched. A response hook on `express-http-proxy` would switch it from streaming to buffering every response, so the cache has its own path for cacheable reads.
- A miss streams the node's bytes to the client as they arrive and keeps a copy, checked and stored after the response is sent.
- A hit is a stored Buffer with the caller's `id` spliced in, no JSON parsing.
- Identical requests in flight share one node call. Status codes pass through (429 stays 429), a timeout answers 504 like the proxy, and a connection error hands over to the proxy.

### Rollout
`RPC_CACHE` is `off` by default, so merging changes nothing.
1. Deploy with `RPC_CACHE=shadow`: the cache fills and compares with every node answer, but always serves the node's answer.
2. After a day, check `rpc_cache_count` (would-be hits), `rpc_cache_store_count` and `rpc_cache_mismatch_count` (must stay 0).
3. Switch to `RPC_CACHE=on`.

### Test plan
- [x] 49 new tests: request classification, LRU eviction by bytes, invalid env values, hits with hostile ids, empty/error/null/429 not stored, depth rule, shared in-flight requests, shared timeout, shadow mismatches, timeout 504, node down falls back to the proxy, node dropping the connection mid-answer
- [x] `yarn lint`, `yarn typecheck`, `yarn test`: 164/168 pass. The 4 failures are the `subgraph` and `delegation` e2e tests, which fail the same way on `master` locally (live subgraphs answer 400 without the CI key)
- [x] Real data: 394 requests on 9 chains through `master`, this branch with `on` (twice) and `shadow` (twice), compared with the node's direct answer. 300 repeats served from memory, all identical. The only differences were errors for an unknown block hash that the node itself answers differently between calls. 0 shadow mismatches
- [x] Failure injection against a fake node, `master` vs this branch: same result for 200, 429, 500 HTML, gzip, truncated JSON, hang (504 after 30 s) and node down (500). One difference: when the node drops the connection mid-answer, `master` leaves the client waiting and this closes it right away
- [x] Benchmark, real router against a fake node at 30 ms, 60 s per mode: uncacheable requests and first fetches unchanged (p50 about 34 ms, p99 37 to 40 ms in every mode), repeats 1 to 2 ms p50, CPU per request off 2.43 ms, shadow 2.99 ms, on 2.42 ms
- [ ] Shadow mode for a day in production, then `on`

author: ovitrif
body:
Closes #1399
Refs: #1397

Keeps a node stop, a failed start or a node change from acting on another node's event loop, lock or caches.

### Description

- The event loop slot now records the node its loop serves. A stop, a failed `start()` or a node change cancels and waits for only that node's loop. Before, a `stop()` that finished after a restart cancelled the new node's loop, leaving it running with no listener, and a failed `start()` could cancel a loop another start installed.
- `stop()` clears the event callback and channel cache only while its node is still configured, then releases the node and unlocks `.lightning` together under `setupLock`. A stop that finishes after its node was released or replaced leaves the replacement's loop, lock, callback and channels alone.
- A stop with no node no longer unlocks `.lightning`: during `setup()` that lock is the setup's. A native stop that fails, other than `NotRunning`, leaves the node configured and keeps the lock while that node may still run; `restart()` and its recovery release it only after its loop ended.
- `start()` throws `nodeNotSetup` when its node was replaced before its loop started, instead of starting a node nothing holds. A new loop also waits for a loop of the same node that a stop is still ending.
- `waitForEnd` no longer reports a finished task as timed out: a timer whose sleep was cancelled reports nothing.

#### Out of Scope

- A stopped node's write that lands after the 5 s wait is fenced only once the app pins an ldk-node release with synonymdev/ldk-node#140; #1397 closes with the rc.82 bump.
- `Bitkit/Services/LightningService.swift`: restart paths can release a stale node when a replacement's native stop fails; tracked in #1422 ([review](https://github.com/synonymdev/bitkit-ios/pull/1417#pullrequestreview-6055227880)).
- `Bitkit/Services/LightningService.swift`: `start()` can start a node a concurrent restart replaced, pre-existing; tracked in #1423 ([review](https://github.com/synonymdev/bitkit-ios/pull/1417#pullrequestreview-6055227880)).

### Design

N/A — no UI changes.

### Preview

N/A

### QA Notes

#### Setup

Regtest build.

#### Journeys

N/A — no user-visible behaviour change.

#### Manual Tests

- [ ] 1. Restart the node 5 times (Settings → Dev Settings → LDK → Restart), then receive a Lightning payment → the payment shows once and the node keeps receiving events

#### Automated Checks

- added `LightningServiceTests` cases: `waitForEnd` reports an ended task as ended over 200 runs, and a `stop()` with no node leaves the `.lightning` lock to its holder. The node-scoped loop ownership needs a real `Node` and has no unit test.

#### Evidence

- Unit suite (CI test selection) on an iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 26.5, ldk-node 0.7.0-rc.81: all passed on b658529f6.

#### Gaps

- 1. not run.

### Models used

- Planning/scoping: `Claude Opus 5.5` (reasoning: `medium`)
- Implementation: `Claude Opus 5.5` (reasoning: `medium`)
- Review: `gemini-4-neon-high` (reasoning: `Not exposed`)
- Review rounds: 2

The pre-PR review run records only its model id.

body:
Part of #337

## What

A new page, `docs/operations/postgres-parameters.md`, documents what `tests/system/pg_config_test.go` and `v1_cluster_spec_test.go` run, plus the keeper code:

- **Changing parameters:** set and remove `pgParameters` with `orion-cli update --patch` (`null` removes one).
- **Reload or restart:** the keeper reloads on a change. A parameter that needs a restart shows as `pending_restart` and sets `orion_keeper_needs_restart`; the keeper only restarts with `automaticPgRestart` (default `false`).
- **Parameters Orion sets itself:** a table of the parameters the keeper ignores in `pgParameters`, and where their values come from. `wal_level` (only `logical` is used, otherwise `replica`) and `wal_keep_size` can be set within limits.
- **`ALTER SYSTEM`** has no effect, because `postgresql.auto.conf` is a link to `/dev/null`.
- **A parameter PostgreSQL doesn't accept:** PostgreSQL keeps its old configuration, the other changes in the same update included, and the keeper doesn't restart it.
- **`mergePgParameters`:** where the parameters of `initdb` (or of the existing instance, or of the restored backup) end up.

The second commit folds in what is still true from `docs/stolon/postgres_parameters.md`, removes that page, and points its links (in other stolon pages) to the new page. The new page is added to `mkdocs.yml` (under Operations, after Point in time recovery) and to `docs/index.md`.

author: otsirh
body:
The privacy page had drifted from the code in places, and nothing held the numbers it quotes. The test that once held them went with the feature it guarded.

**The page (factual edits only)**
- It names Proton, where mail to the contact address arrives, and Microsoft among the push services (Edge's).
- It says Cloudflare is a US company's network that every request goes through; only the backups are said to be in the EU.
- It says what Scaleway keeps of each mail (the address, the subject, when it was sent) for as long as the service is used. This comes from Scaleway's own Transactional Email privacy page, which says sending metadata and logs are kept while the sending domain is active. The deletion section says the address stays there.
- It says requests are counted per address and its network for about an hour, not "without the full address".
- A guest's profile goes once the game isn't opened with it for 400 days. The old text said "400 days without a game", but any visit renews it.
- It says what deletion leaves in the day counts: the days played, under a number with no name or email.
- It names the browser's error reports kept in the logs, without the address, and what the game keeps in the browser itself.

**The tests**
- `TestPrivacyQuotesTheCode` pins each number the page quotes to the value the text was written for, next to its phrase, whether written as a word or as digits. Changing either side fails. Every host in `push.Services` must map to a company the page names.
- `TestDeletionClearsAddressColumns`: every column named like an email address must be cleared by the deletion (`remove`, `mail.Unqueue` or `play.Forget`), except `users`, whose row goes. A new table keyed by an address now fails until deletion clears it. It reads names only, and its comment says so.

Checked: changing `ReportDays` fails the first test. A scratch table with an `email` column, or removing the `code_mails` statement from `remove`, fails the second.

The legal wording (how to name the transfers, and a few other questions) waits for a lawyer and isn't in this PR.

body:
Implements the user's decisions A and B from the PC vs Android audit (`docs/pc-vs-android/`). PC is the default for both switches.

## A. ENEMY TIMING: PC now also covers the melee, slash, smoke and death slow-mo rules

Before changing anything I re-read each row in both binaries: Katana ZERO.exe (Steam, x86) and libyoyo.so (APK 1.1.10).

| Row | PC | Android | How PC is reproduced (exact) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 melee cooldown | `whip_timer = 15` after a shot (enemy, cop, machinegun Step); 30/20/10/25/15 after a melee (Other_24 of 8 enemy types) | the same `+ whip_attack_timer` (4, set only by AI_init) | `whip_attack_timer = 0` after AI_init (`enemy_timing.c`). Those 15 statements are its only readers. |
| 7 slash vs obj_tempdoor | line-of-sight `collision_line(..., obj_block)` with no exclusion | `with (obj_tempdoor) y -= 100000` before the checks, `+= 100000` after (enemy_hurt L11/L30) | Each loop's guard after NewWithIterator becomes `b` instead of `blt` (0x1993f50, 0x1995fb0). That is a `break` at the start of the loop: the body never runs and DeleteWithIterator restores self/other. The guards are rewritten between frames. No veneers are needed: none can reach this function. |
| 8 obj_slash vs door | `harmless = 1` (L49) | `trigger_harmless = 2`, counted down in Step (L53-58) | After the event, a `trigger_harmless` of 2 becomes `harmless = 1`, `trigger_harmless = 0`. **Also found:** Android saves image_angle/xscale at L3-4 and restores them at L58-61, while PC keeps the turned slash. PC mode makes the restore's `BOOL_RValue(change)` return false (veneer). |
| 13 smoked enemy in the air | ai_break_idle L4 `vsp = 0` at once | `falling_smoke_timer = 3` (smokescreen Step), ai_break_idle waits | `falling_smoke_timer = 0` on entry to ai_break_idle, its only reader (entry hook) |
| 15 death slow-mo | `if (gameover_timer > 5) { -= 0.1 ...; gsp += 0.0001 }` | `if (global.fr != 0) { -= 0.12 ...; gsp += 0.00015 }` | **The gate differs too, not only the constants:** PC runs the ramp from frame 6, during the hit freeze. Three veneered calls in obj_master Other_10: the gate's YYCompareVal evaluates `gameover_timer > 5` (the instance comes from an Other_10 wrapper), operator-= subtracts 0.1, operator+= adds 0.0001. |

All of these follow the existing ENEMY TIMING row and `enemyTiming` (yyl.cfg) on the next frame. The AI_init timers, as before, apply to enemies created after a change. Each part installs only if every instruction it relies on matches 1.1.10. Calls may be the APK's `bl` or the direct `bl` that `patch_plt_calls.py` makes of it.

## B. New GAME row TIMER & SLOW-MO: PC / ANDROID (`timerSlowmo=1` in yyl.cfg)

- **Time limits:** 92 statements set `global.max_time`. These are 88 in 82 level-controller Create/Step events, plus obj_master Create, obj_init Create, mobile_reset_game_data and xbox_reset_game_data. Each builds its constant with movw/movt. `timer_slowmo.c` rewrites the two immediates in place between frames: PC 6000/7000/8000/8100/8300/8600/9000, obj_master 4000, init 6000; ANDROID writes the originals back. Every site was checked against the PC version of the same event (`tools/pc-vs-android/timer_sites/`). A scan of all code for the Android values finds nothing else (two unrelated 6000s). obj_hud Draw and every other reader is the same code in both builds, so the HUD bar and the time-out checks follow.
- **Slow-mo:** `bullettime_max` 760 → 380 in obj_player Other_13. Drain, recharge, the katana modifiers and the HUD meter (round(bullettime / bullettime_max * 11)) are identical in both builds.
- **Storage:** the PC build's VSYNC option (`global.vsync`), saved in KatanaOptions.zero. Every reader was scanned: Create, Step, Draw, SAVE, Destroy, load/save_options, init/reset. Its only effect, display_reset, is already dropped or forced to vsync=false by the existing guard. The menu stores 4 (PC) or 5 (ANDROID). Old saves hold 0, or 1-2 from TEXT SMOOTHING; those mean "not chosen", so they follow yyl.cfg (PC).
- **When it applies:** the time limit at the next room or restart (or when a level's Step sets it after the intro), the meter at the next spawn. The boot default (obj_init) follows yyl.cfg, because it runs before load_options; obj_master Create overwrites it in every gameplay room.

## Corrections to the audit (added to docs/pc-vs-android/README.md)
- Row 1: obj_init Create also sets max_time (Android 9000, PC 6000). The audit's variable index missed it. The first Vita3K run showed 9000 at boot in PC mode.
- Row 15: the gate is different, as described above.

## Tests
**Vita3K** (probe build, `exp_pcrulesprobe`, not committed; PC vs `enemyTiming=1 timerSlowmo=1`):
- chinatown_2: `max_time 7000` vs `10500`, `bullettime_max 380` vs `760`; boot default 6000 vs 9000.
- club_1: grunt melee `whip_timer -51 -> 20` (PC) vs `-98 -> 24` (ANDROID).
- slash opening a door: `trigger_harmless 0, harmless 1` (PC) vs `trigger_harmless 2, harmless 0`.
- death: PC ramp from gameover_timer 6, `1 → 0.9 → 0.7999 → 0.6997` with gsp `+0.0001`. Android from about 21 (after the freeze), `1 → 0.88 → 0.75985` with gsp `+0.00015`.
- all 4 pc_rules parts and 93 timer sites install; the rebased build boots and installs in Vita3K.
- Not observed in a run: the falling-smoke case (it needs an enemy in mid-air when smoke loses it) and a slash through a tempdoor. Both rest on the code reading above.

**Vita** (device lock, saves/yyl.cfg/play eboot restored and verified after each hold):
- menu: GAME page shows the new row. Toggling ENEMY TIMING and TIMER & SLOW-MO to ANDROID and saving gives `10500`/`760` in chinatown_2. After a relaunch both still show ANDROID. Back to PC and saving gives `7000`/`380`. `display_reset from the options menu: skipped` as designed.
- combat in chinatown_2 (PC): slashes, a door kick, deaths and restarts. The death ramp matches the Vita3K values; no crash. Holding L for slow-mo works with both settings. The meter itself sits under the perf overlay in the screenshots, so its length was checked through the logged values only.

author: drkostas
body:
### What this changes

The refusal read "would overwrite a hand-written file nothing can bring back", and nothing is false. A file can have a copy outside git, a dated one beside it or one published somewhere else, and such a copy makes the loss recoverable by hand. The claim this check can stand behind is the narrower one, that no checkout can bring the file back, so that is what the refusal says now, and the module's first line and `at_risk`'s own docstring say the same.

A guard that overstates its reason teaches the reader to discount it, which is the one thing a refusal cannot afford. What the hook refuses does not change.

### Two cases the docstring left unsaid

The code already decides both, and each now has a test.

A folder that is no repository at all counts as unrecoverable, because git answers that with a code rather than an error. The test pins that answer with a ceiling directory, so it reads the same wherever the suite runs instead of depending on whether the temporary folder happens to sit inside a repository.

Only a git that cannot be run at all lets the command through. The test raises from the call itself, which is what proves a hook that cannot ask never stops work.

### Proof

`pytest -q tests/test_no_restore.py` is 43 passed, up from 41, and `python -m compileall -q src` is clean. Both sentences were found in review of the change that added the hook.

`Carousel`'s `layout` prop now also takes `"uncontained"`, `"uncontained-multi-aspect-ratio"` and `"full-screen"` (ADR-0040).

author: darkvader12
body:
Refs #7455. One commit (be6b8aaf), only in `RiemannMasullo/Ch10_TraceSpectral/Sec3_Isolated.lean` (imported by nothing). No statement on main changes; `spectralStripConvolution_summable_jetNorms` keeps its `sorry`.

- `spectralSobolevQuotient_markushevich_norm_mul_infDist`: in any Markushevich basis of the strip quotient, ‖xᵢ‖ · dist(Λᵢ, span{Λⱼ : j ≠ i}) = 1 (Remark 10.2.1.2, pp. 440–441). The lower bound holds in any normed space; equality uses `Submodule.quotientEquivOrthogonal`, Riesz and the orthogonal projection (private helpers).
- `spectralStripJet_norm_mul_norm_eq_div_infDist`: for a basis realizing the strip jets, ‖Λⱼ‖‖xⱼ‖ = ‖uⱼ‖ / dist(uⱼ, span{u_k : k ≠ j}), with uⱼ the jet in the reciprocal-weight L² space (D is an isometry).
- `spectralStripConvolution_summable_jetNorms_iff_jetDistances`: the series of #7455 converges iff the basis-free series Σ_z M_z Σ_m ‖u_{z,m}‖ / dist(u_{z,m}, span of the other jets) does.
- `spectralStripConvolution_block_series_of_summable_jetDistances`: the basis-free series gives the block series of #7241 after any bounded insertion.
- `spectralStripConvolution_summable_jetNorms_forces_summable_separation`: conversely, #7455 forces Σ_z M_z Σ_m ‖u‖ / ‖u − u_{c(z,m)}‖ < ∞ for any choice c of another jet, a summed strengthening of `spectralStripConvolution_compact_block_series_forces_jet_separation`.

So #7455 is exactly a statement about distances between the jets in a weighted L² space; the open part, how close distinct jets can come when zeros cluster, is unchanged. Complements @sflicht's analysis on #7455, which is about constructing interpolants; nothing from it is used here.

`#print axioms`: all five theorems use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. `scripts/signatures.sh --compare` against main: 5 new declarations, none changed; `--sorry-in-defs` passes. Module 8.7 s → 11.6 s (`lake lean`). `lake build RiemannMasullo Challenge Main` (19380 jobs) and `scripts/lint.sh` pass. Nothing from a November 2026 RH formalization is used.

author: matthewpipie
body:
**Stacked on #687; merge that first.** Until #687 lands, this PR's diff includes its commits. This PR's own changes are the last two commits, `d8d6e72` and `3caec49`.

Two DRRIP fixes that follow #687's saturating PSEL counter and lookup-miss reporting. Only runs that select DRRIP change: `golden_cove` and `sunny_cove` use true LRU at the MLC and LLC.

## 1. 32+32 leader sets in the paper's constituency layout (`d8d6e72`)

Two of every four sets were leaders, so half the cache was pinned to one policy, and only the other half could follow the winner. There are now `--drrip_leader_sets` (32) SRRIP leaders and as many BRRIP leaders, clamped to half the sets, one of each per constituency as in the paper. They are placed among the `set_mask + 1` sets an index can reach, so a set count that is not a power of two doesn't put leaders in sets nothing maps to.

This is the largest DRRIP fix, given #687's miss reporting. Don't merge it without #687: without the reporting, SPEC MLC+LLC DRRIP falls to −8.27%.

| IPC vs LRU | before (#680 + #687, without #676) | with this commit |
|---|---:|---:|
| Google LLC DRRIP | −5.20% | **−1.47%** |
| Google MLC+LLC DRRIP | −4.36% | **−1.89%** |
| SPEC LLC DRRIP | −2.14% | **−0.54%** |
| SPEC MLC+LLC DRRIP | −4.47% | **−0.71%** |

On Google charlie and delta, LLC DRRIP goes from −13% to +1.0% and −1.6%: the followers now track BRRIP, which wins there.

## 2. A private generator for DRRIP's BRRIP mode (`3caec49`)

DRRIP inserted through `brrip_update_insert`, which draws from the global `rand()`. Its init called `brrip_action_init`, which reseeds `rand()` with `srand()`. So every DRRIP cache reset the stream that other `rand()` users consume (Ramulator refresh, random-replacement tables), and their draws interleaved with DRRIP's.

BRRIP mode now draws from a per-cache xorshift generator with a fixed seed. A fill goes in at the long re-reference interval with probability 2^-(`--drrip_bimodal_throttle_log2`), which is 1/32 as in the paper, and at the distant interval otherwise. `REPL_BRRIP` itself is unchanged.

Measured effect: nothing beyond the different random stream (Google LLC DRRIP −1.47% → −1.55%, MLC+LLC −1.89% → −1.61%; SPEC within 0.03 points). This is about isolation, not performance.

## Testing

**Not yet rerun on this branch (draft).** Both commits cherry-picked onto #687 (with `main` merged in) without conflicts.

The numbers above are from the fork stack (matthewpipie/scarab#5 and #6), measured before it was rebased onto litz-lab `main`. IPC vs TRUE_LRU, top SimPoint per workload, geomean. Repeat runs are bit-identical.
- **Google:** `PARAMS.google` (non-exclusive; 2 MB 16-way MLC, 4 MB 16-way LLC; prefetching off). 10 workloads, 10M warmup + 50M instructions.
- **SPEC:** `PARAMS.sunny_cove` (`--exclusive_caches 1`, stream prefetcher into the LLC). 10 memory-bound SPEC2006 SimPoints, 50M warmup + 10M instructions.

The fork stack was measured without #676's free-way fix, which `main` now has. With #676 added, the whole set (#676, #680, #687 and these two commits) gave Google LLC DRRIP **+3.71%** vs LRU, up from −5.21% before any of them.
