author: jackpohladai
body:
This reduction isolates the behavior of the only OR gates reading vertices 4, 6 and 7 of the nine-vertex Petersen graph.

The first child is proved locally in Lean. Each companion wire is false on every singleton assignment, yet some graph edge disjoint from the chosen vertex turns it on. On that same edge, replacing the OR gate with the chosen input changes the final answer from true to false. The proof uses the minimality and monotonicity hypotheses. The second child rules out circuits of size at most 15 subject to these constraints and remains open.

The one-file reduction compiles. Its two child statements round-trip at 1,753 and 1,935 Unicode characters with the repository's canonical printer.

## Result
Motor de turnos: crear, confirmar, cancelar, reprogramar y marcar asistencia sin solapamientos.
- `POST /api/turnos`, `PATCH /api/turnos/{id}/estado`, `PUT /api/turnos/{id}`, `GET /api/turnos?desde&hasta[&sillonId][&profesionalId][&incluirCancelados]`, `GET /api/turnos/{id}` (ADMIN, PROFESIONAL y RECEPCION).

Los 409 identifican el turno en conflicto sin datos del paciente.
- Máquina de estados RN-AG-05. La reprogramación conserva la duración y revalida RN-AG-01..04.
- Auditoría `CREATE`/`UPDATE` (entidad `Turno`) con `AuditService.registrar` en la misma transacción (fail-closed). Las lecturas de agenda no se auditan. Ningún método combina `@Audited` con `readOnly` (regla de C-06 para MySQL), y lo controla un test de arquitectura.
- Sin migraciones ni dependencias nuevas.

## PR and SHA
Commit `c759a46` en la rama `c-07-turnos-agenda-engine`. Merge SHA: a completar al mergear.

## How to verify
- `cd backend && ./gradlew test` → **707/707** (línea base 545; 162 tests nuevos). JaCoCo `agenda.turno`: 100 % de instrucciones y de ramas.
  - En Windows: `JAVA_HOME` con JDK 21 y `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStoreType=Windows-ROOT` si aparece el error PKIX.

author: joshua-jingu-lee
body:
Closes #2846

## Summary
Treasury의 쓰기 경로(예약·취소/실패 회수·봇 중지 회수·체결 정산)가 DB 쓰기 실패 때 메모리 예산을 연산 전 사본으로 통째로 덮던 것을, **그 연산이 바꾼 증감만 되돌리는 것**으로 바꾼다. DB 쓰기를 기다리는 사이 같은 봇의 다른 연산이 바꾼 `reserved`·`available` 이 더는 지워지지 않는다. 봇 삭제(`release_budget`)는 트랜잭션이 실패하면 미할당 가산을 빼고 꺼낸 예산을 되돌려 넣는다.

- 첫 커밋: 스펙(`docs/specs/treasury/03-treasury-model.md` 「재시작 뒤의 예약 (#2770)」) 정정.

## 동작 변경

- `_restore_budget`(통째 복원) → `_revert_budget(target, before, after)`: 필드마다 현재 == 직후 값이면 직전 값으로(정확 복원), 아니면 `현재 - (직후 - 직전)`. `last_updated` 는 현재 == 직후일 때만 직전으로. 직전·직후 값은 동기 변경 블록 바로 앞·뒤(사이에 await 없음)에서 잡는다.
- 체결 정산: `order_tracker.get` 을 메모리 변경 블록 앞으로 꺼냈다. `_apply_fill_settlement` 는 await 없는 메모리 갱신(+`last_updated`)만 하고, 행 저장·예약 행·거래 기록은 `_persist_fill_settlement` 로 나눴다. `_settle_buy_fill` 은 조회된 record를 받는 동기 함수가 됐다. 직전 값과 예약 항목 사본은 그 await 뒤에 잡는다 → dedup INSERT·tracker 조회 단계에서 실패하면 메모리를 건드리지 않는다.
- `release_budget`: `pop` 과 `_unallocated += released` 는 그대로 트랜잭션 앞의 한 동기 블록. try는 트랜잭션 블록만 감싼다. 실패하면 `_unallocated -= released`(조건 없음)와, 메모리 경로였고 자리가 비어 있을 때만 예산 재삽입. 예약 표 항목 제거는 커밋 직후·`_save_state` 앞으로 당겼다(커밋 뒤의 `_save_state`·`_log_transaction` 실패에도 지운 봇의 항목이 남지 않는다).
- 예약 항목의 이어받음(리뷰 반영): 예약 항목을 바꾼 연산(예약·회수·매수 체결·봇 중지 회수)은 실패 때 그 주문의 항목이 **이 연산이 남긴 값 그대로일 때만** 예산 증감과 항목을 되돌린다. 다른 연산이 그 항목을 바꾸거나 회수했으면 그 연산이 예약을 이어받은 것으로 보고 되돌리지 않는다(경고 로그 한 줄). 봇 중지 회수는 주문별로 판정하고, 일괄 증감을 되돌릴 주문들의 몫으로 좁혀 되돌린다. 항목을 바꾸지 않은 연산(매도 체결 등)은 이전처럼 되돌린다.
- 실패 없는 경로의 금액·판정 시점·`treasury_transactions` 기록·오류 코드·이벤트·CLI/IPC 출력·스키마는 그대로다.

## 범위 밖

- 같은 `order_id` 에 겹치는 두 연산(취소·체결)의 예약 항목 복원.
- `allocate`/`deallocate` 의 실패 되돌림.
- 행 전체 쓰기 잔여(A의 커밋이 아직 커밋 전인 B의 메모리 증감을 행에 씀 — 보수적 방향), 커밋 뒤 취소 창, `DELETE FROM bot_budgets` 의 계좌 조건, `bot_budgets` 기본 키.
- 동기화 경로 자체, `delete_bot` 실패 처리(#2701), 만료 회수(#2842).

## Test Plan

- 새 테스트(`tests/unit/test_treasury_reservation_restart.py`) — 수정 전 7 failed(겹침 a·b·c·d, 봇 삭제 실패·재시도, 동기화 겹침 실패, `_save_state` 실패), 수정 뒤 통과.
- 변형 7종이 각각 의도한 테스트에서 FAIL: 통째 덮기(a·b·c) / 체결 직전 값을 트랜잭션 앞에서 캡처(d) / 미할당 가산을 커밋 뒤로(e·f 성공) / 실패 때 차감 삭제(e·f' 실패) / 예산 재삽입 삭제(e·f' 실패) / 차감 분기를 직전 값 대입으로(a·b·c) / 예약 항목 제거를 기록 뒤로(g).
- 리뷰 반영 테스트: 예약 쓰기 중 봇 중지가 회수한 뒤 예약 실패(수정 전 메모리 1,100,000 / −100,000) · 부분 체결 저장 실패 중 봇 중지가 남은 예약 회수(수정 전 reserved 40,000·spent 0 불일치) · 체결 저장 대기 중 다른 주문 예약 · 봇 중지 회수 중 한 주문이 다시 예약된 경우의 주문별 되돌림. 변형: 「항목 그대로일 때만」 조건 삭제 → 셋 FAIL, 주문별 몫 좁히기 삭제 → 주문별 테스트 FAIL, 차감 분기를 직전 값 대입으로 → 체결 경로 포함 다섯 FAIL.
- 기존 롤백 테스트(`TestTreasuryAtomicityRollback` 넷, `test_reserve/release_rolls_back_memory_when_write_fails`)는 기대값 그대로 통과.
- 관련 묶음(reservation_restart·fill_dedup·treasury·bot_delete_budget·bot_stop_release) 172 passed, `tests/unit/property/test_treasury_conservation.py` 3 passed, `tests/integration` 8 passed.
- `ruff check`·`ruff format --check`·`mypy src/`, 래칫 스크립트 6종 통과.

author: akiezun
body:
Adds statement-only `theorem_wanted` modules in `WantedExt/Biology/StatisticalGenetics/` for ten classical results in statistical genetics and epidemiology not yet formalized in the library:

- `PearsonAitkenLawleySelectionWanted`: Pearson–Aitken–Lawley selection formulas for conditional mean and covariance under linear selection (referencing `GaussianConditioning`).
- `SibTransmissionDisequilibriumWanted`: exact finite-population null mean and variance for the sibling transmission/disequilibrium test (Spielman and Ewens 1998).
- `KongCoxAlleleSharingWanted`: Kong–Cox (1997) one-parameter exponential allele-sharing model, score statistic, and likelihood-ratio identities.
- `CaseOnlyInteractionWanted`: Piegorsch, Weinberg, and Taylor (1994) case-only gene–environment interaction odds ratio under independence.
- `PrenticePykeCaseControlWanted`: Prentice–Pyke (1979) retrospective-to-prospective logistic intercept-shift identity for case-control studies.
- `MantelHaenszelWanted`: Mantel–Haenszel (1959) stratified odds-ratio estimator and homogeneity identities (referencing existing `Hypergeometric` and `CochranArmitageFixedMargin` results).
- `ConditionalLogisticMatchedSetsWanted`: Breslow, Day, Halvorsen, Prentice, and Sabai (1978) conditional logistic likelihood and score equations for matched case-control sets.
- `OddsRatioCollapsibilityWanted`: non-collapsibility of the odds ratio and sufficient collapsibility conditions (Greenland, Robins, and Pearl 1999).
- `PopulationAttributableFractionWanted`: Levin (1953) and Miettinen (1974) population attributable fraction identities and confounding decompositions.
- `BerksonBiasWanted`: Berkson's (1946) hospitalization selection bias and noisy-OR collider distortion bounds.

author: anthonykrupko
body:
FMT 7, the last step of docs/design/format-3.md section 12. Anton decided on 2026-11-24 to ship format 3 in the current release (0.5). A compile now writes format 3 by default, and the engine reads formats 2 and 3. The draft revision key is retired, so the format-3 drafts that development builds wrote (draft revisions 1 to 6) are refused as outdated. Routes and costs are unchanged. Ids change, so Monaco info and the gate baselines are re-recorded.

**What changes**
- `ROUTING_PACKAGE_FORMAT_VERSION` is 3, and `MAX_READ_FORMAT_VERSION` follows it. `MIN_READ_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 2, so 0.5 opens every format-2 package and these stay valid.
- `PackageFormat::default()`, `CompileRequest::new`, `PackageBuildOptions::default()` and the JSON compile request (through the field's default) all write format 3. That covers the CLI, the C ABI's compile and the host protocol.
- Format 2 can still be written on request, for apps whose engines are older than 0.5: `PackageFormat::V2`, or the hidden `wayfarer compile --package-format 2`. It stays byte-identical to main, checked with `cmp` on Monaco and Kraków centre.
- `PackageParams` key 10 (draft revision) is retired and never reused. A package that has it is refused as `Outdated`: "a draft of format 3 (draft revision N) from a development build; recompile it".
- The package build renumbers a road graph that a compile hasn't put in package order, so `package_bytes` and `write_package` build format 3 from any graph. In-memory builds of hand-made graphs used to fail with "renumber the graph first". The renumbering gives the package new ids. A compiled graph is already in package order, which one pass over its ids detects, so a compile doesn't renumber it twice.
- Progress: a format-3 build orders nodes for CCH first. It reports that under `build_package` (fraction 0), and the `cch_order` stage then completes at once in its usual place, so the stages still come in order and each one completes. A cancel at `cch_order` still stops the compile.

**Tests and fixtures**
- `fixtures/routing/short_road.mrt` is regenerated in format 3. `fixtures/routing/format-3/short_road.mrt` is its frozen copy, which `package_formats.rs` opens and routes beside the frozen format 2. There is also a format-3 seed for the `package` fuzz target.
- The tests that name the road graph's own node, edge and shared-info ids, or compare against the reference oracle over the graph, build format 2. Format 2 keeps those ids, and format 3 renumbers them by CCH rank. That covers the engine unit tests' `test_options`, `routing_acceptance.rs`, the compiler's layout tests and the format-2 byte-editing checks in `package_formats.rs`. `package_format_3.rs` still checks that format 3 routes as format 2 does (Monaco, all six profiles). The service, route-output and C ABI tests run on format 3.
- `package_format_3.rs`: the draft test becomes "drafts are refused". A released package writes no key 10, and drafts of revision 1, 6 and 7 are `Outdated`.
- The C ABI reports `readableFormats` [2, 3]. The fixture opens as format 3, with an identity hash apart from the content hash.
- The Monaco golden edge fingerprints in the compiler's determinism test are re-recorded. Distances, durations and costs match the old goldens.

**Re-recorded baselines**
- `fixtures/monaco-info.json`: format 3, 680,704 B (format 2: 665,024 B). It adds `readableFormats` 3 and the stand-alone `region`.
- `benchmarks/gates/krakow-centre-baseline.json`: Kraków centre is 4,336,960 B. Before re-recording, the gate passed on format 3 against the format-2 baseline: 22/22 corpus and 60/60 random, with visited edges going 20,984 → 20,979 and 29,470 → 29,465.
- `benchmarks/gates/malopolskie-baseline.json`: Małopolskie (malopolskie-261118) is 177,901,760 B, 7.05 MB under format 2's 184,954,688 B, and `wayfarer verify` passes. Before re-recording, the gate passed against the old baseline:
  - 124/124 corpus.
  - Random: the same 156 ok, 41 NoCandidate, 2 NoPath and 1 Disconnected.
  - Visited edges: 332,963 → 332,988 and 1,771,540 → 1,771,558.
  - Costs within 1e-7.

**Docs**
- `docs/design/format-3.md`: status released in 0.5, key 10 retired, and an as-built note in section 12.
- README (compatibility: reads 2..=3, and engines before 0.5 don't open format 3), `wayfarer-package/README.md` (versioning), `wayfarer-compiler/README.md` (sizes), the fixture READMEs and `fuzz/README.md`.
- CHANGELOG.md is left to the release PR. The paragraph below is for it.

**Rust API changes** (pre-1.0, for the release notes)
- `ROUTING_PACKAGE_FORMAT_VERSION` and `MAX_READ_FORMAT_VERSION` are 3.
- `PackageFormat`'s default is `V3`, so `PackageBuildOptions::default()` and `CompileRequest::new` write format 3. Code that compares package bytes, or names edges by the road graph's ids, should ask for `PackageFormat::V2`.
- Removed: `FORMAT_3_DRAFT_REVISION` and `PackageParams::draft_revision`. Struct literals of `PackageParams` lose that field.
- `param_key::DRAFT_REVISION` stays, as a retired key.

**Validation**
- `scripts/check.sh` passes:
  - fmt, clippy (`-D warnings`, all targets, plus ffi `--features compiler`) and rustdoc (`-D warnings`).
  - `cargo test --workspace`: 725 passed, 0 failed.
  - The re-recorded Monaco info.
  - The CLI and C ABI runs.
  - The Kraków centre gate on the re-recorded baseline.
- Fuzzing with `--debug-assertions`, no crash:
  - `package`: 5 minutes, 545,871 inputs, with the new format-3 seed.
  - `package_table`: 5 minutes, 100,811 inputs.
- Format 2 on request is byte-identical to the build before this change (Monaco, Kraków centre).

**Changelog.** Changed: compiles write package format 3 (FMT 7; `docs/design/format-3.md`). It has a tagged section table with optional sections that later 1.x releases can add, an identity hash (`datasetHash`) apart from the content hash, implied ids with nodes numbered by CCH rank and every dissection cell one id range (`CchCellTree`), `PackageParams` and `ProfileSlots`, u16 profile masks, versioned attribute-class records, OSM node ids, a stand-alone `RegionInfo`, u64 byte offsets and a request grid on the global 12″ lattice. On Małopolskie it is 7.05 MB (3.8 %) smaller, and routes and costs are unchanged. The engine reads formats 2 and 3, so format-2 packages keep working, but engines before 0.5 don't open format 3. Recompiling changes node, edge and shared-info ids and the dataset hash, so overlay sets bound by edge id need rebinding (stable references survive). The library can still write format 2 for older engines (`PackageFormat::V2`, hidden `--package-format 2`). The format-3 drafts that development builds wrote are refused; recompile them. Breaking (Rust API): `ROUTING_PACKAGE_FORMAT_VERSION` is 3, `PackageFormat` defaults to `V3`, and `FORMAT_3_DRAFT_REVISION` and `PackageParams::draft_revision` are removed.

author: jallum
body:
When two of the compiler's executables tie, something has to decide which comes first. Until now the tie-breaker was the raw `FunctionId`, the number the interner handed a function the first time it saw it. That number depends on which job happened to run first, so the same program could come out differently under a different job order.

It wasn't only the printout. The same tie-break decided:
- the printed `w{n}` / `x{n}` numbers;
- the order of the published wrappers, which the runtime indexes into;
- which return edge on a call cycle the transport layout cuts. That cut is what keeps interface layouts free of dependency loops: without it the distiller has 32 such loops.

Fixture 01574 showed it. A protocol impl and a named module print the same label, and which one became `w1` depended on mint order. Under fifo and lifo job order the backend plans differed.

## What changed
- `Types::cmp_function(a, b)` orders two source functions by their registered typed origin. Two distinct functions with equal origins are a loud assert, never a silent tie.
- `ActivationKey`, `FunctionId` and `ExecutableSymbol` `semantic_cmp` use it.
- The transport cycle cut uses it through `return_edge_is_cut`. Two copies of the same function still compare equal, so a cycle between them is still cut both ways.
- Tests that minted stand-in `FunctionId`s with no origin now register a real one through the cfg(test) `Types::test_function`. `cmp_function` has no fallback.
- 01574 joins `ORDER_FREE_PLANS`.
- The schedule-order drive test gains a lifo pass, because root order alone no longer perturbs arrival. Backend, output and facts must match across every pass. The amount of work matches only across root orders: work under lifo differs on base too, and that is tracked in fz-t93.31.
- `.agent/docs/canonical-form.md` states the ordering fact.

## Example
Before: `w1` = whichever of `Proto.Impl.f` / `Named.f` was minted first.
After: `w1` = whichever comes first by typed origin, in every job order.

## Pins (all fall)
| pin | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| work_start_reason census | (2484, 15, 31, 194) | (2482, 15, 31, 194) |
| work_start_reason second pin | (418, 420, [..202..]) | (416, 418, [..200..]) |
| 00420 cold body walks | 476 | 474 |
| fz2_cli runtime_demand_walks | 631 | 629 |
| distiller largest drive / total requests | 35163 / 35438 | 34654 / 34929 |
| distiller derivations / reads handed | 16291 / 120348 | 16202 / 118607 |

Part of the distiller fall is #863's saving, which this branch's base already carries. The ceilings had not been lowered for it.

## What and why

Closes #3094 — the three cosmetic P3s the #3082 delta seats deferred (Joran's two, Gino's one), all in `internal/api/entity_refs_s6_3081_test.go`; test file only, no production code, no behaviour change (the issue's own scope line):

The emitted message is unchanged for the single-field case.
2. **Reword the fallback sentence to the spec's words.** The old "would have to test a capability token rather than try the operation" garbled cor:api:220:01; the comment now states the rule as the spec does: test for the feature's capability token, and never infer support from the version number or discover it by attempting the operation.

body:
## Root cause
Commit b49137421ada89fe7dd3d80406b9014d6c785ad5 (2026-11-21) replaced automatic `push`-to-`main` conditions for the GHCR publish and `deploy-dev` jobs with `workflow_dispatch` and `deploy_dev=true` only. Consequently push CI was green, but published images and AWS dev deployment were skipped.

## Restored behavior
- On `push` to `main`, GHCR publishes SHA-pinned images **only after** `runtime`, `federation-mysql`, `capital-markets-unit` pass; `deploy-dev` additionally depends on successful image publication and uses protected `AWS TN2026` environment.
- Preserve manual dispatch on main with explicit `deploy_dev=true` and default false.
- PR events cannot publish or deploy; no production deployment is enabled.
- Update architecture gates and CI performance document to enforce the actual main-only deployment logic.

## Operational caution
Merging this PR will trigger a new main push and therefore attempt an AWS dev deployment. Confirm readiness for that deployment, environment protection, migrations, and rollback/backup posture before merge. This PR deliberately does not bypass GitHub Environment gates.

author: user01-2-gitproject
body:
This is step 3–4 of `docs/show-spec.md`. It gives show creation two front doors that lead to one `ShowSpec`. There's no migration.

### `POST /api/shows/spec`
- The body is `{ markdown: "<show.md>" }` (the file door) or `{ spec: {...} }` (the form door).
- File input goes through `parseShowMd`. Form JSON goes through the new `coerceShowSpec`, which forces types and guesses nothing, then `validateShowSpec`. On bad input it returns 400 with every error, and nothing is written. Requests over 128 KB are refused with 413 before parsing.
- **One SQL statement** inserts the show and its pronunciation lexicon using `unnest`, so they land together or not at all. It writes every column the spec maps to, including `style_guide`, `narration_mode` and `image_url`.
- Access is owner-only, through the existing middleware. Non-owner sessions and bearer tokens get 403 on POST.

### Form (`components/ShowSpecForm.tsx`)
This replaces `NewShowForm` on the home page. The fields:
- title, tagline;
- host, voice and host 2;
- cadence, time (`<input type=time>`), timezone (defaults to the browser's);
- minutes, narration, artwork URL;
- a "Show brief" textarea prefilled with the Voice & style / Segments / Sources & guardrails skeleton;
- pronunciations, one `TERM => say as` per line.

Two links work with files. **Import a show.md** fills the form from a file and lists any parse errors. **Download show.md** exports the current form with `toShowMd`. So Matt fills a form, jimmy keeps markdown, and both produce the same request.

### Tests (`tests/show-spec-route.test.cjs`)
- **The file door and the form door write identical SQL values** for the example show, including the built style guide and the lexicon arrays.
- Invalid specs, missing body and bad JSON return 400 with no writes. An oversized body returns 413.
- `coerceShowSpec` rejects wrong types and odd shapes.

`npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (111 pass) and `npm run build` are green locally.

**Not in this PR:** editing an existing show from a show.md, which would be `PUT /api/shows/[id]/spec` and an "Export show.md" button on the show page. That's the natural follow-up.

author: marcopetterson
body:
Partially addresses #7453 (Proposition 10.2.2.2, pp. 446–447, ERRATA I277).

Lean proves that the finite-line assertion for every choice of basepoints is equivalent to the conjunction of two tests in the open right half of the critical strip.

- `spectralStripJet_multiple_zero_bounded_height_representatives` asks for each character's multiple-zero lines to have bounded-height representatives. The bound may depend on the character.
- `spectralStripJet_multiple_real_zeros_finite` tests only real multiple zeros in $(1/2,1)$ across the family, for each choice of section.

The new `spectralStripJet_multiple_zero_lines_iff` proves both directions. Compactness controls a single character on a bounded rectangle. Imaginary norm twists put one chosen ordinate in each component onto the real axis. Choosing a witness component for each abscissa then reduces the union to finitely many single-character sets. The completed functional equation covers the left half.

The original private theorem has its original statement and applies the equivalence to two named `sorry` inputs. The proof uses the meromorphic divisor and the completed functional equation.

**Checks**

- `#print axioms spectralStripJet_multiple_zero_lines_iff` gives `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.
- The original theorem additionally lists `sorryAx` from the two open arithmetic inputs.
- `lake build RiemannMasullo Challenge Main` and `scripts/lint.sh` passed on the submitted commit `e2258415` (19,382 build jobs). The existing section signatures also compare equal before and after this change.

`docs/INFRASTRUCTURE.md` held both Stripe webhook signing secrets (test mode and live mode) in the Stripe table. This removes them from the current tree.

 | STRIPE_SECRET_KEY | sk_test_... | sk_live_... |
-| STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET | <test-mode signing secret> | <live-mode signing secret> |

author: jairaws
body:
### What was the problem/requirement? (What/Why)

A USD Import SOP loads a USD file as geometry. Its file path is in the parm `filepath1`. Houdini doesn't open that file itself. It hands the path to USD, which opens it. So `HOUDINI_PATHMAP`, which only reaches Houdini's own file I/O, never rewrites the path.

When an artist submits from Windows to a Linux worker, the path stays a Windows path, such as `P:/assets/cables.usda`. The SOP can't load it, and the render fails loudly before writing an image:

```
Error: Cook error in input: /stage/...
Error: Invalid source /obj/.../usdimport1/lopimport1.
(Error: Failed to cook LOP node.)
```

This happens even when a path mapping rule covers the path and the file is at the mapped location on the worker.

#355 fixed the same gap for LOP nodes. After the scene loads, the adaptor rewrites the file parms of every LOP node itself (`_remap_lop_file_paths`). But it only visits LOP nodes, and the USD Import SOP is a SOP. A Sublayer LOP with a Windows path renders on the worker. A USD Import SOP with the same path, under the same rule, does not.

The same failure shows up when the USD Import SOP sits inside a locked HDA outside the SOP and LOP contexts, such as an OBJ-level HDA that promotes the SOP's File parm to its own `filepath1`. A parm inside a locked HDA can't be set, so the value USD opens can only be mapped on the HDA node. But no pass visited OBJ, ROP, or TOP nodes.

A third gap: a Windows path typed with backslashes, such as `P:\assets\cables.usda`, didn't map on LOP nodes either. The adaptor writes every rule into `HOUDINI_PATHMAP` with forward slashes (`_set_houdini_pathmap`), and Houdini's `pathmap -t` doesn't match a backslash path against a forward-slash rule.

### What was the solution? (How)

In `houdini_handler.py`:

1. `set_scene_file` now also calls a new `_remap_sop_file_paths()`, after the LOP pass. It collects SOP nodes. It leaves out nodes inside a locked HDA unless they're editable, since their parms can't be set. Deadline 10's Houdini plugin uses the same rule when it path-maps parms at scene load.
2. The per-parm loop from `_remap_lop_file_paths` moves into a shared `_remap_file_parms(nodes, context)`, and both passes use it. Its rules don't change: string parms that are file references or named `filepath*`, skip empty, `$`, and backtick values, and skip and log keyframed or locked parms (#388). The log line names the context: `Remapped SOP parm <path>: <old> -> <new>`, next to the existing `Remapped LOP parm ...`.
3. In that shared loop, a Windows path (a drive letter and a slash, or a `\\` UNC prefix) is looked up in forward-slash form, the same `replace("\\", "/")` the adaptor applies to the rules. A parm is set only when a rule changed the path, so a path no rule covers keeps its value exactly as typed. POSIX paths are looked up as typed.
4. For each SOP left out because it's inside a locked HDA, the new `_outermost_locked_hda()` climbs `parent()` while the parent is itself inside a locked HDA, and returns the outermost locked HDA node. Each such HDA is remapped once, whatever its context, through the same `_remap_file_parms`, and logged as `Remapped HDA parm <path>: <old> -> <new>`. A SOP or LOP HDA is skipped here, because its own pass already remaps it. The SOPs inside the HDA are still never set.

Nodes are chosen by context, not by node type, so any SOP whose file parm reaches USD is covered, not just `Sop/usdimport`.

### What is the impact of this change?

* Scenes with a USD Import SOP whose path is covered by a path mapping rule now cook on workers whose paths differ, for example Windows to Linux. That includes a USD Import SOP inside a locked HDA, at any level, when the path is promoted to the HDA node.
* Sublayer, Reference, and other LOP nodes holding Windows paths with backslashes now map too. Before, those paths reached USD unmapped.
* SOPs that Houdini's file I/O already maps at read time, such as the File SOP, now get the same mapped path written into the parm. They render as before.
* A locked OBJ, DOP, ROP, or TOP HDA that holds a SOP, including HDAs that ship with Houdini, now has its file parms looked up. Values starting with `$`, such as `$HIP` defaults, are still skipped, and a path no rule covers is not set.
* Unchanged:
  * with no path mapping rules, no parm is touched;
  * paths starting with `$` or a backtick are left alone;
  * keyframed and locked parms are skipped and logged, and scene load continues;
  * forward-slash LOP mapping is exactly as before;
  * nodes inside a locked HDA are not edited.
* Not covered:
  * a USD Import SOP inside a locked HDA whose path is stored in the HDA's definition rather than on a promoted parm;
  * a LOP inside a locked HDA that isn't itself a LOP node, such as a ROP or OBJ HDA wrapping a LOP network whose Sublayer reads a promoted path. The LOP pass logs `Skipping LOP parm ...` for the inner LOP, as it did before this PR, and doesn't climb to the HDA. That could be a follow-up;
  * Windows paths written inside the USD file itself.

### How was this change tested?

* `hatch run fmt` and `hatch run lint`: pass.
* `hatch run test`: 1652 passed. New unit tests in `test/unit/deadline_adaptor_for_houdini/unit/HoudiniClient/test_handler.py` cover:
  * forward-slash, backslash, mixed-slash, and UNC paths on SOPs;
  * a backslash path on a LOP;
  * uncovered paths and POSIX paths;
  * keyframed and unsettable parms;
  * nodes inside a locked HDA;
  * an OBJ-level locked HDA whose promoted `filepath1` holds a backslash Windows path;
  * nested locked HDAs, where only the outermost is set;
  * one HDA holding several locked SOPs, set once;
  * a SOP or LOP HDA, left to its own pass;
  * no rules.

  Their `pathmap` fake matches only forward-slash rule sources, as Houdini does. The new mapping tests fail without the fix, and the three HDA tests fail without the HDA change. Mutating the new code in 10 places, then the HDA change in 8 more, made a test fail every time.
* A separate set of tests, written from the expected behavior without reading the fix's tests, passes on this branch: 56 tests, including OBJ, ROP, TOP, and DOP HDA cases and a randomized test over trees of locked HDAs.
* End to end on a Linux service-managed fleet with Houdini 20.5.684: the scene is a USD Import SOP with a Windows path under a WINDOWS path mapping rule, then a Transform SOP, then a SOP Import LOP, a Motion Blur LOP, and a Karma USD Render ROP. Without the fix, frame 1001 failed with `Invalid source .../usdimport1/lopimport1` for both forward-slash and backslash paths. With the fix, both got past the error and wrote frame 1001, and the log shows `Remapped SOP parm .../usdimport1/filepath1`. In this minimal scene, the USD Import geometry doesn't reach the image even with a native path, so the run proves the cook, not the pixels. In the same job, a native-path control, a File SOP reading `.bgeo.sc`, and a Sublayer LOP with a Windows path all rendered.
* A second end-to-end run, on the same fleet with Houdini 20.5, made the scene's OBJ geometry node a locked OBJ HDA. The HDA promotes `filepath1`, and the inner USD Import SOP reads it with `chs("../../filepath1")`. Houdini reported the HDA locked and the inner SOP not editable. Without the HDA change, frame 1001 failed with the same `Invalid source .../usdimport1/lopimport1`, for both slash forms. With the HDA change, both wrote frame 1001, and the log shows one `Remapped HDA parm .../filepath1` line each. A native-path HDA control and the original scene rendered on both.

#### Please run the integration tests and paste the results below.

A new integ test, `test_usd_import_sop_path_is_remapped`, with the scene `test/integ/test_scripts/usd_import_sop_pathmap_test/` (USD Import SOP, Transform, Geometry ROP), follows `test_lop_keyframe_pathmap_does_not_crash`. It has not been run yet: no licensed local `hython` was available. The farm run above covers the same path end to end.

## What

The two refresh frames count each request that a renewing auth sends, a source reads a JSON answer as served with `parse_json`, and a check of one page against another has its place in `Snapshot.sections`.

- `send_once` and a download's refusal keep the answers of an auth's flow in the rebuilt answer's `history` as statuses alone, with no body, header or request (`statuses_before` in `src/xippios/core/client/download.py`), so no bearer or credential stays with them.
- The client keeps a private count of the requests its pools hand to the transport, by httpx's request hook (`AsyncClient._sent`), and both frames read it: the snapshot frame's `_Capture.sent` and the reference frame's `_Meter.sent`. So a login, the resend after a refused bearer and the second login stand in the count, and so do the auth's requests in a call that an error ends, a refused login's among them.
- Both frames print the count as their last line, a failed run's too: the snapshot frame now prints it in a `finally` around its fetch and its compare or write (`_settle`), as the reference frame does. Where the client's auth is a `RenewingBearerAuth`, the line names the auth's token requests and resends.
- `xippios.core.refresh.parse_json` parses a JSON answer, refuses a key twice and a body that is no JSON with `changed`, and returns the document as served, so compact JSON is read. `read_json` reads through it and still holds the document to `dump_json`'s form. It is exported, pinned in `tests/test_public_surface.py` and told in the README's frame section.
- `Page.keyed`, ADR-0062 decision 4, conventions §3 and the README say that a keyed sample is never retried by the frame and that a renewing auth sends it once more after a refused bearer. `RenewingBearerAuth`'s docstring and the README's bearer section say where `observe` sees the token answer and what the frames count. ADR-0062 decision 4 takes the count and the second reader, and decision 14 the reference frame's count, both edited in place since the record is new in this release.
- `Snapshot.sections`, conventions §3 and the README say that a check of one page against another runs in `sections`: it sees every row before anything is written, in every mode, returns `()` and raises `changed`. No code changes for it.
- One changelog fragment, `changed`, its Hand-apply note naming after each script the sources its items concern. Follow-up 17.1's fragment, unreleased, names after `scripts/refresh_reference.py` the nine sources that keep one.

## Proof

- `uv run pytest`: 2013 passed on `main` at https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/commit/e6487d957707bf3ac09b0fc05412970b0f7c0de9, after 17.1. Tests in https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/commit/b2e20bd04fcbc151c2fdd410ea0412a087e5f553 (red: the counts, the history, `parse_json`, the export and the two §3 pins), behavior in https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/commit/cc934550bc51c5b80a559ef446305f9d2ddeb652 and the documents in https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/commit/7fdccdab454a98bdb4f434a11d43dde01c78e64b (green).
- https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/commit/c2c7faeb6fd96e2b83dcd1b83f5d62b024dc9e64 adds a test of behavior that already stood, a check across pages in `sections` stopping the run with nothing written in both modes, so it passes at its commit and comes after them. The count of a failed snapshot run: test in https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/commit/4a5621e9f858e5da1c6c7bfc0d43917e32f3ff7d (red), behavior in https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/commit/9689ab4f75b57e6f5a5457ca1a8db48ae85cb927 (green). Fix round 1: test in https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/commit/418d4da92d908065131d11fef39ff9d0e70c4ec5 (red), fix in https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/commit/9e5a431de5d55cd3df5b506bb5a3fca224527aa3 (green).
- Read first: `test_the_run_counts_each_request_of_a_renewing_auth` in `tests/refresh/test_upstream.py` (a login, a 401, a second login and the resend: 5 requests with the guide, and a run whose login is refused prints 2, the guide and the login), `test_a_failed_run_prints_the_requests_it_sent` and `test_a_call_that_an_error_ends_counts_the_auth_s_requests_before_it` beside it and `test_the_requests_of_a_renewing_auth_are_counted` in `tests/refresh/test_reference.py`.
- `tests/refresh`, `tests/client`, `tests/test_public_surface.py` and `tests/test_conventions.py` on Python 3.13 and 3.14: 651 passed on each. `coordinate-gate` (ruff, format, mypy, pytest), `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` and `python3 -I scripts/adr_index.py --check` pass.
- Live calls: none. Every exchange in the tests is served by respx or `httpx.MockTransport`.
- Assumptions: a source's login is a `RenewingBearerAuth`, the one auth of core that sends requests of its own (ADR-0025). An `httpx.Auth` of a source's own that sends requests is counted by the client too, and its line names no auth.

## Consumers

- Every source with a refresh script: one that keeps a reader of JSON that refuses a duplicate key alone takes `parse_json` in its place, and these six carry one: sdk-x (`spec_document`), sdk-eurostat (the cube's reader), sdk-faostat (`load_json`), and sdk-usda-esr, sdk-usda-gats and sdk-usda-psd (`_document`), whose reader the FAS portal's kit in sdk-usda-fas may take for the three. A check of one page against another moves into `sections`.
- The two sources whose client's auth is a `RenewingBearerAuth`, sdk-faostat's login and sdk-google-mail's refresh token: each drops its own count of the frame's requests and keeps its count of logins.

## Decisions taken

1. The reader is named `parse_json`, beside `read_json` and `decode`, and refuses with `changed`, as the sources' readers do and as every hook stops the run, so `read_json`'s refusal of a key twice or of a body that is no JSON now reads `<url> changed: not usable JSON (...)` with its line on what to do, in place of `GET <url>: not usable JSON (...)`; what it refuses is the same (ADR-0062, decisions 4 and 5; ADR-0059, decision 5; https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/issues/579).
2. The history is kept as statuses alone by one helper, `statuses_before` in `client/download.py`, which `_send_once` and the download's `head_of` both call, so a caller of `send_once` or a hook that sees a download's refusal still sees one status for each earlier request of the call and no bearer. ADR-0037, ADR-0040 and ADR-0066 decide nothing of a rebuilt answer's history, and ADR-0066 decision 3 has `send_once` return the answer as it came (https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/issues/579).
3. Each frame's last line names the auth's requests only where the client's auth is a `RenewingBearerAuth`, so a run without a login prints its line as before (ADR-0025; https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/issues/579).
4. The snapshot frame prints its count in a `finally` around its fetch and its compare or write, a failed run's too once it began to fetch, as ADR-0062 decision 14 has the reference frame print it. The compare or the write moves into `_settle`, and the client that the frame built closes after that line, once the run compared or wrote, where it closed after the last request before (ADR-0062, decisions 4 and 14; https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/issues/579).
5. The line of `CLAUDE.md`'s layout for `upstream.py` stays as it is: it names the frame's declarations, `Snapshot` and `Page`, and none of its readers or helpers, `read_json`, `dump_json`, `decode` or `changed`, so the new reader joins none of them there. An edit of `CLAUDE.md` would make the PR the maintainer's for that line alone (CLAUDE.md, When something is unclear; https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/issues/579).
6. ADR-0062 is edited in place, decision 4 for the count, the keyed resend and the second reader, and decision 14 for the reference frame's count, since the record is accepted in this release and no version holds it yet (ADR-0062, Date 2026-11-24; https://github.com/xippios/sdk-core/issues/579).

author: tannevaled
body:
Validate the Renovate configuration with the same major the runner executes: `renovate@44` instead of `renovate@latest`, in every `npx --package` call of the `validate` job. The comment that records what was measured against `renovate@latest` is left as written.

## Why

`renovatebot/github-action` runs `ghcr.io/renovatebot/renovate:44` — a floating major hardcoded in its `src/docker.ts`, as the note at the foot of this workflow already says. The validator, through `renovate@latest`, follows npm's `latest` instead. Those two agree only until Renovate publishes major 45: from that day the check would judge this organisation's configuration with an engine the runner does not use, and could go red, or green, on a rule the runner never applies.

`renovate@44` keeps both on the same floating major, so nothing has to be raised by hand. The runner and the validator can still be a few minutes apart inside the major (npm and the image are published separately); that window is accepted.

This follows the reasoning of go-fleettools/fleettools#289 (closed in favour of go-fleettools/fleettools#282): the validator must judge the configuration as the thing that runs it sees it, which rules out an exact pin. An exact `RENOVATE_VERSION` pin was weighed and not used here: in go-slides/.github it needed three files and drifted within hours (go-slides/.github#10, go-slides/.github#12).

The same one-line change goes to every organisation whose `ci.yml` validates with `renovate@latest` and has no `RENOVATE_VERSION` pin, one pull request each.

Refs go-fleettools/fleettools#305 — stays open until every organisation is done.
Refs go-fleettools/fleettools#282 — floating versions in a `run:` step; a floating major is still one, so this does not close it.
Refs go-fleettools/fleettools#289 — already closed, cited for its reasoning only.
Refs go-slides/.github#10 — already merged, cited as the pin that drifted.
Refs go-slides/.github#12 — already merged, cited as the fix that pin needed.

author: jitsusama
body:
### 💡 TL;DR

elsewhere's far line now takes away a copy whose job closed a folder in it, and unpacks only archives with a plain ustar header, at the names its list held when checked. A version without each fix fails its test.

### 🧩 Problem

elsewhere runs a job in a copy of its tree on the far machine and takes the copy away once the job ends or is stopped. A job that closed a folder to its owner, as a build may, left rm unable to take what lay under it, so the copy stayed until a later run's sweep, which may never come. The copy step also read the job's list of archives twice, once to check the names and again to unpack, so a list rewritten between the reads unpacked an archive no check saw. And tar finds compression by itself, so an archive sent compressed unpacked past every bound a share keeps.

### 🔧 Solution

A step of its own, `CLEARING`, defines `cleared`, and every script puts it first. It makes each folder under the paths it's given the far line's own to enter and write, then removes them. `find -P` takes a link it meets as itself, so nothing below one is opened. Every clear of a copy, what lies beside it and the handover's folders uses it, as does the sweep.

The copy step reads the list into a variable once and feeds both passes, the check and the unpack, through a pipe into a subshell each. It uses a pipe rather than a here-document, which bash 3.2, the Mac's sh, writes to a temp file a fence may refuse. A list that can't be read is this machine's fault.

Before tar reads an archive, `od` reads its first header's magic, and anything but ustar's eight bytes exactly is refused as the job's fault. That catches an archive no near side of ours wrote, not one built to pass: a compressed archive can carry those bytes and still unpack. Its sender gains nothing, since its job runs on the far line anyway.

### 🔬 Validation

- Added: a job closes a folder in its copy, ends or is stopped, and must leave neither copy nor run file.
- Added: a stand-in tar rewrites the list as the first archive is read; the job sees only the checked archive.
- Added: archives with GNU's magic, or ustar's with its NUL moved, are refused before the job runs.
- Checked at 927ce390: gate `nix-offload there --never-ask --changed` passed; on a Mac, the suite and far:: under sh and dash passed, and the old compare failed only the NUL row.
- Not covered: an archive under 258 bytes is blamed on the machine.

author: itzsoftwaredevops-sys
body:
## Summary
- Updates `fetchUsdPrices` in `frontend/lib/prices.ts` to return `null` on non-OK HTTP responses, empty/invalid payloads, or network errors instead of returning `{}`.
- Updates `usePrices` in `frontend/lib/usePrices.ts` to only call `setPrices` when `fetchUsdPrices` returns a non-empty price map, preserving previously fetched prices across transient poll failures.
- Pauses polling while `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'` and triggers a refresh when the tab becomes visible again.
- Updates `usePrices.test.ts` to verify that empty/null responses do not overwrite prior prices and that background tabs do not poll.

## Why
Previously, `fetchUsdPrices` returned `{}` on failure. Since `{}` is truthy in JS, `if (active && p)` in `usePrices` overwrote valid cached prices with `{}` on any transient polling error, hiding all USD hints across the UI. Additionally, polling continued in hidden background tabs.

## Implementation
- `frontend/lib/prices.ts`: Changed `fetchUsdPrices` return type to `Promise<Record<string, number> | null>` and returned `null` on failure or empty price maps.
- `frontend/lib/usePrices.ts`: Checked `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'` before fetching, added `Object.keys(p).length > 0` check before calling `setPrices`, and subscribed to `visibilitychange` to reload when returning to `'visible'`.
- `frontend/lib/__tests__/usePrices.test.ts`: Added tests for success-then-failure price retention and `visibilityState` polling pause/resume.

## Testing
- Local test execution was not run because `frontend/node_modules` dependencies are not installed locally due to npm registry network timeouts; CI will execute the full test suite.

## Scope / Risk
- Scoped strictly to `frontend/lib/prices.ts`, `frontend/lib/usePrices.ts`, and `frontend/lib/__tests__/usePrices.test.ts`. Non-breaking fix.

Closes #540

author: dmashuda
body:
I ran every code example in LikeC4's DSL documentation (185 snippets from its repository) through `rustc4 check`. Before this, 132 read without a real error; now 181 do. The other four are one snippet that is a JSON-style illustration, not DSL.

The rule here is that anything LikeC4 accepts is either supported or a warning, never an error and never a silent difference. This closes the places where that was not true.

## Breaking: the order of a relationship's strings

`a -> b 'title' 'description' 'technology'`, as LikeC4 has it. The second string used to be the technology, so `a -> b 'calls' 'HTTPS'` now gives a description and no technology. The shop and delivery examples and the README now write `a -> b 'calls' { technology 'HTTPS' }`; `docs/shop.svg` is byte-for-byte the same.

Steps of a dynamic view still read title, then technology: LikeC4's docs show no positional form for them.

## Now supported

- Triple-quoted strings (`'''…'''`, `"""…"""`)
- `metadata` lists: `regions ['us', 'eu']`. A `where metadata.regions is 'eu'` matches any value in the list
- `a <-> b` and `a -[kind]<-> b` (a mark at each end), and `a .kind b`
- `extend a { }` adding tags, metadata and links; `extend a -> b 'title' { }` adding a relationship's tags and metadata; `extend a` with no body
- Tags on element and relationship kinds, inherited and merged; a relationship kind's `title`, `description` and `technology` as defaults
- Colors as `rgb(…)`, `rgba(…)` and 8-digit hex
- Relationship predicates of one kind: `a -[kind]-> b`, `* .kind b`, `-[kind]-> b`

## Now a warning ("not supported yet")

Were errors:
- `deploymentNode` kinds, `diff` blocks, `descriptionFile`
- `group` (what it includes is still included), `rank`, `routing ortho`, `order`, `with { }` after a relationship
- `opt`, `loop`, `alt`, `try`/`catch` in a dynamic view (their steps are kept, in order)
- the shape `agent`; `multiple` on a relationship; a link on a kind

Were silent:
- shapes `component`, `document`, `bucket` (drawn as rectangles); `border none`; arrows `crow` and `vee`
- `navigateTo` on a relationship or step; a view's `link`; a step's `metadata`; a tag's `{ }` body
- see-through colors (drawn solid)

## Still different, and not warned

- `a <-> b` counts as a→b for incoming and outgoing predicates
- `iconColor` does nothing; Markdown in a description is shown as written (the README says so)
- A relationship's links are read and dropped

## Checked

`bazel test //...` passes (11 of 11), rustfmt applied, clippy quiet. Three new tests: the new syntax, kinded predicates and groups, and all 22 new warnings. All three examples still check clean.

Coverage is what LikeC4's docs demonstrate. Syntax its grammar accepts but its docs never show would not have turned up.

author: jonruttan
body:
A bundle's release tarball held `bundle.xon`, `lib/`, `LICENSE` and `README.md`. A bundle that ships more lost the rest: x-roguelike has `data/` and `art/`.

## What changes

A bundle names what else it ships in its `bundle.xon`, on one line:

```x
(payload "data" "art")
```

`tools/bundle-kit/roll.sh` archives each with the rest. It refuses a payload that the tag lacks, that is not at the bundle's top, or that is `bundle.xon`, `lib` or `version`.

This is the release half of jonruttan/x-bundle#5, which makes `x -l bundle -- install DIR` copy the same row's paths. With both, an install from a checkout and an install from a release carry the same files.

The row's name, `payload`, is my pick; say so if you want another. Nothing in the platform reads the row at boot.

## Checked

- `make gates-fast` passed in the pre-push hook, `check-bundle-kit-roll` among them.
- That check has three new cases: the declared payload is in the tarball and no more; a missing payload is refused; one outside the bundle is refused.

Not checked: a real release of a bundle with a payload row.

author: jejjohnson
body:
A surface drifter has neither a third dimension nor a turbulence closure; what a model or a reanalysis gives is a diffusivity K. No library in the stack has a step for it, and its drift term is easy to leave out: without ∂K/∂x, particles gather where K is small, at every step size.

| | Before | After this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Step | none | `displacement_step`, the Itô step with the drift ∂K/∂x |
| Protocol | none | `RandomDisplacement`, a `ParticleStep` in two or three dimensions |
| Diffusivity | none | `Diffusivity`, `ConstantDiffusivity`, `GriddedDiffusivity` |

**What stays the same.** The loop, the walls and the other steps.

**Differences from the issue.**
- The drift comes from one forward-mode pass per axis over all the particles, in place of a gradient per particle. It is the same number, because a particle's K depends on its own position only, and the protocol now says so.
- Walls in two dimensions raise, because they reflect the third column.
- `GriddedDiffusivity` has a `fit`, as `GriddedVelocity` has.

## Evidence
- G1-diffusion: a uniform cloud stays uniform between walls (6 h at 30 s, K between 0.020 and 0.048 m² s⁻¹, K′ ≠ 0 at the walls) and in a periodic domain (KS at 1e-3, 20,000 particles). The same runs without the drift are refused.
- With constant K the displacement variance is 2 K t within four standard errors on each axis (50,000 particles); without noise it is an Euler step to rounding.
- Reciprocity: the time spent in one box from the other, forward, equals the time backward within four combined standard errors, and is 182 s as measured for the issue.
- A gridded linear field gives its slope as the drift to 1e-12. K = 0 leaves the Euler path with finite gradients; gradients in K match central differences to 1e-6.
- It runs under `integrate` in two and three dimensions, forward and backward.
- `ruff`, `ty`, the doctests, `docs-api` and `docs-check` pass.

Closes #24

## Who did the work
- Claude Opus 5.5, in Claude Code.
